attributes.name: Superficie de tierras de cultivo y producción
attributes.description:
### Visión general  
  
El conjunto de datos de Tierras de Cultivo y Producción muestra el área cosechada a nivel mundial, la producción y el rendimiento de seis cultivos principales: trigo, soja, arroz, maíz, café y algodón. El conjunto de datos se derivó del Modelo de Asignación de Producción Espacial (SPAM) de 2010. El modelo de SPAM tenía como objetivo desglosar (a escala reducida) las estadísticas nacionales y subnacionales de cultivos utilizando una variedad de insumos, como la superficie de las tierras de cultivo, la ubicación de las áreas de regadío, la idoneidad de los cultivos y los rendimientos potenciales, las densidades de población rural, las características de los sistemas de producción y los precios de los cultivos. Los datos de los cultivos se redujeron a una resolución espacial de 5 minutos de arco. Esta resolución espacial es de aproximadamente 10 kilómetros x 10 kilómetros en el ecuador, pero [cambia con la distancia] (https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-de-latitud-y-longitud-distancia-4070616) desde el ecuador. 

Juntos, el maíz, el arroz, la soja y el trigo representan casi dos tercios de las calorías agrícolas mundiales. La demanda mundial de estos cultivos está aumentando como resultado de los cambios en la dieta, el aumento de los niveles de población y el aumento de la demanda de biocombustibles. El aumento de la demanda de estos recursos afectará significativamente el uso de la tierra y los recursos, el cambio climático, las agendas políticas y los desarrollos tecnológicos. Es necesaria una comprensión integral de la distribución espacial actual de los cultivos del mundo para abordar preventivamente estos efectos. El conjunto de datos de área de tierras de cultivo y producción se puede utilizar para comprender el alcance y la productividad de los cultivos globales clave, lo que ayudará a abordar la demanda de cultivos alimentarios y sus efectos. 

El conjunto de datos de Área de Tierras de Cultivo y Producción fue generado por el [Grupo Consultivo sobre el Programa Internacional de Investigación Agrícola sobre Políticas, Instituciones y Mercados (CGIAR-PIM)](https://pim.cgiar.org/about/). CGIAR-PIM brinda apoyo a políticas que ayudan a los agricultores a mejorar sus vidas, producir alimentos nutritivos y asequibles, y proteger el suelo, el agua y la biodiversidad en los paisajes rurales. El programa está dirigido por el [Instituto Internacional de Investigación de Políticas Alimentarias (IFPRI)](https://www.ifpri.org/about), un centro de investigación CGIAR-PIM. El IFPRI proporciona soluciones de políticas basadas en la investigación para reducir de manera sostenible la pobreza y acabar con el hambre en los países en desarrollo. El conjunto de datos Crop Land Area and Production fue parte del conjunto de datos SPAM más grande, que se desarrolló para la iniciativa de investigación HarvestChoice. Llevado a cabo por ifpri, [HarvestChoice] (https://www.ifpri.org/project/harvestchoice) generó productos de conocimiento para ayudar a guiar las inversiones estratégicas para mejorar el bienestar de las personas pobres en el África subsahariana y el sur de Asia a través de una agricultura más productiva y rentable.
  
### Metodología  
  
El objetivo principal del SPAM es desglosar las estadísticas de los cultivos (por ejemplo, el área cosechada, la cantidad de producción y el rendimiento) por diferentes sistemas agrícolas y asignar aún más dichas estadísticas desagregadas en unidades espacialmente cuadriculadas. Todo el procedimiento implica un enfoque de fusión de datos que combina información de diferentes fuentes y a diferentes escalas espaciales mediante el despliegue de varias coincidencias.
y procesos de calibración. Luego, todos los elementos de datos son procesados por el modelo de optimización, que genera resultados a nivel de cuadrícula. Hay tres submódulos en un modelo estandarizado de SPAM: desagregación, optimización y asignación. El SPAM2010 se conceptualiza en base a esta configuración general, al tiempo que agrega mejoras metodológicas y de datos adicionales, que incluyen principalmente la actualización del año base, la expansión de la cobertura de unidades administrativas subnacionales, la extensión de la lista de cultivos y la sustitución del último mapa híbrido de tierras de cultivo como capa de asignación básica.

El primer paso para el SPAM es desagregar las estadísticas de cultivos de la producción agrícola (por ejemplo, el rendimiento, el área cosechada y la producción total) por niveles de unidades administrativas (k), tipo de cultivo (j) y sistema agrícola (l) de escala más gruesa a escala más fina. Los cuatro sistemas de producción se definieron por tipo de agua y gestión:
- Irrigado – entrada alta (I)
- Rainfed – alta entrada (H)
- Rainfed – entrada baja (L)
- Rainfed – subsistencia (S)

Los cuatro sistemas agrícolas conceptualizados están delineados principalmente por el sistema de suministro de agua y los insumos utilizados por los agricultores, a pesar de que los datos mundiales sobre las cuotas del sistema agrícola para cada cultivo están en gran medida ausentes. Para un pequeño número de países grandes, por ejemplo, Brasil, China, India, Rusia, Estados Unidos, los autores tienen datos sobre las cuotas del sistema agrícola a nivel ADM1. Para los otros países, los autores asignaron las cuotas del sistema agrícola nacional a cada nivel de ADM1 y luego ajustaron las cuotas individuales del sistema agrícola de ADM1 a la luz de la evidencia de apoyo. En el caso de los sistemas agrícolas de regadío, las cuotas específicas de los cultivos se obtienen dividiendo la superficie cosechada cultivada bajo riego bajo pleno control obtenido del [Sistema Mundial de Información sobre el Agua y la Agricultura (AQUASTAT)](https://www.fao.org/aquastat/en/), [MIRCA](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2008GB003435), y
estadísticas a nivel de país por la superficie total cosechada.

El módulo de optimización en SPAM2010 es casi el mismo que en versiones anteriores. Los autores aplicaron un proceso de entropía cruzada en el Sistema de Modelado Algebraico General (GAMS), que asegura que el procedimiento de optimización itera hasta que se encuentre una solución. Una vez que la asignación es exitosa, lo que significa que se ha encontrado una solución óptima o localmente óptima, la rutina devuelve inmediatamente el área física asignada por red, cultivo y sistema de cultivo, y el programa continúa con el posprocesamiento automáticamente.

El modelo SPAM utilizó insumos biológicos y económicos adicionales para asignar las estadísticas dentro de cada píxel. Datos de entrada incluidos (entre varios otros):
- Unidades administrativas
- Tipo de cultivo
- Sistema agrícola
- Superficie cosechada ajustada
- Superficie total adecuada en cada cuadrícula por cultivo y sistema de cultivo
- Precios de los cultivos
- Accesibilidad al mercado en cada cuadrícula
- Densidad de población

Nuestro catálogo de datos proporciona tres de los indicadores de producto esenciales de SPAM2010:

- Área cosechada: también medida en hectáreas, el área cosechada es al menos tan grande como el área física, pero a veces más, ya que también representa múltiples cosechas de un cultivo en la misma parcela. Al igual que para el área física, el área cosechada se calcula para cada sistema de producción, y la suma de todas las áreas cosechadas de todos los sistemas de producción en un píxel asciende al área total cosechada del
píxel. La suma de todas las áreas cosechadas de los cultivos en un píxel puede ser mayor que el tamaño del píxel.
- Producción: para cada sistema productivo y cultivo, la producción se calcula multiplicando el área cosechada por su rendimiento correspondiente. Se mide en toneladas métricas. La producción total de un cultivo incluye la producción de todos los sistemas de producción de ese cultivo.
- Rendimiento: es la cantidad de producción por superficie cosechada y medida en kilogramos por hectárea. Es una medida de la productividad. El rendimiento total de un cultivo, cuando se consideran todos los sistemas de producción, es el promedio ponderado de los rendimientos de los cuatro sistemas.

Para obtener la documentación completa, consulte la fuente [metodología](https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/12/3545/2020/essd-12-3545-2020.pdf).
  
### Información adicional  
  
Nuestro catálogo de datos muestra solo un subconjunto del conjunto de datos. Los Datos Estadísticos Mundiales de Producción de Cultivos Desagregados Espacialmente para 2010 Versión 2.0 tienen datos para otros 36 cultivos (42 en total). El conjunto de datos completo también incluye el área física y el valor de producción para los 42 cultivos. Para acceder al conjunto de datos completo e información adicional, haga clic en el botón "Más información".

Nuestro catálogo de datos ha mostrado anteriormente datos para [2005](https://bit.ly/3CjoFYc). Este conjunto de datos se archivó porque se ha cambiado la metodología.  
  
### Visualización de los datos  
  
Nuestro equipo reformateó este conjunto de datos antes de mostrarlo en el catálogo de datos de la IRG. Consulte la documentación sobre cómo recuperamos los datos en [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/tree/master/foo_005_rw1_crop_area_production).  
  
### Descargo de responsabilidad  
  
Extractos de esta página de descripción fueron tomados de los metadatos de origen.

info.technical_title: Datos de estadísticas mundiales de producción de cultivos desglosados espacialmente para 2010 versión 2.0
info.functions: Producción, área cosechada y rendimiento de los cultivos de trigo, soja, arroz, maíz, café y algodón para el año 2010
info.cautions:
- Como se indicó anteriormente, las estimaciones de SPAM dependen de la extensión y veracidad de los datos de entrada primarios como la mayoría de los modelos. SPAM2010 requiere datos sobre 42 cultivos en más de 200 países para la temporada de producción. Idealmente, estos datos deberían recopilarse a nivel ADM2; sin embargo, esto no siempre es posible. Es particularmente difícil en algunos países como Somalia y Nigeria, donde la fiabilidad
los datos no están disponibles, o los diferentes datos de entrada simplemente entran en conflicto entre sí.
- Dado que la mayoría de las estadísticas de cultivo no están delineadas por el sistema agrícola, se requieren estimaciones de las cuotas de producción en cada uno de los cuatro sistemas en cuestión. Para convertir las estadísticas del área cosechada en las estadísticas de área física utilizadas en el modelo, se deben recopilar datos adicionales sobre las intensidades de cultivo por cultivo y sistemas agrícolas. Los autores recopilaron datos oficiales o publicados y se basaron en juicios de expertos como último recurso cuando no pudieron encontrar otras fuentes.
- La amplia gama de fuentes de datos, la cobertura y los matices regionales de la producción de cultivos tienen implicaciones metodológicas. En primer lugar, existen posibles compensaciones entre la consistencia de los datos y la fiabilidad de los datos. Por ejemplo, hay requisitos del modelo (es decir, intensidades de cultivo y cuotas del sistema agrícola) que no están disponibles de manera consistente dentro de un país al nivel administrativo necesario. A menudo, estas cifras se toman de los valores a nivel nacional, aunque no reflejen la realidad a nivel administrativo. En segundo lugar, el cultivo múltiple e intercalado no se maneja de manera sofisticada dentro del SPAM. Estos tipos de patrones de cultivo solo se tienen en cuenta utilizando un único valor de intensidad de cultivo por cultivo, sistema agrícola y (posiblemente) unidad subnacional. Por último, el mercado es importante tanto para los agricultores de subsistencia como para los comerciales. En SPAM, los autores se basan en la densidad de población para una representación indirecta de la proximidad del mercado.
- Por último, pero no menos importante, los autores sugieren precaución al comparar los productos SPAM directamente a través de las etapas de tiempo. Esto se debe en gran parte a que existen errores del sistema en varios productos de datos.

attributes.name: பயிர் நில பரப்பு மற்றும் உற்பத்தி
attributes.description:
### கண்ணோட்டம்  
  
கோதுமை, சோயாபீன்ஸ், அரிசி, மக்காச்சோளம், காபி மற்றும் பருத்தி ஆகிய ஆறு முக்கிய பயிர்களுக்கான உலகளாவிய அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதி, உற்பத்தி மற்றும் மகசூல் ஆகியவற்றை பயிர் நிலம் மற்றும் உற்பத்தி தரவுத்தொகுப்பு காட்டுகிறது. தரவுத்தொகுப்பு 2010 இடஞ்சார்ந்த உற்பத்தி ஒதுக்கீடு மாதிரியிலிருந்து (எஸ்பிஏஎம்) பெறப்பட்டது. பயிர் நில மேற்பரப்பு, பாசனப் பகுதிகளின் அமைவிடம், பயிர் பொருத்தம் மற்றும் சாத்தியமான மகசூல், கிராமப்புற மக்கள்தொகை அடர்த்தி, உற்பத்தி அமைப்புகளின் பண்புகள் மற்றும் பயிர் விலைகள் போன்ற பல்வேறு உள்ளீடுகளைப் பயன்படுத்தி தேசிய மற்றும் துணை தேசிய பயிர் புள்ளிவிவரங்களை பிரிப்பதை எஸ்பிஏஎம் மாதிரி நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டது. பயிர்த் தரவு 5 வில் நிமிடங்களின் இடஞ்சார்ந்த தெளிவுத்திறனுக்கு கீழ்மட்டமாக்கப்பட்டது. இந்த இடஞ்சார்ந்த தீர்மானம் பூமத்திய ரேகையில் தோராயமாக 10 கிலோமீட்டர் x 10 கிலோமீட்டர் ஆகும், ஆனால் [தூரத்துடன் மாற்றங்கள்](https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-ன்-அட்சரேகை-மற்றும்-தீர்க்கரேகை-தூரம்-தூரம்-4070616) பூமத்திய ரேகையிலிருந்து. 

ஒன்றாக, மக்காச்சோளம், அரிசி, சோயாபீன்ஸ் மற்றும் கோதுமை ஆகியவை உலகளாவிய விவசாய கலோரிகளில் கிட்டத்தட்ட மூன்றில் இரண்டு பங்கு ஆகும். உணவு மாற்றங்கள், அதிகரித்து வரும் மக்கள் தொகை அளவுகள் மற்றும் அதிகரித்த உயிரி எரிபொருள் தேவை ஆகியவற்றின் விளைவாக இந்த பயிர்களுக்கான உலகளாவிய தேவை அதிகரித்து வருகிறது. இந்த வளங்களுக்கான அதிகரித்த தேவை நிலம் மற்றும் வள பயன்பாடு, காலநிலை மாற்றம், அரசியல் நிகழ்ச்சி நிரல்கள் மற்றும் தொழில்நுட்ப வளர்ச்சிகள் ஆகியவற்றை கணிசமாக பாதிக்கும். இந்த விளைவுகளை முன்கூட்டியே நிவர்த்தி செய்வதற்கு, உலகின் பயிர்களின் தற்போதைய இடஞ்சார்ந்த பரவல் பற்றிய ஒரு விரிவான புரிதல் அவசியம். முக்கிய உலகளாவிய பயிர்களின் அளவு மற்றும் உற்பத்தித்திறன் ஆகியவற்றைப் புரிந்துகொள்ள பயிர் நிலப் பரப்பு மற்றும் உற்பத்தி தரவுத்தொகுப்பைப் பயன்படுத்தலாம், இது உணவுப் பயிர் தேவை மற்றும் அதன் விளைவுகளை நிவர்த்தி செய்ய உதவும். 

பயிர் நிலப் பரப்பு மற்றும் உற்பத்தி தரவுத்தொகுப்பு [கொள்கைகள், நிறுவனங்கள் மற்றும் சந்தைகள் மீதான சர்வதேச விவசாய ஆராய்ச்சித் திட்டம் குறித்த ஆலோசனைக் குழு (சிஜிஐஏஆர்-பி.ஐ.எம்)] (https://pim.cgiar.org/about/) உருவாக்கப்பட்டது. விவசாயிகள் தங்கள் வாழ்க்கையை மேம்படுத்தவும், சத்தான மற்றும் மலிவு விலை உணவுகளை உற்பத்தி செய்யவும், கிராமப்புற நிலப்பரப்புகளில் மண், நீர் மற்றும் பல்லுயிர் பெருக்கத்தைப் பாதுகாக்கவும் உதவும் கொள்கைகளுக்கு சிஜிஐஏஆர்-பிம் ஆதரவளிக்கிறது. இந்த திட்டம் [சர்வதேச உணவுக் கொள்கை ஆராய்ச்சி நிறுவனம் (ஐ.எஃப்.பி.ஆர்.ஐ)](https://www.ifpri.org/about), ஒரு சிஜிஐஆர்-பி.ஐ.எம் ஆராய்ச்சி மையத்தால் வழிநடத்தப்படுகிறது. ஐ.எஃப்.பி.ஆர்.ஐ வளரும் நாடுகளில் வறுமையை நிரந்தரமாகக் குறைப்பதற்கும் பட்டினியை முடிவுக்குக் கொண்டுவருவதற்கும் ஆராய்ச்சி அடிப்படையிலான கொள்கைத் தீர்வுகளை வழங்குகிறது. பயிர் நிலப் பரப்பு மற்றும் உற்பத்தி தரவுத்தொகுப்பு பெரிய ஸ்பேம் தரவுத்தொகுப்பின் ஒரு பகுதியாக இருந்தது, இது ஹார்வெஸ்ட்சாய்ஸ் ஆராய்ச்சி முன்முயற்சிக்காக உருவாக்கப்பட்டது. IFPRI ஆல் நடத்தப்பட்ட, [HarvestChoice](https://www.ifpri.org/project/harvestchoice) அதிக உற்பத்தி மற்றும் இலாபகரமான விவசாயத்தின் மூலம் துணை சஹாரா ஆபிரிக்கா மற்றும் தெற்காசியாவில் உள்ள ஏழை மக்களின் நல்வாழ்வை மேம்படுத்த மூலோபாய முதலீடுகளுக்கு வழிகாட்ட உதவும் அறிவு தயாரிப்புகளை உருவாக்கியது.
  
### முறைமை  
  
எஸ்.பி.ஏ.எம் இன் முக்கிய நோக்கம் பயிர் புள்ளிவிவரங்களை (எ.கா., அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதி, உற்பத்தி அளவு மற்றும் மகசூல்) வெவ்வேறு விவசாய அமைப்புகளால் பிரிப்பதும், அத்தகைய பிரிக்கப்பட்ட புள்ளிவிவரங்களை மேலும் இடஞ்சார்ந்த கட்டமைக்கப்பட்ட அலகுகளாக ஒதுக்குவதும் ஆகும். முழு செயல்முறையும் ஒரு தரவு இணைவு அணுகுமுறையை இன்றியமையாததாக்குகிறது, இது பல்வேறு மூலங்களிலிருந்தும் வெவ்வேறு இடஞ்சார்ந்த அளவீடுகளிலிருந்தும் தகவல்களை ஒருங்கிணைக்கிறது, இது பல்வேறு பொருத்தங்களைப் பயன்படுத்துவதன் மூலம் வெவ்வேறு இடஞ்சார்ந்த அளவீடுகளில் இருந்து தகவல்களை ஒருங்கிணைக்கிறது
மற்றும் அளவுத்திருத்த செயல்முறைகள். பின்னர் அனைத்து தரவு உறுப்புகளும் தேர்வுமுறை மாதிரி மூலம் செயலாக்கப்படுகின்றன, இது கட்டம் மட்டத்தில் முடிவுகளை உருவாக்குகிறது. ஒரு தரப்படுத்தப்பட்ட எஸ்பிஏஎம் மாதிரியில் மூன்று துணை மாதிரிகள் உள்ளன: பிரித்தல், தேர்வுமுறை மற்றும் ஒதுக்கீடு. ஸ்பாம் 2010 இந்த பொதுவான அமைப்பை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டது, அதே நேரத்தில் இது மேலும் வழிமுறை மற்றும் தரவு மேம்பாடுகளைச் சேர்க்கிறது, இதில் முக்கியமாக அடிப்படை ஆண்டின் புதுப்பிப்பு, துணைதேசிய நிர்வாக-அலகு கவரேஜின் விரிவாக்கம், பயிர் பட்டியலின் விரிவாக்கம் மற்றும் சமீபத்திய கலப்பின பயிர் நில வரைபடத்தை அடிப்படை ஒதுக்கீடு அடுக்காக பதிலீடு செய்தல் ஆகியவை அடங்கும்.

விவசாய உற்பத்தியின் (எ.கா., மகசூல், அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதி மற்றும் மொத்த உற்பத்தி) பயிர் புள்ளிவிவரங்களை நிர்வாக அலகு அளவுகள் (கே), பயிர் வகை (ஜே), மற்றும் விவசாய அமைப்பு (எல்) ஆகியவற்றால் கரடுமுரடான அளவு முதல் நேர்த்தியான அளவு வரை பிரிப்பதே எஸ்பிஏஎம் இன் முதல் படியாகும். நான்கு உற்பத்தி அமைப்புகள் நீர் மற்றும் மேலாண்மை வகையால் வரையறுக்கப்பட்டன:
- நீர்ப்பாசனம் – உயர் உள்ளீடு (I)
- மானாவாரி – உயர் உள்ளீடு (எச்)
- மானாவாரி - குறைந்த உள்ளீடு (எல்)
- மானாவாரி - வாழ்வாதாரம் (எஸ்)

ஒவ்வொரு பயிருக்கும் விவசாய முறை பங்குகள் பற்றிய உலகளாவிய தரவுகள் பெரும்பாலும் இல்லாத போதிலும், நான்கு கருத்துருவாக்கப்பட்ட விவசாய முறைகள் முக்கியமாக நீர் வழங்கல் அமைப்பு மற்றும் விவசாயிகள் பயன்படுத்தும் இடுபொருட்களால் விவரிக்கப்படுகின்றன. பிரேசில், சீனா, இந்தியா, ரஷ்யா, அமெரிக்கா போன்ற சிறிய எண்ணிக்கையிலான பெரிய நாடுகளுக்கு, ஏ.டி.எம்.1 அளவில் விவசாய முறை பங்குகள் குறித்த தரவுகள் ஆசிரியர்களிடம் உள்ளன. மற்ற நாடுகளுக்கு ஆசிரியர்கள் தேசிய விவசாய முறையின் பங்குகளை ஒவ்வொரு ஏ.டி.எம்.1 மட்டத்திற்கும் பகிர்ந்தளித்தனர், பின்னர் ஆதரவு ஆதாரங்களின் வெளிச்சத்தில் தனிப்பட்ட ஏ.டி.எம்.1 விவசாய முறை பங்குகளை சரிசெய்தனர். நீர்ப்பாசன விவசாய முறைமைகளுக்கு, [நீர் மற்றும் விவசாயம் பற்றிய உலகளாவிய தகவல் முறைமை (AQUASTAT)] (https://www.fao.org/aquastat/en/), [MIRCA](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2008GB003435) மற்றும்
ஒட்டுமொத்த அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதியின் மூலம் நாடு அளவிலான புள்ளிவிவரங்கள்.

SPAM2010 இல் உள்ள தேர்வுமுறை தொகுதி முந்தைய பதிப்புகளில் இருந்ததைப் போலவே உள்ளது. ஆசிரியர்கள் பொது இயற்கணித மாடலிங் அமைப்பில் (ஜி.ஏ.எம்.எஸ்) ஒரு குறுக்கு-என்ட்ரோபி செயல்முறையைப் பயன்படுத்தினர், இது ஒரு தீர்வு கண்டுபிடிக்கப்படும் வரை தேர்வுமுறை செயல்முறை மீண்டும் செயல்படுகிறது என்பதை உறுதிப்படுத்துகிறது. ஒதுக்கீடு வெற்றிகரமாக இருந்தால், ஒரு உகந்த அல்லது உள்நாட்டில் உகந்த தீர்வு கண்டுபிடிக்கப்பட்டது என்று அர்த்தம், வழக்கமான உடனடியாக கட்டம், பயிர் மற்றும் விவசாய அமைப்பு மூலம் ஒதுக்கப்பட்ட இயற்பியல் பகுதியைத் திருப்பித் தருகிறது, மேலும் நிரல் தானாகவே பிந்தைய செயலாக்கத்துடன் தொடர்கிறது.

எஸ்பிஏஎம் மாதிரி ஒவ்வொரு பிக்சலுக்குள்ளும் புள்ளிவிவரங்களை ஒதுக்க கூடுதல் உயிரியல் மற்றும் பொருளாதார உள்ளீடுகளைப் பயன்படுத்தியது. உள்ளீட்டுத் தரவு சேர்க்கப்பட்டுள்ளது (பலவற்றில்):
- நிர்வாக அலகுகள்
- பயிர் வகை
- விவசாய முறை
- சரிசெய்யப்பட்ட அறுவடை பகுதி
- பயிர் மற்றும் விவசாய முறை மூலம் ஒவ்வொரு கட்டத்திலும் மொத்த பொருத்தமான பரப்பளவு
- பயிர் விலைகள்
- ஒவ்வொரு கட்டத்திலும் சந்தை அணுகல்தன்மை
- சனத்தொகை அடர்த்தி

எங்கள் தரவு அட்டவணை SPAM2010 அத்தியாவசிய வெளியீடு குறிகாட்டிகளில் மூன்றை வழங்குகிறது:

- அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதி: மேலும் ஹெக்டேர்களில் அளவிடப்படுகிறது, அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதி குறைந்தபட்சம் இயற்பியல் பரப்பளவைப் போலவே பெரியது, ஆனால் சில நேரங்களில் அதிகமாக உள்ளது, ஏனெனில் இது ஒரே நிலத்தில் ஒரு பயிரின் பல அறுவடைகளுக்கும் காரணமாகிறது. இயற்பியல் பரப்பளவைப் போலவே, அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதியும் ஒவ்வொரு உற்பத்தி அமைப்புக்கும் கணக்கிடப்படுகிறது, மேலும் ஒரு பிக்சலில் அனைத்து உற்பத்தி அமைப்புகளின் அனைத்து அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதிகளின் கூட்டுத்தொகையானது மொத்த அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பரப்பளவுக்கு சமம்
படவரைபுள்ளி. ஒரு பிக்சலில் பயிர்களின் அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட அனைத்து பகுதிகளின் கூட்டுத்தொகை பிக்சல் அளவை விட பெரியதாக இருக்கலாம்.
- உற்பத்தி: ஒவ்வொரு உற்பத்தி அமைப்பு மற்றும் பயிருக்கும், அதன் தொடர்புடைய மகசூலால் அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பரப்பை பெருக்குவதன் மூலம் உற்பத்தி கணக்கிடப்படுகிறது. இது மெட்ரிக் டன்களில் அளவிடப்படுகிறது. ஒரு பயிரின் மொத்த உற்பத்தியானது, அந்தப் பயிரின் அனைத்து உற்பத்தி முறைகளின் உற்பத்தியையும் உள்ளடக்குகிறது.
- மகசூல்: அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட ஒரு பகுதிக்கான உற்பத்தியின் அளவு மற்றும் ஹெக்டேருக்கு கிலோகிராம்களில் அளவிடப்படுகிறது. இது உற்பத்தித்திறனின் அளவீடு ஆகும். ஒரு பயிரின் மொத்த மகசூல், அனைத்து உற்பத்தி முறைகளையும் கருத்தில் கொள்ளும்போது, நான்கு முறைகளின் விளைச்சலின் எடையிடப்பட்ட சராசரியாகும்.

முழு ஆவணப்படுத்தலுக்கு, தயவுசெய்து மூலத்தைப் பார்க்கவும் [வழிமுறை](https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/12/3545/2020/essd-12-3545-2020.pdf).
  
### கூடுதல் தகவல்  
  
எங்கள் தரவு அட்டவணை தரவுத்தொகுப்பின் துணைக்குழுவை மட்டுமே காட்டுகிறது. 2010 ஆம் ஆண்டிற்கான உலகளாவிய இடஞ்சார்ந்த-பிரிக்கப்பட்ட பயிர் உற்பத்தி புள்ளிவிவரத் தரவு 2.0 பதிப்பு 36 பிற பயிர்களுக்கான தரவுகளைக் கொண்டுள்ளது (மொத்தம் 42). முழு தரவுத்தொகுப்பில் அனைத்து 42 பயிர்களுக்கான இயற்பியல் பரப்பளவு மற்றும் உற்பத்தியின் மதிப்பும் அடங்கும். முழு தரவுத்தொகுப்பு மற்றும் கூடுதல் தகவலுக்கான அணுகலுக்கு, "மேலும் அறிக" பொத்தானைக் கிளிக் செய்யவும்.

எங்கள் தரவு அட்டவணை முன்னர் [2005] (https://bit.ly/3CjoFYc) க்கான தரவைக் காட்டியது. முறைமை மாற்றப்பட்டதால் இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பு காப்பகப்படுத்தப்பட்டது.  
  
### தரவை காட்சிப்படுத்தல்  
  
WRI இன் தரவு அட்டவணையில் காண்பிக்கப்படுவதற்கு முன்பு எங்கள் குழு இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பை மறுவடிவமைத்தது. [Github] இல் தரவை நாங்கள் எவ்வாறு மீட்டெடுத்தோம் என்பதற்கான ஆவணங்களைப் பார்க்கவும் (https://github.com/resource-வாட்ச்/தரவு-முன்-செயலாக்கம்/மரம்/மாஸ்டர்/foo_005_rw1_crop_area_production).  
  
### பொறுப்புத்துறப்பு  
  
இந்த விளக்கப் பக்கத்தின் பகுதிகள் மூல மெட்டாடேட்டாவிலிருந்து எடுக்கப்பட்டன.

info.technical_title: 2010 பதிப்பு 2.0 க்கான உலகளாவிய இடஞ்சார்ந்த-பிரிக்கப்பட்ட பயிர் உற்பத்தி புள்ளிவிவர தரவு
info.functions: 2010 ஆம் ஆண்டுக்கான கோதுமை, சோயாபீன்ஸ், நெல், மக்காச்சோளம், காபி மற்றும் பருத்திப் பயிர்களின் உற்பத்தி, அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பரப்பு மற்றும் மகசூல்
info.cautions:
- முன்னர் குறிப்பிட்டபடி, எஸ்பிஏஎம் மதிப்பீடுகள் பெரும்பாலான மாதிரிகளைப் போலவே முதன்மை உள்ளீட்டுத் தரவின் அளவு மற்றும் உண்மைத்தன்மையைப் பொறுத்தது. SPAM2010 உற்பத்தி பருவத்தில் 200 க்கும் மேற்பட்ட நாடுகளில் 42 பயிர்கள் பற்றிய தரவு தேவைப்படுகிறது. வெறுமனே, இந்த தரவு ஒரு ADM2 மட்டத்தில் சேகரிக்கப்பட வேண்டும்; இருப்பினும், இது எப்போதும் சாத்தியமில்லை. சோமாலியா மற்றும் நைஜீரியா போன்ற ஒரு சில நாடுகளில் இது குறிப்பாக கடினமாக உள்ளது, அங்கு நம்பகமான
தரவு கிடைக்கவில்லை, அல்லது வெவ்வேறு உள்ளீட்டு தரவு ஒருவருக்கொருவர் முரண்படுகிறது.
- பெரும்பாலான பயிர்ச்செய்கைப் புள்ளிவிபரங்கள் விவசாய முறையினால் வரையறுக்கப்படுவதில்லை என்பதால், கேள்விக்குரிய நான்கு முறைமைகளில் ஒவ்வொன்றின் கீழும் உற்பத்திப் பங்குகளின் மதிப்பீடுகள் தேவைப்படுகின்றன. அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதி புள்ளிவிவரங்களை மாதிரியில் பயன்படுத்தப்படும் இயற்பியல்-பரப்பு புள்ளிவிவரங்களாக மாற்றுவதற்கு, பயிர் மற்றும் விவசாய முறைகள் மூலம் பயிர் தீவிரம் குறித்த கூடுதல் தரவுகள் சேகரிக்கப்பட வேண்டும். ஆசிரியர்கள் அதிகாரப்பூர்வ அல்லது வெளியிடப்பட்ட தரவுகளைச் சேகரித்து, மற்ற ஆதாரங்களைக் கண்டுபிடிக்க முடியாதபோது நிபுணர்களின் தீர்ப்புகளை கடைசி முயற்சியாக நம்பியிருந்தனர்.
- பயிர் உற்பத்தியின் பரந்த அளவிலான தரவு மூலங்கள், கவரேஜ் மற்றும் பிராந்திய நுணுக்கங்கள் ஆகியவை முறைசார் தாக்கங்களைக் கொண்டுள்ளன. முதலாவதாக, தரவு நிலைத்தன்மை மற்றும் தரவு நம்பகத்தன்மைக்கு இடையில் சாத்தியமான வர்த்தக-ஆஃப்கள் உள்ளன. எடுத்துக்காட்டாக, தேவையான நிர்வாக மட்டத்தில் ஒரு நாட்டிற்குள் தொடர்ந்து கிடைக்காத மாதிரியின் தேவைகள் (அதாவது, பயிர் தீவிரம் மற்றும் விவசாய முறை பங்குகள்) உள்ளன. பெரும்பாலும், இந்த எண்கள் நிர்வாக மட்டத்தில் யதார்த்தத்தை பிரதிபலிக்காவிட்டாலும், தேசிய அளவிலான மதிப்புகளிலிருந்து எடுக்கப்படுகின்றன. இரண்டாவதாக, எஸ்பிஏஎம்-க்குள் பல மற்றும் ஊடுபயிர்களை அதிநவீன முறையில் கையாளுவதில்லை. இந்த வகையான பயிர் முறைகள் ஒரு பயிருக்கு ஒற்றை பயிர் தீவிர மதிப்பு, விவசாய முறை மற்றும் (சாத்தியமான) துணை தேசிய அலகு ஆகியவற்றைப் பயன்படுத்துவதற்கு மட்டுமே கணக்கிடப்படுகின்றன. இறுதியாக, வாழ்வாதார விவசாயிகளுக்கும், வணிக விவசாயிகளுக்கும் சந்தை முக்கியமானது. எஸ்.பி.ஏ.எம் இல், ஆசிரியர்கள் சந்தை அருகாமையின் மறைமுக பிரதிநிதித்துவத்திற்காக மக்கள்தொகை அடர்த்தியை நம்பியுள்ளனர்.
- கடைசியாக ஆனால் குறைந்தது அல்ல, எஸ்பிஏஎம் தயாரிப்புகளை நேர கட்டங்களில் நேரடியாக ஒப்பிடும் போது ஆசிரியர்கள் எச்சரிக்கையுடன் இருக்க பரிந்துரைக்கின்றனர். பல்வேறு தரவு தயாரிப்புகளில் கணினி பிழைகள் இருப்பதால் இது பெரும்பாலும் உள்ளது.

[www.resourcewatch.org] (https://www.resourcewatch.org).

attributes.name: పంట భూమి వైశాల్యం మరియు ఉత్పత్తి
attributes.description:
### అవలోకనం  
  
పంట భూమి మరియు ఉత్పత్తి డేటాసెట్ ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా పండించిన ప్రాంతం, ఉత్పత్తి మరియు ఆరు ప్రధాన పంటలకు దిగుబడిని చూపిస్తుంది: గోధుమ, సోయాబీన్, వరి, మొక్కజొన్న, కాఫీ మరియు పత్తి. డేటాసెట్ 2010 ప్రాదేశిక ఉత్పత్తి కేటాయింపు నమూనా (స్పామ్) నుండి తీసుకోబడింది. పంట భూమి ఉపరితలం, నీటిపారుదల ప్రాంతాల యొక్క స్థానం, పంట అనుకూలత మరియు సంభావ్య దిగుబడులు, గ్రామీణ జనాభా సాంద్రతలు, ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థల లక్షణాలు మరియు పంట ధరలు వంటి వివిధ రకాల ఇన్పుట్లను ఉపయోగించి జాతీయ మరియు ఉప-జాతీయ పంట గణాంకాలను (డౌన్ స్కేల్) విడదీయడం (డౌన్ స్కేల్) ఎస్పిఎఎమ్ నమూనా లక్ష్యంగా పెట్టుకుంది. పంట డేటా 5 ఆర్క్ నిమిషాల ప్రాదేశిక రిజల్యూషన్ కు డౌన్ స్కేల్ చేయబడింది. ఈ ప్రాదేశిక రిజల్యూషన్ భూమధ్యరేఖ వద్ద సుమారు 10 కిలోమీటర్లు x 10 కిలోమీటర్లు ఉంటుంది, కానీ [దూరాన్ని బట్టి మారుతుంది](https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-ఆఫ్-అక్షాంశం-మరియు-రేఖాంశం-దూరం-4070616) భూమధ్యరేఖ నుండి. 

మొక్కజొన్న, వరి, సోయాబీన్ మరియు గోధుమలు కలిసి ప్రపంచ వ్యవసాయ కేలరీలలో మూడింట రెండు వంతుల వాటాను కలిగి ఉన్నాయి. ఆహార మార్పులు, పెరుగుతున్న జనాభా స్థాయిలు మరియు పెరిగిన జీవ ఇంధన డిమాండ్ ఫలితంగా ఈ పంటలకు ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా డిమాండ్ పెరుగుతోంది. ఈ వనరులకు పెరిగిన గిరాకీ భూమి మరియు వనరుల వినియోగం, వాతావరణ మార్పు, రాజకీయ అజెండాలు మరియు సాంకేతిక అభివృద్ధిని గణనీయంగా ప్రభావితం చేస్తుంది. ఈ ప్రభావాలను ముందస్తుగా పరిష్కరించడానికి ప్రపంచ పంటల ప్రస్తుత ప్రాదేశిక పంపిణీ గురించి సమగ్ర అవగాహన అవసరం. కీలకమైన ప్రపంచ పంటల యొక్క పరిధి మరియు ఉత్పాదకతను అర్థం చేసుకోవడానికి క్రాప్ ల్యాండ్ ఏరియా మరియు ప్రొడక్షన్ డేటాసెట్ ఉపయోగించబడుతుంది, ఇది ఆహార పంట డిమాండ్ మరియు దాని ప్రభావాలను పరిష్కరించడంలో సహాయపడుతుంది. 

క్రాప్ ల్యాండ్ ఏరియా అండ్ ప్రొడక్షన్ డేటాసెట్ [పాలసీలు, ఇన్ స్టిట్యూషన్స్, అండ్ మార్కెట్స్ పై ఇంటర్నేషనల్ అగ్రికల్చరల్ రీసెర్చ్ ప్రోగ్రామ్ పై కన్సల్టేటివ్ గ్రూప్ ఆన్ ఇంటర్నేషనల్ అగ్రికల్చరల్ రీసెర్చ్ ప్రోగ్రామ్(సిజిఐఎఆర్-పిఐఎం)](https://pim.cgiar.org/about/) ద్వారా జనరేట్ చేయబడింది. సిజిఐఎఆర్-పిఐఎమ్ రైతుల జీవితాలను మెరుగుపరచడానికి, పోషకమైన మరియు చౌకైన ఆహారాన్ని ఉత్పత్తి చేయడానికి మరియు గ్రామీణ ప్రకృతి దృశ్యాలలో నేల, నీరు మరియు జీవవైవిధ్యాన్ని రక్షించడానికి సహాయపడే విధానాలకు మద్దతు ఇస్తుంది. ఈ కార్యక్రమానికి [ఇంటర్నేషనల్ ఫుడ్ పాలసీ రీసెర్చ్ ఇనిస్టిట్యూట్ (IFPRI)](https://www.ifpri.org/about), ఒక CGIAR-PIM రీసెర్చ్ సెంటర్ నాయకత్వం వహిస్తుంది. అభివృద్ధి చెందుతున్న దేశాలలో పేదరికాన్ని సుస్థిరంగా తగ్గించడానికి మరియు ఆకలిని అంతం చేయడానికి ఐఎఫ్ పిఆర్ ఐ పరిశోధన ఆధారిత విధాన పరిష్కారాలను అందిస్తుంది. పంట భూమి ప్రాంతం మరియు ఉత్పత్తి డేటాసెట్ అనేది పెద్ద స్పామ్ డేటాసెట్ లో భాగంగా ఉంది, ఇది హార్వెస్ట్ ఛైస్ రీసెర్చ్ ఇనిషియేటివ్ కొరకు అభివృద్ధి చేయబడింది. ఐ.ఎఫ్.పి.ఆర్.ఐ చే నిర్వహించబడింది, [హార్వెస్ట్ చోయిస్](https://www.ifpri.org/project/harvestchoice) మరింత ఉత్పాదక మరియు లాభదాయకమైన వ్యవసాయం ద్వారా ఉప-సహారా ఆఫ్రికా మరియు దక్షిణాసియాలోని పేద ప్రజల శ్రేయస్సును మెరుగుపరచడానికి వ్యూహాత్మక పెట్టుబడులకు మార్గనిర్దేశం చేయడంలో సహాయపడటానికి జ్ఞాన ఉత్పత్తులను ఉత్పత్తి చేసింది.
  
#### మెథడాలజీ  
  
వివిధ వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థల ద్వారా పంట గణాంకాలను (ఉదా. కోసిన ప్రాంతం, ఉత్పత్తి పరిమాణం మరియు దిగుబడి) విడదీయడం మరియు అటువంటి విడదీయబడిన గణాంకాలను ప్రాదేశికంగా గ్రిడ్ చేయబడ్డ యూనిట్ లుగా మరింత కేటాయించడం స్పామ్ యొక్క ప్రధాన ఉద్దేశ్యం. ఈ మొత్తం ప్రక్రియ డేటా ఫ్యూజన్ అప్రోచ్ ని కలిగి ఉంటుంది, ఇది వివిధ వనరుల నుండి సమాచారాన్ని మిళితం చేస్తుంది మరియు వివిధ ప్రాదేశిక ప్రమాణాల వద్ద వివిధ మ్యాచింగ్ లను మోహరించడం ద్వారా
మరియు క్రమాంకన ప్రక్రియలు. అప్పుడు అన్ని డేటా ఎలిమెంట్లు ఆప్టిమైజేషన్ మోడల్ ద్వారా ప్రాసెస్ చేయబడతాయి, ఇది గ్రిడ్ స్థాయిలో ఫలితాలను జనరేట్ చేస్తుంది. ఒక ప్రామాణిక స్పామ్ నమూనాలో మూడు ఉపమాడ్యూల్స్ ఉన్నాయి: డిసాగ్రెగేషన్, ఆప్టిమైజేషన్ మరియు కేటాయింపు. ఈ సాధారణ అమరిక ఆధారంగా స్పామ్2010 భావనాత్మకంగా రూపొందించబడింది, అయితే ఇది మరింత మెథడాలజికల్ మరియు డేటా మెరుగుదలలను జోడిస్తుంది, వీటిలో ప్రధానంగా బేస్ ఇయర్ యొక్క నవీకరణ, ప్రత్యామ్నాయ పరిపాలనా-యూనిట్ కవరేజ్ యొక్క విస్తరణ, పంట జాబితా యొక్క విస్తరణ, మరియు తాజా హైబ్రిడ్ క్రాప్ ల్యాండ్ మ్యాప్ ను ప్రాథమిక కేటాయింపు పొరగా భర్తీ చేయడం వంటివి ఉంటాయి.

వ్యవసాయ ఉత్పత్తి యొక్క పంట గణాంకాలను (ఉదా. దిగుబడి, కోత విస్తీర్ణం మరియు మొత్తం ఉత్పత్తి) పరిపాలనా-యూనిట్ స్థాయిలు (కె), పంట రకం (జె), మరియు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ (l) ముతక స్కేలు నుండి సూక్ష్మమైన స్కేలుకు విడదీయడం స్పామ్ యొక్క మొదటి దశ. నాలుగు ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థలు నీరు మరియు నిర్వహణ రకం ద్వారా నిర్వచించబడ్డాయి:
- నీటిపారుదల - అధిక ఇన్ పుట్ (I)
- వర్షాధారం - అధిక ఇన్పుట్ (H)
- వర్షాధారం - తక్కువ ఇన్పుట్ (ఎల్)
- వర్షాధారం - జీవనోపాధి (ఎస్)

ప్రతి పంటకు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ వాటాలపై ప్రపంచ డేటా ఎక్కువగా లేనప్పటికీ, నాలుగు భావనాత్మక వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థలు ప్రధానంగా నీటి సరఫరా వ్యవస్థ మరియు రైతులు ఉపయోగించే ఇన్ పుట్ ల ద్వారా వర్ణించబడ్డాయి. బ్రెజిల్, చైనా, ఇండియా, రష్యా, యునైటెడ్ స్టేట్స్ వంటి చిన్న సంఖ్యలో పెద్ద దేశాలకు, రచయితలు ఎడిఎమ్1 స్థాయిలో వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ వాటాలపై డేటాను కలిగి ఉన్నారు. ఇతర దేశాలకు రచయితలు జాతీయ వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ వాటాలను ప్రతి ఎడిఎమ్ 1 స్థాయికి కేటాయించారు మరియు తరువాత మద్దతు ఇచ్చే సాక్ష్యాల వెలుగులో వ్యక్తిగత ఎడిఎమ్ 1 వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ వాటాలను సర్దుబాటు చేశారు. నీటి పారుదల వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థల కొరకు, [గ్లోబల్ ఇన్ఫర్మేషన్ సిస్టమ్ ఆన్ వాటర్ అండ్ అగ్రికల్చర్ (AQUASTAT)](https://www.fao.org/aquastat/en/), [MIRCA](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2008GB003435) నుంచి పొందిన పూర్తి నియంత్రణ నీటిపారుదల కింద సాగు చేయబడ్డ పంట విస్తీర్ణాన్ని విభజించడం ద్వారా పంట-నిర్దిష్ట వాటాలు పొందబడతాయి.
మొత్తం కోత విస్తీర్ణం ద్వారా దేశ-స్థాయి గణాంకాలు.

స్పామ్2010లోని ఆప్టిమైజేషన్ మాడ్యూల్, మునుపటి వెర్షన్ ల వలేనే దాదాపుగా ఒకేవిధంగా ఉంటుంది. సాధారణ బీజగణిత మోడలింగ్ సిస్టమ్ (జిఎఎంఎస్) లో రచయితలు క్రాస్-ఎంట్రోపీ ప్రక్రియను వర్తింపజేశారు, ఇది ఒక పరిష్కారం కనుగొనే వరకు ఆప్టిమైజేషన్ ప్రక్రియ పునరావృతమయ్యేలా చూస్తుంది. కేటాయింపు విజయవంతం అయిన తరువాత, అంటే ఒక అనుకూలమైన లేదా స్థానికంగా అనుకూలమైన పరిష్కారం కనుగొనబడింది, రొటీన్ వెంటనే గ్రిడ్, పంట మరియు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ ద్వారా కేటాయించబడిన భౌతిక ప్రాంతాన్ని తిరిగి ఇస్తుంది, మరియు ప్రోగ్రామ్ ఆటోమేటిక్ గా పోస్ట్ ప్రాసెసింగ్ తో కొనసాగుతుంది.

స్పామ్ నమూనా ప్రతి పిక్సెల్ లోపల గణాంకాలను కేటాయించడానికి అదనపు జీవ మరియు ఆర్థిక ఇన్పుట్లను ఉపయోగించింది. ఇన్ పుట్ డేటా చేర్చబడింది (అనేక ఇతర వాటి మధ్య):
- పరిపాలనా విభాగాలు
- పంట రకం
- వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ
- సర్దుబాటు చేయబడిన కోత ప్రాంతం
- పంట మరియు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ ద్వారా ప్రతి గ్రిడ్ లో మొత్తం అనువైన ప్రాంతం
- పంట ధరలు
- ప్రతి గ్రిడ్ లో మార్కెట్ యాక్సెసబిలిటీ
- జనసాంద్రత

మా డేటా కేటలాగ్ మూడు SPAM2010 ఆవశ్యక అవుట్ పుట్ ఇండికేటర్ లను అందిస్తుంది:

- కోసిన ప్రాంతం: హెక్టార్లలో కూడా కొలుస్తారు, కోతకు గురైన ప్రాంతం కనీసం భౌతిక ప్రాంతం అంత పెద్దదిగా ఉంటుంది, అయితే కొన్నిసార్లు ఎక్కువ ఎందుకంటే ఇది ఒకే పొలంలో ఒక పంట యొక్క బహుళ కోతలకు కూడా కారణమవుతుంది. భౌతిక వైశాల్యం వలె, కోతకు గురైన ప్రాంతం ప్రతి ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థ కొరకు లెక్కించబడుతుంది, మరియు పిక్సెల్ లో అన్ని ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థల యొక్క అన్ని కోత ప్రాంతాల యొక్క మొత్తం కోతకు గురైన ప్రాంతం యొక్క మొత్తం కోతకు గురైన ప్రాంతానికి సమానం అవుతుంది.
పిక్సెల్. ఒక పిక్సెల్ లో పంట కోతకు గురైన అన్ని ప్రాంతాల మొత్తం పిక్సెల్ పరిమాణం కంటే పెద్దదిగా ఉండవచ్చు.
- ఉత్పత్తి: ప్రతి ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థ మరియు పంటకు, దాని సంబంధిత దిగుబడి ద్వారా కోసిన విస్తీర్ణాన్ని గుణించడం ద్వారా ఉత్పత్తిని లెక్కిస్తారు. దీనిని మెట్రిక్ టన్నులలో కొలుస్తారు. ఒక పంట యొక్క మొత్తం ఉత్పత్తిలో ఆ పంట యొక్క అన్ని ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థల ఉత్పత్తి ఉంటుంది.
- దిగుబడి: కోతకు వచ్చిన ప్రతి ప్రాంతానికి ఉత్పత్తి మొత్తం మరియు హెక్టారుకు కిలోగ్రాములలో లెక్కించబడుతుంది. ఇది ఉత్పాదకత యొక్క కొలత. అన్ని ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థలను పరిగణనలోకి తీసుకున్నప్పుడు, ఒక పంట యొక్క మొత్తం దిగుబడి నాలుగు వ్యవస్థల యొక్క దిగుబడి యొక్క బరువు కలిగిన సగటు.

పూర్తి డాక్యుమెంటేషన్ కొరకు, దయచేసి సోర్స్ [మెథడాలజీ](https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/12/3545/2020/essd-12-3545-2020.pdf) చూడండి.
  
### అదనపు సమాచారం  
  
మా డేటా కేటలాగ్ డేటాసెట్ యొక్క ఉపసమితిని మాత్రమే చూపుతుంది. 2010 వెర్షన్ 2.0 కొరకు గ్లోబల్ స్పేషియల్లీ-డిస్అగ్రెగేటెడ్ క్రాప్ ప్రొడక్షన్ స్టాటిస్టిక్స్ డేటా 36 ఇతర పంటలకు సంబంధించిన డేటాను కలిగి ఉంది (మొత్తం 42). పూర్తి డేటాసెట్ లో భౌతిక వైశాల్యం మరియు మొత్తం 42 పంటల కొరకు ఉత్పత్తి విలువ కూడా ఉంటుంది. పూర్తి డేటాసెట్ మరియు అదనపు సమాచారానికి ప్రాప్యత కోసం, "మరింత తెలుసుకోండి" బటన్ మీద క్లిక్ చేయండి.

మా డేటా కేటలాగ్ ఇంతకు ముందు [2005](https://bit.ly/3CjoFYc) కొరకు డేటాను చూపించింది. ఈ డేటాసెట్ ఆర్కైవ్ చేయబడింది ఎందుకంటే మెథడాలజీ మార్చబడింది.  
  
### డేటాను విజువలైజ్ చేయడం  
  
డబ్ల్యుఆర్ఐ యొక్క డేటా కేటలాగ్ లో ప్రదర్శించడానికి ముందు మా బృందం ఈ డేటాసెట్ ను పునర్నిర్మించింది. [Github](https://github.com/resource-వాచ్/డేటా-ప్రీ-ప్రాసెసింగ్/ట్రీ/మాస్టర్/foo_005_rw1_crop_area_production)పై డేటాను మేం ఏవిధంగా తిరిగి పొందాం అనే దానిపై డాక్యుమెంటేషన్ ని చూడండి.  
  
### డిస్ క్లెయిమర్  
  
ఈ వివరణ పేజీ యొక్క సారాంశాలు మూల మెటాడేటా నుండి తీసుకోబడ్డాయి.

info.cautions:
- ఇంతకు ముందు పేర్కొన్నట్లుగా, స్పామ్ అంచనాలు చాలా మోడల్స్ వలె ప్రాథమిక ఇన్ పుట్ డేటా యొక్క పరిధి మరియు వాస్తవికతపై ఆధారపడి ఉంటాయి. స్పామ్2010 ఉత్పత్తి సీజన్ కొరకు 200కు పైగా దేశాల్లోని 42 పంటలకు సంబంధించిన డేటా అవసరం అవుతుంది. ఆదర్శవంతంగా, ఈ డేటాను ఎడిఎమ్2 స్థాయిలో సేకరించాలి; అయితే, ఇది ఎల్లప్పుడూ సాధ్యం కాదు. సోమాలియా మరియు నైజీరియా వంటి కొన్ని దేశాలలో ఇది ముఖ్యంగా కష్టంగా ఉంది, ఇక్కడ నమ్మదగినది
డేటా లభ్యం కావడం లేదు, లేదా విభిన్న ఇన్ పుట్ డేటా ఒకదానితో మరొకటి విభేదిస్తుంది.
- చాలా పంటల గణాంకాలు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థచే వర్ణించబడనందున, ప్రశ్నార్ధకమైన నాలుగు వ్యవస్థలలో ప్రతి దాని క్రింద ఉత్పత్తి వాటాల అంచనాలు అవసరం. కోతకు గురైన ప్రాంత గణాంకాలను నమూనాలో ఉపయోగించిన భౌతిక-ప్రాంత గణాంకాలకు మార్చడానికి, పంట మరియు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థల ద్వారా పంట తీవ్రతలపై అదనపు డేటాను సేకరించాలి. రచయితలు అధికారిక లేదా ప్రచురించిన డేటాను సేకరించారు మరియు ఇతర వనరులను కనుగొనలేనప్పుడు చివరి ప్రయత్నంగా నిపుణుల తీర్పులపై ఆధారపడారు.
- విస్తృత శ్రేణి డేటా వనరులు, కవరేజీ మరియు పంట ఉత్పత్తి యొక్క ప్రాంతీయ సూక్ష్మాంశాలు విధానపరమైన చిక్కులను కలిగి ఉంటాయి. మొదట, డేటా స్థిరత్వం మరియు డేటా విశ్వసనీయత మధ్య సంభావ్య ట్రేడ్-ఆఫ్ లు ఉన్నాయి. ఉదాహరణకు, అవసరమైన పరిపాలనా స్థాయిలో ఒక దేశంలో స్థిరంగా అందుబాటులో లేని నమూనా యొక్క ఆవశ్యకతలు (అంటే, పంట తీవ్రతలు మరియు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ వాటాలు) ఉన్నాయి. తరచుగా, ఈ సంఖ్యలు జాతీయ స్థాయి విలువల నుండి తీసుకోబడతాయి, అయినప్పటికీ అవి పరిపాలనా స్థాయిలో వాస్తవికతను ప్రతిబింబించకపోవచ్చు. రెండవది, బహుళ మరియు అంతరపంటలు స్పామ్ లోపల అధునాతన రీతిలో నిర్వహించబడవు. ఈ రకమైన పంట పోకడలు ప్రతి పంటకు, వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ, మరియు (బహుశా) ఉపజాతి యూనిట్ కు ఒకే పంట తీవ్రత విలువను ఉపయోగించడానికి మాత్రమే లెక్కించబడతాయి. చివరగా, మార్కెట్ జీవనోపాధి రైతులకు మరియు వాణిజ్య రైతులకు ముఖ్యమైనది. స్పామ్ లో, రచయితలు మార్కెట్ సామీప్యం యొక్క పరోక్ష ప్రాతినిధ్యం కోసం జనసాంద్రతపై ఆధారపడతారు.
- చివరిది కానీ కనీసం కాదు, స్పామ్ ఉత్పత్తులను సమయ దశలలో నేరుగా పోల్చేటప్పుడు రచయితలు జాగ్రత్తగా ఉండాలని సూచిస్తున్నారు. వివిధ డేటా ఉత్పత్తుల్లో సిస్టమ్ దోషాలు ఉండటం దీనికి ప్రధాన కారణం.
info.citation: ఇంటర్నేషనల్ ఫుడ్ పాలసీ రీసెర్చ్ ఇన్స్టిట్యూట్, 2019, "గ్లోబల్ స్పేషియల్లీ-డిస్అగ్రెగేటెడ్ క్రాప్ ప్రొడక్షన్ స్టాటిస్టిక్స్ డేటా ఫర్ 2010 వెర్షన్ 2.0", https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/PRFF8V, హార్వర్డ్ డేటావర్స్, వి4. వరల్డ్ రిసోర్సెస్ ఇనిస్టిట్యూట్, (తేదీ) ద్వారా యాక్సెస్ చేసుకోబడింది. attributes.name: dis.006 ReliefWeb Disaster Events in the News
Current Disaster Events
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
This dataset shows countries experiencing disaster events that are actively being monitored by ReliefWeb. These disaster events include floods, droughts, severe local storms, tropical cyclones, storm surges, tsunamis, earthquakes, wildfires, cold waves, heat waves, volcanic activity, landslides, mudslides, snow avalanches, epidemics, insect infestations, and technological disasters.
  
  

ReliefWeb is the leading humanitarian information source on global crises and disasters. ReliefWeb continuously collects the latest information on ongoing crises and monitors for emerging situations. By providing reliable and timely information, they enable humanitarian workers to make informed decisions and plan effective responses.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
ReliefWeb's editorial team monitors and collects information from more than 4,000 key sources, including humanitarian agencies at the international and local levels, governments, think tanks and research institutions, and the media. From this information, ReliefWeb editors identify and select the content that is most relevant to global humanitarian workers. For the full documentation, please click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/nrt-scripts/tree/master/dis_006_reliefweb_disasters). Coordinates provided in the source data were used to map this data for display on Resource Watch.   
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

info.name: Current Disaster Events
info.technical_title: ReliefWeb Disasters
info.functions: Current and ongoing global disaster events
info.cautions:
Because ReliefWeb editors select the content that is most relevant to global humanitarian workers, not all current disasters may be reported in this dataset.
  
  

Each point is located in the center of a particular country to show that the country is currently experiencing at least one disaster event. The location of this point does not indicate the actual location of the disaster.

attributes.name: Aqueduct Baseline Water Stress
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
Baseline water stress measures the ratio of total water withdrawals to available renewable surface and groundwater supplies. A higher ratio indicates more competition among users. These ratios were then converted into risk scores based on the thresholds defined in the methodology. These risk scores range from low water stress (<10%) to extremely high water stress (>80%). Water withdrawals include domestic, industrial, irrigation and livestock consumptive and non-consumptive uses. Available renewable water supplies include surface and groundwater supplies and the impact of upstream consumptive water use and large dams on downstream water availability. Water stress values are available per sub-basin (HydroBASIN level 6).   
  
### Methodology  
  
Aqueduct used the global hydrological model, PCRaster Global Water Balance (PCR-GLOBWB
2), to calculate five indicators. Baseline water stress is one of those indicators and was calculated using the gross and net total withdrawal and available water per sub-basin time series from the default model run.   
  
The model was first used to calculate a time series of water stress per catchment per month. To calculate water stress, total withdrawals were divided by the available renewable surface and groundwater supplies. Net consumptive water use was subtracted from the total available renewable water supply before the ratio was calculated. The results were output in 12 monthly time series time series of water stress per sub-basin. Water resources in delta sub-basins were pooled.  
  
Next, the time series were converted into baseline values using an ordinary least squares (OLS) regression. For example, the regression output for January 2020 represents the chronic, long-term condition of water stress in January’s from 1960 to 2020. This was repeated for every month and then averaged into an annual value.  All raw values were limited to a maximum of 100% and a minimum of 0%.   
  
Sub-basins that were classified “Arid and low water use” were handled separately and were given a raw value for baseline water stress of -1.  
  
Finally, raw baseline water stress values were converted to risk scores between 0 and 5, based on quantiles. These scores were placed into categories indicating how high the risk for this indicator is. The thresholds for raw baseline water stress values and the corresponding risk scores that were used in each category are defined below as Risk Category (Risk Scores): Raw Value Thresholds.  
  
- Low (0-1): < 10%  
  
- Low to medium (1-2): 10-20%  
  
- Medium to high (2-3): 20-40%  
  
- High (3-4): 40-80%  
  
- Extremely high (4-5): >80%  
  
- Arid and low water use (5): -1  
  
For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://www.wri.org/publication/aqueduct-30).  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

info.name: Aqueduct 4.0 Baseline Water Stress
info.technical_title: Baseline Water Stress, Aqueduct 4.0
info.functions: Measures the ratio of water withdrawals to available renewable surface and groundwater at the catchment scale
info.cautions:
Although the underlying models have been validated, the results were not. Water stress remains subjective and cannot be measured directly. The lack of direct validation makes it impossible to assess some of the parameters in our calculation such as the length of the input time series, regression method and optimal moving window size.  
  
The water stress indicator presented here did not explicitly take environmental flow requirements, water quality or access to water into account. Multiple views exists regarding what to include in a water stress indicator. Views differ regarding what to include in a water stress indicator [(Vanham et al. 2018)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2017.09.056).  
  
Coastal and island sub-basins were often grouped to make the area of the sub-basins more homogeneous. The assumption of shared water resources might not hold in aggregated coastal sub-basins.  
  
Water resources in PCR-GLOBWB 2 were pooled in abstraction zones. This assumption differs from the sub-basin approach in Aqueduct. This is one of the prime reasons for further processing of the PCR-GLOBWB 2 data.  
  
Results were tailored towards large scale comparison of water related risks. The indicators have limited added value on a local scale.
info.citation: Hofste, R., S. Kuzma, S. Walker, E.H. Sutanudjaja, et. al. 2019. “Aqueduct 3.0: Updated Decision-Relevant Global Water Risk Indicators.” Technical Note. Washington, DC: World Resources Institute. Available online at: https://www.wri.org/publication/aqueduct-30. Accessed through Resource Watch, (date). [www.resourcewatch.org](https://www.resourcewatch.org)

attributes.name: Built-Up Area Change
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Built-Up Area Change dataset shows areas of built-up extent and change from 2000 to 2020, and the data is available at 30 m spatial resolution, globally. The dataset was created by the Global Land Analysis and Discovery Lab (GLAD) laboratory. Built-up lands represent the most intensive land uses of humankind in the form of cities, villages and infrastructure. Given the heterogeneous nature of built-up lands, advanced algorithms such as deep learning neural networks, which examine spatial context, are a powerful alternative to traditional per pixel classifiers. The presented maps are the first of their kind for the GLAD lab and will soon be produced at annual time-scales and temporally filtered to provide a consistent record of global built-up land development.
  
  
The Global Land Analysis and Discovery Lab (GLAD) laboratory in the Department of Geographical Sciences at UMD investigates methods, causes, and impacts of global land surface change. Earth observation imagery is the primary data source, and the land cover extent and change is the primary topic of interest. GLAD aspires to generate new science insights concerning land resources, educate the next generation of remote sensing-based land change scientists, and disseminate land monitoring capabilities to operational settings nationally and internationally.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
Built-up land consists of human constructed land surfaces associated with infrastructure, commercial and residential land uses. The global annual built-up land extent and gain map was made using annual metrics derived from the Landsat 5, 7 and 8 satellites for 2000 through 2020. To facilitate the deep learning application, GLAD only employed interquartile metrics from the red, near-infrared and both shortwave infrared bands. Training data were primarily from the Open Street Map data base. 
  
  
Due to the contextual nature of built-up lands, particularly settlements, GLAD employed a deep learning convolution neural network algorithm. The input metrics were related to the training data through the U-Net convolutional neural network architecture, which has proven to work robustly over a variety of tasks in remote sensing ([Brandt et al., 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2824-5?proof=t%29Nature), and [Feng, et al., 2018)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8573826). For parameterizing the algorithm, GLAD randomly sampled patches with a size of 128x128 pixels (each pixel corresponds to 30x30 m). Weight decay and data augmentation were utilized in the form of down sampling, rotations, and flips for the gradient-based optimization of the U-Net parameters. A moving window approach employing 10x10 degree tiles was employed to better fit to local development patterns. Final 2000 and 2020 per pixel probabilities were generated and validation data used to assist in final thresholding of the layers in depicting 2000 and 2020 extents and 2000-2020 gain in built-up lands. 
  
  
For the full documentation, please click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows datasets from the GLAD laboratory for [Cropland Extent](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/50634b51-ea2e-4cc1-9e4b-8f26a389a301), [Cropland Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/ec282483-4f5c-4fb8-ace7-8e557826781a), [Tree Height Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/64a3e126-000b-46fb-aaf4-8ac765a8263b), [Water Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/b83ad197-eb95-44e2-8ec3-3351ab926421), [Snow/Ice Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/5a796ce9-71d4-42b0-922d-056a86e5eb72), and [Land Cover Map](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/06e734af-66f0-4c3e-ac71-1b99f3cbfe1d).
  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch.  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

info.name: Built-Up Area Change
info.technical_title: Built-up land extent and gain, 2000-2020
info.functions: Built-up area extent and change from 2000 to 2020
info.cautions:
- A probability-based sample analysis is the recommended good practice approach to estimating land cover and land use extent and change. The global surface built-up land map enables a higher sampling efficiency through stratification and can be extended to report on regional and national dynamics. Current validation results inform only the global scale.
  
  
- Small features, such as isolated farm houses or huts, are generally not captured by this prototype map. Future versions will employ reference data to refine the definition at the sub-pixel scale.
  
  
- Small roads, especially with dirt or gravel surfaces, are inconsistently characterized and result in both omission and commission errors in areas with linear features, for example agriculture lands.
  
  
- Deep learning parameterization, for example normalization, can lead to boundaries along our moving windows. Future iterations will address this issue, hoping to avoid any artifacts from the algorithm itself.

(2022) The global 2000-2020 land cover and land use change dataset derived from the Landsat archive: first results. Frontiers in Remote Sensing. attributes.name: [Archived] Subnational Political Boundaries
attributes.description:
_**This dataset has been archived, and we will no longer be updating or maintaining it. We recommend using [this dataset](8011fc2e-7b0b-4107-849f-c44a9031b8e0) as a replacement.**_
  
The Database of Global Administrative Areas (GADM) is a spatial database of the location of the world's administrative areas (or administrative boundaries). Administrative areas in this database are countries and lower-level subdivisions such as provinces, departments, bibhag, Bundesländer, daerah istimewa, fivondronana, krong, landsvæðun, opština, sous-préfectures, counties, and thana.   
  
GADM describes where these administrative areas are (the "spatial features"), and for each area it provides some attributes, such as the name and variant names. This data set does not include disputed areas. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Learn More link.  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

attributes.name: Projected Permafrost Loss
attributes.description:
Projected permafrost extents, created through the research of Chadburn et al. (2017), estimates a sensitivity of permafrost area loss to global mean warming at stabilization of 2°C. The latest climate models all predict warming of high-latitude soils and thus thawing of permafrost under future climate change, but with widely varying magnitudes of permafrost thaw. It is estimated that permafrost area will eventually be reduced by over 40% if the climate is stabilized at 2°C above preindustrial levels. This research showed that it is possible to infer the sensitivity of permafrost to future global warming by using present-day spatial distribution of permafrost and mean annual air temperature (MAAT). Permafrost extent is estimated at a 0.5 degree spatial resolution and is restricted to the Northern Hemisphere. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Learn More link.

info.cautions: The robustness of this approach depends on the extent to which this relationship between permafrost area and air temperature remains consistent under climate change. In addition, this approach calculates the committed permafrost distribution for each global mean temperature. During a period of warming, the actual changes in permafrost area will lag behind this quasi-equilibrium state, due to the long timescale of warming for the deep ground.

attributes.name: foo.027.rw1 Observed and Potential Crop Yields
Observed and Potential Crop Yields
attributes.description:
The Yield Gap and Potential Yield for Major Crops data set was created by EarthStat, the University of Minnesota's Institute on the Environment and the Land Use (UMN IonE), and the Global Environment Lab at the University of British Columbia (LUGE Lab at UBC) for 16 major crops. Yield gaps are defined as the difference between observed crop yields and the potential yield at the same location. Yield gaps were estimated by comparing observed yields to potential yields determined by identifying high-yielding areas within zones, or bins, of similar climate. To classify climates, 2 parameters, which are known to be fundamental drivers of plant growth, were used to describe a region's climate: growing degree days (GDD) and a crop soil moisture index (the ratio of actual evapotranspiration to potential evapotranspiration). For each climate zone and each crop, a table was generated containing the yield, harvest area, and latitude/longitude position information for each grid cell included in the distribution. The data were sorted from the grid cells by their yield values, ranking them from lowest to highest yield. The grid cells' respective harvest areas were then accumulated until arriving at the statistical information of interest: the mean, median, and 90th percentile yields. The percentage of a crop's harvested area was calculated to define a percentile yield value. The data draw on average of census data between 1997 and 2003 and are shown as 2000 at a 5 minute x 5 minute spatial resolution. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Learn More link.

attributes.name: Biodiversity Intactness
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The biodiversity intactness map shows global estimates of how land use pressures have affected the numbers of species and individuals found in an area. This data is important because if biodiversity loss goes unchecked, it will undermine efforts toward long-term sustainable development. The data, created by [Newbold et al. (2016)](https://science.sciencemag.org/content/353/6296/288), represents intactness in 2005 at a 1 kilometer resolution.   
  
### Methodology  
  
The Biodiversity Intactness dataset shows global estimates of how land use pressures have affected the numbers of species and individuals found in samples from local terrestrial ecological assemblages. The map represents the average losses of originally present species. The datasets used 2,382,624 data points from the Projecting Responses of Ecological Diversity in Changing Terrestrial Systems (PREDICTS) database, a global database of how local terrestrial biodiversity responds to human impacts. The map modeled how richness and abundance respond to land use pressures. The models included 4 pressure variables—land use, land use intensity, human population density, and proximity to the nearest road. The values of the response variables were expressed relative to an intact assemblage undisturbed by humans. For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://science.sciencemag.org/content/353/6296/288).

attributes.name: Nighttime Lights 2012 and 2016
attributes.description:
The "Earth at Night" map images were generated by National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) using the Suomi National Polar-Orbiting Partnership (Suomi NPP) satellite, managed by NASA and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). Suomi NPP observes nearly every location on Earth at roughly 1:30 p.m. and 1:30 a.m. (local time) each day, as it images the planet in vertical 3,000 km (2,000-mile) strips from pole to pole. The satellite’s workhorse instrument is the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS), which detects photons of light reflected from the Earth’s surface and atmosphere in 22 different wavelengths. The final Earth at Night products show the areas of man-made visible and infrared light in the world at night, excluding moonlight, fires, and other natural sources of light. Areas with the brightest light points tend to be population centers and are often located in coastal areas. Earth at Night maps are available for the years 2012 and 2016, in both color and grayscale, in both JPEG and GeoTIFF formats and with resolution from 500 m to 3 km. The 2016 images were processed using a compositing technique that selected the best cloud-free nights in each month over each land mass. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Learn More link.

attributes.name: Fire Weather
attributes.description:
The Fire Weather data set is derived from the Fire Weather Index (FWI) System, which was developed by the Canadian Forest Service and is the most widely used fire danger rating system in the world. The Global Fire WEather Database (GFWED) is a global database of daily FWI System calculations, produced by National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Institute for Space Studies. This system combines different weather factors that may influence the start and spread of a vegetation fire and is comprised of three moisture codes and three fire behavior indices. The moisture codes describe the moisture content of three general fuel classes. The fire behavior indices describe the rate of spread, fuel consumption and intensity of a fire if it were to start. 

  
  
 The data inputs for these calculations are measurements of 12:00 local time temperature at 2 m, relative humidity at 2 m and wind speed at 10 m. Daily snow-depth and precipitation were totaled over the previous 24 hours. GFWED includes several different versions of these calculations, each of which uses a different input weather and precipitation data. The version of these calculations shown on Resource Watch uses input data from GEOS-5 for temperature, relative humidity, wind-speed and snow depth; input precipitation comes from the 'Late' version of GPM IMERG Daily Precipitation. Global daily calculations of the FWI System indices using these data inputs are available from 2015 to present with 0.1° resolution. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Learn More link.  
  
### Additional Information

attributes.name: Tree Height Change
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The global tree canopy height and change dataset at 30 m spatial resolution was developed through the integration of the [Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI)](https://gedi.umd.edu/) lidar forest structure measurements and [Landsat analysis-ready data (Landsat ARD)](https://www.usgs.gov/core-science-systems/nli/landsat/us-landsat-analysis-ready-data?qt-science_support_page_related_con=0#qt-science_support_page_related_con) time series. The NASA GEDI is a spaceborne lidar instrument operating onboard the International Space Station since April 2019. It provides point-based measurements of vegetation structure, including tree canopy height between 52°N and 52°S globally. The Global Land Analysis and Discover (GLAD) team at the University of Maryland (UMD) integrated the GEDI point-based tree height measurements with the global wall-to-wall Landsat analysis-ready time-series data (Landsat ARD). The GEDI relative height at 95% (GEDI RH95) metric was used to calibrate the model. The Landsat multi-temporal metrics that represent the surface phenology serve as the independent variables for global tree height modeling. The “moving window” locally calibrated and applied regression tree ensemble model was implemented to ensure high quality of tree height prediction and global map consistency. The model was extrapolated in the boreal regions to create the global tree height prototype map. The model was applied for the years 2000 and 2020 and the maps were temporally filtered to provide a two-decade global forest structure and change metrics.
  
  
The GLAD laboratory in the Department of Geographical Sciences at UMD investigates methods, causes and impacts of global land surface change.  Earth observation imagery are the primary data source and land cover extent and change the primary topic of interest. GLAD aspires to generate new science insights concerning land resources, educate the next generation of remote sensing-based land change scientists, and disseminate land monitoring capabilities to operational settings nationally and internationally.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
The year 2000 and 2020 global tree height was modeled through the integration of the Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) lidar forest structure measurements and Landsat analysis-ready data (Landsat ARD) time-series. The NASA GEDI is a spaceborne lidar instrument operating onboard the International Space Station since April 2019. It provides point-based measurements of vegetation structure between 52°N and 52°S globally [(Dubayah et al., 2020)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666017220300018). The GEDI relative height of returned energy (RH) metrics were filtered to exclude low quality observations and gridded to the Landsat 30-m spatial resolution. The RH metrics were compared with 90th percentile of the tree height at 30-m pixel resolution derived from the airborne lidar instruments and found that the GEDI RH95 (relative height at 95%) metric is highly correlated with the airborne lidar canopy height product. This metric was selected as the calibration data for the global tree height map. To exclude non-woody vegetation from the training,  a zero height was assigned to all GEDI observations with RH95 values below 3 meters.
  
  
A global 16-day normalized surface reflectance Landsat ARD was employed as input data for tree height modeling [(Potapov et al., 2020)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0034425720305381?via%3Dihub). The per-pixel 16-day time-series data were composed only of clear-sky observations during the snow-free season.  A set of annual multitemporal metrics was generated to provide consistent land surface phenology inputs for model application. To facilitate spatiotemporal consistency of the reflectance time-series, gap-filling of the missing 16-day data with data from preceding years was implemented. Annual metrics include selected ranks, inter-rank averages, and amplitudes of surface reflectance and vegetation indices values, and surface reflectance averages for land surface phenology stages defined by vegetation indices (i.e., surface reflectance for the maximum and minimum greenness periods). The Landsat metrics were augmented with elevation data.
  
  
The 2019 GEDI RH95 was used as a dependent variable and the Landsat multitemporal metrics from the same year as independent variables to calibrate the regression tree ensembles. A separate model was calibrated for each Landsat ARD tile (1×1°) using training data collected within the neighboring tiles. The prototype for the boreal tree height map, where GEDI data were absent (north of 52°N), was calibrated using training data extracted from the modeled tree height between 40°N and 52°N. To address the overestimation of tree height over wetlands and tundra, additional non-forest training was manually collected in areas indicated as treeless by the year 2010 tree canopy cover product [(Hansen et al., 2013)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24233722/).
  
  
The model calibrated for the year 2019 was applied to the multitemporal metrics for other years (2000-2003 and 2017-2020). The tree height value for the years 2000 and 2020 was calculated as the median of 2000, 2001, 2003 and 2017, 2019, 2020, respectively, unless forest loss was indicated by the forest change product [(Hansen et al., 2013)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24233722/). To reduce errors and noise in the model outputs due to remaining atmospheric contamination and differences in the radiometric resolution of Landsat sensors in 2000 and 2020, extensive filtering of the output products was implemented. Pixels that did not experience forest loss according to the Hansen et al. (2013) product and that had an overlap of ranges of tree height values for 2000-2003 and 2017-2020 intervals were considered stable forests. Manual masks were also used to clean up incorrectly mapped forest loss and gain, especially in the short seasonal forests. 
  
  
For the full documentation, please click on the “Learn more” button.
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows datasets from the GLAD laboratory for [Cropland Extent](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/50634b51-ea2e-4cc1-9e4b-8f26a389a301), [Cropland Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/ec282483-4f5c-4fb8-ace7-8e557826781a), [Water Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/b83ad197-eb95-44e2-8ec3-3351ab926421), [Snow/Ice Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/5a796ce9-71d4-42b0-922d-056a86e5eb72), [Built-Up Area Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/e6a3f803-1222-46c2-8e6c-0ae94b3d80c8), and [Land Cover Map](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/06e734af-66f0-4c3e-ac71-1b99f3cbfe1d).
  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Visualizing the Data

info.name: Tree Height Change
info.technical_title: Global tree height mapped through the integration of GEDI and Landsat data, 2000 and 2020
info.functions: Global tree canopy height and change for the years 2000 and 2020
info.cautions:
- A probability-based sample analysis is the recommended good practice approach to estimating land cover and land use extent and change. The global land cover map time-series enables a higher sampling efficiency through stratification at the sub-national, national, and global scales. The maps should not be used as the only source data for national and international reporting due to unknown variability of map uncertainty in space and between years.
  
  
- The tree height product has issues related to GEDI data quality and Landsat data availability. GEDI data overestimate tree height on slopes within temperate and subtropical mountain grasslands, e.g., in New Zealand and Lesotho. The tree height over cities and suburbs may be confounded with the building height, as GEDI data do not discriminate between the height of vegetation and man-made objects. The GEDI calibration uncertainties, specifically geolocation precision and land surface height estimation, may be responsible for some of the map errors. 
  
  
- The tree height model saturated above 30 m and may not adequately represent the height of the tallest trees. The tree extent may be inconsistent for the areas with short (4-6 meters) seasonal forests.
  
  
- The tree height model above 52°N (the GEDI data range) is a prototype derived using a combination of GEDI data below 52°N and non-forest training data collected manually above 52°N. The product may incorrectly represent the height of the boreal forests, especially in the far North. 
  
  
- The model application for the year 2000 may over/underestimate the tree canopy height due to the different radiometric properties of the Landsat ETM/TM and Landsat OLI sensors. The tree height change between the years 2000 and 2020 was temporally filtered and manually corrected to remove most of the artifacts. This correction, however, may reduce the product sensitivity to tree height changes (i.e., some of the tree loss and gain events may be omitted).
info.citation: Potapov P., Hansen M.C., Pickens A., Hernandez-Serna A., Tyukavina A., Turubanova S., Zalles V., Li X., Khan A., Stolle F., Harris N., Song X.-P., Baggett A., Kommareddy I., Kommareddy A. (2022) The global 2000-2020 land cover and land use change dataset derived from the Landsat archive: first results. Frontiers in Remote Sensing. [https://doi.org/10.3389/frsen.2022.856903](https://doi.org/10.3389/frsen.2022.856903). Accessed through Resource Watch, (date). [www.resourcewatch.org](https://www.resourcewatch.org).

attributes.name: cit.038.nrt Air Quality - Modeled Forecast - WACCM (CO)
Air Quality: Carbon Monoxide (CO) Modeled Next-day Forecast
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
This dataset shows forecasted carbon monoxide (CO) concentrations at Earth's surface, modeled by the Whole Atmosphere Community Climate Model (WACCM). Carbon monoxide is a colorless, odorless gas that is toxic when inhaled in large amounts. Carbon monoxide exposure can be fatal.  
  
According to the U.S. [Center for Disease Control](https://www.cdc.gov/co/faqs.htm) (CDC), carbon monoxide is released when fossil fuels are burned. Common household sources include grills, cars, fireplaces, and gas stoves that aren’t properly ventilated. Major sources of carbon monoxide to outdoor air include cars, trucks and other fossil-fuel-burning machinery. Breathing air with a high concentration of carbon monoxide reduces oxygen availability in the bloodstream for critical organs like the heart and brain. Symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning include headache, dizziness, weakness, upset stomach, vomiting, chest pain, and confusion.   
  
WACCM creates global forecasts for a variety of other air quality indicators, as well. While this dataset shows forecasted carbon monoxide concentrations, Resource Watch also shows WACCM forecasts for [sulfur dioxide (SO₂)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-SO),  [fine particulate matter (PM2.5)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-PM-25), [black carbon (BC)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-Black-Carbon), [ozone (O₃)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-O), and [nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-NO). WACCM runs the model daily, and on their website you can find forecasted concentrations for each compound up to nine days into the future at three-hour time steps.   
  
WACCM was developed by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) and the University Corporation for Atmospheric Research (UCAR). The data has global coverage at 1.9 x 2.5 degree resolution.  
  
### Methodology  
  
WACCM is a comprehensive numerical model, driven by meteorological fields from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration’s (NASA) Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO) Goddard Earth Observing System Model, Version 5 (GEOS-5) model. The development of WACCM is an inter-divisional collaboration that unifies modeling from the High Altitude Observatory ([HAO](http://www2.hao.ucar.edu/)), the Atmospheric Chemistry Observations and Modeling ([ACOM](https://www2.acom.ucar.edu/)) Laboratory, and the Climate and Global Dynamics ([CGD](http://www2.cgd.ucar.edu/)) Laboratory. Upper atmospheric modeling from HAO, middle atmospheric modeling from ACOM, and tropospheric modeling from CGD are combined using the NCAR [Community Earth System Model (CESM)](http://www.cesm.ucar.edu/) as a common numerical framework. For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://opensky.ucar.edu/islandora/object/articles%3A12836).  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows WACCM forecasts for [sulfur dioxide (SO₂)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-SO), [fine particulate matter (PM2.5)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-PM-25), [black carbon (BC)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-Black-Carbon), [ozone (O₃)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-O), and [nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-NO).
  
  

Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. Additional forecasted data for other compounds, times, and levels of the atmosphere are also produced by WACCM. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.
  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/nrt-scripts/tree/master/cit_038_waccm_atmospheric_chemistry_model).

attributes.name: Ramsar Internationally Important Wetlands
attributes.description:
Ramsar wetlands refer to "internally important" wetlands as defined by the Convention on Wetlands and are designated by each contracting party. At the time of joining the Convention, each contracting party must designate at least one wetland site within their territory for inclusion in the List of Wetlands of International Importance (the Ramsar List). These Ramsar sites acquire a new national and international status. They are recognized as being of significant value not only for the country or the countries in which they are located but for humanity as a whole. There are currently over 2,400 Ramsar sites around the world. They cover over 2.1 million km2, an area larger than Mexico. Parties continue to designate wetlands for inclusion on the list. They select suitable wetlands for designation by referring to the criteria for identifying wetlands of international importance. The Convention has provided guidance to contracting parties on the management of Ramsar sites, in addition to its guidance on the wise use of all wetlands. The inclusion of a wetland on the list signifies the government’s commitment to take the steps necessary to ensure that the site’s ecological character is maintained. The Convention includes various measures to respond to threats to the ecological character of sites. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Learn More link.

Wastewater Inputs in Coastal Areas
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Wastewater Inputs to Coastal Areas dataset, produced by National Center for Ecological Analysis and Synthesis, maps human sewage inputs into coastal waters for the year 2015. This dataset maps the locations of coastal pourpoints, where surface water empties into the ocean. At these pourpoints nitrogen and pathogens from human sewage are transported to coastal ecosystems. Nitrogen concentration at each pourpoint is measured in grams/year.

  
  
Human sewage is considered both an ecological and a human health issue, because it contributes both increased levels of nitrogen and pathogens to coastal waters.  Excess nitrogen plays a key role in the ecological degradation of coastal ecosystems through a process called [eutrophication](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/eutrophication.html). Eutrophication leads to harmful algal blooms and low-oxygen waters, which can kill fish, and degrade essential fish habitats. Pathogens in coastal waters can promote disease in marine organisms, such as coral reefs, and can cause human health impacts. It is important to monitor both nitrogen and pathogen concentrations, to understand trends and inform management.  

  
  
The National Center for Ecological Analysis and Synthesis created this map of pourpoints, along with a model of nitrogen dispersion into the ocean, to inform marine conservation and public health work. The data allows for the comparison of global models of nitrogen sources and traditional water quality monitoring to identify priority hotspots. In-depth local monitoring can then pinpoint the true sources of and quantities of pollutants like nitrogen to benefit conservation and management. The model also links nitrogen inputs with data on pathogens in coastal waters to inform policy decisions around wastewater treatment options. 
  
  
### Methodology  
  
High-resolution watershed vector data and pourpoints were used with an automated flow-accumulation process to determine the boundaries for ~135,000 global basins that drain into the ocean. Population and settlement data for each basin were used to estimate the levels of nitrogen and pathogen inputs to coastal waters. Nitrogen concentrations in grams per year (g/yr) were modeled from data on three types of wastewater (treated, septic, and open defecation) and the estimated amount of nitrogen removed by each treatment type. The inputs to coastal waters at each pourpoint were determined by totaling the estimates that fell within the watershed boundary. Pourpoints that transferred less than 1 gram of nitrogen per year were discarded by the authors.

  
  
For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0258898#sec002).
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also provides data on the dispersion of nitrogen into the coastal ocean from the pourpoints in [Wastewater Plumes in Coastal Areas](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/11804f04-d9c7-47b9-8d27-27ce6ed6c042) and on the size and shape of the watersheds that feed into the pourpoints in [Watersheds Transporting Wastewater to Coastal Ocean](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/784732cc-8e7e-4dac-be51-d4506ff2ee04).
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.   
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch retrieved the data on [Github]((https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/blob/master/ocn_027b_rw0_wastewater_pourpoints/).  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

info.cautions:
- The model does not fully account for differences in land cover, watershed size, ecosystem processes, sanitation efficiency, and other biogeochemical processes. This may lead to overestimation of impacts in coastal ecosystems with slow-flowing water, and underestimation for areas with rapid flush times.
  
  
- Data on the location of most septic systems and sewer outfalls were modeled not observed and did not include information on septic failure rates or permitted or accidental sewer overflow events. This adds uncertainty to the model, and potentially underestimates the impacts of nitrogen given the high rates of septic tank failure.
  
  
- For treated nitrogen, the model may overestimate actual nitrogen removal rates by treatment plants, leading to underestimation of impacts in the model.
