attributes.name: Renewable Energy Consumption
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
This dataset shows renewable energy consumption in 259 countries from 1990 to present. In this dataset, renewable energy sources are defined as hydropower, solid and liquid biofuels, wind, solar, biogas, geothermal, marine, and waste to energy. 

  
  
The dataset was published as part of the Sustainable Energy for All (SE4ALL) initiative, and the data was compiled by the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the United Nations Statistics Divisions (UNSD). IEA and UNDC are the primary developers of internationally comparable national energy statistics. This dataset tracks the progress of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicator 7.2, to advance the target of increase substantially the share of renewable energy in the global energy mix by 2030. 

  
  
Resource Watch also shows [energy intensity](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/ene029a-Energy-Intensity) and [percentage of energy consumption from renewable sources](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/bced4001-425a-4fad-8c22-8214d9340ea4) data from the SE4ALL Database.  
  
### Methodology  
  
This dataset was compiled using data from the International Energy Agency (IEA) energy statistics, complemented by the United Nations (UN) database when IEA data was not available. IEA data contained the most comprehensive and accurate data for countries that were a part of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), as well as 75 non-OECD countries. In the case of smaller non-OECD countries, extrapolations of country data provided by the UN Statistics Division were used. 

  
  
For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://www.seforall.org/sites/default/files/l/2013/09/9-gtf_ch4.pdf).  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows [energy intensity](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/ene029a-Energy-Intensity) and [percentage of energy consumption from renewable sources](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/bced4001-425a-4fad-8c22-8214d9340ea4) data from the SE4ALL Database.  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. Additional data related to electricity access and renewable energy electricity is available from the data provider. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/nrt-scripts/tree/master/upload_worldbank_data). This data has been mapped on Resource Watch by joining it with Natural Earth boundaries.  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

info.cautions:
- Existing renewable energy statistics do not distinguish whether renewable energy is sustainably produced (e.g the use of wood from unsustainable forestry). 
  
  
- Renewable energy consumption from electricity and heat output assumes that transmission and distribution losses are the same across technologies. This assumption may not always hold true since renewables in remote areas may incur larger losses.
  
  
- Data on the use of biomass for heating and cooking is particularly challenging to gather because in many countries, biomass use happens in the informal economy, which is not monitored by the government. 
  
  
- Small, distributed grid-connected generation such as small-scale photovoltaic (PV) or wind and solar water heating may not be included since data collection for these sources is inconsistent across countries. Off-grid and mini-grid data is often not captured in energy statistics.

attributes.name: [Archived] Solar Energy Potential
attributes.description:
_**This dataset has been archived, and we will no longer be updating or maintaining it. We recommend using [this dataset](2063964b-56c8-4080-b2a5-5a7710f321b9) as a replacement.**_
  
Vaisala created this global data set of average annual global horizontal irradiance (GHI, the key variable for photovoltaic (PV) projects, measured in W/m²) at a 2 arc minute resolution. Solar energy investors and project developers can use these data to identify regions of the world likely to have sufficient solar resources to make a solar generation facility a worthwhile investment. Vaisala is an industry leader in the solar resource assessment space. It has been at the forefront of research regarding the estimation of surface solar conditions to better understand and predict solar energy generation. In 2010, Vaisala produced the world's first high-resolution, globally consistent data set mapping the world's solar resource potential. The annual average GHI information from this data set is provided here at a 2 arc minute resolution and based on over a decade of half-hourly, high-resolution visible satellite imagery via the broadband visible wavelength channel. The values have been processed using a combination of peer-reviewed, industry-standard techniques and in-house, including a cloud-index algorithm that produces consistent results when used with the large number of satellites that must be combined to construct a global data set. Vaisala's complete global solar database includes 2 decades of hourly estimates of GHI, direct normal irradiance (DNI), and diffuse irradiance (DIF) and is regularly maintained and updated across 5 different versions of the data set. GHI is most relevant for fixed-panel PV installations, and DNI is most relevant for concentrated solar power (CSP) projects and PV tracking systems. This data set can be used for rapid prospecting for solar energy generation sites or conducting national or regional infrastructure, policy, or transmission planning. However, the development of specific utility-scale projects generally requires additional site-specific research after this step. The global solar data set is intended as a tool to help narrow the focus of project developers and investors to accelerate the growth of solar energy worldwide. The data set has been validated against nearly 200 publicly available ground stations around the world. For more information, please visit http://www.vaisala.com/Vaisala%20Documents/Scientific%20papers/3TIER%20Solar%20Dataset%20Methodology%20and%20Validation.pdf. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Learn More link.  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.

attributes.name: Gridded Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
attributes.description:
Global Gridded Geographically Based Economic Data (G-Econ), Version 4, provides a measure of global cell product (GCP): estimates for the amount of gross domestic product (GDP) produced in each grid cell of a 1-degree grid of the world using 2 metrics: GCP measured in the market exchange rate (MER) from local currencies into US$, and GCP measured in purchasing power parity (PPP), which adjusts country currency GCP according to the equivalent amount of US$ needed to purchase a standardized collection of goods in the country using the country's currency. GCP is defined as the gross value added by activities in a grid cell. Gross value is calculated as the total value of the outputs of local businesses providing goods and services in the grid cell, minus the value of inputs bought by those businesses. The data and methods used to calculate local added value are different for different countries, as the data available are different for different countries. State- and county level gross value data are used whenever possible.

PREPdata shows only a subset of this data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Download from Original Source link.

info.cautions: Subnational data describing gross output are of higher quality in countries that have high incomes and are in periods of peace and conversely of lower quality in low-income countries or those that are experiencing war or revolution. This variable quality of underlying data affects the reliability of GCP calculations. A proportional allocation technique is applied to spatially rescale data reported at a county or state level to the 1 degree grid used to report GCP. This includes a measure of assumption that may result in unrealistic allocations. This is often referred to as the modifiable area unit problem (MAUP), a well-recognized challenge when attempting to make statements regarding the spatial distribution of a variable within the smallest geographic unit at which that variable was reported. The Yale team experimented with various spatial rescaling techniques and decided that the proportional allocation method produced results that were most reasonable.

attributes.name: foo.005.rw2 Crop Land Area and Production
Crop Land Area and Production
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Crop Land and Production dataset shows the global harvested area, production, and yield for six major crops: wheat, soybean, rice,  maize, coffee, and cotton. The dataset was derived from the 2020 Spatial Production Allocation Model (SPAM). The SPAM model aimed to disaggregate (downscale) national and sub-national crop statistics using a variety of inputs, such as cropland surface, location of irrigated areas, crop suitability and potential yields, rural population densities, production systems characteristics and crop prices. Crop data was downscaled to a spatial resolution of 5 arc minutes. This spatial resolution is approximately 10 kilometers x 10 kilometers at the equator, but [changes with distance](https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-of-latitude-and-longitude-distance-4070616) from the equator. 

Together, maize, rice, soybean, and wheat account for nearly two-thirds of global agricultural calories. Global demand for these crops is rising as a result of diet shifts, rising population levels, and increased biofuel demand. Increased demand for these resources will significantly affect land and resource use, climate change, political agendas, and technological developments. A comprehensive understanding of the current spatial distribution of the world’s crops is necessary in order to preemptively address these effects. The Crop Land Area and Production dataset can be used to understand the extent and productivity of key global crops, which will help address food crop demand and its effects. 

The Crop Land Area and Production dataset was generated by the [Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research Program on Policies, Institutions, and Markets (CGIAR-PIM)](https://pim.cgiar.org/about/). CGIAR-PIM provides support for policies that help farmers improve their lives, produce nutritious and affordable foods, and protect the soil, water and biodiversity in rural landscapes. The program is led by the [International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI)](https://www.ifpri.org/about), a CGIAR-PIM research center. IFPRI provides research-based policy solutions to sustainably reduce poverty and end hunger in developing countries. The Crop Land Area and Production dataset was part of the larger SPAM dataset, which was developed for the HarvestChoice research initiative. Conducted by IFPRI, [HarvestChoice](https://www.ifpri.org/project/harvestchoice) generated knowledge products to help guide strategic investments to improve the well-being of poor people in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia through more productive and profitable farming.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
The main purpose of SPAM is to disaggregate crop statistics (e.g., harvested area, production quantity, and yield) by different farming systems and to further allocate such disaggregated statistics into spatially gridded units. The whole procedure entails a data fusion approach that combines information from different sources and at different spatial scales by deploying various matching
and calibration processes. Then all the data elements are processed by the optimization model, which generates results at the grid level. There are three submodules in a standardized SPAM model: disaggregation, optimization, and allocation. The SPAM2020 is conceptualized based on this general setting, while it adds further methodological and data improvements, which mainly include the update of base year, the expansion of subnational administrative-unit coverage, the extension of crop list, and the substitution of the latest hybrid cropland map as the basic allocation layer.

The first step for SPAM is to disaggregate crop statistics of agricultural production (e.g., the yield, harvested area, and total production) by administrative-unit levels (k), crop type (j), and farming system (l) from coarser scale to finer scale. The four production systems were defined by water and management type:
- Irrigated – high input (I)
- Rainfed – high input (H)
- Rainfed – low input (L)
- Rainfed – subsistence (S)

The four conceptualized farming systems are mainly delineated by the water supply system and inputs used by farmers, despite global data on farming system shares for each crop being largely absent. For a small number of large countries, e.g., Brazil, China, India, Russia, the United States, the authors have data on farming system shares at the ADM1 level. For the other countries the authors assigned the national farming system shares to each ADM1 level and then adjusted individual ADM1 farming system shares in light of the supporting evidence. For irrigated farming systems, the crop-specific shares are derived by dividing the harvested area cultivated under full control irrigation obtained from [Global Information System on Water and Agriculture (AQUASTAT)](https://www.fao.org/aquastat/en/), [MIRCA](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2008GB003435), and
country-level statistics by the overall harvested area.

The optimization module in SPAM2020 is almost the same as that in previous versions. The authors applied a cross-entropy process in the General Algebraic Modeling System (GAMS), which ensures that the optimization procedure iterates until a solution is found. Once the allocation is successful, meaning that an optimal or locally optimal solution has been found, the routine immediately returns the allocated physical area by grid, crop and farming system, and the program continues with post-processing automatically.

The SPAM model used additional biological and economic inputs to allocate the statistics within each pixel. Input data included (among several others):
- Administrative units
- Crop Type
- Farming system
- Adjusted harvested area
- Total suitable area in each grid by crop and farming system
- Crop prices
- Market accessibility in each grid
- Population density

Our data catalog provides three of the SPAM2020 essential output indicators:

- Harvested Area: also measured in hectares, harvested area is at least as large as physical area but sometimes more since it also accounts for multiple harvests of a crop on the same plot. Like for physical area, the harvested area is calculated for each production system, and the sum of all harvested areas of all production systems in a pixel amounts to the total harvested area of the
pixel. The sum of all the harvested areas of the crops in a pixel can be larger than the pixel size.
- Production: for each production system and crop, production is calculated by multiplying the area harvested by its corresponding yield. It is measured in metric tons. The total production of a crop includes the production of all production systems of that crop.
- Yield: is the amount of production per harvested area and measured in kilograms per hectare. It is a measure of productivity. The total yield of a crop, when considering all production systems, is the weighted average of the four systems’ yields.

For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/12/3545/2020/essd-12-3545-2020.pdf).
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Our data catalog shows only a subset of the dataset. The Global Spatially-Disaggregated Crop Production Statistics Data for 2020 Version 3.0 has data for 36 other crops (42 total). The full dataset also includes physical area and value of production for all 42 crops. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click the “Learn more” button.

Our data catalog has previously shown data for [2005](https://bit.ly/3CjoFYc). This dataset was archived because the methodology has been changed.  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on WRI’s data catalog. See the documentation on how we retrieved the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/tree/master/foo_005_rw2_crop_area_production).  
  
### Disclaimer

sources.source-description: Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research Program on Policies, Institutions, and Markets (CGIAR-PIM)

info.technical_title: Global Spatially-Disaggregated Crop Production Statistics Data for 2020 Version 3.0
info.functions: Production, harvested area, and yield for wheat, soybean, rice, maize, coffee, and cotton crops for the year 2020
info.cautions:
- As stated previously, the SPAM estimates are dependent on the extent and veracity of the primary input data like most models. SPAM2020 requires data on 42 crops in over 200 countries for the production season. Ideally, these data should be collected at an ADM2 level; however, this is not always possible. It is particularly difficult in a few countries such as Somalia and Nigeria, where reliable
data are not available, or different input data just conflict with each other.
- Since most cropping statistics are not delineated by the farming system, estimates of the shares of production under each of the four systems in question are required. To convert harvested area statistics to the physical-area statistics used in the model, additional data on cropping intensities by crop and farming systems must be collected. The authors collected official or published data and relied on expert judgments as the last resort when they could not find other sources.
- The wide range of data sources, coverage, and regional nuances of crop production have methodological implications. First, there are possible trade-offs between data consistency and data reliability. For example, there are requirements of the model (i.e., cropping intensities and farming system shares) that are not consistently available within a country at the administrative level needed. Often, these numbers are taken from national-level values, even though they may not reflect the reality at the administrative level. Secondly, multi- and intercropping are not handled in a sophisticated manner within SPAM. These types of cropping patterns are only accounted for using a single cropping intensity value per crop, farming system, and (possibly) subnational unit. Finally, the market is important for both subsistence farmers and commercial ones. In SPAM, the authors rely on population density for an indirect representation of market proximity.
- Last but not least, the authors suggest caution when comparing SPAM products directly across time stages. It is largely because system errors exist across various data products.

Accessed through World Resources Institute, (date). [www.resourcewatch.org](https://www.resourcewatch.org).

attributes.name: Superficie de tierras de cultivo y producción
attributes.description:
### Visión general  
  
El conjunto de datos de Tierras de Cultivo y Producción muestra el área cosechada a nivel mundial, la producción y el rendimiento de seis cultivos principales: trigo, soja, arroz, maíz, café y algodón. El conjunto de datos se derivó del Modelo de Asignación de Producción Espacial (SPAM) de 2010. El modelo de SPAM tenía como objetivo desglosar (a escala reducida) las estadísticas nacionales y subnacionales de cultivos utilizando una variedad de insumos, como la superficie de las tierras de cultivo, la ubicación de las áreas de regadío, la idoneidad de los cultivos y los rendimientos potenciales, las densidades de población rural, las características de los sistemas de producción y los precios de los cultivos. Los datos de los cultivos se redujeron a una resolución espacial de 5 minutos de arco. Esta resolución espacial es de aproximadamente 10 kilómetros x 10 kilómetros en el ecuador, pero [cambia con la distancia] (https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-de-latitud-y-longitud-distancia-4070616) desde el ecuador. 

Juntos, el maíz, el arroz, la soja y el trigo representan casi dos tercios de las calorías agrícolas mundiales. La demanda mundial de estos cultivos está aumentando como resultado de los cambios en la dieta, el aumento de los niveles de población y el aumento de la demanda de biocombustibles. El aumento de la demanda de estos recursos afectará significativamente el uso de la tierra y los recursos, el cambio climático, las agendas políticas y los desarrollos tecnológicos. Es necesaria una comprensión integral de la distribución espacial actual de los cultivos del mundo para abordar preventivamente estos efectos. El conjunto de datos de área de tierras de cultivo y producción se puede utilizar para comprender el alcance y la productividad de los cultivos globales clave, lo que ayudará a abordar la demanda de cultivos alimentarios y sus efectos. 

El conjunto de datos de Área de Tierras de Cultivo y Producción fue generado por el [Grupo Consultivo sobre el Programa Internacional de Investigación Agrícola sobre Políticas, Instituciones y Mercados (CGIAR-PIM)](https://pim.cgiar.org/about/). CGIAR-PIM brinda apoyo a políticas que ayudan a los agricultores a mejorar sus vidas, producir alimentos nutritivos y asequibles, y proteger el suelo, el agua y la biodiversidad en los paisajes rurales. El programa está dirigido por el [Instituto Internacional de Investigación de Políticas Alimentarias (IFPRI)](https://www.ifpri.org/about), un centro de investigación CGIAR-PIM. El IFPRI proporciona soluciones de políticas basadas en la investigación para reducir de manera sostenible la pobreza y acabar con el hambre en los países en desarrollo. El conjunto de datos Crop Land Area and Production fue parte del conjunto de datos SPAM más grande, que se desarrolló para la iniciativa de investigación HarvestChoice. Llevado a cabo por ifpri, [HarvestChoice] (https://www.ifpri.org/project/harvestchoice) generó productos de conocimiento para ayudar a guiar las inversiones estratégicas para mejorar el bienestar de las personas pobres en el África subsahariana y el sur de Asia a través de una agricultura más productiva y rentable.
  
### Metodología  
  
El objetivo principal del SPAM es desglosar las estadísticas de los cultivos (por ejemplo, el área cosechada, la cantidad de producción y el rendimiento) por diferentes sistemas agrícolas y asignar aún más dichas estadísticas desagregadas en unidades espacialmente cuadriculadas. Todo el procedimiento implica un enfoque de fusión de datos que combina información de diferentes fuentes y a diferentes escalas espaciales mediante el despliegue de varias coincidencias.
y procesos de calibración. Luego, todos los elementos de datos son procesados por el modelo de optimización, que genera resultados a nivel de cuadrícula. Hay tres submódulos en un modelo estandarizado de SPAM: desagregación, optimización y asignación. El SPAM2010 se conceptualiza en base a esta configuración general, al tiempo que agrega mejoras metodológicas y de datos adicionales, que incluyen principalmente la actualización del año base, la expansión de la cobertura de unidades administrativas subnacionales, la extensión de la lista de cultivos y la sustitución del último mapa híbrido de tierras de cultivo como capa de asignación básica.

El primer paso para el SPAM es desagregar las estadísticas de cultivos de la producción agrícola (por ejemplo, el rendimiento, el área cosechada y la producción total) por niveles de unidades administrativas (k), tipo de cultivo (j) y sistema agrícola (l) de escala más gruesa a escala más fina. Los cuatro sistemas de producción se definieron por tipo de agua y gestión:
- Irrigado – entrada alta (I)
- Rainfed – alta entrada (H)
- Rainfed – entrada baja (L)
- Rainfed – subsistencia (S)

Los cuatro sistemas agrícolas conceptualizados están delineados principalmente por el sistema de suministro de agua y los insumos utilizados por los agricultores, a pesar de que los datos mundiales sobre las cuotas del sistema agrícola para cada cultivo están en gran medida ausentes. Para un pequeño número de países grandes, por ejemplo, Brasil, China, India, Rusia, Estados Unidos, los autores tienen datos sobre las cuotas del sistema agrícola a nivel ADM1. Para los otros países, los autores asignaron las cuotas del sistema agrícola nacional a cada nivel de ADM1 y luego ajustaron las cuotas individuales del sistema agrícola de ADM1 a la luz de la evidencia de apoyo. En el caso de los sistemas agrícolas de regadío, las cuotas específicas de los cultivos se obtienen dividiendo la superficie cosechada cultivada bajo riego bajo pleno control obtenido del [Sistema Mundial de Información sobre el Agua y la Agricultura (AQUASTAT)](https://www.fao.org/aquastat/en/), [MIRCA](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2008GB003435), y
estadísticas a nivel de país por la superficie total cosechada.

El módulo de optimización en SPAM2010 es casi el mismo que en versiones anteriores. Los autores aplicaron un proceso de entropía cruzada en el Sistema de Modelado Algebraico General (GAMS), que asegura que el procedimiento de optimización itera hasta que se encuentre una solución. Una vez que la asignación es exitosa, lo que significa que se ha encontrado una solución óptima o localmente óptima, la rutina devuelve inmediatamente el área física asignada por red, cultivo y sistema de cultivo, y el programa continúa con el posprocesamiento automáticamente.

El modelo SPAM utilizó insumos biológicos y económicos adicionales para asignar las estadísticas dentro de cada píxel. Datos de entrada incluidos (entre varios otros):
- Unidades administrativas
- Tipo de cultivo
- Sistema agrícola
- Superficie cosechada ajustada
- Superficie total adecuada en cada cuadrícula por cultivo y sistema de cultivo
- Precios de los cultivos
- Accesibilidad al mercado en cada cuadrícula
- Densidad de población

Nuestro catálogo de datos proporciona tres de los indicadores de producto esenciales de SPAM2010:

- Área cosechada: también medida en hectáreas, el área cosechada es al menos tan grande como el área física, pero a veces más, ya que también representa múltiples cosechas de un cultivo en la misma parcela. Al igual que para el área física, el área cosechada se calcula para cada sistema de producción, y la suma de todas las áreas cosechadas de todos los sistemas de producción en un píxel asciende al área total cosechada del
píxel. La suma de todas las áreas cosechadas de los cultivos en un píxel puede ser mayor que el tamaño del píxel.
- Producción: para cada sistema productivo y cultivo, la producción se calcula multiplicando el área cosechada por su rendimiento correspondiente. Se mide en toneladas métricas. La producción total de un cultivo incluye la producción de todos los sistemas de producción de ese cultivo.
- Rendimiento: es la cantidad de producción por superficie cosechada y medida en kilogramos por hectárea. Es una medida de la productividad. El rendimiento total de un cultivo, cuando se consideran todos los sistemas de producción, es el promedio ponderado de los rendimientos de los cuatro sistemas.

Para obtener la documentación completa, consulte la fuente [metodología](https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/12/3545/2020/essd-12-3545-2020.pdf).
  
### Información adicional  
  
Nuestro catálogo de datos muestra solo un subconjunto del conjunto de datos. Los Datos Estadísticos Mundiales de Producción de Cultivos Desagregados Espacialmente para 2010 Versión 2.0 tienen datos para otros 36 cultivos (42 en total). El conjunto de datos completo también incluye el área física y el valor de producción para los 42 cultivos. Para acceder al conjunto de datos completo e información adicional, haga clic en el botón "Más información".

Nuestro catálogo de datos ha mostrado anteriormente datos para [2005](https://bit.ly/3CjoFYc). Este conjunto de datos se archivó porque se ha cambiado la metodología.  
  
### Visualización de los datos  
  
Nuestro equipo reformateó este conjunto de datos antes de mostrarlo en el catálogo de datos de la IRG. Consulte la documentación sobre cómo recuperamos los datos en [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/tree/master/foo_005_rw1_crop_area_production).  
  
### Descargo de responsabilidad  
  
Extractos de esta página de descripción fueron tomados de los metadatos de origen.

info.technical_title: Datos de estadísticas mundiales de producción de cultivos desglosados espacialmente para 2010 versión 2.0
info.functions: Producción, área cosechada y rendimiento de los cultivos de trigo, soja, arroz, maíz, café y algodón para el año 2010
info.cautions:
- Como se indicó anteriormente, las estimaciones de SPAM dependen de la extensión y veracidad de los datos de entrada primarios como la mayoría de los modelos. SPAM2010 requiere datos sobre 42 cultivos en más de 200 países para la temporada de producción. Idealmente, estos datos deberían recopilarse a nivel ADM2; sin embargo, esto no siempre es posible. Es particularmente difícil en algunos países como Somalia y Nigeria, donde la fiabilidad
los datos no están disponibles, o los diferentes datos de entrada simplemente entran en conflicto entre sí.
- Dado que la mayoría de las estadísticas de cultivo no están delineadas por el sistema agrícola, se requieren estimaciones de las cuotas de producción en cada uno de los cuatro sistemas en cuestión. Para convertir las estadísticas del área cosechada en las estadísticas de área física utilizadas en el modelo, se deben recopilar datos adicionales sobre las intensidades de cultivo por cultivo y sistemas agrícolas. Los autores recopilaron datos oficiales o publicados y se basaron en juicios de expertos como último recurso cuando no pudieron encontrar otras fuentes.
- La amplia gama de fuentes de datos, la cobertura y los matices regionales de la producción de cultivos tienen implicaciones metodológicas. En primer lugar, existen posibles compensaciones entre la consistencia de los datos y la fiabilidad de los datos. Por ejemplo, hay requisitos del modelo (es decir, intensidades de cultivo y cuotas del sistema agrícola) que no están disponibles de manera consistente dentro de un país al nivel administrativo necesario. A menudo, estas cifras se toman de los valores a nivel nacional, aunque no reflejen la realidad a nivel administrativo. En segundo lugar, el cultivo múltiple e intercalado no se maneja de manera sofisticada dentro del SPAM. Estos tipos de patrones de cultivo solo se tienen en cuenta utilizando un único valor de intensidad de cultivo por cultivo, sistema agrícola y (posiblemente) unidad subnacional. Por último, el mercado es importante tanto para los agricultores de subsistencia como para los comerciales. En SPAM, los autores se basan en la densidad de población para una representación indirecta de la proximidad del mercado.
- Por último, pero no menos importante, los autores sugieren precaución al comparar los productos SPAM directamente a través de las etapas de tiempo. Esto se debe en gran parte a que existen errores del sistema en varios productos de datos.

attributes.description:
### கண்ணோட்டம்  
  
கோதுமை, சோயாபீன்ஸ், அரிசி, மக்காச்சோளம், காபி மற்றும் பருத்தி ஆகிய ஆறு முக்கிய பயிர்களுக்கான உலகளாவிய அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதி, உற்பத்தி மற்றும் மகசூல் ஆகியவற்றை பயிர் நிலம் மற்றும் உற்பத்தி தரவுத்தொகுப்பு காட்டுகிறது. தரவுத்தொகுப்பு 2010 இடஞ்சார்ந்த உற்பத்தி ஒதுக்கீடு மாதிரியிலிருந்து (எஸ்பிஏஎம்) பெறப்பட்டது. பயிர் நில மேற்பரப்பு, பாசனப் பகுதிகளின் அமைவிடம், பயிர் பொருத்தம் மற்றும் சாத்தியமான மகசூல், கிராமப்புற மக்கள்தொகை அடர்த்தி, உற்பத்தி அமைப்புகளின் பண்புகள் மற்றும் பயிர் விலைகள் போன்ற பல்வேறு உள்ளீடுகளைப் பயன்படுத்தி தேசிய மற்றும் துணை தேசிய பயிர் புள்ளிவிவரங்களை பிரிப்பதை எஸ்பிஏஎம் மாதிரி நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டது. பயிர்த் தரவு 5 வில் நிமிடங்களின் இடஞ்சார்ந்த தெளிவுத்திறனுக்கு கீழ்மட்டமாக்கப்பட்டது. இந்த இடஞ்சார்ந்த தீர்மானம் பூமத்திய ரேகையில் தோராயமாக 10 கிலோமீட்டர் x 10 கிலோமீட்டர் ஆகும், ஆனால் [தூரத்துடன் மாற்றங்கள்](https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-ன்-அட்சரேகை-மற்றும்-தீர்க்கரேகை-தூரம்-தூரம்-4070616) பூமத்திய ரேகையிலிருந்து. 

ஒன்றாக, மக்காச்சோளம், அரிசி, சோயாபீன்ஸ் மற்றும் கோதுமை ஆகியவை உலகளாவிய விவசாய கலோரிகளில் கிட்டத்தட்ட மூன்றில் இரண்டு பங்கு ஆகும். உணவு மாற்றங்கள், அதிகரித்து வரும் மக்கள் தொகை அளவுகள் மற்றும் அதிகரித்த உயிரி எரிபொருள் தேவை ஆகியவற்றின் விளைவாக இந்த பயிர்களுக்கான உலகளாவிய தேவை அதிகரித்து வருகிறது. இந்த வளங்களுக்கான அதிகரித்த தேவை நிலம் மற்றும் வள பயன்பாடு, காலநிலை மாற்றம், அரசியல் நிகழ்ச்சி நிரல்கள் மற்றும் தொழில்நுட்ப வளர்ச்சிகள் ஆகியவற்றை கணிசமாக பாதிக்கும். இந்த விளைவுகளை முன்கூட்டியே நிவர்த்தி செய்வதற்கு, உலகின் பயிர்களின் தற்போதைய இடஞ்சார்ந்த பரவல் பற்றிய ஒரு விரிவான புரிதல் அவசியம். முக்கிய உலகளாவிய பயிர்களின் அளவு மற்றும் உற்பத்தித்திறன் ஆகியவற்றைப் புரிந்துகொள்ள பயிர் நிலப் பரப்பு மற்றும் உற்பத்தி தரவுத்தொகுப்பைப் பயன்படுத்தலாம், இது உணவுப் பயிர் தேவை மற்றும் அதன் விளைவுகளை நிவர்த்தி செய்ய உதவும். 

பயிர் நிலப் பரப்பு மற்றும் உற்பத்தி தரவுத்தொகுப்பு [கொள்கைகள், நிறுவனங்கள் மற்றும் சந்தைகள் மீதான சர்வதேச விவசாய ஆராய்ச்சித் திட்டம் குறித்த ஆலோசனைக் குழு (சிஜிஐஏஆர்-பி.ஐ.எம்)] (https://pim.cgiar.org/about/) உருவாக்கப்பட்டது. விவசாயிகள் தங்கள் வாழ்க்கையை மேம்படுத்தவும், சத்தான மற்றும் மலிவு விலை உணவுகளை உற்பத்தி செய்யவும், கிராமப்புற நிலப்பரப்புகளில் மண், நீர் மற்றும் பல்லுயிர் பெருக்கத்தைப் பாதுகாக்கவும் உதவும் கொள்கைகளுக்கு சிஜிஐஏஆர்-பிம் ஆதரவளிக்கிறது. இந்த திட்டம் [சர்வதேச உணவுக் கொள்கை ஆராய்ச்சி நிறுவனம் (ஐ.எஃப்.பி.ஆர்.ஐ)](https://www.ifpri.org/about), ஒரு சிஜிஐஆர்-பி.ஐ.எம் ஆராய்ச்சி மையத்தால் வழிநடத்தப்படுகிறது. ஐ.எஃப்.பி.ஆர்.ஐ வளரும் நாடுகளில் வறுமையை நிரந்தரமாகக் குறைப்பதற்கும் பட்டினியை முடிவுக்குக் கொண்டுவருவதற்கும் ஆராய்ச்சி அடிப்படையிலான கொள்கைத் தீர்வுகளை வழங்குகிறது. பயிர் நிலப் பரப்பு மற்றும் உற்பத்தி தரவுத்தொகுப்பு பெரிய ஸ்பேம் தரவுத்தொகுப்பின் ஒரு பகுதியாக இருந்தது, இது ஹார்வெஸ்ட்சாய்ஸ் ஆராய்ச்சி முன்முயற்சிக்காக உருவாக்கப்பட்டது. IFPRI ஆல் நடத்தப்பட்ட, [HarvestChoice](https://www.ifpri.org/project/harvestchoice) அதிக உற்பத்தி மற்றும் இலாபகரமான விவசாயத்தின் மூலம் துணை சஹாரா ஆபிரிக்கா மற்றும் தெற்காசியாவில் உள்ள ஏழை மக்களின் நல்வாழ்வை மேம்படுத்த மூலோபாய முதலீடுகளுக்கு வழிகாட்ட உதவும் அறிவு தயாரிப்புகளை உருவாக்கியது.
  
### முறைமை  
  
எஸ்.பி.ஏ.எம் இன் முக்கிய நோக்கம் பயிர் புள்ளிவிவரங்களை (எ.கா., அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதி, உற்பத்தி அளவு மற்றும் மகசூல்) வெவ்வேறு விவசாய அமைப்புகளால் பிரிப்பதும், அத்தகைய பிரிக்கப்பட்ட புள்ளிவிவரங்களை மேலும் இடஞ்சார்ந்த கட்டமைக்கப்பட்ட அலகுகளாக ஒதுக்குவதும் ஆகும். முழு செயல்முறையும் ஒரு தரவு இணைவு அணுகுமுறையை இன்றியமையாததாக்குகிறது, இது பல்வேறு மூலங்களிலிருந்தும் வெவ்வேறு இடஞ்சார்ந்த அளவீடுகளிலிருந்தும் தகவல்களை ஒருங்கிணைக்கிறது, இது பல்வேறு பொருத்தங்களைப் பயன்படுத்துவதன் மூலம் வெவ்வேறு இடஞ்சார்ந்த அளவீடுகளில் இருந்து தகவல்களை ஒருங்கிணைக்கிறது
மற்றும் அளவுத்திருத்த செயல்முறைகள். பின்னர் அனைத்து தரவு உறுப்புகளும் தேர்வுமுறை மாதிரி மூலம் செயலாக்கப்படுகின்றன, இது கட்டம் மட்டத்தில் முடிவுகளை உருவாக்குகிறது. ஒரு தரப்படுத்தப்பட்ட எஸ்பிஏஎம் மாதிரியில் மூன்று துணை மாதிரிகள் உள்ளன: பிரித்தல், தேர்வுமுறை மற்றும் ஒதுக்கீடு. ஸ்பாம் 2010 இந்த பொதுவான அமைப்பை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டது, அதே நேரத்தில் இது மேலும் வழிமுறை மற்றும் தரவு மேம்பாடுகளைச் சேர்க்கிறது, இதில் முக்கியமாக அடிப்படை ஆண்டின் புதுப்பிப்பு, துணைதேசிய நிர்வாக-அலகு கவரேஜின் விரிவாக்கம், பயிர் பட்டியலின் விரிவாக்கம் மற்றும் சமீபத்திய கலப்பின பயிர் நில வரைபடத்தை அடிப்படை ஒதுக்கீடு அடுக்காக பதிலீடு செய்தல் ஆகியவை அடங்கும்.

விவசாய உற்பத்தியின் (எ.கா., மகசூல், அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதி மற்றும் மொத்த உற்பத்தி) பயிர் புள்ளிவிவரங்களை நிர்வாக அலகு அளவுகள் (கே), பயிர் வகை (ஜே), மற்றும் விவசாய அமைப்பு (எல்) ஆகியவற்றால் கரடுமுரடான அளவு முதல் நேர்த்தியான அளவு வரை பிரிப்பதே எஸ்பிஏஎம் இன் முதல் படியாகும். நான்கு உற்பத்தி அமைப்புகள் நீர் மற்றும் மேலாண்மை வகையால் வரையறுக்கப்பட்டன:
- நீர்ப்பாசனம் – உயர் உள்ளீடு (I)
- மானாவாரி – உயர் உள்ளீடு (எச்)
- மானாவாரி - குறைந்த உள்ளீடு (எல்)
- மானாவாரி - வாழ்வாதாரம் (எஸ்)

ஒவ்வொரு பயிருக்கும் விவசாய முறை பங்குகள் பற்றிய உலகளாவிய தரவுகள் பெரும்பாலும் இல்லாத போதிலும், நான்கு கருத்துருவாக்கப்பட்ட விவசாய முறைகள் முக்கியமாக நீர் வழங்கல் அமைப்பு மற்றும் விவசாயிகள் பயன்படுத்தும் இடுபொருட்களால் விவரிக்கப்படுகின்றன. பிரேசில், சீனா, இந்தியா, ரஷ்யா, அமெரிக்கா போன்ற சிறிய எண்ணிக்கையிலான பெரிய நாடுகளுக்கு, ஏ.டி.எம்.1 அளவில் விவசாய முறை பங்குகள் குறித்த தரவுகள் ஆசிரியர்களிடம் உள்ளன. மற்ற நாடுகளுக்கு ஆசிரியர்கள் தேசிய விவசாய முறையின் பங்குகளை ஒவ்வொரு ஏ.டி.எம்.1 மட்டத்திற்கும் பகிர்ந்தளித்தனர், பின்னர் ஆதரவு ஆதாரங்களின் வெளிச்சத்தில் தனிப்பட்ட ஏ.டி.எம்.1 விவசாய முறை பங்குகளை சரிசெய்தனர். நீர்ப்பாசன விவசாய முறைமைகளுக்கு, [நீர் மற்றும் விவசாயம் பற்றிய உலகளாவிய தகவல் முறைமை (AQUASTAT)] (https://www.fao.org/aquastat/en/), [MIRCA](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2008GB003435) மற்றும்
ஒட்டுமொத்த அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதியின் மூலம் நாடு அளவிலான புள்ளிவிவரங்கள்.

SPAM2010 இல் உள்ள தேர்வுமுறை தொகுதி முந்தைய பதிப்புகளில் இருந்ததைப் போலவே உள்ளது. ஆசிரியர்கள் பொது இயற்கணித மாடலிங் அமைப்பில் (ஜி.ஏ.எம்.எஸ்) ஒரு குறுக்கு-என்ட்ரோபி செயல்முறையைப் பயன்படுத்தினர், இது ஒரு தீர்வு கண்டுபிடிக்கப்படும் வரை தேர்வுமுறை செயல்முறை மீண்டும் செயல்படுகிறது என்பதை உறுதிப்படுத்துகிறது. ஒதுக்கீடு வெற்றிகரமாக இருந்தால், ஒரு உகந்த அல்லது உள்நாட்டில் உகந்த தீர்வு கண்டுபிடிக்கப்பட்டது என்று அர்த்தம், வழக்கமான உடனடியாக கட்டம், பயிர் மற்றும் விவசாய அமைப்பு மூலம் ஒதுக்கப்பட்ட இயற்பியல் பகுதியைத் திருப்பித் தருகிறது, மேலும் நிரல் தானாகவே பிந்தைய செயலாக்கத்துடன் தொடர்கிறது.

எஸ்பிஏஎம் மாதிரி ஒவ்வொரு பிக்சலுக்குள்ளும் புள்ளிவிவரங்களை ஒதுக்க கூடுதல் உயிரியல் மற்றும் பொருளாதார உள்ளீடுகளைப் பயன்படுத்தியது. உள்ளீட்டுத் தரவு சேர்க்கப்பட்டுள்ளது (பலவற்றில்):
- நிர்வாக அலகுகள்
- பயிர் வகை
- விவசாய முறை
- சரிசெய்யப்பட்ட அறுவடை பகுதி
- பயிர் மற்றும் விவசாய முறை மூலம் ஒவ்வொரு கட்டத்திலும் மொத்த பொருத்தமான பரப்பளவு
- பயிர் விலைகள்
- ஒவ்வொரு கட்டத்திலும் சந்தை அணுகல்தன்மை
- சனத்தொகை அடர்த்தி

எங்கள் தரவு அட்டவணை SPAM2010 அத்தியாவசிய வெளியீடு குறிகாட்டிகளில் மூன்றை வழங்குகிறது:

- அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதி: மேலும் ஹெக்டேர்களில் அளவிடப்படுகிறது, அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதி குறைந்தபட்சம் இயற்பியல் பரப்பளவைப் போலவே பெரியது, ஆனால் சில நேரங்களில் அதிகமாக உள்ளது, ஏனெனில் இது ஒரே நிலத்தில் ஒரு பயிரின் பல அறுவடைகளுக்கும் காரணமாகிறது. இயற்பியல் பரப்பளவைப் போலவே, அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதியும் ஒவ்வொரு உற்பத்தி அமைப்புக்கும் கணக்கிடப்படுகிறது, மேலும் ஒரு பிக்சலில் அனைத்து உற்பத்தி அமைப்புகளின் அனைத்து அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதிகளின் கூட்டுத்தொகையானது மொத்த அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பரப்பளவுக்கு சமம்
படவரைபுள்ளி. ஒரு பிக்சலில் பயிர்களின் அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட அனைத்து பகுதிகளின் கூட்டுத்தொகை பிக்சல் அளவை விட பெரியதாக இருக்கலாம்.
- உற்பத்தி: ஒவ்வொரு உற்பத்தி அமைப்பு மற்றும் பயிருக்கும், அதன் தொடர்புடைய மகசூலால் அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பரப்பை பெருக்குவதன் மூலம் உற்பத்தி கணக்கிடப்படுகிறது. இது மெட்ரிக் டன்களில் அளவிடப்படுகிறது. ஒரு பயிரின் மொத்த உற்பத்தியானது, அந்தப் பயிரின் அனைத்து உற்பத்தி முறைகளின் உற்பத்தியையும் உள்ளடக்குகிறது.
- மகசூல்: அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட ஒரு பகுதிக்கான உற்பத்தியின் அளவு மற்றும் ஹெக்டேருக்கு கிலோகிராம்களில் அளவிடப்படுகிறது. இது உற்பத்தித்திறனின் அளவீடு ஆகும். ஒரு பயிரின் மொத்த மகசூல், அனைத்து உற்பத்தி முறைகளையும் கருத்தில் கொள்ளும்போது, நான்கு முறைகளின் விளைச்சலின் எடையிடப்பட்ட சராசரியாகும்.

முழு ஆவணப்படுத்தலுக்கு, தயவுசெய்து மூலத்தைப் பார்க்கவும் [வழிமுறை](https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/12/3545/2020/essd-12-3545-2020.pdf).
  
### கூடுதல் தகவல்  
  
எங்கள் தரவு அட்டவணை தரவுத்தொகுப்பின் துணைக்குழுவை மட்டுமே காட்டுகிறது. 2010 ஆம் ஆண்டிற்கான உலகளாவிய இடஞ்சார்ந்த-பிரிக்கப்பட்ட பயிர் உற்பத்தி புள்ளிவிவரத் தரவு 2.0 பதிப்பு 36 பிற பயிர்களுக்கான தரவுகளைக் கொண்டுள்ளது (மொத்தம் 42). முழு தரவுத்தொகுப்பில் அனைத்து 42 பயிர்களுக்கான இயற்பியல் பரப்பளவு மற்றும் உற்பத்தியின் மதிப்பும் அடங்கும். முழு தரவுத்தொகுப்பு மற்றும் கூடுதல் தகவலுக்கான அணுகலுக்கு, "மேலும் அறிக" பொத்தானைக் கிளிக் செய்யவும்.

எங்கள் தரவு அட்டவணை முன்னர் [2005] (https://bit.ly/3CjoFYc) க்கான தரவைக் காட்டியது. முறைமை மாற்றப்பட்டதால் இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பு காப்பகப்படுத்தப்பட்டது.  
  
### தரவை காட்சிப்படுத்தல்  
  
WRI இன் தரவு அட்டவணையில் காண்பிக்கப்படுவதற்கு முன்பு எங்கள் குழு இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பை மறுவடிவமைத்தது. [Github] இல் தரவை நாங்கள் எவ்வாறு மீட்டெடுத்தோம் என்பதற்கான ஆவணங்களைப் பார்க்கவும் (https://github.com/resource-வாட்ச்/தரவு-முன்-செயலாக்கம்/மரம்/மாஸ்டர்/foo_005_rw1_crop_area_production).  
  
### பொறுப்புத்துறப்பு  
  
இந்த விளக்கப் பக்கத்தின் பகுதிகள் மூல மெட்டாடேட்டாவிலிருந்து எடுக்கப்பட்டன.

info.name: பயிர் நில பரப்பு மற்றும் உற்பத்தி

sources.source-description: கொள்கைகள், நிறுவனங்கள் மற்றும் சந்தைகள் மீதான சர்வதேச விவசாய ஆராய்ச்சி நிகழ்ச்சித்திட்டம் பற்றிய ஆலோசனைக் குழு (CGIAR-PIM)

info.technical_title: 2010 பதிப்பு 2.0 க்கான உலகளாவிய இடஞ்சார்ந்த-பிரிக்கப்பட்ட பயிர் உற்பத்தி புள்ளிவிவர தரவு
info.functions: 2010 ஆம் ஆண்டுக்கான கோதுமை, சோயாபீன்ஸ், நெல், மக்காச்சோளம், காபி மற்றும் பருத்திப் பயிர்களின் உற்பத்தி, அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பரப்பு மற்றும் மகசூல்
info.cautions:
- முன்னர் குறிப்பிட்டபடி, எஸ்பிஏஎம் மதிப்பீடுகள் பெரும்பாலான மாதிரிகளைப் போலவே முதன்மை உள்ளீட்டுத் தரவின் அளவு மற்றும் உண்மைத்தன்மையைப் பொறுத்தது. SPAM2010 உற்பத்தி பருவத்தில் 200 க்கும் மேற்பட்ட நாடுகளில் 42 பயிர்கள் பற்றிய தரவு தேவைப்படுகிறது. வெறுமனே, இந்த தரவு ஒரு ADM2 மட்டத்தில் சேகரிக்கப்பட வேண்டும்; இருப்பினும், இது எப்போதும் சாத்தியமில்லை. சோமாலியா மற்றும் நைஜீரியா போன்ற ஒரு சில நாடுகளில் இது குறிப்பாக கடினமாக உள்ளது, அங்கு நம்பகமான
தரவு கிடைக்கவில்லை, அல்லது வெவ்வேறு உள்ளீட்டு தரவு ஒருவருக்கொருவர் முரண்படுகிறது.
- பெரும்பாலான பயிர்ச்செய்கைப் புள்ளிவிபரங்கள் விவசாய முறையினால் வரையறுக்கப்படுவதில்லை என்பதால், கேள்விக்குரிய நான்கு முறைமைகளில் ஒவ்வொன்றின் கீழும் உற்பத்திப் பங்குகளின் மதிப்பீடுகள் தேவைப்படுகின்றன. அறுவடை செய்யப்பட்ட பகுதி புள்ளிவிவரங்களை மாதிரியில் பயன்படுத்தப்படும் இயற்பியல்-பரப்பு புள்ளிவிவரங்களாக மாற்றுவதற்கு, பயிர் மற்றும் விவசாய முறைகள் மூலம் பயிர் தீவிரம் குறித்த கூடுதல் தரவுகள் சேகரிக்கப்பட வேண்டும். ஆசிரியர்கள் அதிகாரப்பூர்வ அல்லது வெளியிடப்பட்ட தரவுகளைச் சேகரித்து, மற்ற ஆதாரங்களைக் கண்டுபிடிக்க முடியாதபோது நிபுணர்களின் தீர்ப்புகளை கடைசி முயற்சியாக நம்பியிருந்தனர்.
- பயிர் உற்பத்தியின் பரந்த அளவிலான தரவு மூலங்கள், கவரேஜ் மற்றும் பிராந்திய நுணுக்கங்கள் ஆகியவை முறைசார் தாக்கங்களைக் கொண்டுள்ளன. முதலாவதாக, தரவு நிலைத்தன்மை மற்றும் தரவு நம்பகத்தன்மைக்கு இடையில் சாத்தியமான வர்த்தக-ஆஃப்கள் உள்ளன. எடுத்துக்காட்டாக, தேவையான நிர்வாக மட்டத்தில் ஒரு நாட்டிற்குள் தொடர்ந்து கிடைக்காத மாதிரியின் தேவைகள் (அதாவது, பயிர் தீவிரம் மற்றும் விவசாய முறை பங்குகள்) உள்ளன. பெரும்பாலும், இந்த எண்கள் நிர்வாக மட்டத்தில் யதார்த்தத்தை பிரதிபலிக்காவிட்டாலும், தேசிய அளவிலான மதிப்புகளிலிருந்து எடுக்கப்படுகின்றன. இரண்டாவதாக, எஸ்பிஏஎம்-க்குள் பல மற்றும் ஊடுபயிர்களை அதிநவீன முறையில் கையாளுவதில்லை. இந்த வகையான பயிர் முறைகள் ஒரு பயிருக்கு ஒற்றை பயிர் தீவிர மதிப்பு, விவசாய முறை மற்றும் (சாத்தியமான) துணை தேசிய அலகு ஆகியவற்றைப் பயன்படுத்துவதற்கு மட்டுமே கணக்கிடப்படுகின்றன. இறுதியாக, வாழ்வாதார விவசாயிகளுக்கும், வணிக விவசாயிகளுக்கும் சந்தை முக்கியமானது. எஸ்.பி.ஏ.எம் இல், ஆசிரியர்கள் சந்தை அருகாமையின் மறைமுக பிரதிநிதித்துவத்திற்காக மக்கள்தொகை அடர்த்தியை நம்பியுள்ளனர்.
- கடைசியாக ஆனால் குறைந்தது அல்ல, எஸ்பிஏஎம் தயாரிப்புகளை நேர கட்டங்களில் நேரடியாக ஒப்பிடும் போது ஆசிரியர்கள் எச்சரிக்கையுடன் இருக்க பரிந்துரைக்கின்றனர். பல்வேறு தரவு தயாரிப்புகளில் கணினி பிழைகள் இருப்பதால் இது பெரும்பாலும் உள்ளது.
info.citation: சர்வதேச உணவு கொள்கை ஆராய்ச்சி நிறுவனம், 2019, "உலகளாவிய இடஞ்சார்ந்த-பிரிக்கப்பட்ட பயிர் உற்பத்தி புள்ளிவிவரத் தரவு 2010 பதிப்பு 2.0", https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/PRFF8V, ஹார்வர்ட் டேட்டாவெர்ஸ், வி 4. உலக வளங்கள் நிறுவனம் மூலம் அணுகப்பட்டது, (தேதி). [www.resourcewatch.org] (https://www.resourcewatch.org).

attributes.name: పంట భూమి వైశాల్యం మరియు ఉత్పత్తి
attributes.description:
### అవలోకనం  
  
పంట భూమి మరియు ఉత్పత్తి డేటాసెట్ ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా పండించిన ప్రాంతం, ఉత్పత్తి మరియు ఆరు ప్రధాన పంటలకు దిగుబడిని చూపిస్తుంది: గోధుమ, సోయాబీన్, వరి, మొక్కజొన్న, కాఫీ మరియు పత్తి. డేటాసెట్ 2010 ప్రాదేశిక ఉత్పత్తి కేటాయింపు నమూనా (స్పామ్) నుండి తీసుకోబడింది. పంట భూమి ఉపరితలం, నీటిపారుదల ప్రాంతాల యొక్క స్థానం, పంట అనుకూలత మరియు సంభావ్య దిగుబడులు, గ్రామీణ జనాభా సాంద్రతలు, ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థల లక్షణాలు మరియు పంట ధరలు వంటి వివిధ రకాల ఇన్పుట్లను ఉపయోగించి జాతీయ మరియు ఉప-జాతీయ పంట గణాంకాలను (డౌన్ స్కేల్) విడదీయడం (డౌన్ స్కేల్) ఎస్పిఎఎమ్ నమూనా లక్ష్యంగా పెట్టుకుంది. పంట డేటా 5 ఆర్క్ నిమిషాల ప్రాదేశిక రిజల్యూషన్ కు డౌన్ స్కేల్ చేయబడింది. ఈ ప్రాదేశిక రిజల్యూషన్ భూమధ్యరేఖ వద్ద సుమారు 10 కిలోమీటర్లు x 10 కిలోమీటర్లు ఉంటుంది, కానీ [దూరాన్ని బట్టి మారుతుంది](https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-ఆఫ్-అక్షాంశం-మరియు-రేఖాంశం-దూరం-4070616) భూమధ్యరేఖ నుండి. 

మొక్కజొన్న, వరి, సోయాబీన్ మరియు గోధుమలు కలిసి ప్రపంచ వ్యవసాయ కేలరీలలో మూడింట రెండు వంతుల వాటాను కలిగి ఉన్నాయి. ఆహార మార్పులు, పెరుగుతున్న జనాభా స్థాయిలు మరియు పెరిగిన జీవ ఇంధన డిమాండ్ ఫలితంగా ఈ పంటలకు ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా డిమాండ్ పెరుగుతోంది. ఈ వనరులకు పెరిగిన గిరాకీ భూమి మరియు వనరుల వినియోగం, వాతావరణ మార్పు, రాజకీయ అజెండాలు మరియు సాంకేతిక అభివృద్ధిని గణనీయంగా ప్రభావితం చేస్తుంది. ఈ ప్రభావాలను ముందస్తుగా పరిష్కరించడానికి ప్రపంచ పంటల ప్రస్తుత ప్రాదేశిక పంపిణీ గురించి సమగ్ర అవగాహన అవసరం. కీలకమైన ప్రపంచ పంటల యొక్క పరిధి మరియు ఉత్పాదకతను అర్థం చేసుకోవడానికి క్రాప్ ల్యాండ్ ఏరియా మరియు ప్రొడక్షన్ డేటాసెట్ ఉపయోగించబడుతుంది, ఇది ఆహార పంట డిమాండ్ మరియు దాని ప్రభావాలను పరిష్కరించడంలో సహాయపడుతుంది. 

క్రాప్ ల్యాండ్ ఏరియా అండ్ ప్రొడక్షన్ డేటాసెట్ [పాలసీలు, ఇన్ స్టిట్యూషన్స్, అండ్ మార్కెట్స్ పై ఇంటర్నేషనల్ అగ్రికల్చరల్ రీసెర్చ్ ప్రోగ్రామ్ పై కన్సల్టేటివ్ గ్రూప్ ఆన్ ఇంటర్నేషనల్ అగ్రికల్చరల్ రీసెర్చ్ ప్రోగ్రామ్(సిజిఐఎఆర్-పిఐఎం)](https://pim.cgiar.org/about/) ద్వారా జనరేట్ చేయబడింది. సిజిఐఎఆర్-పిఐఎమ్ రైతుల జీవితాలను మెరుగుపరచడానికి, పోషకమైన మరియు చౌకైన ఆహారాన్ని ఉత్పత్తి చేయడానికి మరియు గ్రామీణ ప్రకృతి దృశ్యాలలో నేల, నీరు మరియు జీవవైవిధ్యాన్ని రక్షించడానికి సహాయపడే విధానాలకు మద్దతు ఇస్తుంది. ఈ కార్యక్రమానికి [ఇంటర్నేషనల్ ఫుడ్ పాలసీ రీసెర్చ్ ఇనిస్టిట్యూట్ (IFPRI)](https://www.ifpri.org/about), ఒక CGIAR-PIM రీసెర్చ్ సెంటర్ నాయకత్వం వహిస్తుంది. అభివృద్ధి చెందుతున్న దేశాలలో పేదరికాన్ని సుస్థిరంగా తగ్గించడానికి మరియు ఆకలిని అంతం చేయడానికి ఐఎఫ్ పిఆర్ ఐ పరిశోధన ఆధారిత విధాన పరిష్కారాలను అందిస్తుంది. పంట భూమి ప్రాంతం మరియు ఉత్పత్తి డేటాసెట్ అనేది పెద్ద స్పామ్ డేటాసెట్ లో భాగంగా ఉంది, ఇది హార్వెస్ట్ ఛైస్ రీసెర్చ్ ఇనిషియేటివ్ కొరకు అభివృద్ధి చేయబడింది. ఐ.ఎఫ్.పి.ఆర్.ఐ చే నిర్వహించబడింది, [హార్వెస్ట్ చోయిస్](https://www.ifpri.org/project/harvestchoice) మరింత ఉత్పాదక మరియు లాభదాయకమైన వ్యవసాయం ద్వారా ఉప-సహారా ఆఫ్రికా మరియు దక్షిణాసియాలోని పేద ప్రజల శ్రేయస్సును మెరుగుపరచడానికి వ్యూహాత్మక పెట్టుబడులకు మార్గనిర్దేశం చేయడంలో సహాయపడటానికి జ్ఞాన ఉత్పత్తులను ఉత్పత్తి చేసింది.
  
#### మెథడాలజీ  
  
వివిధ వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థల ద్వారా పంట గణాంకాలను (ఉదా. కోసిన ప్రాంతం, ఉత్పత్తి పరిమాణం మరియు దిగుబడి) విడదీయడం మరియు అటువంటి విడదీయబడిన గణాంకాలను ప్రాదేశికంగా గ్రిడ్ చేయబడ్డ యూనిట్ లుగా మరింత కేటాయించడం స్పామ్ యొక్క ప్రధాన ఉద్దేశ్యం. ఈ మొత్తం ప్రక్రియ డేటా ఫ్యూజన్ అప్రోచ్ ని కలిగి ఉంటుంది, ఇది వివిధ వనరుల నుండి సమాచారాన్ని మిళితం చేస్తుంది మరియు వివిధ ప్రాదేశిక ప్రమాణాల వద్ద వివిధ మ్యాచింగ్ లను మోహరించడం ద్వారా
మరియు క్రమాంకన ప్రక్రియలు. అప్పుడు అన్ని డేటా ఎలిమెంట్లు ఆప్టిమైజేషన్ మోడల్ ద్వారా ప్రాసెస్ చేయబడతాయి, ఇది గ్రిడ్ స్థాయిలో ఫలితాలను జనరేట్ చేస్తుంది. ఒక ప్రామాణిక స్పామ్ నమూనాలో మూడు ఉపమాడ్యూల్స్ ఉన్నాయి: డిసాగ్రెగేషన్, ఆప్టిమైజేషన్ మరియు కేటాయింపు. ఈ సాధారణ అమరిక ఆధారంగా స్పామ్2010 భావనాత్మకంగా రూపొందించబడింది, అయితే ఇది మరింత మెథడాలజికల్ మరియు డేటా మెరుగుదలలను జోడిస్తుంది, వీటిలో ప్రధానంగా బేస్ ఇయర్ యొక్క నవీకరణ, ప్రత్యామ్నాయ పరిపాలనా-యూనిట్ కవరేజ్ యొక్క విస్తరణ, పంట జాబితా యొక్క విస్తరణ, మరియు తాజా హైబ్రిడ్ క్రాప్ ల్యాండ్ మ్యాప్ ను ప్రాథమిక కేటాయింపు పొరగా భర్తీ చేయడం వంటివి ఉంటాయి.

వ్యవసాయ ఉత్పత్తి యొక్క పంట గణాంకాలను (ఉదా. దిగుబడి, కోత విస్తీర్ణం మరియు మొత్తం ఉత్పత్తి) పరిపాలనా-యూనిట్ స్థాయిలు (కె), పంట రకం (జె), మరియు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ (l) ముతక స్కేలు నుండి సూక్ష్మమైన స్కేలుకు విడదీయడం స్పామ్ యొక్క మొదటి దశ. నాలుగు ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థలు నీరు మరియు నిర్వహణ రకం ద్వారా నిర్వచించబడ్డాయి:
- నీటిపారుదల - అధిక ఇన్ పుట్ (I)
- వర్షాధారం - అధిక ఇన్పుట్ (H)
- వర్షాధారం - తక్కువ ఇన్పుట్ (ఎల్)
- వర్షాధారం - జీవనోపాధి (ఎస్)

ప్రతి పంటకు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ వాటాలపై ప్రపంచ డేటా ఎక్కువగా లేనప్పటికీ, నాలుగు భావనాత్మక వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థలు ప్రధానంగా నీటి సరఫరా వ్యవస్థ మరియు రైతులు ఉపయోగించే ఇన్ పుట్ ల ద్వారా వర్ణించబడ్డాయి. బ్రెజిల్, చైనా, ఇండియా, రష్యా, యునైటెడ్ స్టేట్స్ వంటి చిన్న సంఖ్యలో పెద్ద దేశాలకు, రచయితలు ఎడిఎమ్1 స్థాయిలో వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ వాటాలపై డేటాను కలిగి ఉన్నారు. ఇతర దేశాలకు రచయితలు జాతీయ వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ వాటాలను ప్రతి ఎడిఎమ్ 1 స్థాయికి కేటాయించారు మరియు తరువాత మద్దతు ఇచ్చే సాక్ష్యాల వెలుగులో వ్యక్తిగత ఎడిఎమ్ 1 వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ వాటాలను సర్దుబాటు చేశారు. నీటి పారుదల వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థల కొరకు, [గ్లోబల్ ఇన్ఫర్మేషన్ సిస్టమ్ ఆన్ వాటర్ అండ్ అగ్రికల్చర్ (AQUASTAT)](https://www.fao.org/aquastat/en/), [MIRCA](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2008GB003435) నుంచి పొందిన పూర్తి నియంత్రణ నీటిపారుదల కింద సాగు చేయబడ్డ పంట విస్తీర్ణాన్ని విభజించడం ద్వారా పంట-నిర్దిష్ట వాటాలు పొందబడతాయి.
మొత్తం కోత విస్తీర్ణం ద్వారా దేశ-స్థాయి గణాంకాలు.

స్పామ్2010లోని ఆప్టిమైజేషన్ మాడ్యూల్, మునుపటి వెర్షన్ ల వలేనే దాదాపుగా ఒకేవిధంగా ఉంటుంది. సాధారణ బీజగణిత మోడలింగ్ సిస్టమ్ (జిఎఎంఎస్) లో రచయితలు క్రాస్-ఎంట్రోపీ ప్రక్రియను వర్తింపజేశారు, ఇది ఒక పరిష్కారం కనుగొనే వరకు ఆప్టిమైజేషన్ ప్రక్రియ పునరావృతమయ్యేలా చూస్తుంది. కేటాయింపు విజయవంతం అయిన తరువాత, అంటే ఒక అనుకూలమైన లేదా స్థానికంగా అనుకూలమైన పరిష్కారం కనుగొనబడింది, రొటీన్ వెంటనే గ్రిడ్, పంట మరియు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ ద్వారా కేటాయించబడిన భౌతిక ప్రాంతాన్ని తిరిగి ఇస్తుంది, మరియు ప్రోగ్రామ్ ఆటోమేటిక్ గా పోస్ట్ ప్రాసెసింగ్ తో కొనసాగుతుంది.

స్పామ్ నమూనా ప్రతి పిక్సెల్ లోపల గణాంకాలను కేటాయించడానికి అదనపు జీవ మరియు ఆర్థిక ఇన్పుట్లను ఉపయోగించింది. ఇన్ పుట్ డేటా చేర్చబడింది (అనేక ఇతర వాటి మధ్య):
- పరిపాలనా విభాగాలు
- పంట రకం
- వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ
- సర్దుబాటు చేయబడిన కోత ప్రాంతం
- పంట మరియు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ ద్వారా ప్రతి గ్రిడ్ లో మొత్తం అనువైన ప్రాంతం
- పంట ధరలు
- ప్రతి గ్రిడ్ లో మార్కెట్ యాక్సెసబిలిటీ
- జనసాంద్రత

మా డేటా కేటలాగ్ మూడు SPAM2010 ఆవశ్యక అవుట్ పుట్ ఇండికేటర్ లను అందిస్తుంది:

- కోసిన ప్రాంతం: హెక్టార్లలో కూడా కొలుస్తారు, కోతకు గురైన ప్రాంతం కనీసం భౌతిక ప్రాంతం అంత పెద్దదిగా ఉంటుంది, అయితే కొన్నిసార్లు ఎక్కువ ఎందుకంటే ఇది ఒకే పొలంలో ఒక పంట యొక్క బహుళ కోతలకు కూడా కారణమవుతుంది. భౌతిక వైశాల్యం వలె, కోతకు గురైన ప్రాంతం ప్రతి ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థ కొరకు లెక్కించబడుతుంది, మరియు పిక్సెల్ లో అన్ని ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థల యొక్క అన్ని కోత ప్రాంతాల యొక్క మొత్తం కోతకు గురైన ప్రాంతం యొక్క మొత్తం కోతకు గురైన ప్రాంతానికి సమానం అవుతుంది.
పిక్సెల్. ఒక పిక్సెల్ లో పంట కోతకు గురైన అన్ని ప్రాంతాల మొత్తం పిక్సెల్ పరిమాణం కంటే పెద్దదిగా ఉండవచ్చు.
- ఉత్పత్తి: ప్రతి ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థ మరియు పంటకు, దాని సంబంధిత దిగుబడి ద్వారా కోసిన విస్తీర్ణాన్ని గుణించడం ద్వారా ఉత్పత్తిని లెక్కిస్తారు. దీనిని మెట్రిక్ టన్నులలో కొలుస్తారు. ఒక పంట యొక్క మొత్తం ఉత్పత్తిలో ఆ పంట యొక్క అన్ని ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థల ఉత్పత్తి ఉంటుంది.
- దిగుబడి: కోతకు వచ్చిన ప్రతి ప్రాంతానికి ఉత్పత్తి మొత్తం మరియు హెక్టారుకు కిలోగ్రాములలో లెక్కించబడుతుంది. ఇది ఉత్పాదకత యొక్క కొలత. అన్ని ఉత్పత్తి వ్యవస్థలను పరిగణనలోకి తీసుకున్నప్పుడు, ఒక పంట యొక్క మొత్తం దిగుబడి నాలుగు వ్యవస్థల యొక్క దిగుబడి యొక్క బరువు కలిగిన సగటు.

పూర్తి డాక్యుమెంటేషన్ కొరకు, దయచేసి సోర్స్ [మెథడాలజీ](https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/12/3545/2020/essd-12-3545-2020.pdf) చూడండి.
  
### అదనపు సమాచారం  
  
మా డేటా కేటలాగ్ డేటాసెట్ యొక్క ఉపసమితిని మాత్రమే చూపుతుంది. 2010 వెర్షన్ 2.0 కొరకు గ్లోబల్ స్పేషియల్లీ-డిస్అగ్రెగేటెడ్ క్రాప్ ప్రొడక్షన్ స్టాటిస్టిక్స్ డేటా 36 ఇతర పంటలకు సంబంధించిన డేటాను కలిగి ఉంది (మొత్తం 42). పూర్తి డేటాసెట్ లో భౌతిక వైశాల్యం మరియు మొత్తం 42 పంటల కొరకు ఉత్పత్తి విలువ కూడా ఉంటుంది. పూర్తి డేటాసెట్ మరియు అదనపు సమాచారానికి ప్రాప్యత కోసం, "మరింత తెలుసుకోండి" బటన్ మీద క్లిక్ చేయండి.

మా డేటా కేటలాగ్ ఇంతకు ముందు [2005](https://bit.ly/3CjoFYc) కొరకు డేటాను చూపించింది. ఈ డేటాసెట్ ఆర్కైవ్ చేయబడింది ఎందుకంటే మెథడాలజీ మార్చబడింది.  
  
### డేటాను విజువలైజ్ చేయడం  
  
డబ్ల్యుఆర్ఐ యొక్క డేటా కేటలాగ్ లో ప్రదర్శించడానికి ముందు మా బృందం ఈ డేటాసెట్ ను పునర్నిర్మించింది. [Github](https://github.com/resource-వాచ్/డేటా-ప్రీ-ప్రాసెసింగ్/ట్రీ/మాస్టర్/foo_005_rw1_crop_area_production)పై డేటాను మేం ఏవిధంగా తిరిగి పొందాం అనే దానిపై డాక్యుమెంటేషన్ ని చూడండి.  
  
### డిస్ క్లెయిమర్  
  
ఈ వివరణ పేజీ యొక్క సారాంశాలు మూల మెటాడేటా నుండి తీసుకోబడ్డాయి.

info.functions: 2010 సంవత్సరానికి గోధుమ, సోయాబీన్, వరి, మొక్కజొన్న, కాఫీ, మరియు పత్తి పంటలకు ఉత్పత్తి, కోత ప్రాంతం మరియు దిగుబడి
info.cautions:
- ఇంతకు ముందు పేర్కొన్నట్లుగా, స్పామ్ అంచనాలు చాలా మోడల్స్ వలె ప్రాథమిక ఇన్ పుట్ డేటా యొక్క పరిధి మరియు వాస్తవికతపై ఆధారపడి ఉంటాయి. స్పామ్2010 ఉత్పత్తి సీజన్ కొరకు 200కు పైగా దేశాల్లోని 42 పంటలకు సంబంధించిన డేటా అవసరం అవుతుంది. ఆదర్శవంతంగా, ఈ డేటాను ఎడిఎమ్2 స్థాయిలో సేకరించాలి; అయితే, ఇది ఎల్లప్పుడూ సాధ్యం కాదు. సోమాలియా మరియు నైజీరియా వంటి కొన్ని దేశాలలో ఇది ముఖ్యంగా కష్టంగా ఉంది, ఇక్కడ నమ్మదగినది
డేటా లభ్యం కావడం లేదు, లేదా విభిన్న ఇన్ పుట్ డేటా ఒకదానితో మరొకటి విభేదిస్తుంది.
- చాలా పంటల గణాంకాలు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థచే వర్ణించబడనందున, ప్రశ్నార్ధకమైన నాలుగు వ్యవస్థలలో ప్రతి దాని క్రింద ఉత్పత్తి వాటాల అంచనాలు అవసరం. కోతకు గురైన ప్రాంత గణాంకాలను నమూనాలో ఉపయోగించిన భౌతిక-ప్రాంత గణాంకాలకు మార్చడానికి, పంట మరియు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థల ద్వారా పంట తీవ్రతలపై అదనపు డేటాను సేకరించాలి. రచయితలు అధికారిక లేదా ప్రచురించిన డేటాను సేకరించారు మరియు ఇతర వనరులను కనుగొనలేనప్పుడు చివరి ప్రయత్నంగా నిపుణుల తీర్పులపై ఆధారపడారు.
- విస్తృత శ్రేణి డేటా వనరులు, కవరేజీ మరియు పంట ఉత్పత్తి యొక్క ప్రాంతీయ సూక్ష్మాంశాలు విధానపరమైన చిక్కులను కలిగి ఉంటాయి. మొదట, డేటా స్థిరత్వం మరియు డేటా విశ్వసనీయత మధ్య సంభావ్య ట్రేడ్-ఆఫ్ లు ఉన్నాయి. ఉదాహరణకు, అవసరమైన పరిపాలనా స్థాయిలో ఒక దేశంలో స్థిరంగా అందుబాటులో లేని నమూనా యొక్క ఆవశ్యకతలు (అంటే, పంట తీవ్రతలు మరియు వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ వాటాలు) ఉన్నాయి. తరచుగా, ఈ సంఖ్యలు జాతీయ స్థాయి విలువల నుండి తీసుకోబడతాయి, అయినప్పటికీ అవి పరిపాలనా స్థాయిలో వాస్తవికతను ప్రతిబింబించకపోవచ్చు. రెండవది, బహుళ మరియు అంతరపంటలు స్పామ్ లోపల అధునాతన రీతిలో నిర్వహించబడవు. ఈ రకమైన పంట పోకడలు ప్రతి పంటకు, వ్యవసాయ వ్యవస్థ, మరియు (బహుశా) ఉపజాతి యూనిట్ కు ఒకే పంట తీవ్రత విలువను ఉపయోగించడానికి మాత్రమే లెక్కించబడతాయి. చివరగా, మార్కెట్ జీవనోపాధి రైతులకు మరియు వాణిజ్య రైతులకు ముఖ్యమైనది. స్పామ్ లో, రచయితలు మార్కెట్ సామీప్యం యొక్క పరోక్ష ప్రాతినిధ్యం కోసం జనసాంద్రతపై ఆధారపడతారు.
- చివరిది కానీ కనీసం కాదు, స్పామ్ ఉత్పత్తులను సమయ దశలలో నేరుగా పోల్చేటప్పుడు రచయితలు జాగ్రత్తగా ఉండాలని సూచిస్తున్నారు. వివిధ డేటా ఉత్పత్తుల్లో సిస్టమ్ దోషాలు ఉండటం దీనికి ప్రధాన కారణం.

attributes.name: U.S. Monthly Precipitation Normals
attributes.description: The Parameter-elevation Relationships on Independent Slopes Model (PRISM) Climate Group monthly climate normals are baseline data sets describing average monthly conditions over the most recent three full decades. The most recent PRISM normals are for the period 1981-2010. Spatial climate data sets for mean monthly precipitation and minimum and maximum temperature were developed for the conterminous United States. These 30-arcsec (∼800-m) grids are the official spatial climate data sets of the U.S. Department of Agriculture. The PRISM interpolation method was used to develop data sets that reflected, as closely as possible, the current state of knowledge of spatial climate patterns in the United States. PRISM calculates a climate–elevation regression for each digital elevation model (DEM) grid cell, and stations entering the regression are assigned weights based primarily on the physiographic similarity of the station to the grid cell. Factors considered are location, elevation, coastal proximity, topographic facet orientation, vertical atmospheric layer, topographic position, and orographic effectiveness of the terrain. Surface stations used in the analysis numbered nearly 13,000 for precipitation and 10,000 for temperature. Station data were spatially quality controlled, and short-period-of-record averages adjusted to better reflect the 1981–2010 period.

attributes.name: Urban Expansion Probabilities
attributes.description:
The Global Grid of Probabilities of Urban Expansion to 2030 by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration Socioeconomic Data and Applications Center (NASA SEDAC) presents spatially explicit probabilistic forecasts of global urban land cover change from 2000 through 2030 at a 2.5 arc-minute resolution. For each grid cell that is nonurban in 2000, a Monte Carlo model assigned a probability of becoming urban by the year 2030. The authors first extracted urban extent circa 2000 from the NASA MODIS Land Cover Type Product, Version 5, which provides a conservative estimate of global urban land cover. The authors then used population densities from the Global Rural-Urban Mapping Project, Version 1 (GRUMP v1), to create the population density driver map. They estimated the amount of new urban land in each UN region by 2030 in a Monte Carlo fashion based on present empirical distribution of regional urban population densities and probability density functions of projected regional population and GDP values for 2030.

PREPdata shows only a subset of this data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Download from Original Source link.

attributes.name: [Archived] Soil Carbon Stocks
attributes.description:
_**This dataset has been archived, and we will no longer be updating or maintaining it. We recommend using [this dataset](c5a62289-bdc8-4821-83f0-6f05e3d36bdc) as a replacement.**_
  
The International Soil Reference and Information Centre - World Soil Information (ISRIC-WIS) uses machine learning techniques to develop global maps of soil properties at various soil depths, as well as characterizing bedrock depth. Soil organic carbon stocks are reported in tons per hectare for six standard depth intervals: depths of 0-5 cm, 5-15 cm, 15-30 cm, 30-60 cm, 60-100 cm, and 100-200 cm. Soil organic carbon stocks are important because they are correlated with the productive capacity of land to generate food and other plant life. Soil property estimates are generated using machine learning techniques that combine soil samples, expert opinion, and remote-sensing data. 150,000 soil profiles from a variety of reporting organizations are used in conjunction with a stack of 158 remote sensing-based soil covariates (primarily derived from MODIS land products, SRTM DEM derivatives, climatic images and global landform and lithology maps) to fit an ensemble of machine learning methods—random forest and gradient boosting and/or multinomial logistic regression—as implemented in the R packages ranger, xgboost, nnet and caret. The results of 10–fold cross-validation show that the ensemble models explain between 56% (coarse fragments) and 83% (pH) of variation with an overall average of 61%. Improvements in the relative accuracy considering the amount of variation explained, in comparison to the previous version of SoilGrids at 1 km spatial resolution, range from 60 to 230%.   
  
 Improvements can be attributed to:   
  
 (1) the use of machine learning instead of linear regression,   
  
 (2) to considerable investments in preparing finer resolution covariate layers and (3) to insertion of additional soil profiles.   
  
 Further development of SoilGrids could include refinement of methods to incorporate input uncertainties and derivation of posterior probability distributions (per pixel), and further automation of spatial modeling so that soil maps can be generated for potentially hundreds of soil variables. attributes.name: Costa Rica Projected Coffee Suitability
attributes.description:
The Coffee Suitability Projections Under Four Scenarios data set was produced by Centro Internacional de Agricultura Tropical (CIAT) and shows coffee suitability projections. It was created as part of a study that attempts to utilize data from four Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) emissions scenarios (RCP 2.6, 4.5, 6.0, and 8.5) in two time periods (2050 and 2080) to determine the impact of climate change on coffee cultivation in coffee growing regions of Costa Rica. The study was done using georeferenced points obtained from Instituto del Café de Costa Rica (ICAFE), and using the MaxEnt model to simulate the adaptability of coffee production. 

Environmental layers taken into account comprise 19 bioclimatic variables from the Worldclim database. Developed by Hijmans et al. 2005, thousands of data points from meteorological stations around the world were collected for the time period of 1960 to 1990, using an interpolation to create environmental layers (rasters) of average temperature with 24,542 locations, minimum and maximum temperatures with 14,835 locations, and precipitation with 47,554 locations. These were all calculated by month, with a resolution of 1 square km. Bioclimatic variables were derived from monthly temperature and precipitation values with the goal of generating biologically significant and indispensable variables so that cultivation may develop properly.

PREPdata shows only a subset of this data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Download from Original Source link.

attributes.name: [Archived] Gridded Livestock
attributes.description:
_**This dataset has been archived, and we will no longer be updating or maintaining it. We recommend using [this dataset](6b523d76-ca2d-4059-b0a6-d90a6b8ba5a6) as a replacement.**_
  
The GLW is a global livestock mapping project by the Food and Agriculture Organization's Animal Production and Health Division (FAO-AGA). The data shows livestock distributions for the year 2006 at a 0.05° resolution.The methodology and sources of data are fully described in a document entitled: "The Gridded Livestock of the World. FAO (2007)". In summary, for each country the most recent available sub-national livestock census data and corresponding administrative boundaries have been collected. These are then converted into densities, excluding land unsuitable for livestock (either monogastric or ruminant), to provide the 'observed' data. The data are then disaggregated based on statistical relations with some environmental variables in similar agro-ecological zones to produce the 'predicted' distribution. The predicted data are further manipulated to match national census totals for the year 2000 according to the FAOSTAT database. The project also includes: a global network of data providers on livestock and sub-national boundaries; an Oracle database in which these data are managed and processed; a system for predicting livestock distributions based on environmental data and an interactive web application, the Global Livestock Production and Health Atlas (GLiPHA), through which data are viewed and disseminated. The files are in a raster GRID format. Pixel values represent actual densities (per square kilometre). These data have been produced by FAO's Animal Production and Health Division in collaboration with ERGO and the TALA research group, University of Oxford, UK.

info.cautions: The accuracy of the predictions varied significantly according to species and the level of detail in the input training data, and were comparable to those found by Van Boeckel et al. (2011) in Asia, Van Boeckel et al. (2012) in Thailand, and Prosser et al. (2011) in Asia. The administrative level of the training data had a strong influence on model accuracy; with greater accuracy observed with higher administrative levels of training data for both cattle in Brazil and chickens in Thailand. Accuracy also varies in areas where production is highly intensive. As production intensifies it becomes increasingly detached from the land resource base (for example as feeds are brought in that are grown in completely different places) and thus more difficult to predict based on spatial, agro-ecological variables. This effect is particularly marked for chickens and pigs, where the locations of intensive farming units often have more to do with accessibility to markets or to inputs of one sort or another, than to the agro-ecological characteristics of the land that can be quantified through remotely sensed variables. With general trends toward intensified production, the modelling could be improved in the future by incorporating a wider set of anthropogenic, socio-economic and perhaps demand- or trade-related predictor variables.

attributes.name: Cropland Change
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
_**The Cropland Change data is still a draft product and data are subject to change in the future.**_
  
  
The Cropland Change dataset at 30 m spatial resolution was developed by the Global Land Analysis and Discovery Lab (GLAD) at the University of Maryland (UMD) using Landsat satellite data time-series. Cropland is defined as land used to produce herbaceous crops for human consumption, forage and biofuel. Perennial woody crops, permanent pastures, and shifting cultivation are excluded from the definition. The four year time intervals allow for a fallow length up to four years for the cropland class. The map is based on the machine learning classification of the global Landsat data archive using locally calibrated models. Model calibration data were collected through visual interpretation of Landsat and high spatial resolution satellite images. The mapping was performed for the 2000-2003 and 2016-2019 time intervals. For each four-year interval, a 30x30 m pixel was mapped as cropland if a growing crop was detected during any of these years. Cropland patches below 0.5 hectares were excluded from the final map. The cropland change refers to areas with cropland establishment (gain) and cropland abandonment or conversion to other land uses (loss) between 2000-2003 and 2016-2019 time intervals.

  
  
Global population growth and increasing standards of living inevitably cause the expansion and intensification of global agricultural land use to fulfill growing demands for food, biofuel, and other commodities. In turn, agriculture expansion and intensification threaten ecosystem functioning and lead to species extinction through habitat loss and fragmentation. The [United Nations 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)](https://www.undp.org/sustainable-development-goals) call for balancing increasing agricultural production with maintenance of ecosystem services. 

  
  
Implementation of SDG’s to improve food security, protect freshwater and terrestrial ecosystems, and mitigate climate change require national policies and international cooperation that are based on consistent, independent, and timely data on agriculture extent and productivity. The Cropland Extent and Change dataset can serve as a tool for monitoring national and global progress towards SDG’s.

  
  
The GLAD laboratory in the Department of Geographical Sciences at UMD investigates methods, causes and impacts of global land surface change.  Earth observation imagery are the primary data source and land cover extent and change the primary topic of interest. GLAD aspires to generate new science insights concerning land resources, educate the next generation of remote sensing-based land change scientists, and disseminate land monitoring capabilities to operational settings nationally and internationally.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
Cropland is defined as land used for the production of annual and perennial herbaceous crops for human consumption, forage (including hay), and biofuel. Perennial woody crops, permanent pastures, and shifting cultivation are excluded from the definition. The fallow length is limited to four years for the cropland class. The cropland class definition is largely consistent with the arable land category reported by the [Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations](https://www.fao.org/3/Y4171E/Y4171E20.htm).

  
  
The analysis was performed in four-year epochs, 2000-2003 and 2016-2019. One cropland map per epoch was created, named by the last year of the interval (e.g., the 2019 map represents the 2016-2019 epoch). Using a four-year interval (rather than a single year) increased the number of clear-sky satellite observations in the time-series, which improves the representation of land surface phenology and the accuracy of cropland detection. For each four-year interval, an area was mapped as cropland if a growing crop was detected during any of these years. This way, the criterion of the maximum fallow length was implemented: if an area was not used as cropland for more than four years, it was not included in the cropland map for the corresponding time interval.

  
  
The global 16-day normalized surface reflectance Landsat Analysis Ready Data (Landsat ARD) was employed as input data for cropland mapping [(Potapov et al., 2020)](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-4292/12/3/426). For each four-year interval, a single annualized gap-free 16-day observation time-series was created. For each 16-day interval, the observation with the highest near-infrared reflectance value was selected (to prioritize observations with the highest vegetation cover) from four years of Landsat data. The annualized 16-day time-series within each four-year interval was transformed into a set of multitemporal metrics that provide consistent land surface phenology inputs for global cropland mapping. Metrics include selected ranks, inter-rank averages, and amplitudes of surface reflectance and vegetation indices values, and surface reflectance averages for selected land surface phenology stages defined by vegetation indices (i.e., surface reflectance for the maximum and minimum greenness periods). The Landsat metrics were augmented with elevation data. 

  
  
Global cropland mapping included three stages that enabled extrapolation of visually delineated cropland training data to a temporally consistent global cropland map time-series using machine learning. At all three stages, a bagged decision tree ensembles were employed as a supervised classification algorithm that uses class presence and absence data as the dependent variable and a set of multitemporal metrics as independent variables at a Landsat ARD pixel scale. The first stage consisted of performing individual cropland classifications for a set of 924 Landsat ARD 1°×1° tiles for the 2016-2019 interval. The tiles were chosen to represent diverse global agriculture landscapes. Classification training data (cropland class presence and absence) were manually selected through visual interpretation of Landsat metric composites and high-resolution data from Google Earth. At the second stage, the 924 tiles that had been classified as cropland/other land and the 2016-2019 metric set were used to train a series of regional cropland mapping models. The classification was iterated by adding training tiles and assessing the results until the resulting map was satisfactory. At the third stage, the preliminary global cropland maps were used as training data to generate temporally consistent global cropland data. The goal of this third stage was to create a robust spatiotemporally consistent set of locally calibrated cropland detection models. For each 1°×1° Landsat ARD tile (13,451 tiles total) training data for each four-year interval was collected from the preliminary cropland extent maps within a 3° radius of the target tile, with preference to select stable cropland and non-cropland pixels as training. Training data from all intervals were used to calibrate a single decision tree ensemble for each ARD tile. The per-tile models were then applied to each time interval, and the results were post-processed to remove single cropland class detections and omissions within time-series and eliminate cropland patches below 0.5 ha. Manual masks to remove map artifacts (e.g., cropland overestimation over temperate wetlands and flooded grasslands) were applied in some regions to improve the final map.

For the full documentation, please click on the “Learn more” button.

info.technical_title: Global cropland extent and change, 2003-2019
info.functions: Cropland extent, loss and gain from 2000-2003 and 2016-2019
info.cautions:
- A probability-based sample analysis is the recommended good practice approach to estimating land cover and land use extent and change. The global land cover map time-series enables a higher sampling efficiency through stratification at the sub-national, national, and global scales. The maps should not be used as the only source data for national and international reporting due to unknown map uncertainty that may vary in space and between time intervals.
  
  
- Cropland maps have higher accuracy in regions dominated by large-scale industrial farming, e.g. North and South America. In Europe, Asia, and Africa, the global map may underestimate small-scale cropland areas due to Landsat spatial resolution limitations in mapping heterogeneous landscapes.
  
  
- Cropland class may be confused with the intensively managed permanent pastures as both classes have similar spectral response and phenology. This issue may cause an overestimation of cropland area in Australia, New Zealand, and parts of Western Europe.
  
  
- Dryland rainfed agriculture and summer wheat production areas, especially when intermittent with long fallow, may be partially omitted in Central Asia and the Middle East. The short vegetation season and the lack of cloud-free Landsat data in some years may preclude dryland agriculture detection.
  
  
- Croplands that were repeatedly abandoned and recultivated may be inconsistently mapped as cropland loss or gain.

attributes.name: Snow/Ice Change
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Snow/Ice Change dataset at 30 m spatial resolution was developed by the Global Land Analysis and Discovery Lab (GLAD) at the University of Maryland (UMD) using Landsat satellite data time-series. The map shows the extent of glaciers and perennial snowfields and their net change from the year 2000 to 2020. Areas with seasonal snow cover are excluded from the map. The map extent is limited to continents and large islands between 75°N and 56°S. Greenland, the Antarctic, and Arctic Islands are excluded from the map. Model calibration data were collected through the visual interpretation of Landsat and high spatial resolution satellite images. A set of regionally calibrated models were developed and implemented to map perennial snow and ice cover time-series. The snow/ice loss represents areas where the year 2000 perennial snow or ice cover was transformed into seasonal snow cover or completely disappeared by the year 2020. The gain areas represent the expansion of perennial snowfields and glaciers from the year 2000 to 2020.
  
  
The GLAD laboratory in the Department of Geographical Sciences at UMD investigates methods, causes, and impacts of global land surface change.  Earth observation imagery is the primary data source, and the land cover extent and change is the primary topic of interest. GLAD aspires to generate new science insights concerning land resources, educate the next generation of remote sensing-based land change scientists, and disseminate land monitoring capabilities to operational settings nationally and internationally.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
The GLAD laboratory mapped permanent snow and ice using regionally calibrated supervised classification models (decision tree ensembles). The classification model was calibrated with manually collected training data from multitemporal Landsat metrics [(Potapov et al., 2020)](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs12030426). They used the Landsat data from the years 2000, 2005, and 2020 for training data collection. For each year, they selected Landsat observations during the peak land surface temperature and peak vegetation index values to separate perennial and annual snow cover. The training data from different years were integrated and used to create a single regional model. Overall, they created fourteen regional models, one model per mountain system or a geographic region. The models were iterated until the results were sufficiently correct. The final product was filtered using a set of rules to remove noise in the time series and possible omission/commission due to the remaining cloud/cloud shadow contamination of Landsat data.
  
  
For the full documentation, please click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows datasets from the GLAD laboratory for [Cropland Extent](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/50634b51-ea2e-4cc1-9e4b-8f26a389a301), [Cropland Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/ec282483-4f5c-4fb8-ace7-8e557826781a), [Tree Height Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/64a3e126-000b-46fb-aaf4-8ac765a8263b), [Water Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/b83ad197-eb95-44e2-8ec3-3351ab926421), [Built-Up Area Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/e6a3f803-1222-46c2-8e6c-0ae94b3d80c8), and [Land Cover Map](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/06e734af-66f0-4c3e-ac71-1b99f3cbfe1d).
  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.

info.name: Snow/Ice Change
info.technical_title: Global glaciers and perennial snowfields extent and change, 2000-2020
info.functions: Global glaciers and perennial snowfields extent, loss, and gain from the year 2000 to 2020
info.cautions:
- A probability-based sample analysis is the recommended good practice approach to estimating land cover and land use extent and change. The global land cover map time-series enables a higher sampling efficiency through stratification at the sub-national, national, and global scales. The maps should not be used as the only source data for national and international reporting due to unknown map uncertainty that may vary in space and between time intervals.
  
  
- The model performance is compromised by the low radiometric resolution and observation frequency of Landsat TM and ETM+ data in the year 2000 compared to the Landsat ETM+ and OLI data in 2020. The year 2000 map overestimated the area of perennial snow and ice due to the inclusion of seasonal snow and classification errors within topographic shadows. As a result, the rate of snow and ice reduction from the year 2000 to 2020 is overestimated by the map. The areas of snow and ice gain and loss should be considered as indicator products. 
  
  
- The product quality depends on the availability of Landsat data during the hottest time of the year. The absence of cloud-free Landsat data during the hottest month may cause an overestimation of perennial snow cover. Small Arctic lakes can be classified as “permanent snow” if no cloud-free observations during the hottest time of the years were available for several years in a row. Confusion of snow/ice with clouds may compromise model performance in regions with persistent cloud cover.
  
  
- Dirt, soot, and volcanic ash on top of the glaciers may compromise their detection. This issue affected data near active volcanos in Iceland and Kamchatka and may compromise detection of melting glaciers covered with rocks and sand.
