attributes.name: ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைவீழ்ச்சியில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம்
attributes.description:
### கண்ணோட்டம்  
  
ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைவீழ்ச்சி தரவுத் தொகுப்பில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம் 1960-1990 இன் அடிப்படை காலத்துடன் ஒப்பிடும்போது, 2000 மற்றும் 2080 க்கு இடையில் பத்து ஆண்டு இடைவெளியில் வருடாந்திர சராசரி மொத்த மழைப்பொழிவில் ஏற்பட்ட மாற்றத்தைக் காட்டுகிறது. ஒவ்வொரு பத்து ஆண்டு இடைவெளியிலும் காட்டப்படும் தரவு 31 ஆண்டு சராசரியைக் குறிக்கிறது, இது குறிக்கப்பட்ட ஆண்டை மையமாகக் கொண்டது. எடுத்துக்காட்டாக, 2000 ஆம் ஆண்டில் மொத்த மழைப்பொழிவு உண்மையில் 1985 மற்றும் 2015 ஆண்டுகளுக்கு இடையில் ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைப்பொழிவின் சராசரியாகும். காலநிலை மாற்றம் (ஐபிசிசியின்) பிரதிநிதித்துவ செறிவு பாதைகள் (ஆர்.சி.பி) 8.5 இன் அரசாங்கங்களுக்கிடையிலான குழுவால் தீர்மானிக்கப்படும் எதிர்கால பசுமை இல்ல வாயு உமிழ்வு விகிதங்களை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டது மழைவீழ்ச்சி கணிப்புகள். ஆர்சிபி 8.5 என்பது 21 ஆம் நூற்றாண்டுக்குள் கிரீன்ஹவுஸ் வாயு உமிழ்வு விகிதங்களில் எந்த குறைவும் இல்லாத ஒரு கற்பனையான காட்சியாகும். ஒட்டுமொத்த சராசரி மழைப்பொழிவு திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றத்தை கணக்கிட அடிப்படை சராசரியால் வகுக்கப்படுகிறது. 1 ஐ விட அதிகமான மதிப்புகள் ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைப்பொழிவு அதிகரித்து வருவதைக் குறிக்கின்றன, அதே நேரத்தில் ஒன்றுக்கும் குறைவான மதிப்புகள் எண்ணிக்கை குறைந்து வருவதைக் குறிக்கின்றன. தரவு 0.25° இடஞ்சார்ந்த தெளிவுத்திறனில் வழங்கப்படுகிறது.
  
உலகளாவிய கிரீன்ஹவுஸ் வாயு செறிவுகளின் அதிகரிப்பும், அதன் விளைவாக காலநிலை மாற்றமும், விவசாயம், உள்கட்டமைப்பு, பேரழிவு மேலாண்மை மற்றும் மனித மோதலைப் பாதிக்கும் கிரகத்துடனான நமது உறவை அடிப்படையாக மாற்றியமைக்கும். இந்த மாற்றங்களை எதிர்பார்க்கவும், தகவமைத்துக் கொள்ளவும், ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைவீழ்ச்சி தரவுத்தொகுப்பில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம் வரவிருக்கும் தசாப்தங்களில் மழைவீழ்ச்சி வடிவங்கள் எவ்வாறு மாறக்கூடும் என்பதற்கான கணிப்புகளை வழங்குகிறது. மழைப்பொழிவு மாற்றங்கள் உலகம் முழுவதும் மிகவும் மாறுபட்டதாக இருக்கும் என்று கணிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது, பொதுவாக உயர்-அட்சரேகை பகுதிகளில் சராசரி மழைப்பொழிவு அதிகரிப்பு மற்றும் மிதவெப்ப மண்டல வறண்ட பகுதிகளில் ஒரு துருவ-வார்டு மாற்றம் ஆகியவற்றைக் காட்டுகிறது. கூடுதலாக, மழைப்பொழிவு குறைவான, ஆனால் மிகவும் தீவிரமான நிகழ்வுகளில் ஏற்படும் என்று கணிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. கணிசமான அளவு உலர்வதைக் காண எதிர்பார்க்கப்படும் சில பகுதிகளைத் தவிர, வரலாற்று ரீதியாக தீவிர மழை நிகழ்வுகள் உலகெங்கிலும் அடிக்கடி நிகழும் என்று எதிர்பார்க்கப்படுகிறது. மழைப்பொழிவு அதிகரிக்கும் போது கூட, வறண்ட காலங்கள் நீளம் மற்றும் அதிர்வெண் அதிகரிக்கும் என்று கணிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. 
  
இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பை Vizzuality மற்றும் உலக வளங்கள் நிறுவனம் மூலம் தேசிய ஏரோநாட்டிக்ஸ் மற்றும் விண்வெளி நிர்வாகம் (நாசா) எர்த் எக்ஸ்சேஞ்ச் குளோபல் டெய்லி டவுன்ஸ்கேல்ட் ப்ரொஜெக்ஷன்ஸ் (நெக்ஸ்-ஜி.டி.டி.பி) பயன்படுத்தி செயலாக்கியுள்ளது. நெக்ஸ்-ஜி.டி.டி.பி தரவுத்தொகுப்பு, உள்ளூர் முதல் பிராந்திய அளவிலான காலநிலை மாற்ற தாக்கங்கள் குறித்த ஆய்வுகளை நடத்துவதில் அறிவியல் சமூகத்திற்கு உதவுவதையும், தனிப்பட்ட நகரங்கள், நகரங்கள் மற்றும் நீர்ப்பிடிப்புப் பகுதிகளின் இடஞ்சார்ந்த அளவில் எதிர்கால உலகளாவிய காலநிலை வடிவங்கள் குறித்த பொது புரிதலை மேம்படுத்துவதையும் நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது. இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பின் முந்தைய பதிப்பு செயலாக்கப்பட்டு தயாரிக்கப்பட்டது [பின்னடைவு மற்றும் தயார்நிலைக்கான கூட்டாண்மை (பி.ஆர்.இ.பி)] (https://prepdata.org/), காலநிலை தரவுகளுக்கான அணுகலை மேம்படுத்துவதன் மூலம் காலநிலை மாற்றத்திற்கு பின்னடைவைக் கட்டியெழுப்புவதற்கான பி.ஆர்.இ.பி.யின் பணியில் உதவியது.  
  
### முறைமை  
  
ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைவீழ்ச்சி தரவுத்தொகுப்பில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம் நெக்ஸ்-ஜி.டி.டி.பி.யிலிருந்து மழை தரவுகளுடன் உருவாக்கப்பட்டது. நெக்ஸ்-ஜி.டி.டி.பி தரவுத் தொகுப்புகள் உலகளாவிய சுழற்சி மாதிரி (ஜி.சி.எம்) சோதனைகளிலிருந்து பெறப்பட்டன, அவை [காலநிலை மாற்றத்திற்கான அரசாங்கங்களுக்கு இடையிலான குழு (ஐபிசிசி) ஐந்தாவது மதிப்பீட்டு அறிக்கை (ஏஆர்5)] (https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/05/SYR_AR5_FINAL_full_wcover.pdf). இணைந்த மாதிரி இண்டர்கம்பரிசன் திட்டம் கட்டம் 5 (சிஎம்ஐபி5) என அழைக்கப்படும் இந்த சோதனைகள், கிரீன்ஹவுஸ் வாயு செறிவுகளின் பல்வேறு நிலைகளில் காலநிலையை உருவகப்படுத்த வடிவமைக்கப்பட்ட காலநிலை மாதிரிகளின் முடிவுகளை உள்ளடக்கியது.  

சி.எம்.ஐ.பி 5 தரவு மாதிரிகள் (45), காலநிலை காட்சிகள் (4), ஆண்டுகள் (150+), மற்றும் மாறிகள் (20-40) ஆகியவற்றை உள்ளடக்கியது. அதன் கரடுமுரடான தீர்மானத்தில் (1-4° ) கூட இது பில்லியன் கணக்கான அடுக்குகளில் விளைகிறது. டவுன்ஸ்கேலிங் மூலம், நெக்ஸ்-ஜி.டி.டி.பி அவர்கள் தேவைப்படும் தரவை மட்டுமே பிரித்தெடுக்கிறது மற்றும் [ஷெஃபீல்ட் மற்றும் பலர். (2006)] (https://journals.ametsoc.org/jcli/article/19/13/3088/30860/Development-இன்-ஒரு-50-ஆண்டு-உயர்-தெளிவுத்திறன்-உலகளாவிய) தரவுத்தொகுப்பை வரலாற்றுக் குறிப்புகளாகப் பயன்படுத்தி, தரவின் ஒட்டுமொத்த அளவையும் குறைக்கிறது.  

ஒவ்வொரு ஆண்டும் ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைப்பொழிவு, காலநிலை மாதிரி, மற்றும் சூழ்நிலை ஒரு பிக்சல் அடிப்படையில் நெக்ஸ்-ஜி.டி.டி.பி தரவைப் பயன்படுத்தி கணக்கிடப்பட்டது. இது ஒரு குறிப்பிட்ட ஆண்டில் அனைத்து தினசரி மழைவீழ்ச்சி தரவுகளையும் சேர்ப்பதன் மூலம் செய்யப்பட்டது. ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைவீழ்ச்சிகள் பின்னர் 1960-1990 அடிப்படை காலத்திற்கான 31 ஆண்டு சராசரிகளாக இணைக்கப்பட்டன மற்றும் 2000 முதல் 2080 வரை ஒவ்வொரு தசாப்தத்தின் தொடக்கத்திலும் ஒன்பது காலங்கள் மையப்படுத்தப்பட்டன. பின்னர் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட ஒன்பது தசாப்தங்களில் ஒவ்வொன்றும் ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைவீழ்ச்சியில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றத்தைக் கணக்கிட அடிப்படை சராசரியால் பிரிக்கப்பட்டன. 1 ஐ விட அதிகமான மதிப்புகள் ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைப்பொழிவு அதிகரித்து வருவதைக் குறிக்கின்றன, அதே நேரத்தில் ஒன்றுக்கும் குறைவான மதிப்புகள் ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைப்பொழிவு குறைந்து வருவதைக் குறிக்கின்றன.

ஒவ்வொரு பத்து ஆண்டு இடைவெளியிலும் காட்டப்படும் தரவு 31 ஆண்டு சராசரியைக் குறிக்கிறது, இது குறிக்கப்பட்ட ஆண்டை மையமாகக் கொண்டது. எடுத்துக்காட்டாக, 2000 ஆம் ஆண்டில் ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைப்பொழிவு 1985 மற்றும் 2015 ஆண்டுகளுக்கு இடையில் ஒட்டுமொத்த மழைப்பொழிவின் சராசரியாக கணக்கிடப்பட்டது. 31 ஆண்டு சராசரிகள் தேர்ந்தெடுக்கப்பட்டன, ஏனெனில் அவை வருடாந்திர மற்றும் தசாப்த மாறுபாட்டின் விளைவுகளைக் குறைத்து, நீண்ட கால காலநிலை சமிக்ஞையை முன்னிலைப்படுத்துகின்றன. உலக வானிலை அமைப்பின் நீண்டகால வழிகாட்டுதலுடன் ஒத்துப்போக அடிப்படை காலம் தேர்ந்தெடுக்கப்பட்டது.
  
### கூடுதல் தகவல்  
  
Resource Watch மேலும் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம் NEX-GDDP RCP 8.5 தரவு காட்டுகிறது [வருடாந்திர சராசரி வெப்பநிலையில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம்](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/4ca6826c-718d-457d-b4e2-e9277d7ed62c), [வருடாந்திர சராசரி குறைந்தபட்ச வெப்பநிலையில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம்](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/3d8e2e82-b33a-4898-90e5-6e4a1d007b82), [வருடாந்திர சராசரி அதிகபட்ச வெப்பநிலையில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம்](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/c4b12251-2d61-458f-4898-90e5-6e4a1d007b82), [வருடாந்திர சராசரி அதிகபட்ச வெப்பநிலையில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம்](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/c4b12251-2d61-458f-0007b82) வெப்பமாக்கும் டிகிரி நாட்களில் மாற்றம்](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/1d2f4eae-10e1-4ea6-980c-501b34106de2), [கூலிங் டிகிரி நாட்களில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம்](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/6fa000b5-8d91-46c8-8502-07427bc5eafc), [உறைபனி இல்லாத பருவத்தில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம்](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/d3f512c0-fbb0-47d5-9ac9-a452574c8e58), [தீவிர வெப்ப நாட்களில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம்](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/3941bbba-181b-434a-84cdf55) உலர் எழுத்துப்பிழைகளில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம்](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/d0f46576-411d-48aa-8df8-d89a3792cdce), [தீவிர மழைவீழ்ச்சி நாட்களில் திட்டமிடப்பட்ட மாற்றம்](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/66d28bbc-1e6e-4156-9ba2-875ecab665af).

Resource Watch தரவின் ஒரு துணைக்குழுவை மட்டுமே காட்டுகிறது. உமிழ்வு சூழ்நிலை RCP 4.5 க்கான கூடுதல் தரவு கிடைக்கிறது. அசல் NEX-GDDP தரவுத்தொகுப்பு மற்றும் கூடுதல் தகவலுக்கான அணுகலுக்கு, மேலும் அறிக இணைப்பைப் பார்க்கவும்.
  
### தரவை காட்சிப்படுத்தல்  
  
Resource Watch இல் காண்பிக்கப்படுவதற்கு முன்பு எங்கள் குழு இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பை மறுவடிவமைத்தது. [Github] (https://github.com/resource-வாட்ச்/தரவு-முன் செயலாக்கம்/மரம்/மாஸ்டர்/cli_050-059_066-075_nexgddp_and_loca) இல் உள்ள தரவை Resource Watch எவ்வாறு செயலாக்கியது என்பதற்கான ஆவணங்களைப் பார்க்கவும்.  
  
### பொறுப்புத்துறப்பு  
  
இந்த விளக்கப் பக்கத்தின் பகுதிகள் மூல மெட்டாடேட்டாவிலிருந்து எடுக்கப்பட்டன.

info.cautions:
- சில ஜி.சி.எம். மழைக்காலங்கள் போன்ற பிராந்திய காலநிலை வடிவங்களை மீண்டும் உருவாக்குவதில் மற்றவர்களை விட சிறப்பாக செயல்படுகிறது. குறிப்பிட்ட பயன்பாடுகளுக்கு, பிராந்திய செயல்திறன் அடிப்படையில் தனிப்பட்ட மாதிரிகளைத் தேர்ந்தெடுப்பது பொருத்தமானதாக இருக்கலாம்.
- இந்த குறிகாட்டிகளை உருவாக்கப் பயன்படுத்தப்படும் கீழ்நோக்கிய அணுகுமுறைகள், வெப்பநிலை மற்றும் மழைவீழ்ச்சியில் உள்ள ஒப்பீட்டு இடஞ்சார்ந்த வடிவங்கள் எதிர்கால காலநிலை மாற்றத்தின் கீழ் மாறாமல் இருக்கும் என்று இயல்பாகவே கருதுகின்றன. முக்கிய காற்று மற்றும் கடல் நீரோட்டங்கள் மெதுவாக அல்லது தலைகீழாக மாறுவது போன்ற உலகளாவிய வானிலை வடிவங்களில் வியத்தகு மாற்றங்கள் சாத்தியமாகும், ஆனால் இந்த குறிகாட்டிகளில் பிடிக்கப்படாது.
- கீழிறக்கத்திற்குப் பயன்படுத்தப்படும் வரலாற்றுத் தரவுகள் உலகெங்கிலும் தரத்தில் வேறுபடுகின்றன. குறிப்பாக, குறுகிய பதிவுகள் அல்லது வானிலை அவதானிப்புகளின் குறைவான கவரேஜ் கொண்ட பகுதிகள் துல்லியத்தைக் குறைத்திருக்கலாம்.
- ஜி.சி.எம் சுயாதீன ஆராய்ச்சிக் குழுக்களால் உருவாக்கப்பட்டு, வெவ்வேறு அனுமானங்கள் மற்றும் வழிமுறைகளை உள்ளடக்கியிருப்பதால், அவை கணிசமான அளவிலான எதிர்காலங்களை உள்ளடக்கியிருக்கலாம். நாங்கள் குறைந்த மற்றும் உயர் மதிப்பீடுகளை வழங்குகிறோம், இதனால் பயனர்கள் இந்த சாத்தியமான அளவிலான விளைவுகளைப் பார்க்கவும் மதிப்பிடவும் முடியும்.

"காலநிலை தரவை அணுகக்கூடியதாக ஆக்குதல்: நெக்ஸ்-ஜி.டி.டி.பி மற்றும் எல்.ஓ.சி.ஏ கீழ்மட்ட காலநிலை குறிகாட்டிகளை உற்பத்தி செய்வதற்கான முறைகள்" தொழில்நுட்ப குறிப்பு. வாஷிங்டன், டி.சி: வேர்ல்ட் ரிசோர்சஸ் இன்ஸ்டிடியூட். https://www.wri.org/research/making-climate-data-accessible ஆன்லைனில் கிடைக்கிறது. [www.resourcewatch.org] (https://www.resourcewatch.org/).

சி.எம்.ஐ.பி.க்கு பொறுப்பான உலக காலநிலை ஆராய்ச்சித் திட்டத்தின் ஒருங்கிணைந்த மாடலிங் பணிக் குழுவை நாங்கள் அங்கீகரிக்கிறோம், மேலும் அவற்றின் மாதிரி வெளியீட்டை உற்பத்தி செய்து கிடைக்கச் செய்த காலநிலை மாடலிங் குழுக்களுக்கு நாங்கள் நன்றி தெரிவிக்கிறோம். அமெரிக்க எரிசக்தித் துறையின் காலநிலை மாதிரி நோய் கண்டறிதல் மற்றும் இண்டர்கம்பரிசன் திட்டம் சிஎம்ஐபிக்கான புவி அமைப்பு அறிவியல் போர்ட்டல்களுக்கான உலகளாவிய அமைப்புடன் இணைந்து மென்பொருள் உள்கட்டமைப்பின் ஒருங்கிணைப்பு ஆதரவு மற்றும் மேம்பாட்டை வழங்குகிறது.

பயன்படுத்தப்படும் காலநிலை காட்சிகள் நெக்ஸ்-ஜி.டி.டி.பி தரவுத்தொகுப்பில் இருந்து வந்தன, இது காலநிலை பகுப்பாய்வு குழு மற்றும் நாசா அமேஸ் ஆராய்ச்சி மையத்தால் நாசா எர்த் எக்ஸ்சேஞ்சைப் பயன்படுத்தி தயாரிக்கப்பட்டது, மேலும் காலநிலை உருவகப்படுத்துதலுக்கான நாசா மையத்தால் (என்.சி.சி.எஸ்) விநியோகிக்கப்பட்டது.
info.date_of_content: 1960-1990 இன் அடிப்படைக் காலம் மற்றும் 2000 முதல் 2080 வரையிலான ஒவ்வொரு தசாப்தத்திற்கும் எதிர்பார்க்கப்படும் பெறுமதிகள்

attributes.name: సంచిత అవపాతంలో ఊహించిన మార్పు
attributes.description:
### అవలోకనం  
  
క్యుమిలేటివ్ అవపాత డేటాసెట్ లో ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ ఛేంజ్ 1960-1990 యొక్క బేస్ లైన్ కాల వ్యవధితో పోలిస్తే 2000 మరియు 2080 మధ్య పది సంవత్సరాల విరామాల వద్ద వార్షిక సగటు మొత్తం అవపాతంలో మార్పును చూపుతుంది. ప్రతి పది సంవత్సరాల విరామం వద్ద చూపించబడ్డ డేటా 31 సంవత్సరాల సగటుకు ప్రాతినిధ్యం వహిస్తుంది, ఇది సూచించబడ్డ సంవత్సరం చుట్టూ కేంద్రీకృతమై ఉంటుంది. ఉదాహరణకు, 2000 లో మొత్తం అవపాతం వాస్తవానికి 1985 మరియు 2015 సంవత్సరాల మధ్య సంచిత అవపాతం యొక్క సగటు. వాతావరణ మార్పులపై ఇంటర్ గవర్నమెంటల్ ప్యానెల్ (ఐపిసిసి యొక్క) ప్రతినిధి ఏకాగ్రత మార్గాలు (ఆర్ సిపి) 8.5 ద్వారా నిర్ణయించబడ్డ భవిష్యత్ గ్రీన్ హౌస్ వాయువు ఉద్గార రేట్లపై అవపాత అంచనాలు ఆధారపడి ఉంటాయి. ఆర్ సిపి 8.5 అనేది 21వ శతాబ్దంలో గ్రీన్ హౌస్ వాయువుల ఉద్గార రేట్లు ఏమాత్రం తగ్గని ఒక ఊహాజనిత దృశ్యం. క్యుమిలేటివ్ సరాసరి అవపాతం బేస్ లైన్ సగటుతో భాగించబడుతుంది, ఇది అంచనా వేయబడ్డ మార్పును లెక్కించడానికి. 1 కంటే ఎక్కువ విలువలు సంచిత అవపాతం పెరుగుతున్నట్లు సూచిస్తాయి, అయితే ఒకటి కంటే తక్కువ విలువలు సంఖ్య తగ్గుతున్నట్లు సూచిస్తాయి. డేటా 0.25° ప్రాదేశిక రిజల్యూషన్ వద్ద ప్రజంట్ చేయబడుతుంది.
  
గ్లోబల్ గ్రీన్హౌస్ వాయువుల సాంద్రతలు పెరగడం, ఫలితంగా వాతావరణంలో మార్పు, వ్యవసాయం, మౌలిక సదుపాయాలు, విపత్తు నిర్వహణ మరియు మానవ సంఘర్షణను ప్రభావితం చేస్తూ, గ్రహంతో మన సంబంధాన్ని ప్రాథమికంగా మార్చడానికి సెట్ చేయబడింది. ఈ మార్పులను ఊహించడానికి మరియు స్వీకరించడానికి, క్యుమిలేటివ్ అవపాతం డేటాసెట్ లో ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ చేంజ్ రాబోయే దశాబ్దాల్లో అవపాత నమూనాలు ఎలా మారే అవకాశం ఉందనే దానిపై అంచనాలను అందిస్తుంది. అవపాత మార్పులు ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా మరింత వైవిధ్యంగా ఉంటాయని అంచనా వేయబడింది, సాధారణంగా అధిక-అక్షాంశ ప్రాంతాలలో సగటు అవపాతంలో పెరుగుదలను మరియు ఉపఉష్ణమండల శుష్క ప్రాంతాల పోల్-వార్డ్ షిఫ్ట్ ను చూపిస్తుంది. అదనంగా, అవపాతం తక్కువ, కానీ మరింత తీవ్రమైన సంఘటనలలో సంభవిస్తుందని అంచనా వేయబడింది. గణనీయమైన ఎండబెట్టడం చూడవచ్చని అంచనా వేయబడిన కొన్ని ప్రాంతాలలో తప్ప, చారిత్రాత్మకంగా విపరీతమైన అవపాత సంఘటనలు ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా మరింత తరచుగా ఉంటాయని భావిస్తున్నారు. అవపాతం పెరిగినప్పటికీ, పొడి కాలాలు పొడవు మరియు పౌనఃపున్యంలో పెరుగుతాయని అంచనా వేయబడింది. 
  
నేషనల్ ఏరోనాటిక్స్ అండ్ స్పేస్ అడ్మినిస్ట్రేషన్ (నాసా) ఎర్త్ ఎక్స్ఛేంజ్ గ్లోబల్ డైలీ డౌన్ స్కేల్డ్ ప్రొజెక్షన్స్ (నెక్స్-జిడిడిపి) ను ఉపయోగించి విజ్జువాలిటీ మరియు వరల్డ్ రిసోర్సెస్ ఇనిస్టిట్యూట్ ద్వారా ఈ డేటాసెట్ ప్రాసెస్ చేయబడింది. ఎన్ ఈఎక్స్-జిడిడిపి డేటాసెట్ అనేది స్థానిక మరియు ప్రాంతీయ స్థాయిల వద్ద వాతావరణ మార్పు ప్రభావాల యొక్క అధ్యయనాలను నిర్వహించడంలో శాస్త్రీయ సమాజానికి సహాయపడటానికి మరియు వ్యక్తిగత పట్టణాలు, నగరాలు మరియు వాటర్ షెడ్ ల ప్రాదేశిక స్థాయిలో భవిష్యత్తు ప్రపంచ వాతావరణ నమూనాలపై ప్రజా అవగాహనను పెంపొందించడానికి ఉద్దేశించబడింది. ఈ డేటాసెట్ యొక్క మునుపటి వెర్షన్ [పార్టనర్ షిప్ ఫర్ రెజిలియెన్స్ అండ్ ప్రిపేర్డ్ నెస్ (ప్రెప్)]](https://prepdata.org/) ద్వారా ప్రాసెస్ చేయబడింది మరియు ఉత్పత్తి చేయబడింది, ఇది వాతావరణ డేటాకు ప్రాప్యతను మెరుగుపరచడం ద్వారా వాతావరణ మార్పులకు స్థితిస్థాపకతను నిర్మించడానికి పి.ఆర్.ఇ.పి యొక్క మిషన్ కు సహాయపడుతుంది.  
  
#### మెథడాలజీ  
  
క్యుమిలేటివ్ అవపాతం డేటాసెట్ లో ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ చేంజ్ ఎన్ ఈఎక్స్-జిడిడిపి నుండి అవపాత డేటాతో రూపొందించబడింది. ఎన్ ఈఎక్స్-జిడిడిపి డేటాసెట్ లు గ్లోబల్ సర్క్యులేషన్ మోడల్ (జిసిఎమ్) ప్రయోగాల నుండి తీసుకోబడ్డాయి, ఇవి [ఇంటర్ గవర్నమెంటల్ ప్యానెల్ ఆన్ క్లైమేట్ చేంజ్ (ఐపిసిసి) ఐదవ అసెస్ మెంట్ రిపోర్ట్ (ఎఆర్ 5)] (https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/05/SYR_AR5_FINAL_full_wcover.pdf) కొరకు ఉత్పత్తి చేయబడ్డాయి. కపుల్డ్ మోడల్ ఇంటర్ కంపారిసన్ ప్రాజెక్ట్ ఫేజ్ 5 (సిఎమ్ ఐపి5) గా పిలువబడే ఈ ప్రయోగాల్లో గ్రీన్ హౌస్ వాయువు సాంద్రతల యొక్క వివిధ స్థాయిల కింద శీతోష్ణస్థితిని అనుకరించడానికి రూపొందించిన వాతావరణ నమూనాల నుండి ఫలితాలు ఉన్నాయి.  

సిఎమ్ఐపి5 డేటాలో పెద్ద సంఖ్యలో మోడల్స్ (45), క్లైమేట్ దృష్టాంతాలు (4), సంవత్సరాలు (150+), మరియు వేరియబుల్స్ (20-40) ఉన్నాయి. దాని ముతక రిజల్యూషన్ (1-4°) వద్ద కూడా ఇది బిలియన్ల కొద్దీ పొరలకు దారితీస్తుంది. డౌన్ స్కేలింగ్ ద్వారా, నెక్స్-జిడిడిపి తమకు అవసరమైన డేటాను మాత్రమే సంగ్రహిస్తుంది మరియు [షెఫీల్డ్ ఎట్ అల్. (2006)] (https://journals.ametsoc.org/jcli/article/19/13/3088/30860/Development-ఆఫ్-ఎ-50-ఇయర్-హై-రిజల్యూషన్-గ్లోబల్) డేటాసెట్ ను చారిత్రాత్మక రిఫరెన్స్ గా ఉపయోగించి డేటా యొక్క మొత్తం పరిమాణాన్ని తగ్గిస్తుంది.  

ప్రతి సంవత్సరం సంచిత అవపాతం, వాతావరణ నమూనా, మరియు దృష్టాంతం ప్రతి-పిక్సెల్ ప్రాతిపదికన నెక్స్-జిడిడిపి డేటాను ఉపయోగించి లెక్కించబడ్డాయి. ఇవ్వబడ్డ సంవత్సరంలో రోజువారీ అవపాత డేటా మొత్తం జోడించడం ద్వారా ఇది చేయబడింది. సంచిత అవపాతాలు తరువాత 1960-1990 బేస్ లైన్ కాలానికి 31-సంవత్సరాల సగటులుగా మరియు 2000 నుండి 2080 వరకు ప్రతి దశాబ్దం ప్రారంభంలో కేంద్రీకృతమైన తొమ్మిది కాలాలుగా కలపబడ్డాయి. అప్పుడు క్యుమిలేటివ్ అవపాతంలో అంచనా వేయబడిన మార్పును లెక్కించడానికి తొమ్మిది అంచనా వేయబడిన దశాబ్దాలలో ప్రతి ఒక్కటి బేస్ లైన్ సగటుతో భాగించబడ్డాయి. 1 కంటే ఎక్కువ విలువలు సంచిత అవపాతం పెరుగుతున్నట్లు సూచిస్తాయి, ఒకటి కంటే తక్కువ విలువలు సంచిత అవపాతం తగ్గుతున్నట్లు సూచిస్తున్నాయి.

ప్రతి పది సంవత్సరాల విరామం వద్ద చూపించబడ్డ డేటా 31 సంవత్సరాల సగటుకు ప్రాతినిధ్యం వహిస్తుంది, ఇది సూచించబడ్డ సంవత్సరం చుట్టూ కేంద్రీకృతమై ఉంటుంది. ఉదాహరణకు, 2000లో సంచిత అవపాతం 1985 మరియు 2015 సంవత్సరాల మధ్య సంచిత అవపాతం యొక్క సగటుగా లెక్కించబడింది. 31-సంవత్సరాల సగటులు ఎంచుకోబడ్డాయి ఎందుకంటే అవి వార్షిక మరియు దశాబ్ధ వైవిధ్యం యొక్క ప్రభావాలను కనిష్టం చేస్తాయి మరియు దీర్ఘకాలిక వాతావరణ సంకేతాన్ని హైలైట్ చేస్తాయి. ప్రపంచ వాతావరణ సంఘం నుండి దీర్ఘకాలిక మార్గదర్శకత్వంతో సమలేఖనం చేయడానికి బేస్ లైన్ కాలం ఎంచుకోబడింది.
  
### అదనపు సమాచారం  
  
రిసోర్స్ వాచ్ [వార్షిక సగటు ఉష్ణోగ్రతలో ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ చేంజ్](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/4ca6826c-718d-457d-b4e2-e9277d7d7ed62c), [వార్షిక సగటు కనిష్ట ఉష్ణోగ్రతలో అంచనా వేయబడ్డ మార్పు](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/3d8e2e82-b33a-4898-90e5-6e4a1d007b82 కొరకు ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ ఛేంజ్ NEX-GDDP RCP 8.5 డేటాను కూడా చూపిస్తుంది.[https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/c4b12251-2d61-458f-718d-457d-457d-457d-457d-457d-457d-457d-457d-457d-457d-457d-b4e2c కొరకు ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ ఛేంజ్ NEX-GDDP RCP 8.5 డేటాను కూడా రిసోర్స్ వాచ్ చూపిస్తుంది, [వార్షిక సగటు ఉష్ణోగ్రతలో ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ ఛేంజ్](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/3d8e2e82-b33a-4898-90e5-6e4a1d007b82లో ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ ఛేంజ్ హీటింగ్ డిగ్రీ డేస్ లో మార్పు](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/1d2f4eae-10e1-4ఈ6-980c-501b34106de2), [కూలింగ్ డిగ్రీ డేస్ లో ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ చేంజ్](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/6fa000b5-8d91-46c8-8502-07427bc5eafc), [ఫ్రాస్ట్ ఫ్రీ సీజన్ లో ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ ఛేంజ్](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/d3f512c0-fbb0-47d5-9ac9-a452574c8e58), [ఎక్స్ ట్రీమ్ హీట్ డేస్ లో ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ ఛేంజ్](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/3941bbba-181b-4800 డ్రై స్పెల్స్ లో ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ ఛేంజ్](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/d0f46576-411d-48aa-8df8-d89a3792cdce), [ఎక్స్ ట్రీమ్ అవపాత రోజుల్లో ప్రొజెక్టెడ్ ఛేంజ్](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/66d28bbc-1e6e-4156-9ba2-875ecab665af).

రిసోర్స్ వాచ్ డేటా యొక్క ఒక ఉపసమితిని మాత్రమే చూపుతుంది. ఉద్గారాల సందర్భం RCP 4.5 కొరకు అదనపు డేటా లభ్యం అవుతుంది. ఒరిజినల్ NEX-GDDP డేటాసెట్ మరియు అదనపు సమాచారాన్ని యాక్సెస్ చేసుకోవడానికి, లెర్న్ మోర్ లింక్ చూడండి.
  
### డేటాను విజువలైజ్ చేయడం  
  
రిసోర్స్ వాచ్ లో ప్రదర్శించడానికి ముందు మా టీమ్ ఈ డేటాసెట్ ని రీఫార్మాట్ చేసింది. రిసోర్స్ వాచ్ [Github](https://github.com/resource-వాచ్/డేటా-ప్రీ-ప్రాసెసింగ్/ట్రీ/మాస్టర్/cli_050-059_066-075_nexgddp_and_loca)పై డేటాను ఏవిధంగా ప్రాసెస్ చేసిందనే దానిపై డాక్యుమెంటేషన్ ని చూడండి.  
  
### డిస్ క్లెయిమర్  
  
ఈ వివరణ పేజీ యొక్క సారాంశాలు మూల మెటాడేటా నుండి తీసుకోబడ్డాయి.

info.name: సంచిత అవపాతంలో ఊహించిన మార్పు
info.technical_title: నాసా ఎర్త్ ఎక్స్ఛేంజ్ గ్లోబల్ డైలీ డౌన్ స్కేల్డ్ ప్రొజెక్షన్స్ (నెక్స్-జిడిడిపి) నుండి ఉత్పన్నమైన క్యుమిలేటివ్ అవపాతం
info.functions: వార్షిక సంచిత అవపాతంలో అంచనా వేయబడ్డ మార్పు
info.cautions:
- కొన్ని జిసిఎమ్ లు హిండ్ కాస్ట్ ల్లో రుతుపవనాలు వంటి ప్రాంతీయ వాతావరణ నమూనాలను పునఃసృష్టించడంలో ఇతరుల కంటే మెరుగ్గా పనిచేస్తాయి. నిర్దిష్ట అనువర్తనాల కొరకు, ప్రాంతీయ పనితీరు ఆధారంగా వ్యక్తిగత నమూనాలను ఎంచుకోవడం సముచితంగా ఉండవచ్చు.
- ఈ సూచికలను ఉత్పత్తి చేయడానికి ఉపయోగించే డౌన్ స్కేలింగ్ విధానాలు సహజంగానే ఉష్ణోగ్రత మరియు అవపాతంలో సాపేక్ష ప్రాదేశిక నమూనాలు భవిష్యత్తు వాతావరణ మార్పులలో స్థిరంగా ఉంటాయని ఊహిస్తాయి. ప్రధాన గాలి మరియు సముద్ర ప్రవాహాలు మందగించడం లేదా తిరోగమనం చెందడం వంటి ప్రపంచ వాతావరణ నమూనాలలో నాటకీయ మార్పులు సాధ్యమే, కానీ ఈ సూచికలలో సంగ్రహించబడవు.
- డౌన్ స్కేలింగ్ కోసం ఉపయోగించే చారిత్రక డేటా ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా నాణ్యతలో మారుతుంది. ప్రత్యేకించి, చిన్న రికార్డులు లేదా సిటు వాతావరణ పరిశీలనల యొక్క తక్కువ కవరేజీ ఉన్న ప్రాంతాలు కచ్చితత్త్వాన్ని తగ్గించి ఉండవచ్చు.
- జిసిఎమ్ స్వతంత్ర పరిశోధనా బృందాలచే అభివృద్ధి చేయబడి, విభిన్న ఊహలు మరియు యంత్రాంగాలను కలిగి ఉన్నందున, అవి సంభావ్య భవిష్యత్తు యొక్క గణనీయమైన శ్రేణిని కవర్ చేసే అవకాశం ఉంది. మేము తక్కువ మరియు అధిక అంచనాలు రెండింటినీ అందిస్తాము, తద్వారా వినియోగదారులు ఈ సంభావ్య శ్రేణి ఫలితాలను చూడవచ్చు మరియు మదింపు చేయవచ్చు.
info.citation:
గాస్సెర్ట్, ఎఫ్., ఇ. కార్నెజో, మరియు ఇ. నీల్సన్. 2021. "మేకింగ్ క్లైమేట్ డేటా యాక్సెసబుల్: మెథడ్స్ ఫర్ ప్రొడ్యూసింగ్ నెక్స్-జిడిడిపి అండ్ ఎల్ఓసిఎ డౌన్ స్కేల్డ్ క్లైమేట్ ఇండికేటర్స్" టెక్నికల్ నోట్. వాషింగ్టన్, డిసి: వరల్డ్ రిసోర్సెస్ ఇన్స్టిట్యూట్. https://www.wri.org/research/making-climate-data-accessible వద్ద ఆన్ లైన్ లో లభ్యం అవుతుంది. [www.resourcewatch.org] (https://www.resourcewatch.org/).

సిఎమ్ ఐపికి బాధ్యత వహించే కపుల్డ్ మోడలింగ్ పై వరల్డ్ క్లైమేట్ రీసెర్చ్ ప్రోగ్రామ్ యొక్క వర్కింగ్ గ్రూప్ కు మేం అభినందనలు తెలియజేస్తున్నాం, మరియు వారి మోడల్ అవుట్ పుట్ ని ఉత్పత్తి చేయడం మరియు లభ్యం చేయడం కొరకు క్లైమేట్ మోడలింగ్ గ్రూపులకు మేం ధన్యవాదాలు తెలియజేస్తున్నాం. యు.ఎస్. డిపార్ట్ మెంట్ ఆఫ్ ఎనర్జీ యొక్క ప్రోగ్రామ్ ఫర్ క్లైమేట్ మోడల్ డయాగ్నోస్టిక్స్ అండ్ ఇంటర్ కంపారిసన్ సిఎమ్ ఐపి కొరకు గ్లోబల్ ఆర్గనైజేషన్ ఫర్ ఎర్త్ సిస్టమ్ సైన్స్ పోర్టల్స్ భాగస్వామ్యంతో సాఫ్ట్ వేర్ ఇన్ ఫ్రాస్ట్రక్చర్ యొక్క కో ఆర్డినేటింగ్ సపోర్ట్ మరియు డెవలప్ మెంట్ ని అందిస్తుంది.

attributes.name: Burned Areas
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Burned Areas dataset shows areas that have experienced fire events in near real-time. The dataset provides the approximate date in which the burning occurred for each of the 500 meter (m) grid cells. Data is available starting in November 2000 and is updated on a monthly basis. 
  
  

[According to the United States Geological Survey (USGS)](https://www.usgs.gov/land-resources/nli/landsat/landsat-burned-area?qt-science_support_page_related_con=0#qt-science_support_page_related_con), data on burned areas is needed to characterize drivers of fire occurrence, project future fire behavior, and help with assessments of fire impacts on both natural and social systems.
  
  

The dataset was created by the USGS using satellite imagery. The final product has a resolution of 500 m.  
  
### Methodology  
  
The Burned Areas dataset was produced and is continually updated by combining data from both 500 m Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) Surface Reflectance imagery and 1 kilometer (km) MODIS active fire observations. This hybrid algorithm uses a burn-sensitive vegetation index derived from MODIS short-wave infrared bands 5 and 7. In addition, the active fire maps are used to guide the selection of burned and unburned training samples. 
  
  

If a grid cell has been marked as burned, the dataset identifies the date when the burn occurred within that cell. The dataset also includes special values for missing data, unburned cells, and water grid cells. 
  
  

For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/documents/114/MCD64_User_Guide_V6.pdf).  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. Additional information on the uncertainty of burn date data, quality assurance indicators, and the first and last days of the burn for each burned area can be found in the original source data. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click the “Learn more” button.   
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. The original dataset contained burned, unburned, and water grid cells. Only burned area grid cells are displayed on Resource Watch.  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

attributes.name: Global Surface Water Extent
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
This dataset displays the global location and temporal distribution of water surfaces from 1984 to 2018 at a spatial resolution of 30 meters. 
  
  
 The dataset includes individual layers of water occurrence, occurrence change intensity, seasonality, recurrence, and maximum water extent. Water occurrence is the frequency in which water was present on the surface. Occurrence change intensity shows where surface water occurrence increased, decreased or remained the same across the 35 years. Seasonality suggests the difference between permanent and seasonal water and the number of months water was present. Recurrence displays the changes in surface water classes. Maximum water extent provides information on all the locations ever detected as water over the 35 year period. 

  
  
The dataset was created using a combination of Landsat 5, 7, and 8 satellite imagery that was analyzed using a variety of information extraction techniques. The dataset was tested and found to have less than 1% error. 

  
  
Surface water affects the exchange of heat, gas, and water vapor between the earth’s surface and atmosphere. Water is essential for plants, animals, and human activities. The dataset was commissioned by the European Commission’s Joint Research Center to support water resource management, climate modeling, biodiversity conservation, and food security. Understanding Earth’s water will continue to grow in importance as world temperature and human population rises.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
This dataset used a combination of Landsat satellite imagery. Data from Landsat 5 Thematic Mapper, Landsat 7 Enhanced Thematic Mapper-plus, and Landsat 8 Operational Land Imager were analyzed for the period of  1984 to 2018. The satellite imagery was corrected for top-of-atmosphere reflectance and brightness temperature images. Information from the Global Human Settlement Data Layer (GHSL) was used to determine the location of buildings and correct the final map for interference from their shadows.
 
  
  
Due to the difficulty of using satellite imagery to detect water across geography and temporality, researchers used big data exploration and information extraction techniques to analyze the remote imaging data.  Researchers largely relied on a series of expert systems, visual analytics, and evidential reasoning. The expert system classified each image pixel into one of three categories: water, land, or non-valid observations (unusable data). It used both multispectral and multitemporal attributes from Landsat images and was created using a string of If-Then rules to create a reliable line of reasoning. . Visual analytics were used to verify the accuracy of the categories determined in the expert system and to create an equation to help describe pixel clusters of different categories. Lastly, evidential reasoning assisted in guiding class assignments in the expert system. It used geographic location and temporal trajectory to delineate boundaries of often misinterpreted areas, like glaciers and lava flows.
 
  
  
The final dataset was created using raster format at a spatial resolution of 30 meters.
  
  


For the full documentation about calculation for individual layers, please see the source [publication](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature20584).   
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch.  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

info.name: Global Surface Water Extent

sources.source-description: European Commission Joint Research Centre (EC JRC)

info.technical_title: Global Surface Water 1984-2018
info.functions: Location and temporal distribution of water surfaces from 1984 to 2018
info.cautions:
- The accuracy of the dataset was calculated using over 40,000 control points from around the world and across the 32 years. The validation results show that the water detection expert system produced less than 1%  false water detections and less than 5% of water surfaces were missed.

- Known omissions include bodies of water smaller than 30m by 30m, those obscured by floating, overhanging and standing vegetation or hidden by infrastructure such as bridges. There are also issues with Irrigated fields that stand in open water and paddy fields on steep terrain. 

- The first year of observation is 1984, except the Siberian plateau and Kolyma (1999 & 1995). Users should interpret changes in these regions with caution. 

- High latitudes in the Northern Hemisphere have shorter observation periods due to long hours of darkness during winter months. Changes in water cover are accurate, but are shown much more abruptly. 

- Melt ponds and streams on the surface of glaciers are identified as permanent water surfaces, but this permanence is questionable. 

- The recurrence value may be overestimated for water surfaces that came into existence in the last few years of the time series.

- Some isolated commission errors are present in urban areas. Roofs, coal and waste heaps, and runways are the most common sources of confusion.

  
  
Additional known issues and planned improvements of the dataset can be found in this [publication](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature20584).

attributes.name: cit.035d.nrt Air Quality - Satellite Measurements - TROPOMI (O₃)
Air Quality: Ozone (O₃) Satellite Measurements
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Air Quality: O₃ Satellite Measurements dataset provides global monthly averages of ozone (O₃) densities in the total atmospheric column. Each value shown in the dataset represents the density of O₃ found between Earth’s surface and the top of the atmosphere. The O₃ density is reported with units of moles of O₃ per square meter of air (mol/m²).

  
  
Unlike stratospheric ozone, which forms naturally in the upper atmosphere and protects us from the sun's harmful ultraviolet rays, ground-level (or tropospheric) ozone is created through the interactions of man-made (and natural) emissions of volatile organic compounds and nitrogen oxides in the presence of heat and sunlight. Cars and gasoline-burning engines are large sources of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). VOCs also come from consumer products such as paints, insecticides, and cleaners as well as industrial solvents and chemical manufacturing. High concentrations of ozone near ground level can be harmful to people, animals, crops, and other materials. Ozone can irritate the respiratory system, causing coughing and irritation. Ozone can aggravate pre existing respiratory problems like asthma, emphysema, and bronchitis and reduce the immune system's ability to fight off infections. Additionally, it can inflame and damage cells that line the lungs. It is possible for ozone to cause irreparable lung damage. These effects can be worse in children and exercising adults.

  
  
The dataset is made up of data collected from the Sentinel-5 Precursor (S5p) mission, a low Earth orbit polar satellite system.The S5p mission is part of the Global Monitoring of the Environment and Security (GMES/COPERNICUS) space component program headed by the European Commission (EC) in partnership with the European Space Agency (ESA). Its goal is to  provide information and services on air quality, climate, and the ozone layer. The S5p mission includes the TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI), which takes daily global observations of key atmospheric components, such as O₃, at a 5.5 x 3.5 kilometer (km) resolution.

  
  
Resource Watch also shows TROPOMI data for [nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/Air-Quality-Measurements-TROPOMI-NO),  [carbon monoxide (CO)] (https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/Air-Quality-Measurements-TROPOMI-CO), and [absorbing aerosol index (AAI)] (https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/Air-Quality-Measurements-TROPOMI-AER-AI).
  
  
### Methodology  
  
The TROPOMI O₃ dataset was created with data collected by the S5P satellite mission. O₃ data was collected by determining the amount of radiation reflected by the troposphere in the UV Huggins bands (325-335 nanometers) spectral range of the solar spectrum. A spectral range is the range of light wavelengths that a specific spectrometer can measure and in this case it refers to the wavelength of light that O₃ molecules produce in the atmosphere. The O₃ data collected using this method was then input into the GODFIT (GOME Direct-FITting) algorithm, created by the European Space Agency. Along with O₃ data, the following information was input into GODFIT:

  
  
- Relative profile of O₃ and sulfur dioxide (SO₂) in the atmosphere for a given region
  
  
- Estimated surface albedo for the region 
  
  
- Solar/viewing geometry and geo-location of the S5P satellite
  
  
- Surface pressure, elevation map, snow and ice maps for the earth’s surface, ozone temperature, cloud cover/pressure profiles, and the absorbing aerosol index for the tropospheric column being measured

  
  
SO₂ profiles were required as SO₂ converts to sulfuric acid in the atmosphere and blocks incoming solar radiation. This interferes with O₃ readings by TROPOMI. The results from GODFIT were analyzed with the convective-cloud-differential method (CCD) combined with cloud measurement data to produce the final dataset. The final result produced was vertical total column density of O₃ (mol/m²).

  
  
The dataset shown on Resource Watch was mapped by the Google Earth Engine team using the [harpconvert] (https://cdn.rawgit.com/stcorp/harp/master/doc/html/harpconvert.html) tool. For more information on this conversion please see the Google Earth Engine documentation. The offline version of this data is displayed on Resource Watch, which is more complete than its near real-time counterpart, but is released on a greater delay due to the additional processing time needed. For the full documentation, please see the [source methodology](https://sentinel.esa.int/web/sentinel/technical-guides/sentinel-5p/products-algorithms) associated with the “Ozone (O₃) Total Column”.  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows TROPOMI data for [nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/Air-Quality-Measurements-TROPOMI-NO),  [carbon monoxide] (https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/Air-Quality-Measurements-TROPOMI-CO), and [absorbing aerosol index (AAI)] (https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/Air-Quality-Measurements-TROPOMI-AER-AI).
  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. Additional data for formaldehyde (CH₂O), sulphur dioxide (SO₂), methane (CH₄) and clouds are available from the data provider. Both a near real-time and an offline version of each of these compounds are available. Please see the [Google Earth Engine data catalog](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/tags/tropomi) to access this data. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.
  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/nrt-scripts/tree/master/cit_035_tropomi_atmospheric_chemistry_model).  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

info.name: Air Quality: Ozone (O₃) Satellite Measurements
info.technical_title: Sentinel 5 Precursor Tropospheric Monitoring Instrument (S5P/TROPOMI) Offline (OFFL) Level 3 (L3) Ozone (O₃)
info.functions: Average monthly density of ozone (O₃) in the total atmospheric column
info.cautions:
- Large amounts of SO₂ interferes with O₃ readings. Regions with high levels of  SO₂ have a larger uncertainty and margin of error for O₃ values calculated.

  
  
- Tropospheric ozone readings are not used if a significant amount of absorbing aerosol is present, based on a threshold value from the absorbing aerosol index. The main reason is that the altitude profiles of the aerosol properties which are needed to correct for its interference with the ozone profile are unavailable. Furthermore, calculations with large amounts of aerosols leads to a significant increase in calculation time.

  
  
- Validation results for O₃ have found the global difference between TROPOMI data and ground-based measurements is below 1%, which is well within the mission requirements of maximum 3-4%.
  
  
- For more information on the data quality, please see the [product readme file] (https://sentinel.esa.int/documents/247904/3541451/Sentinel-5P-Readme-OFFL-Total-Ozone.pdf).

attributes.name: Universal Thermal Climate Index
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) provides a metric that identifies outdoor conditions that cause discomfort to people. It uses a combination of temperature, humidity, wind, and radiation to determine the stress (sweating, shivering, skin wetness, etc.) a person undergoes when exposed to outdoor conditions. UTCI comes from the ERA5-HEAT (Human thErmAl comforT) dataset from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). UTCI outputs are calculated globally (with the exception of Antarctica) and published on a monthly basis. UTCI is shown in degrees Celsius and presented at a spatial resolution of 0.25 degrees by 0.25 degrees, which is approximately 28 km x 28 km at the equator but [changes with distance](https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-of-latitude-and-longitude-distance-4070616) from the equator.

UTCI is a metric that provides critical information on how humans perceive the outdoor conditions they’re exposed to, and has implications for human health and well being. Extremes in temperatures, such as cold spells and heatwaves, cause an increase in morbidity and mortality and knowing where and when these occur is imperative. The UTCI enables people to better prepare and cope with temperature extremes.

ECMWF is an operational research institution that produces weather forecasts and data. They implement the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) which provides free and accessible climate information and data for a wide range of users.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
The ERA5-HEAT (Human thErmAL comforT) dataset comes from the ECMWF ERA5 reanalysis data, which combines model data with observations from around the globe. The merging of modeled data with observations allows for a globally consistent and complete dataset, both geographically and through time. ERA5-HEAT calculates the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI), which is computed from air temperature, humidity, wind speed, and radiation. Outputs of UTCI are provided in Kelvin on an hourly basis and at 0.25 degrees spatial resolution.

UTCI is a metric that relates human comfort/discomfort levels to outdoor conditions. It is a standard developed by the European Cooperation in Science and Technology (COST) Action 730 in 2009. It describes the air temperature of a reference outdoor environment that would evoke strain on the human body. It is calculated by an algorithm that takes into account a number of environmental variables, namely air temperature and relative humidity at 2 meters above ground, wind speed at 10 meters above ground, and the Mean Radiant Temperature (MRT). UTCI outputs are calculated globally (with the exception of Antarctica) for each hour and are provided in Kelvin. Outputs from ERA5 are available 2 to 3 months behind real time and the UTCI is calculated and published on a monthly basis.

For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://rmets.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/gdj3.102).  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Our data catalog shows only a subset of the dataset. Additional data for every year between 1979 and 2022 are available from the data provider. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on WRI’s data catalog. We converted the original units from Kelvin to Celsius and averaged over time. See the documentation on how we processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/tree/master/cli_079_rw0_universal_thermal_climate_index).  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

attributes.description:
### Visión general  
  
El Índice Universal de Clima Térmico (UTCI) proporciona una métrica que identifica las condiciones exteriores que causan incomodidad a las personas. Utiliza una combinación de temperatura, humedad, viento y radiación para determinar el estrés (sudoración, escalofríos, humedad de la piel, etc.) que sufre una persona cuando se expone a condiciones al aire libre. UTCI proviene del conjunto de datos ERA5-HEAT (Human thErmAl comforT) del Centro Europeo de Pronósticos Meteorológicos a Medio Plazo (ECMWF). UTCI se muestra en grados Celsius y se presenta a una resolución espacial de 0,25 grados por 0,25 grados, que es aproximadamente 28 km x 28 km en el ecuador pero [cambia con la distancia] (https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-de-latitud-y-longitud-distancia-4070616) desde el ecuador.

UTCI es una métrica que proporciona información crítica sobre cómo los humanos perciben las condiciones al aire libre a las que están expuestos, y tiene implicaciones para la salud y el bienestar humanos. Las temperaturas extremas, como las olas de frío y las olas de calor, causan un aumento de la morbilidad y la mortalidad y es imperativo saber dónde y cuándo ocurren. El UTCI permite a las personas prepararse mejor y hacer frente a las temperaturas extremas.

ECMWF es una institución de investigación operativa que produce pronósticos y datos meteorológicos. Implementan el Servicio de Cambio Climático de Copernicus (C3S) que proporciona información y datos climáticos gratuitos y accesibles para una amplia gama de usuarios.  
### Metodología  
  
El conjunto de datos ERA5-HEAT (Human thErmAL comforT) proviene de los datos de reanálisis ECMWF ERA5, que combina datos de modelos con observaciones de todo el mundo. La fusión de datos modelados con observaciones permite un conjunto de datos globalmente consistente y completo, tanto geográficamente como a través del tiempo. ERA5-HEAT calcula el Índice Climático Térmico Universal (UTCI), que se calcula a partir de la temperatura del aire, la humedad, la velocidad del viento y la radiación. Las salidas de UTCI se proporcionan en Kelvin cada hora y a una resolución espacial de 0,25 grados.

UTCI es una métrica que relaciona los niveles de comodidad / incomodidad humana con las condiciones al aire libre. Es un estándar desarrollado por la Acción 730 de cooperación europea en Ciencia y Tecnología (COST) en 2009. Describe la temperatura del aire de un entorno exterior de referencia que evocaría tensión en el cuerpo humano. Se calcula mediante un algoritmo que tiene en cuenta una serie de variables ambientales, a saber, la temperatura del aire y la humedad relativa a 2 metros sobre el suelo, la velocidad del viento a 10 metros sobre el suelo y la temperatura radiante media (MRT). Las salidas de UTCI se calculan globalmente (con la excepción de la Antártida) para cada hora y se proporcionan en Kelvin. Los resultados de ERA5 están disponibles de 2 a 3 meses en tiempo real y el UTCI se calcula y publica mensualmente.

Para obtener la documentación completa, consulte la fuente [metodología](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/cdsapp#!/dataset/derived-utci-historical?tab=overview).  
  
### Información adicional  
  
Nuestro catálogo de datos muestra solo un subconjunto del conjunto de datos. Los datos adicionales para cada año entre 1979 y 2022 están disponibles en el proveedor de datos. Para acceder al conjunto de datos completo e información adicional, haga clic en el botón "Más información".  
  
### Visualización de los datos  
  
Nuestro equipo reformateó este conjunto de datos antes de mostrarlo en el catálogo de datos de la IRG. Convertimos las unidades originales de Kelvin a Celsius y promediamos con el tiempo. Consulte la documentación sobre cómo procesamos los datos en [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/tree/master/cli_079_rw0_universal_thermal_climate_index).  
  
### Descargo de responsabilidad  
  
Extractos de esta página de descripción fueron tomados de los metadatos de origen.

attributes.name: உலகளாவிய வெப்ப காலநிலை குறியீட்டெண்
attributes.description:
### கண்ணோட்டம்  
  
யுனிவர்சல் தெர்மல் க்ளைமேட் இண்டெக்ஸ் (யு.டி.சி.ஐ) மக்களுக்கு அசௌகரியத்தை ஏற்படுத்தும் வெளிப்புற நிலைமைகளை அடையாளம் காணும் ஒரு அளவீட்டை வழங்குகிறது. வெளிப்புற நிலைமைகளுக்கு வெளிப்படும் போது ஒரு நபர் அனுபவிக்கும் மன அழுத்தத்தை (வியர்வை, நடுக்கம், தோல் ஈரப்பதம், முதலியன) தீர்மானிக்க வெப்பநிலை, ஈரப்பதம், காற்று மற்றும் கதிர்வீச்சு ஆகியவற்றின் கலவையை இது பயன்படுத்துகிறது. UTCI நடுத்தர-தூர வானிலை முன்னறிவிப்புகளுக்கான ஐரோப்பிய மையத்தின் (ECMWF) ERA5-HEAT (Human thErmAl comforT) தரவுத்தொகுப்பிலிருந்து வருகிறது. யு.டி.சி.ஐ டிகிரி செல்சியஸில் காட்டப்படுகிறது மற்றும் பூமத்திய ரேகையில் தோராயமாக 28 கி.மீ x 28 கி.மீ ஆகும், ஆனால் [தூரத்துடன் மாற்றங்கள்](https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-ன்-அட்சரேகை-மற்றும்-தீர்க்கரேகை-தூரம்-தூரம்-4070616) பூமத்திய ரேகையிலிருந்து 0.25 டிகிரி செல்சியஸ் இல் காட்டப்பட்டுள்ளது.

யு.டி.சி.ஐ என்பது ஒரு மெட்ரிக் ஆகும், இது மனிதர்கள் அவர்கள் வெளிப்படும் வெளிப்புற நிலைமைகளை எவ்வாறு உணர்கிறார்கள் என்பதற்கான முக்கியமான தகவல்களை வழங்குகிறது, மேலும் மனித ஆரோக்கியம் மற்றும் நல்வாழ்வில் தாக்கங்களைக் கொண்டுள்ளது. குளிர் மற்றும் வெப்ப அலைகள் போன்ற வெப்பநிலைகளில் உள்ள அதீதங்கள், நோயுற்ற தன்மை மற்றும் இறப்பு விகிதத்தில் அதிகரிப்பை ஏற்படுத்துகின்றன, மேலும் இவை எங்கு, எப்போது நிகழ்கின்றன என்பதை அறிவது இன்றியமையாதது. யு.டி.சி.ஐ வெப்பநிலை உச்சநிலையை சிறப்பாகத் தயாரிக்கவும் சமாளிக்கவும் மக்களுக்கு உதவுகிறது.

ECMWF என்பது வானிலை முன்னறிவிப்புகள் மற்றும் தரவுகளை உற்பத்தி செய்யும் ஒரு செயல்பாட்டு ஆராய்ச்சி நிறுவனமாகும். அவர்கள் கோப்பர்நிக்கஸ் காலநிலை மாற்ற சேவையை (C3S) செயல்படுத்துகிறார்கள், இது பரந்த அளவிலான பயனர்களுக்கு இலவச மற்றும் அணுகக்கூடிய காலநிலை தகவல் மற்றும் தரவை வழங்குகிறது.  
### முறைமை  
  
எரா5-ஹீட் (மனித எர்மால் காம்போர்ட்) தரவுத்தொகுப்பு ஈ.சி.எம்.டபிள்யூ.எஃப் ஈரா 5 மறு பகுப்பாய்வு தரவிலிருந்து வருகிறது, இது மாதிரி தரவை உலகெங்கிலும் உள்ள அவதானிப்புகளுடன் ஒருங்கிணைக்கிறது. மாதிரியாக்கப்பட்ட தரவுகளை அவதானிப்புகளுடன் இணைப்பதன் மூலம் பூகோளரீதியாகவும், காலப் போக்கிலும் உலகளாவிய ரீதியில் சீரான மற்றும் முழுமையான தரவுத்தொகுப்பை அனுமதிக்கிறது. ERA5-HEAT யுனிவர்சல் வெப்ப காலநிலை குறியீட்டெண் (UTCI) கணக்கிடுகிறது, இது காற்று வெப்பநிலை, ஈரப்பதம், காற்று வேகம் மற்றும் கதிர்வீச்சு ஆகியவற்றிலிருந்து கணக்கிடப்படுகிறது. யு.டி.சி.ஐ.யின் வெளியீடுகள் கெல்வினில் ஒரு மணி நேர அடிப்படையில் மற்றும் 0.25 டிகிரி இடஞ்சார்ந்த தெளிவுத்திறனில் வழங்கப்படுகின்றன.

யு.டி.சி.ஐ என்பது மனித ஆறுதல் / அசௌகரியம் நிலைகளை வெளிப்புற நிலைமைகளுடன் தொடர்புபடுத்தும் ஒரு மெட்ரிக் ஆகும். இது 2009 ஆம் ஆண்டில் அறிவியல் மற்றும் தொழில்நுட்பத்தில் ஐரோப்பிய ஒத்துழைப்பு (COST) நடவடிக்கை 730 ஆல் உருவாக்கப்பட்ட ஒரு தரநிலையாகும். இது மனித உடலில் அழுத்தத்தைத் தூண்டும் ஒரு குறிப்பு வெளிப்புற சூழலின் காற்று வெப்பநிலையை விவரிக்கிறது. இது பல சுற்றுச்சூழல் மாறிகள், அதாவது காற்று வெப்பநிலை மற்றும் தரையிலிருந்து 2 மீட்டர் உயரத்தில் ஒப்பீட்டு ஈரப்பதம், தரையில் இருந்து 10 மீட்டர் உயரத்தில் காற்றின் வேகம் மற்றும் சராசரி கதிரியக்க வெப்பநிலை (எம்.ஆர்.டி) ஆகியவற்றை கணக்கில் எடுத்துக் கொள்ளும் ஒரு வழிமுறையால் கணக்கிடப்படுகிறது. யு.டி.சி.ஐ வெளியீடுகள் ஒவ்வொரு மணி நேரத்திற்கும் உலகளவில் (அண்டார்டிகாவைத் தவிர) கணக்கிடப்பட்டு கெல்வினில் வழங்கப்படுகின்றன. ERA5 இலிருந்து வெளியீடுகள் 2 முதல் 3 மாதங்கள் வரை நிகழ்நேரத்திற்குப் பின்னால் கிடைக்கின்றன, மேலும் UTCI கணக்கிடப்பட்டு மாதாந்திர அடிப்படையில் வெளியிடப்படுகிறது.

முழு ஆவணப்படுத்தலுக்கு, தயவுசெய்து மூலத்தைப் பார்க்கவும் [வழிமுறை](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/cdsapp#!/dataset/derived-utci-historical?tab=overview).  
  
### கூடுதல் தகவல்  
  
எங்கள் தரவு அட்டவணை தரவுத்தொகுப்பின் துணைக்குழுவை மட்டுமே காட்டுகிறது. 1979 மற்றும் 2022 க்கு இடையில் ஒவ்வொரு ஆண்டும் கூடுதல் தரவு தரவு வழங்குநரிடமிருந்து கிடைக்கிறது. முழு தரவுத்தொகுப்பு மற்றும் கூடுதல் தகவலுக்கான அணுகலுக்கு, "மேலும் அறிக" பொத்தானைக் கிளிக் செய்க.  
  
### தரவை காட்சிப்படுத்தல்  
  
WRI இன் தரவு அட்டவணையில் காண்பிக்கப்படுவதற்கு முன்பு எங்கள் குழு இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பை மறுவடிவமைத்தது. அசல் அலகுகளை கெல்வினில் இருந்து செல்சியஸுக்கு மாற்றினோம், காலப்போக்கில் சராசரியாக இருந்தோம். [Github] இல் உள்ள தரவை நாங்கள் எவ்வாறு செயலாக்கினோம் என்பதற்கான ஆவணங்களைப் பார்க்கவும் (https://github.com/resource-வாட்ச்/தரவு-முன்-செயலாக்கம்/மரம்/மாஸ்டர்/cli_079_rw0_universal_thermal_climate_index).  
  
### பொறுப்புத்துறப்பு  
  
இந்த விளக்கப் பக்கத்தின் பகுதிகள் மூல மெட்டாடேட்டாவிலிருந்து எடுக்கப்பட்டன.

info.technical_title: ERA5-HEAT (Human thErmAl comforT) உலகளாவிய வெப்ப காலநிலை குறியீட்டெண்
info.functions: வெளிப்புற நிலைமைகள் பற்றிய மனித உணர்வு
info.cautions:
-உற்பத்தி சேவையின் மாற்றத்தின் போது ஒரு பிழை இருந்ததால் தரவுத்தொகுப்பின் பதிப்பு 1 சிதைக்கப்படுகிறது. பயனர்கள் பதிப்பு 1.1 ஐ பதிவிறக்கம் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
  
தரவுத்தொகுப்பு [மறு பகுப்பாய்வு] (https://www.ecmwf.int/en/about/media-மையம் / கவனம் / 2020 / உண்மை-தாள்-மறு பகுப்பாய்வு) தரவை உருவாக்கப் பயன்படுத்தப்படும் மாதிரியிலிருந்து பெறப்பட்ட உள்ளார்ந்த நிச்சயமற்ற தன்மைகளைக் கொண்டுள்ளது.
  
-ஆடை அணிந்த மனித உடலின் எமிசிட்டிவிட்டி சராசரி கதிரியக்க வெப்பநிலை கணக்கீட்டில் 0.97 ஆக அமைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.
info.citation:
(1) கோப்பர்நிக்கஸ் காலநிலை மாற்ற சேவை தகவல், 2022 ஐப் பயன்படுத்தி உருவாக்கப்பட்டது. உலக வளங்கள் நிறுவனம் மூலம் அணுகப்பட்டது, (தேதி). [www.resourcewatch.org] (https://www.resourcewatch.org).
  
(2) டி நாபோலி சி, பர்னார்ட் சி, ப்ருதோம் சி, க்ளோக் எச்எல் மற்றும் பாப்பென்பெர்கர் எஃப் (2020) எரா5-ஹீட்: காலநிலை மறு பகுப்பாய்வுகளிலிருந்து மனித வெப்ப ஆறுதல் குறியீடுகளின் உலகளாவிய கட்டமைக்கப்பட்ட வரலாற்று தரவுத்தொகுப்பு. புவி அறிவியல் தரவு இதழ், https://rmets.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/gdj3.102

attributes.name: యూనివర్సల్ థర్మల్ క్లైమేట్ ఇండెక్స్
attributes.description:
### అవలోకనం  
  
యూనివర్సల్ థర్మల్ క్లైమేట్ ఇండెక్స్ (యుటిసిఐ) ప్రజలకు అసౌకర్యం కలిగించే బహిరంగ పరిస్థితులను గుర్తించే మెట్రిక్ ను అందిస్తుంది. బహిరంగ పరిస్థితులకు గురైనప్పుడు ఒక వ్యక్తి ఎదుర్కొనే ఒత్తిడిని (చెమట పట్టడం, వణుకు, చర్మం తడిగా ఉండటం మొదలైనవి) తెలుసుకోవడానికి ఇది ఉష్ణోగ్రత, తేమ, గాలి మరియు రేడియేషన్ యొక్క కలయికను ఉపయోగిస్తుంది. యుటిసిఐ యూరోపియన్ సెంటర్ ఫర్ మీడియం-రేంజ్ వెదర్ ఫోర్కాస్ట్స్ (ECMWF) నుండి ERA5-HOT (హ్యూమన్ థెర్మల్ కామ్ఫోర్ట్) డేటాసెట్ నుండి వచ్చింది. యుటిసిఐ డిగ్రీల సెల్సియస్ లో చూపించబడింది మరియు 0.25 డిగ్రీల బై 0.25 డిగ్రీల ప్రాదేశిక రిజల్యూషన్ వద్ద ప్రదర్శించబడుతుంది, ఇది భూమధ్యరేఖ వద్ద సుమారు 28 కి.మీ x 28 కి.మీ. అయితే [దూరంతో మారుతుంది](https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-అక్షాంశం-మరియు-రేఖాంశం-దూరం-4070616) భూమధ్యరేఖ నుండి.

యుటిసిఐ అనేది ఒక మెట్రిక్, ఇది మానవులు తాము బహిర్గతం చేసే బహిరంగ పరిస్థితులను ఎలా గ్రహిస్తారనే దానిపై క్లిష్టమైన సమాచారాన్ని అందిస్తుంది మరియు మానవ ఆరోగ్యం మరియు శ్రేయస్సుపై ప్రభావాలను కలిగి ఉంటుంది. చలి స్పెల్స్ మరియు హీట్ వేవ్స్ వంటి ఉష్ణోగ్రతలలో విపరీతాలు, అనారోగ్యం మరియు మరణాల పెరుగుదలకు కారణమవుతాయి మరియు ఇవి ఎక్కడ మరియు ఎప్పుడు సంభవిస్తాయో తెలుసుకోవడం అత్యవసరం. యుటిసిఐ ప్రజలు ఉష్ణోగ్రత విపరీతాలను మెరుగ్గా సిద్ధం చేయడానికి మరియు ఎదుర్కోవటానికి వీలు కల్పిస్తుంది.

ECMWF అనేది వాతావరణ సూచనలు మరియు డేటాను ఉత్పత్తి చేసే ఒక ఆపరేషనల్ రీసెర్చ్ ఇన్ స్టిట్యూషన్. వారు కోపర్నికస్ క్లైమేట్ ఛేంజ్ సర్వీస్ (సి 3ఎస్) ను అమలు చేస్తారు, ఇది విస్తృత శ్రేణి వినియోగదారులకు ఉచిత మరియు ప్రాప్యత వాతావరణ సమాచారం మరియు డేటాను అందిస్తుంది.  
#### మెథడాలజీ  
  
ఎరా5-హీట్ (హ్యూమన్ థర్మల్ కామ్ఫోర్ట్) డేటాసెట్ ఈసిఎమ్ డబ్ల్యుఎఫ్ ఎరా5 రీఅనాలిసిస్ డేటా నుండి వచ్చింది, ఇది మోడల్ డేటాను ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా ఉన్న పరిశీలనలతో మిళితం చేస్తుంది. పరిశీలనలతో నమూనా డేటాను విలీనం చేయడం ద్వారా భౌగోళికంగా మరియు సమయం ద్వారా ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా స్థిరమైన మరియు సంపూర్ణ డేటాసెట్ కు అనుమతిస్తుంది. ఎరా5-హీట్ అనేది యూనివర్సల్ థర్మల్ క్లైమేట్ ఇండెక్స్ (యుటిసిఐ) ను లెక్కిస్తుంది, ఇది గాలి ఉష్ణోగ్రత, తేమ, గాలి వేగం మరియు రేడియేషన్ నుండి లెక్కించబడుతుంది. యుటిసిఐ యొక్క అవుట్ పుట్ లు కెల్విన్ లో గంటవారీగా మరియు 0.25 డిగ్రీల ప్రాదేశిక రిజల్యూషన్ వద్ద అందించబడతాయి.

యుటిసిఐ అనేది ఒక మెట్రిక్, ఇది మానవ సౌకర్యం/అసౌకర్య స్థాయిలను బహిరంగ పరిస్థితులకు సంబంధించినది. ఇది 2009లో యూరోపియన్ కోఆపరేషన్ ఇన్ సైన్స్ అండ్ టెక్నాలజీ (కాస్ట్) యాక్షన్ 730 ద్వారా అభివృద్ధి చేయబడిన ఒక ప్రమాణం. ఇది మానవ శరీరంపై ఒత్తిడిని రేకెత్తించే రిఫరెన్స్ అవుట్ డోర్ వాతావరణం యొక్క గాలి ఉష్ణోగ్రతను వివరిస్తుంది. ఇది భూమి నుండి 2 మీటర్ల ఎత్తులో గాలి ఉష్ణోగ్రత మరియు సాపేక్ష తేమ, భూమికి 10 మీటర్ల ఎత్తులో గాలి వేగం మరియు సగటు రేడియంట్ టెంపరేచర్ (MRT) వంటి అనేక పర్యావరణ వేరియబుల్స్ ను పరిగణనలోకి తీసుకునే ఒక అల్గారిథమ్ ద్వారా లెక్కించబడుతుంది. యుటిసిఐ అవుట్ పుట్ లు ప్రతి గంటకు ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా (అంటార్కిటికా మినహాయించి) లెక్కించబడతాయి మరియు కెల్విన్ లో అందించబడతాయి. ERA5 నుంచి అవుట్ పుట్ లు రియల్ టైమ్ కంటే 2 నుంచి 3 నెలల తరువాత లభ్యం అవుతాయి మరియు యుటిసిఐ నెలవారీ ప్రాతిపదికన లెక్కించబడుతుంది మరియు పబ్లిష్ చేయబడుతుంది.

పూర్తి డాక్యుమెంటేషన్ కొరకు, దయచేసి సోర్స్ [మెథడాలజీ](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/cdsapp#!/dataset/derived-utci-హిస్టారికల్?ట్యాబ్=అవలోకనం) చూడండి.  
  
### అదనపు సమాచారం  
  
మా డేటా కేటలాగ్ డేటాసెట్ యొక్క ఉపసమితిని మాత్రమే చూపుతుంది. డేటా ప్రొవైడర్ నుండి 1979 మరియు 2022 మధ్య ప్రతి సంవత్సరానికి అదనపు డేటా అందుబాటులో ఉంది. పూర్తి డేటాసెట్ మరియు అదనపు సమాచారాన్ని యాక్సెస్ చేసుకోవడానికి, "మరింత తెలుసుకోండి" బటన్ మీద క్లిక్ చేయండి.  
  
### డేటాను విజువలైజ్ చేయడం  
  
డబ్ల్యుఆర్ఐ యొక్క డేటా కేటలాగ్ లో ప్రదర్శించడానికి ముందు మా బృందం ఈ డేటాసెట్ ను పునర్నిర్మించింది. మేము అసలు యూనిట్లను కెల్విన్ నుండి సెల్సియస్ కు మార్చాము మరియు కాలక్రమేణా సగటుగా ఉన్నాము. [Github](https://github.com/resource-వాచ్/డేటా-ప్రీ-ప్రాసెసింగ్/ట్రీ/మాస్టర్/cli_079_rw0_universal_thermal_climate_index)పై డేటాను మేం ఏవిధంగా ప్రాసెస్ చేశాం అనే దానిపై డాక్యుమెంటేషన్ ని చూడండి.  
  
### డిస్ క్లెయిమర్  
  
ఈ వివరణ పేజీ యొక్క సారాంశాలు మూల మెటాడేటా నుండి తీసుకోబడ్డాయి.

sources.source-description: యూరోపియన్ సెంటర్ ఫర్ మీడియం రేంజ్ వెదర్ ఫోర్కాస్ట్స్ (ECMWF)

info.technical_title: ERA5-HOT (హ్యూమన్ థర్మల్ కామ్ ఫోర్ట్) యూనివర్సల్ థర్మల్ క్లైమేట్ ఇండెక్స్
info.functions: బహిరంగ పరిస్థితుల యొక్క మానవ అవగాహన
info.cautions:
-ప్రొడక్షన్ సర్వీస్ యొక్క పరివర్తన సమయంలో దోషం ఉన్నందున డేటాసెట్ యొక్క వెర్షన్ 1 డీప్రెకేట్ చేయబడింది. యూజర్లు వెర్షన్ 1.1ని డౌన్ లోడ్ చేసుకోవాలి.
  
-డేటాసెట్ లో అంతర్లీనంగా అనిశ్చితులు ఉన్నాయి, ఇవి [రీఅనాలిసిస్](https://www.ecmwf.int/en/about/media-సెంటర్/ఫోకస్/2020/ఫ్యాక్ట్-షీట్-రీఅనాలసిస్) డేటాను జనరేట్ చేయడానికి ఉపయోగించే మోడల్ నుంచి తీసుకోబడ్డాయి.
  
- సగటు రేడియంట్ ఉష్ణోగ్రత లెక్కింపులో దుస్తులు ధరించిన మానవ శరీరం యొక్క ఎమిసివిటీ 0.97 కు సెట్ చేయబడింది.

attributes.name: Global Cropland Extent
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Global Cropland Extent dataset at 30 m spatial resolution was developed by the Global Land Analysis and Discovery Lab  (GLAD) at the University of Maryland (UMD) using Landsat satellite data time-series. Cropland is defined as land used to produce herbaceous crops for human consumption, forage, and biofuel. Perennial woody crops, permanent pastures, and shifting cultivation are excluded from the definition. The map is based on the machine learning classification of the global Landsat data archive using locally calibrated models. Model calibration data were collected through visual interpretation of Landsat and high spatial resolution satellite images. The mapping was performed for 2000-2003, 2004-2007, 2008-2011, 2012-2015, and 2016-2019 time intervals. For each four-year interval, a 30x30 m pixel was mapped as cropland if a growing crop was detected during any of these years. **Cropland change data are available**[here](https://bit.ly/34QydNx).
  
  
Global population growth and increasing standards of living inevitably cause the expansion and intensification of global agricultural land use to fulfill growing demands for food, biofuel, and other commodities. In turn, agriculture expansion and intensification threaten ecosystem functioning and lead to species extinction through habitat loss and fragmentation. The [United Nations 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)](https://www.undp.org/sustainable-development-goals) call for balancing increasing agricultural production with maintenance of ecosystem services. 
  
  
Implementation of SDGs to improve food security, protect freshwater and terrestrial ecosystems, and mitigate climate change require national policies and international cooperation that are based on consistent, independent, and timely data on agriculture extent and productivity. The Cropland Extent and Change dataset can serve as a tool for monitoring national and global progress towards SDGs.
  
  
The GLAD laboratory in the Department of Geographical Sciences at UMD investigates methods, causes, and impacts of global land surface change. Earth observation imagery is the primary data source and land cover extent and change is the primary topic of interest. GLAD aspires to generate new science insights concerning land resources, educate the next generation of remote sensing-based land change scientists, and disseminate land monitoring capabilities to operational settings nationally and internationally.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
Cropland is defined as land used for the production of annual and perennial herbaceous crops for human consumption, forage (including hay), and biofuel. Perennial woody crops, permanent pastures, and shifting cultivation are excluded from the definition. The fallow length is limited to four years for the cropland class. The cropland class definition is largely consistent with the arable land category reported by the [Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations](https://www.fao.org/3/Y4171E/Y4171E20.htm).
  
  
The analysis was performed in four-year epochs, 2000-2003, 2004-2007, 2008-2011, 2012-2015, and 2016-2019. One cropland map per epoch was created. Using a four-year interval (rather than a single year) increased the number of clear-sky satellite observations in the time-series, which improves the representation of land surface phenology and the accuracy of cropland detection. For each four-year interval, an area was mapped as cropland if a growing crop was detected during any of these years. This way, the criterion of the maximum fallow length was implemented: if an area was not used as cropland for more than four years, it was not included in the cropland map for the corresponding time interval.
  
  
The global 16-day normalized surface reflectance Landsat Analysis Ready Data (Landsat ARD) was employed as input data for cropland mapping [(Potapov et al., 2020)](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-4292/12/3/426). For each four-year interval, a single annualized gap-free 16-day observation time-series was created. For each 16-day interval, the observation with the highest near-infrared reflectance value was selected (to prioritize observations with the highest vegetation cover) from four years of Landsat data. The annualized 16-day time series within each four-year interval was transformed into a set of multitemporal metrics that provide consistent land surface phenology inputs for global cropland mapping. The Landsat metrics were augmented with elevation data. 
  
  
Global cropland mapping included three stages that enabled extrapolation of visually delineated cropland training data to a temporally consistent global cropland map time-series using machine learning. At all three stages, bagged decision tree ensembles were employed as a supervised classification algorithm that uses class presence and absence data as the dependent variable and a set of multitemporal metrics as independent variables at a Landsat ARD pixel scale. The first stage consisted of performing individual cropland classifications for a set of 924 Landsat ARD 1°×1° tiles for the 2016-2019 interval. At the second stage, the 924 tiles that had been classified as cropland/other land and the 2016-2019 metric set were used to train a series of regional cropland mapping models. At the third stage, the preliminary global cropland maps were used as training data to generate temporally consistent global cropland data. The goal of this third stage was to create a robust spatiotemporally consistent set of locally calibrated cropland detection models. For each 1°×1° Landsat ARD tile (13,451 tiles total) training data for each four-year interval was collected from the preliminary cropland extent maps within a 3° radius of the target tile, with preference to select stable cropland and non-cropland pixels as training. Training data from all intervals were used to calibrate a single decision tree ensemble for each ARD tile. The per-tile models were then applied to each time interval, and the results were post-processed to remove single cropland class detections and omissions within time-series and eliminate cropland patches below 0.5 ha. Manual masks to remove map artifacts (e.g., cropland overestimation over temperate wetlands and flooded grasslands) were applied in some regions to improve the final map.
  
  
For the full documentation, please click on the “Learn more” button.
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows datasets from the GLAD laboratory for [Cropland Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/ec282483-4f5c-4fb8-ace7-8e557826781a), [Tree Height Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/64a3e126-000b-46fb-aaf4-8ac765a8263b), [Water Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/b83ad197-eb95-44e2-8ec3-3351ab926421), [Snow/Ice Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/5a796ce9-71d4-42b0-922d-056a86e5eb72), [Built-Up Area Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/e6a3f803-1222-46c2-8e6c-0ae94b3d80c8), and [Land Cover Map](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/06e734af-66f0-4c3e-ac71-1b99f3cbfe1d).

info.name: Global Cropland Extent
info.technical_title: Global cropland expansion in the 21st century
info.functions: Cropland extent for 4-year periods from 2000 to 2019
info.cautions:
- A probability-based sample analysis is the recommended good practice approach to estimating land cover and land use extent and change. The global land cover map time-series enables a higher sampling efficiency through stratification at the sub-national, national, and global scales. The maps should not be used as the only source data for national and international reporting due to unknown map uncertainty that may vary in space and between time intervals.
  
  
- Cropland maps have higher accuracy in regions dominated by large-scale industrial farming, e.g. North and South America. In Europe, Asia, and Africa, the global map may underestimate small-scale cropland areas due to Landsat spatial resolution limitations in mapping heterogeneous landscapes.
  
  
- Cropland class may be confused with the intensively managed permanent pastures as both classes have similar spectral response and phenology. This issue may cause an overestimation of cropland areas in Australia, New Zealand, and parts of Western Europe.
  
  
- Dryland rainfed agriculture and summer wheat production areas, especially when intermittent with long fallow, maybe partially omitted in Central Asia and the Middle East. The short vegetation season and the lack of cloud-free Landsat data in some years may preclude dryland agriculture detection.
  
  
- Croplands that were repeatedly abandoned and recultivated may be inconsistently mapped as cropland loss or gain.

attributes.name: Electricity Consumption
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
This dataset shows the net electricity consumption in 230 countries from 1980 to 2019. This dataset is published by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), [which calculates net electricity consumption](https://www.eia.gov/tools/glossary/index.php?id=Net%20electricity%20consumption) as “generation + imports - exports - transmission and distribution losses.”
  
  

Electricity consumption is a key indicator of the environmental impact and input costs of economic activity. The intensity of electricity consumption and the sources of energy are among the key indicators of sustainable energy, as defined by Sustainable Development Goal 7.  
  
### Methodology  
  
EIA collected and analyzed consumption data from multiple external sources. The estimates in this dataset are based on a time series analysis, and the performance of the model was evaluated with hold‐out validation.
  
  

For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://www.eia.gov/beta/international/images/International_Energy_Statistics_Estimation_for_Lagged_Data.pdf).  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows the [total energy consumption](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/67cf410f-4cdf-4437-aa09-187e5fa590ae) dataset by EIA.

attributes.name: Combined Sea Surface and Air Temperature Anomalies
attributes.description:
The GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP) was created by NASA's Goddard Institute for Space Studies (GISS) and is now run by NOAA's Earth System Research Laboratory Physical Sciences Division (ESRL-PSD). GISTEMP provides an estimate of global surface and air temperature changes. The basic GISS temperature analysis scheme was defined by James Hansen in the late 1970s, when a method of estimating global temperature change was needed for comparison with 1-dimensional global climate models. The scheme was based on the finding that the correlation of temperature change was reasonably strong for stations separated by up to 1,200 km, especially at middle and high latitudes. This fact proved sufficient to obtain useful estimates for global mean temperature changes. The analysis method was fully documented in Hansen and Lebedeff (1987), including quantitative estimates of the error in annual and 5-year mean temperature change. This was done by sampling at station locations a spatially complete data set of a long run of a global climate model, which was shown to have realistic spatial and temporal variability. This however only addresses the error due to incomplete spatial coverage of measurements. As there are other potential sources of error, such as urban warming near meteorological stations, many other methods have been used to verify the approximate magnitude of inferred global warming. These methods include inference of surface temperature change from vertical temperature profiles in the ground (bore holes) at many sites around the world, rate of glacier retreat at many locations, and studies by several groups of the effect of urban and other local human influences on the global temperature record. All of these yield consistent estimates of the approximate magnitude of global warming, which reached about 0.8°C in 2010, twice the magnitude reported in 1981. Further affirmation of the reality of the warming is its spatial distribution, which has largest values at locations remote from any local human influence, with a global pattern consistent with that expected for response to global climate forcings (larger in the Northern Hemisphere than the Southern Hemisphere, larger at high latitudes than low latitudes, larger over land than over ocean). More recent documentation compares alternative analyses and addresses questions about perception and reality of global warming; various choices for the ocean data are tested; it is also shown that global temperature change is sensitive to estimated temperature change in polar regions, where observations are limited. A multiyear smoothing is applied to fully remove the annual cycle and improve information content in temperature graphs. Despite large year-to-year fluctuations associated with the El Niño-La Niña cycle of tropical ocean temperature, the conclusion could be drawn that global temperature continued to rise rapidly in the 21st century, new record heights being reached in every decade. One of the improvements—introduced in 1998—was the implementation of a method to address the problem of urban warming: The urban and periurban (i.e., other than rural) stations are adjusted so that their long-term trend matches that of the mean of neighboring rural stations. Urban stations without nearby rural stations are dropped. This preserves local short-term variability without affecting long-term trends. Originally, the classification of stations was based on population size near that station; the current analysis uses satellite-observed night-lights to determine which stations are located in urban and periurban areas. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, see the Learn More link.

attributes.name: Water Change
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The global annual surface water percent and surface water dynamics maps were created by the Global Land Analysis and Discovery Lab (GLAD) laboratory, and the data is available at 30 m spatial resolution, globally, from 2000 to 2020. The GLAD laboratory classified all available Landsat 5, 7, and 8 scenes. Each scene was classified per pixel to identify land, water, and ground obscured by cloud, shadow, haze, or ice. Land and water observations were summed by month from all available images. These counts were aggregated to estimate the annual temporal percent of the year each pixel had water presence, resulting in values of 0-100, and pixels with no observations a no-data value of 255. In order to characterize the type of surface water dynamic over the 21 years, the annual water percent was estimated for each year and temporally filtered to provide greater consistency. A series of rules were applied to this time series to characterize it into permanent land or water, stable seasonal, unidirectional loss or gain, temporary dry or wet period, and high-frequency transitions between annual states of water and land. The pixels that experienced temporary dry or wet periods and high frequency transitions were mapped as variable water. 
  
  
The Global Land Analysis and Discovery Lab (GLAD) laboratory in the Department of Geographical Sciences at UMD investigates methods, causes, and impacts of global land surface change.  Earth observation imagery is the primary data source, and the land cover extent and change is the primary topic of interest. GLAD aspires to generate new science insights concerning land resources, educate the next generation of remote sensing-based land change scientists, and disseminate land monitoring capabilities to operational settings nationally and internationally.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
Open surface water, or simply water, is defined as inland water that covers ≥50% of a pixel and is not obscured by objects on or above the water surface, for example, forest canopy, floating aquatic vegetation, bridges, or ice. The analysis had three major steps: (1) classify every Landsat scene 1999-2020; (2) create an annual percent water time-series; and (3) characterize the time-series into various dynamics classes. 
  
  
All Landsat 5, 7, and 8 scenes from 2000-2020 were classified into land, water, and unusable data. Due to the diversity of reflectance patterns for open surface water targets, an ensemble of hierarchical, bagged classification trees were used to discriminate clear observations from those contaminated by cloud, shadow, and ice and to discriminate water from land. These classification trees were developed from a training set of 150-180 fully labeled scenes per sensor [(Potapov et al., 2015)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2014.11.027). The classification models utilize all the Landsat bands, normalized difference ratios of each pair of spectral bands, and 3x3 pixel spatial averages of all bands and ratios, as well as, utilize topographic inputs of elevation and derived slope, aspect, and hillshade data.
  
  
The annual water percent time series was derived from the counts of water and land observations. To account for intra-annual variation in clear observation frequency (e.g. fewer observations in the far north in winter due to low sun elevations or in tropical monsoon environments due to high cloud cover), the percent of land and water observations flagged as water (water / (water + land)) was first calculated per meteorological season (December-February, March-May, June-August, September-November) of each year. Then the average water percent of the seasons with data was assigned as the annual water percent. Temporal filters and manual masks were applied to remove noise and omission/commission errors. 
  
  
An inter-annual water dynamics model was developed to characterize and visualize the dynamics of water presence 2000-2020. The annual water percent time series was first smoothed using a 3-year mean moving window, and the range and mean were calculated per pixel. Pixels with a range of ≤33% and a mean of ≤10% or ≥90% were labeled permanent land and water, respectively, providing a stable target with low sensitivity to possible omission or commission effects due to image artifacts or atmospheric conditions. Change pixels were identified as pixels with a range of ≥50%, and all other pixels labeled as stable seasonal, characterized by having little or no inter-annual variation in water presence and consistent intra-annual variation. By an analysis of all local maxima and minima in the time-series, pixels labeled as change were further characterized into the following main change types: gain, loss, dry period (water-land-water), wet period (land-water-land), and high-frequency (3 or more) land-water transitions. For more details, please refer to Pickens et al. [(2020)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2020.111792).
  
  
For the full documentation, please click on the “Learn more” button.
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows datasets from the GLAD laboratory for [Cropland Extent](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/50634b51-ea2e-4cc1-9e4b-8f26a389a301), [Cropland Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/ec282483-4f5c-4fb8-ace7-8e557826781a), [Tree Height Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/64a3e126-000b-46fb-aaf4-8ac765a8263b), [Snow/Ice Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/5a796ce9-71d4-42b0-922d-056a86e5eb72), [Built-Up Area Change](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/e6a3f803-1222-46c2-8e6c-0ae94b3d80c8), and [Land Cover Map](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/06e734af-66f0-4c3e-ac71-1b99f3cbfe1d).
  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.

info.name: Water Change
info.technical_title: Global surface water dynamics 2000-2020
info.functions: Global surface water dynamics from the year 2000 to 2020
info.cautions:
- A probability-based sample analysis is the recommended good practice approach to estimating land cover and land use extent and change. The global surface water dynamics map enables a higher sampling efficiency through stratification at the sub-national, national, and global scales. The map should not be used as the only source data for national and international reporting due to unknown map uncertainty that may vary in space and between time intervals.
  
  
- Ice cover, lava, dark vegetation cover, high turbidity or very shallow water, the combination of unmasked shadow or haze with one of these covers, and mixed pixels are the most common sources of error in mapped water and land in the Landsat imagery.
  
  
- The dynamics map overestimates the extent of dynamic water presence, labeling some of the reference areas of permanent water or land as places with dynamic water presence. Much of this overestimation is within the above land covers or in the mixed pixels on the edge of water bodies. Conversely, the areas mapped as permanent water or land can be used with high confidence, committing only 1.2 (±0.7)% and 0.1 (±0.0)%, respectively.
  
  
- Individual classes representing dynamic water presence should be used with care, having lower accuracies. However, most errors are either mixed pixels or real dynamics mislabeled as another type of dynamic water presence rather than as permanent land or water.
