attributes.name: cli.005f Historical Minimum Antarctic Sea Ice
Minimum Antarctic Sea Ice
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Minimum Antarctic Sea Ice dataset shows the annual minimum extent of sea ice in the Antarctic for select years between 1980-2020. Antarctic sea ice typically reaches its minimum extent in February. In this map, light blue represents locations where sea ice was present during February for each year. Sea ice extent data was collected by satellite microwave sensing instruments at a spatial resolution of 25 kilometers (km). This dataset is derived from two products: a near real-time daily dataset and a separate daily dataset that is processed yearly. For the most recent 6-18 months, sea ice extents were derived from near real-time data; all older data was derived from the separate daily dataset. 

  
  
This dataset can be used to understand changes in annual minimum Antarctic sea ice extent over the past 40 years. Although Antarctic sea ice extent varies significantly from year to year, the average ice extent has not changed over the past 40 years. According to the [National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration](https://www.climate.gov/news-features/understanding-climate/understanding-climate-antarctic-sea-ice-extent), natural variability in the Southern Ocean and in atmospheric circulation patterns have a greater impact on Antarctic sea ice extent than climate change. However, climate change is disrupting wind patterns, currents and ocean temperatures across the globe. These changes may eventually impact Antarctic sea ice extent.

  
  
The [National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC)](https://nsidc.org/) was founded in 1976 as the World Data Center for Glaciology. Over time, the NSIDC evolved to become a data distribution and research center specializing in remote sensing of cryospheric data such as snow, sea ice, frozen ground, ice sheets and glaciers. In addition to managing and distributing this data, the NSIDC creates and supports data access tools for its users. They also use the datasets for climate research and education. The NSIDC is part of University of Colorado Boulder’s [Cooperative Institute for Research in Environmental Sciences (CIRES)](https://cires.colorado.edu/). It is supported by the [National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)](https://www.nasa.gov/), the [National Science Foundation (NSF)](https://www.nsf.gov/) and the [National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)](https://www.noaa.gov/).  
  
### Methodology  
  
Minimum Antarctic Sea Ice was produced from two sources: NASA's [Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC)](https://nsidc.org/data/nsidc-0051) and NSIDC’s [Near-Real-Time DMSP SSMIS Daily Polar Gridded Sea Ice Concentrations (NRTSI)](https://nsidc.org/data/nsidc-0081).
  
  
Data for the GSFC and NRTSI datasets was collected by the following six sensors:
- GSFC data:
  - [Nimbus-7 Satellite](https://eospso.nasa.gov/missions/nimbus-7) Scanning Multichannel Microwave Radiometer (SMMR) from October 1978 to August 1987
  - [Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP)](https://www.ospo.noaa.gov/Operations/DMSP/index.html) F8 Special Sensor Microwave/Imager (SSM/I) from August 1987 to December 1991
  - DMSP-F11 SSM/I from December 1991 to September 1995
  - DMSP-F13 SSM/I from September 1995 to December 2007
  - DMSP-F17 Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder (SSMIS) from January 2008 to present
- NRTSI data:
  - DMSP-F18 SSMIS from April 2016 to present

  
  
The SMMR, SSM/I, and SSMIS instruments sense emitted microwave radiation. Data was collected daily by the SSM/I and SSMIS sensors and on alternate days by the SMMR sensor. An object's physical properties, such as atomic composition and crystalline structure, determine the amount of microwave radiation it emits. The crystalline structure of ice typically emits more microwave energy than liquid ocean water. Thus, the microwave sensors can easily distinguish sea ice from the ocean. The satellite data was converted to [brightness temperature](https://glossary.ametsoc.org/wiki/Brightness_temperature), a descriptive measure of an object's radiation. Brightness temperature data was then converted to gridded ice concentration using the [NASA Team algorithm](https://nsidc.org/support/faq/nasa-team-vs-bootstrap-algorithm#NASATeam1) at a spatial resolution of 25 km. Gridded ice concentration is the percentage of ice (relative to water) in a given cell. Each cell’s daily ice concentrations were averaged to produce monthly concentrations. 

  
  
Sea ice extent is delineated by the location where ice ends and water (open ocean) begins. Cells were classified as water if their average monthly ice concentration was below 15%, and as ice if the concentration was above 15%. Images of sea ice extent were created for each month, with ice shown in light blue. The process was the same for both the NRTSI and GSFC datasets. 

  
  
GSFC data had a tighter quality control than NRTSI data. However, GSFC data is only released once per year. NRTSI data was available at the end of each month, so it was used to produce sea ice extents while GSFC data was being processed. GSFC data replaced NRTSI data once it was available. Thus, data from the most recent 6-18 months was derived from the NRTSI dataset and older data was derived from the GSFC dataset. 

  
  
For the full documentation, please click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows additional NSIDC sea ice extent data: [Historical Sea Ice Medians](http://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/b1ebea96-5963-4c2c-9273-7d08536ac07d), [Minimum Arctic Sea Ice](http://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/a99c5cf5-f141-4bed-a36d-b04c8e171dfa), [Maximum Arctic Sea Ice](http://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/15a0b176-8313-4859-af90-5c198e50a605), [Arctic Sea Ice Extent](http://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/484fbba1-ac34-402f-8623-7b1cc9c34f17), [Maximum Antarctic Sea Ice](http://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/7667bdd8-9adb-44de-b51c-d2d26e461af1) and [Antarctic Sea Ice Extent](http://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/e740efec-c673-431a-be2c-b214613f641a).

attributes.name: Climate Hazard Indicators (Annual mean temperatures) Historical and SSP scenarios - Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
attributes.description:
### Overview
 
 
The dataset includes five major climatic indicators viz. annual values for minimum temperature (℃), maximum temperature (℃), mean temperature (℃), total precipitation (mm/year), and the number of rainy days (represented as integers) for two Indian states, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. It features decadal averages from 2020-2100 for Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs), including SSP5-8.5, which reflects a high emissions scenario, and SSP2-4.5, representing moderate challenges to both mitigation and adaptation. Additionally, the dataset provides historical data for all the five indicators averaged over the period from 2005 to 2014.
 
 
### Methodology
 
 
**Pre-Processing**: The decadal time periods were labeled as follows: 2020-2029 as 2020, 2030-2039 as 2030, 2040-2049 as 2040, 2050-2059 as 2050, 2060-2069 as 2060, 2070-2079 as 2070, 2080-2089 as 2080, and 2090-2099 as 2090.
 
 
**Layers of interest**: Annual averages of minimum temperature (℃), maximum temperature (℃), mean temperature (℃), Annual total precipitation (mm/year), and the annual total number of rainy days (represented as integers).
 
 
**Data**: The ERA5 reanalysis dataset (ECMWF 2022), a satellite data product of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts with a spatial resolution of 31 kilometers (km), is used as a reference dataset. The ensemble of downscaled daily time series outputs from global climate models (GCMs). These time series include the historical years covered by the observation time series as well as the specified future years of interest. We have used the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 product, which includes outputs from 34 Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) models at approximately 25 km spatial resolution.
 
 
### Estimation Methods
 
 
Out of the 35 models, we select the top 3 climate models that perform best for a specific weather variable in a particular geographic region, and present the ensemble mean of these models. The ERA5 dataset is used as a reference, and the comparison is made for the historical period between 1980 and 2014. After selecting the models, we apply a calibration/bias correction procedure to the future time series of the models. This involves aligning the model's frequency distribution with the historical data by shifting the percentiles of the model's distribution. For instance, if the 20th percentile of the model data corresponds to the 30th percentile of the observations, then the 30th percentile of the calibrated model data will match the 20th percentile of the uncalibrated model data.
 
 
For the full documentation, please see the source methodology at Wong, T., and P Switzer. 2023. 'Estimating future local climate hazard probabilities.' Technical Note. Washington, DC: World Resources Institute. Available online at: doi.org/10.46830/writn.22.00074.v2.
 
 
### Description of the Layers
 
 
**Annual Maximum Temperature (℃)**: The daily maximum temperature data for each year is extracted and averaged to calculate the yearly average maximum temperature. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
**Annual Minimum Temperature (℃)**: The daily minimum temperature data for each year is extracted and averaged to calculate the yearly average minimum temperature. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
**Annual Mean Temperature (℃)**: The daily mean temperature is calculated by averaging the daily minimum and maximum temperatures. The annual mean temperature is obtained by averaging the daily mean temperatures over the course of a year. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
**Annual Total Precipitation (mm/year)**: The daily precipitation values are summed over the entire year to calculate the annual total precipitation. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
**Annual Rainy Days (represented as integers)**: A rainy day is defined as a day with precipitation exceeding 2.5 mm (as per the India Meteorological Department). The total number of rainy days in a year is calculated by summing the rainy days throughout the year. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
### Visualizing the Data
 
 
The data is provided at a 25-km resolution and is presented as a raster with a time slider with a separate layer for each variable. The values are visualized using a gradient based on the selected year in the slider, ranging from lighter shade (indicating low values) to darker shade (representing higher values).
 
 
### Disclaimer

attributes.name: Multidimensional Poverty Index
attributes.description:
The UN Development Programme (UNDP) compiles the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) as part of its Human Development Report initiative. First published in 2010, the MPI identifies multiple deprivations at the household level in health, education, and standard of living. It uses microdata from household surveys, and—unlike the Inequality-Adjusted Human Development Index—all the indicators needed to construct the measure must come from the same survey. Each person in a given household is classified as poor or nonpoor depending on the weighted number of deprivations his or her household experiences. These data are then aggregated into the national measure of poverty. The MPI reflects both the prevalence of multidimensional deprivation and its intensity—the percentage of simultaneous deprivations poor people experience. It can be used to create a comprehensive picture of people living in poverty and permits comparisons both across countries, regions, and the world and within countries by ethnic group, urban, or rural location, as well as other key household and community characteristics. The MPI offers a valuable complement to income-based poverty measures. Indicators shown in the MPI include the following: (1) health: nutrition and child mortality; (2) education: years of schooling and children enrolled; and (3) standard of living: cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, and assets. The MPI is calculated by multiplying the incidence of poverty by the intensity of poverty. The incidence of poverty is the proportion of people considered to experience multidimensional poverty, in other words, that are considered deprived in at least one-third of the MPI's weighted indicators. The intensity of multidimensional poverty is the weighted average number of deprivations poor people experience at the same time. The main data sources of the MPI are the Macro Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) of the Inner City Fund (ICF) and the Multiple Indicators Cluster Survey (MICS) of the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF). The 2020 Human Development Report (HDR) presents estimates for 107 countries—28
low income, 76 middle income, and 3 high income—and 5.9 billion people in developing regions. About 1.3 billion people in the 107 developing countries covered—22% of their entire population—lived in multidimensional poverty. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Learn More link.
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.

sources.source-description: Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)

info.technical_title: Multidimensional Poverty Index
info.functions: Index on multidimensional poverty across health, education, and standard of living
info.cautions:
- The indicators may not reflect capabilities but instead reflect outputs (such as years of schooling) or inputs (such as cooking fuel).
- The health dimension indicators are not consistently collected across countries and overlook some groups’ deprivations, especially for nutrition, though the patterns that emerge are plausible and familiar.
- Child deaths that occurred at any time (instead of in the last 5 years previous to the survey) are used in 10 countries because the survey did not collect the date of child deaths. 
- In some cases, careful judgments were needed to address data that was not collected. For example, data on nutrition was not collected for children older than 5 years in both DHS and MICS, data on adult nutrition was not collected in MICS, data on adult nutrition was collected only for women of ages 15 and 49 in DHS (though in a few small number of countries it was collected for men), and child mortality was not collected in households without women of reproductive age. In these situations, households without eligible members to be measured for nutrition and without eligible members to report child mortality are assumed to be not deprived in these indicators. This is a strong assumption that may biases the results and we are conducting research to find a better alternative. However, to be considered multidimensionally poor, households must be deprived in at least six standard of living indicators or in three standard of living indicators and one health or education indicator, or in two health or education indicators. This requirement makes the MPI less sensitive to such assumption.
- Intra-household inequalities may be severe, but these could not be captured.
- While the MPI goes well beyond a headcount ratio to include the intensity of poverty, it does not measure inequality among the poor, although a separate measure of inequality has been published since 2019 (variance of individual deprivation scores of poor people). Also, decompositions by groups can be used to reveal group-based inequalities.
- The estimates presented are mostly based on publicly available data and cover various years between 2008 and 2019, which limits direct cross-country comparability.

attributes.name: ocn.006b Projected Ocean Acidification for Coral Reefs
Projected Ocean Acidification: Suitability for Coral Reefs
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
This dataset shows projections of aragonite saturation in the world’s oceans from 2006-2099, described in terms of suitability for coral reefs. The aragonite saturation state (Ωarag) is commonly used to track ocean acidification because it is a measure of carbonate ion concentration, which indicates the availability of the calcium carbonate that is widely used by marine calcifiers, from lobsters to clams to starfish. Aragonite itself is the building block of stony corals that are the primary framework and habitat builders of coral reef ecosystems. Corals and other calcifiers are most likely to survive and reproduce when the aragonite saturation state is greater than 4. Saturation above 3.5 is adequate; above 3 is considered marginal, with growth difficult. When the saturation state falls below 3, these organisms are in danger. Below 1, reefs, shells, and other aragonite structures begin to dissolve entirely.

  
  
These projections are based on future greenhouse gas emission rates determined by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change’s (IPCC’s) Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP) 8.5. The RCP 8.5 scenario presumes no decrease in greenhouse gas emission rates within the 21st century. More information on these scenarios can be found [here](http://tntcat.iiasa.ac.at:8787/RcpDb/dsd?Action=htmlpage&page=about). The projections have a spatial resolution of 1 degree, and cover the entire globe, although the significance of carbonate ion concentrations outside of areas containing warm-water coral reefs is beyond the scope of this discussion.  

  
  
The dataset was created by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) National Environmental Satellite, Data and Information Service (NESDIS) as part of their Coral Reef Watch program. It was created as a way to both incite and inform discussions about the effects of climate change on coral reefs. These may be dramatic: the predicted acidification during the 21st century would be a greater change than possibly at any time in the last 300 million years.

  
  
Coral reefs are among the most biologically rich and productive ecosystems on earth and provide valuable ecosystem benefits to millions of people in coastal areas. They are, however, widely threatened by both local threats (such as overfishing, pollution, and direct physical damage) and the global threats of ocean warming and acidification. These have already caused widespread damage to most of the world’s coral reefs, resulting in reduced areas of living coral, increased algal cover, diminished species diversity, and lower fish abundance, as well as degraded economic and social benefits to many coastal communities.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
Ensembles of climate models were used to generate projections of the year when severe coral bleaching events will start to occur annually, and of changes in Ωarag. The models were used to generate projected monthly data for the following variables: sea surface temperature (SST), surface pressure of CO₂, pH, and salinity. Each model independently generated monthly data for the listed variables, and these model outputs were then adjusted to the mean and annual cycle of observations of SST based on the [OISST V2 1982‐2005 climatology](https://www.ncdc.noaa.gov/oisst/optimum-interpolation-sea-surface-temperature-oisst-v20). 

  
  
Projections were generated for all four RCP scenarios (known as RCP 2.6, 4.5, 6.0, and 8.5); those corresponding to RCP 8.5 were produced using 9 fully coupled models in the [Coupled Model Intercomparison Project 5 (CMIP5)](https://esgf-node.llnl.gov/projects/cmip5/). For each model, Ωarag was computed independently on the basis of those four key variables, as forecast by that same model, by adopting the routines of the Matlab program [CO2SYS](https://cdiac.ess-dive.lbl.gov/ftp/oceans/co2sys/CO2SYS_calc_MATLAB_v1.1/). Finally, the calculated Ωarag projections from all models were combined, as averaging over multiple models can reduce errors and generally increases the accuracy, skill, and consistency of model forecasts.

  
  
All modeled data were remapped to a 1º resolution. Some model outputs were reduced to a sub-set of only reef locations. These were obtained from the United Nations Environmental Program-World Conservation Monitoring Center’s [Millennium Coral Reef Mapping Project Seascape](http://imars.usf.edu/MC/). A cell was counted as a reef cell if it contained any tropical coral reefs according to the original Seascape database.

  
  
For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/gcb.12394).
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. Ωarag is projected annually, but shown on Resource Watch only at decadal intervals. The full dataset also includes projections of coral bleaching and reductions in calcification, as well as additional ocean acidification projections, under four climate scenarios (RCP 2.6, 4.5, 6.0, 8.5). For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/tree/master/ocn_006alt_projected_ocean_acidification_coral_reefs).  
  
### Disclaimer

info.technical_title: Projections of Coral Bleaching and Ocean Acidification for Coral Reef Areas
info.functions: Projected suitability of conditions for coral reefs vis a vis ocean acidification, as indicated by carbonate ion concentration
info.cautions:
- Data and images hosted on the STAR webservers are not official NOAA operational products, and are provided only as examples for experimental use by remote sensing researchers, experienced meteorologists, or oceanographers. Although STAR provides "operational" data for some products, the STAR website primarily hosts examples of ongoing experimental product development. STAR pages and data sources may therefore be interrupted, changed, or canceled at any time without notice. STAR websites are not managed to meet operational data standards of uptime or redundant operations.
  
  
 - Climate model resolution is very coarse. A 1º grid cell can contain many individual coral reefs. Each reef can in turn be highly diverse in terms of the communities present, geomorphology, and level of stress from human activities. All of these will determine the local spatial and temporal patterns of impacts from acidification and thermal stress. 
  
  
 - The models describe surface and oceanic waters only and thus do not resolve near reef and near-coastal processes such as upwelling that can influence Ωarag and sea temperatures. Also, the models do not reflect the temporal (diurnal, weekly) variability in Ωarag on reefs. There are considerable biases in the representation of the annual cycle in the models. - There are the standard issues with the use of climate model data, in that all models used have uncertainties and a varying capacity to project trends in key drivers of climate in the tropics such as the El Niño Southern Oscillation.

attributes.name: foo.069.rw0 Relative Change in Crop Yield
Relative Change in Crop Yield
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
Relative change in crop yield shows climate projections for crop yield at the national and sub-national levels under different concentration pathways (RCP 4.5 and 8.5). Data is aggregated annually for either national or sub-national boundaries and depict changes in crop yield over time from 2015 through 2050. Changes in yield are compared to the reference period of 1986-2006 and are shown in percentages.

Understanding how climate change will affect crop yields is important for agricultural planning, food security, and global commodity flows. This dataset provides needed information on how climate change will impact yield under several emissions scenarios at the country and provincial levels and for near- and longer-term timeframes. The global economy is intimately tied to agricultural production, and this provides insight into future changes that will have impact on global systems.

Climate Analytics is dedicated to advancing scientific literacy of climate change and providing support and capacity building to stakeholders. They support science-based policy to enable sustainable development and provide solutions to climate change policy challenges.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
Input data for crop yield change uses greenhouse gas concentration scenarios derived from the Representative Concentration Pathways (RCP) framework, which was developed within the Coupled Intercomparison Modeling Project 5 (CMIP5) and is widely used in the climate modeling community. RCP 4.5 depicts an intermediate scenario whereas 8.5 represents a high emissions pathway. Other data is derived from the Inter-Sectoral Impact Model Intercomparison Project (ISIMIP), which provides changes in biophysical systems and extreme events.
 
Climate projections for crop yield were modeled for different emissions scenarios from 2015 to 2100 and are compared against the baseline period of 1986-2006. Results show the annual average changes in crop yield over the area of interest (national/sub-national levels). Projections of future impacts to changes in crop yield are calculated assuming that socio-economic (population, land-use, etc.) factors remain constant at 2005 levels.
 
For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](http://climate-impact-explorer.climateanalytics.org/methodology/).
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Our data catalog also shows Relative Humidity data from Climate Analytics. Additional projections for other crops, impacts, emissions scenarios, and timeframes are also produced by Climate Analytics. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on WRI’s data catalog. See the documentation on how we processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/tree/master/foo_069_rw0_relative_change_crop_yield). This data has been mapped on our data catalog by joining it with Natural Earth boundaries.

attributes.name: Cambio relativo en el rendimiento de los cultivos
attributes.description:
### Visión general  
  
El cambio relativo en el rendimiento de los cultivos muestra proyecciones climáticas para el rendimiento de los cultivos a nivel nacional y subnacional bajo diferentes vías de concentración (RCP 4.5 y 8.5). Los datos se agregan anualmente para las fronteras nacionales o subnacionales y representan los cambios en el rendimiento de los cultivos a lo largo del tiempo desde 2015 hasta 2050. Los cambios en el rendimiento se comparan con el período de referencia de 1986-2006 y se muestran en porcentajes.

Comprender cómo el cambio climático afectará los rendimientos de los cultivos es importante para la planificación agrícola, la seguridad alimentaria y los flujos mundiales de productos básicos. Este conjunto de datos proporciona la información necesaria sobre cómo el cambio climático afectará el rendimiento en varios escenarios de emisiones a nivel nacional y provincial y para plazos a corto y largo plazo. La economía mundial está íntimamente ligada a la producción agrícola, y esto proporciona información sobre los cambios futuros que tendrán un impacto en los sistemas globales.

Climate Analytics se dedica a promover la alfabetización científica sobre el cambio climático y a brindar apoyo y desarrollo de capacidades a las partes interesadas. Apoyan políticas basadas en la ciencia para permitir el desarrollo sostenible y proporcionar soluciones a los desafíos de las políticas de cambio climático.
  
### Metodología  
  
Los datos de entrada para el cambio en el rendimiento de los cultivos utilizan escenarios de concentración de gases de efecto invernadero derivados del marco de las Vías de Concentración Representativas (RCP), que se desarrolló dentro del Proyecto de Modelado de Intercomparación Acoplada 5 (CMIP5) y es ampliamente utilizado en la comunidad de modelado climático. RCP 4.5 representa un escenario intermedio, mientras que 8.5 representa una vía de altas emisiones. Otros datos se derivan del Proyecto de Intercomparación del Modelo de Impacto Intersectorial (ISIMIP), que proporciona cambios en los sistemas biofísicos y eventos extremos.
 
Las proyecciones climáticas para el rendimiento de los cultivos se modelaron para diferentes escenarios de emisiones de 2015 a 2100 y se comparan con el período de referencia de 1986-2006. Los resultados muestran los cambios promedio anuales en el rendimiento de los cultivos sobre el área de interés (nivel nacional / subnacional). Las proyecciones de los impactos futuros en los cambios en el rendimiento de los cultivos se calculan teniendo en cuenta que los factores socioeconómicos (población, uso de la tierra, etc.) permanecen constantes en los niveles de 2005.
 
Para obtener la documentación completa, consulte la fuente [metodología](http://climate-impact-explorer.climateanalytics.org/methodology/).
  
### Información adicional  
  
Nuestro catálogo de datos también muestra datos de humedad relativa de Climate Analytics. Climate Analytics también produce proyecciones adicionales para otros cultivos, impactos, escenarios de emisiones y marcos de tiempo. Para acceder al conjunto de datos completo e información adicional, haga clic en el botón "Más información".  
  
### Visualización de los datos  
  
Nuestro equipo reformateó este conjunto de datos antes de mostrarlo en el catálogo de datos de la IRG. Consulte la documentación sobre cómo procesamos los datos en [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/tree/master/foo_069_rw0_relative_change_crop_yield). Estos datos se han mapeado en nuestro catálogo de datos uniéndolos con los límites naturales de la Tierra.  
  
### Descargo de responsabilidad  
  
Extractos de esta página de descripción fueron tomados de los metadatos de origen.

attributes.name: பயிர் விளைச்சலில் ஒப்பீட்டு மாற்றம்
attributes.description:
### கண்ணோட்டம்  
  
பயிர் மகசூலில் ஒப்பீட்டு மாற்றம், வெவ்வேறு செறிவு பாதைகளின் கீழ் தேசிய மற்றும் துணை தேசிய மட்டங்களில் பயிர் மகசூலுக்கான காலநிலை கணிப்புகளைக் காட்டுகிறது (ஆர்சிபி 4.5 மற்றும் 8.5). தேசிய அல்லது துணை தேசிய எல்லைகளுக்காக ஆண்டுதோறும் தரவுகள் திரட்டப்பட்டு, 2015 முதல் 2050 வரையிலான காலத்தில் பயிர் விளைச்சலில் ஏற்படும் மாற்றங்களை சித்தரிக்கின்றன. விளைச்சலில் ஏற்படும் மாற்றங்கள் 1986-2006 ஆம் ஆண்டின் குறிப்புக் காலத்துடன் ஒப்பிடப்பட்டு, அவை சதவீதங்களில் காட்டப்பட்டுள்ளன.

பருவநிலை மாற்றம் பயிர் விளைச்சலை எவ்வாறு பாதிக்கும் என்பதைப் புரிந்துகொள்வது விவசாயத் திட்டமிடல், உணவுப் பாதுகாப்பு மற்றும் உலகளாவிய பொருட்களின் பாய்வுகளுக்கு முக்கியமானது. இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பு காலநிலை மாற்றம் நாடு மற்றும் மாகாண மட்டங்களில் பல உமிழ்வு காட்சிகளின் கீழ் விளைச்சலை எவ்வாறு பாதிக்கும் என்பது குறித்த தேவையான தகவல்களை வழங்குகிறது மற்றும் அருகிலுள்ள மற்றும் நீண்ட கால வரையறைகளுக்கு. உலகளாவிய பொருளாதாரம் விவசாய உற்பத்தியுடன் நெருக்கமாக பிணைந்துள்ளது, மேலும் இது உலகளாவிய அமைப்புகளில் தாக்கத்தை ஏற்படுத்தும் எதிர்கால மாற்றங்கள் பற்றிய நுண்ணறிவை வழங்குகிறது.

காலநிலை பகுப்பாய்வு என்பது காலநிலை மாற்றம் குறித்த விஞ்ஞான ரீதியான கல்வியறிவை மேம்படுத்துவதற்கும் பங்குதாரர்களுக்கு ஆதரவு மற்றும் திறன் மேம்பாட்டை வழங்குவதற்கும் அர்ப்பணிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. அவை நிலையான வளர்ச்சியை செயல்படுத்தவும், காலநிலை மாற்ற கொள்கை சவால்களுக்கு தீர்வுகளை வழங்கவும் அறிவியல் அடிப்படையிலான கொள்கையை ஆதரிக்கின்றன.
  
### முறைமை  
  
பயிர் மகசூல் மாற்றத்திற்கான உள்ளீட்டுத் தரவு பிரதிநிதித்துவ செறிவு பாதைகள் (ஆர்.சி.பி) கட்டமைப்பிலிருந்து பெறப்பட்ட கிரீன்ஹவுஸ் வாயு செறிவு காட்சிகளைப் பயன்படுத்துகிறது, இது இணைந்த இன்டர்காம்பரிசன் மாடலிங் திட்டம் 5 (சி.எம்.ஐ.பி 5) க்குள் உருவாக்கப்பட்டது மற்றும் காலநிலை மாடலிங் சமூகத்தில் பரவலாகப் பயன்படுத்தப்படுகிறது. ஆர்.சி.பி 4.5 ஒரு இடைநிலை காட்சியை சித்தரிக்கிறது, அதே நேரத்தில் 8.5 அதிக உமிழ்வு பாதையைக் குறிக்கிறது. பிற தரவுகள் துறைகளுக்கிடையிலான தாக்க மாதிரி இன்டர்காம்பாரிசன் திட்டத்திலிருந்து (ஐ.எஸ்.ஐ.எம்.ஐ.பி) பெறப்படுகின்றன, இது உயிர் இயற்பியல் அமைப்புகள் மற்றும் தீவிர நிகழ்வுகளில் மாற்றங்களை வழங்குகிறது.
 
பயிர் மகசூலுக்கான காலநிலை கணிப்புகள் 2015 முதல் 2100 வரையிலான வெவ்வேறு உமிழ்வு காட்சிகளுக்கு மாதிரியாக இருந்தன, மேலும் அவை 1986-2006 இன் அடிப்படை காலத்துடன் ஒப்பிடப்படுகின்றன. வட்டி பகுதியில் (தேசிய / துணை தேசிய மட்டங்கள்) பயிர் விளைச்சலில் வருடாந்திர சராசரி மாற்றங்களை முடிவுகள் காட்டுகின்றன. பயிர் விளைச்சலில் ஏற்படும் மாற்றங்களுக்கான எதிர்கால தாக்கங்களின் கணிப்புகள் சமூக-பொருளாதார (மக்கள்தொகை, நிலப் பயன்பாடு, முதலியன) காரணிகள் 2005 மட்டங்களில் மாறாமல் இருப்பதாகக் கருதி கணக்கிடப்படுகின்றன.
 
முழு ஆவணப்படுத்தலுக்கு, தயவுசெய்து மூலத்தைப் பார்க்கவும் [வழிமுறை](http://climate-தாக்கம்-explorer.climateanalytics.org/methodology/).
  
### கூடுதல் தகவல்  
  
எங்கள் தரவு அட்டவணை காலநிலை பகுப்பாய்வு இருந்து ஒப்பீட்டு ஈரப்பதம் தரவு காட்டுகிறது. பிற பயிர்களுக்கான கூடுதல் கணிப்புகள், தாக்கங்கள், உமிழ்வு காட்சிகள் மற்றும் காலக்கெடு ஆகியவையும் காலநிலை பகுப்பாய்வுகளால் தயாரிக்கப்படுகின்றன. முழு தரவுத்தொகுப்பு மற்றும் கூடுதல் தகவலுக்கான அணுகலுக்கு, "மேலும் அறிக" பொத்தானைக் கிளிக் செய்க.  
  
### தரவை காட்சிப்படுத்தல்  
  
WRI இன் தரவு அட்டவணையில் காண்பிக்கப்படுவதற்கு முன்பு எங்கள் குழு இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பை மறுவடிவமைத்தது. [Github] (https://github.com/resource-வாட்ச்/data-pre-Processing/tree/master/foo_069_rw0_relative_change_crop_yield) இல் உள்ள தரவை நாங்கள் எவ்வாறு செயலாக்கினோம் என்பதற்கான ஆவணப்படுத்தலைப் பார்க்கவும். இந்த தரவு இயற்கை பூமி எல்லைகளுடன் இணைப்பதன் மூலம் எங்கள் தரவு அட்டவணையில் வரைபடமாக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.  
  
### பொறுப்புத்துறப்பு  
  
இந்த விளக்கப் பக்கத்தின் பகுதிகள் மூல மெட்டாடேட்டாவிலிருந்து எடுக்கப்பட்டன.

info.cautions:
- ஐ.எஸ்.ஐ.எம்.ஐ.பி தரவு 0.5 டிகிரி (பூமத்திய ரேகையில் சுமார் 50 கிலோமீட்டர்) தீர்மானத்தில் மாதிரியாக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது, மேலும் வரைபடங்களை விளக்கும்போது, குறிப்பாக சிறிய தேசிய மற்றும் துணை தேசிய பகுதிகளில் மனதில் வைக்கப்பட வேண்டும்.
- உமிழ்வு காட்சிகள் மக்கள்தொகை, மொத்த உள்நாட்டு உற்பத்தி, ஆற்றல் பயன்பாடு மற்றும் கலவை, நிலப் பயன்பாடு, முதலியன பற்றிய பல்வேறு அனுமானங்களைக் கொண்டிருக்கின்றன, எனவே கணிசமான நிச்சயமற்ற தன்மைகளைக் கொண்டுள்ளன.

attributes.name: పంట దిగుబడిలో సాపేక్ష మార్పు
attributes.description:
### అవలోకనం  
  
పంట దిగుబడిలో సాపేక్ష మార్పు వివిధ సాంద్రత మార్గాల కింద జాతీయ మరియు ఉప-జాతీయ స్థాయిలలో పంట దిగుబడి కోసం వాతావరణ అంచనాలను చూపిస్తుంది (ఆర్ సిపి 4.5 మరియు 8.5). డేటా జాతీయ లేదా ఉప-జాతీయ సరిహద్దుల కోసం వార్షికంగా క్రోడీకరించబడుతుంది మరియు 2015 నుండి 2050 వరకు కాలక్రమేణా పంట దిగుబడిలో మార్పులను వర్ణిస్తుంది. దిగుబడిలో మార్పులను 1986-2006 రిఫరెన్స్ పీరియడ్ తో పోల్చి చూస్తే శాతాల్లో చూపించారు.

వ్యవసాయ ప్రణాళిక, ఆహార భద్రత మరియు ప్రపంచ సరుకుల ప్రవాహాలకు వాతావరణ మార్పులు పంట దిగుబడులను ఎలా ప్రభావితం చేస్తాయో అర్థం చేసుకోవడం చాలా ముఖ్యం. ఈ డేటాసెట్ దేశం మరియు ప్రాంతీయ స్థాయిల్లో అనేక ఉద్గారాల దృష్టాంతాల కింద మరియు సమీప మరియు దీర్ఘకాలిక కాలవ్యవధులలో వాతావరణ మార్పు దిగుబడిని ఎలా ప్రభావితం చేస్తుందనే దానిపై అవసరమైన సమాచారాన్ని అందిస్తుంది. ప్రపంచ ఆర్థిక వ్యవస్థ వ్యవసాయ ఉత్పత్తితో సన్నిహితంగా ముడిపడి ఉంది, మరియు ఇది ప్రపంచ వ్యవస్థలపై ప్రభావం చూపే భవిష్యత్తు మార్పులపై అంతర్దృష్టిని అందిస్తుంది.

క్లైమేట్ ఎనలిటిక్స్ వాతావరణ మార్పుల యొక్క శాస్త్రీయ అక్షరాస్యతను పెంపొందించడానికి మరియు వాటాదారులకు మద్దతు మరియు సామర్థ్యాన్ని పెంపొందించడానికి అంకితం చేయబడింది. వారు సుస్థిర అభివృద్ధిని ప్రారంభించడానికి మరియు వాతావరణ మార్పు విధాన సవాళ్లకు పరిష్కారాలను అందించడానికి సైన్స్ ఆధారిత విధానానికి మద్దతు ఇస్తారు.
  
#### మెథడాలజీ  
  
పంట దిగుబడి మార్పు కొరకు ఇన్ పుట్ డేటా రిప్రజెంటేటివ్ కాన్సంట్రేషన్ పాత్ వేస్ (ఆర్ సిపి) ఫ్రేమ్ వర్క్ నుంచి పొందిన గ్రీన్ హౌస్ గ్యాస్ గాఢత దృష్టాంతాలను ఉపయోగిస్తుంది, ఇది కపుల్డ్ ఇంటర్ కంపారిసన్ మోడలింగ్ ప్రాజెక్ట్ 5 (సిఎమ్ ఐపి5) లోపల అభివృద్ధి చేయబడింది మరియు ఇది క్లైమేట్ మోడలింగ్ కమ్యూనిటీలో విస్తృతంగా ఉపయోగించబడుతుంది. ఆర్ సిపి 4.5 మధ్యంతర దృష్టాంతాన్ని వర్ణిస్తుంది, అయితే 8.5 అధిక ఉద్గారాల మార్గాన్ని సూచిస్తుంది. ఇతర డేటా ఇంటర్ సెక్టోరల్ ఇంపాక్ట్ మోడల్ ఇంటర్ కంపారిసన్ ప్రాజెక్ట్ (ఐఎస్ఐఎమ్ఐపి) నుండి తీసుకోబడింది, ఇది బయోఫిజికల్ సిస్టమ్స్ మరియు విపరీతమైన సంఘటనలలో మార్పులను అందిస్తుంది.
 
పంట దిగుబడి కోసం వాతావరణ అంచనాలు 2015 నుండి 2100 వరకు వివిధ ఉద్గారాల దృష్టాంతాల కోసం నమూనా చేయబడ్డాయి మరియు 1986-2006 యొక్క బేస్ లైన్ కాలంతో పోల్చబడ్డాయి. ఆసక్తి ఉన్న ప్రాంతం (జాతీయ/ఉప-జాతీయ స్థాయిలు) పై పంట దిగుబడిలో వార్షిక సగటు మార్పులను ఫలితాలు చూపుతాయి. 2005 స్థాయిలలో సామాజిక-ఆర్థిక (జనాభా, భూమి-ఉపయోగం మొదలైనవి) కారకాలు స్థిరంగా ఉన్నాయని భావించి పంట దిగుబడిలో మార్పులకు భవిష్యత్తు ప్రభావాల అంచనాలు లెక్కించబడ్డాయి.
 
పూర్తి డాక్యుమెంటేషన్ కొరకు, దయచేసి సోర్స్ [మెథడాలజీ](http://climate-ఇంపాక్ట్-explorer.climateanalytics.org/methodology/) చూడండి.
  
### అదనపు సమాచారం  
  
మా డేటా కేటలాగ్ క్లైమేట్ ఎనలిటిక్స్ నుండి సాపేక్ష ఆర్ద్రత డేటాను కూడా చూపిస్తుంది. ఇతర పంటలు, ప్రభావాలు, ఉద్గారాల దృశ్యాలు మరియు కాలవ్యవధుల కొరకు అదనపు అంచనాలు కూడా క్లైమేట్ ఎనలిటిక్స్ ద్వారా ఉత్పత్తి చేయబడతాయి. పూర్తి డేటాసెట్ మరియు అదనపు సమాచారాన్ని యాక్సెస్ చేసుకోవడానికి, "మరింత తెలుసుకోండి" బటన్ మీద క్లిక్ చేయండి.  
  
### డేటాను విజువలైజ్ చేయడం  
  
డబ్ల్యుఆర్ఐ యొక్క డేటా కేటలాగ్ లో ప్రదర్శించడానికి ముందు మా బృందం ఈ డేటాసెట్ ను పునర్నిర్మించింది. [Github](https://github.com/resource-వాచ్/డేటా-ప్రీ-ప్రాసెసింగ్/ట్రీ/మాస్టర్/foo_069_rw0_relative_change_crop_yield)పై డేటాను మేం ఏవిధంగా ప్రాసెస్ చేశాం అనే దానిపై డాక్యుమెంటేషన్ ని చూడండి. ఈ డేటా సహజ భూమి సరిహద్దులతో జతచేయడం ద్వారా మా డేటా కేటలాగ్ లో మ్యాప్ చేయబడింది.  
  
### డిస్ క్లెయిమర్  
  
ఈ వివరణ పేజీ యొక్క సారాంశాలు మూల మెటాడేటా నుండి తీసుకోబడ్డాయి.

attributes.name: cit.038.nrt Air Quality - Modeled Forecast - WACCM (SO₂)
Air Quality: Sulfur Dioxide (SO₂) Modeled Next-day Forecast
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
This dataset shows forecasted sulfur dioxide (SO₂) concentrations at Earth's surface, modeled by the Whole Atmosphere Community Climate Model (WACCM).   
  
Sulfur dioxide is a colorless, reactive air pollutant with a strong odor. The gas is a respiratory irritant that can harm human health. According to the [Australian Department of Environment and Energy](https://www.environment.gov.au/protection/publications/factsheet-sulfur-dioxide-so2), sulfur dioxide irritates the nose, throat, and airways. It can cause shortness of breath, coughing, wheezing, or a tight feeling around the chest. High concentrations of sulfur dioxide can affect lung function, worsen asthma attacks, and worsen existing heart disease in sensitive groups.  
  
Most sulfur dioxide emissions come from the burning of coal, oil or gas for electricity and transportation; these fossil fuels contain sulfur, which is emitted as sulfur dioxide when burned. Sulfur dioxide does not contribute to global warming, but it [reacts easily](https://www.environment.gov.au/protection/publications/factsheet-sulfur-dioxide-so2) with other substances to form harmful compounds such as sulfuric acid and small sulfate particles. When sulfur dioxide reacts with water and oxygen, it [creates acid rain](https://www.epa.gov/acidrain/what-acid-rain). Acid rain has a number of [environmental impacts](https://www.ucsusa.org/clean-energy/coal-and-other-fossil-fuels/hidden-cost-of-fossils), including making lakes, rivers, wetlands and other water bodies more acidic, which can be harmful to fish and other aquatic wildlife.  
  
WACCM creates global forecasts for a variety of other air quality indicators, as well. While this dataset shows forecasted sulfur dioxide concentrations, Resource Watch also shows WACCM forecasts for [fine particulate matter (PM2.5)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-PM-25), [black carbon (BC)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-Black-Carbon), [ozone (O₃)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-O), [nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-NO), and [carbon monoxide (CO)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-CO).  WACCM runs the model daily, and on their website you can find forecasted concentrations for each compound up to nine days into the future at three-hour time steps.   
  
WACCM was developed by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) and the University Corporation for Atmospheric Research (UCAR). The data has global coverage at 1.9 x 2.5 degree resolution.  
  
### Methodology  
  
WACCM is a comprehensive numerical model, driven by meteorological fields from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration’s (NASA) Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO) Goddard Earth Observing System Model, Version 5 (GEOS-5) model. The development of WACCM is an inter-divisional collaboration that unifies modeling from the High Altitude Observatory ([HAO](http://www2.hao.ucar.edu/)), the Atmospheric Chemistry Observations and Modeling ([ACOM](https://www2.acom.ucar.edu/)) Laboratory, and the Climate and Global Dynamics ([CGD](http://www2.cgd.ucar.edu/)) Laboratory. Upper atmospheric modeling from HAO, middle atmospheric modeling from ACOM, and tropospheric modeling from CGD are combined using the NCAR [Community Earth System Model (CESM)](http://www.cesm.ucar.edu/) as a common numerical framework. For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://opensky.ucar.edu/islandora/object/articles%3A12836).  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows WACCM forecasts for [fine particulate matter (PM2.5)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-PM-25), [black carbon (BC)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-Black-Carbon), [ozone (O₃)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-O), [nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-NO), and [carbon monoxide (CO)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit038-Air-Quality-Modeled-Forecast-WACCM-CO).
  
  

Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. Additional forecasted data for other compounds, times, and levels of the atmosphere are also produced by WACCM. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.
  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/nrt-scripts/tree/master/cit_038_waccm_atmospheric_chemistry_model).  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

attributes.name: Air Quality: Carbon Monoxide (CO) Station Measurements
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Air Quality: Carbon Monoxide (CO) Station Measurements dataset is a global dataset that shows real-time air quality data from around the world for carbon monoxide (CO) . It presents data collected from government and international organizations at the station level. This means the data is more accurate to specific areas than national or regional data. As of June 2017 OpenAQ data was available for 5,400 locations in 48 countries and is being continually updated with new sources.

  
  
Carbon monoxide (CO) is a colorless, odorless gas that can be harmful when inhaled in large amounts. CO is released during combustion, so the largest outdoor sources of CO are cars, trucks and other vehicles, and machinery that burn fossil fuels. Breathing air with a high concentration of CO reduces the amount of oxygen that can be transported in the bloodstream to critical organs like the heart and brain. At very high levels, which are possible indoors or in other enclosed environments, CO can cause dizziness, confusion, unconsciousness, and death. Very high levels of CO are not likely to occur outdoors. However, when CO levels are elevated outdoors it can be of particular concern to people with preexisting heart disease. These people already have a reduced ability for getting oxygenated blood to their heart. They are especially vulnerable to the effects of CO when exercising or under increased stress. In these situations, short-term exposure to elevated CO may result in reduced oxygen to the heart accompanied by chest pain also known as angina.

  
  
OpenAQ is an open-source project to surface live, real-time air quality data from around the world. Its “mission is to enable previously impossible science, impact policy, and empower the public to fight air pollution.” Scientists, researchers, developers, and citizens can use these data to understand how air quality in different locations changes over time.

  
  
Resource Watch also shows continually updated air quality data from OpenAQ on [inhalable particulates (PM10)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit003bnrt-Air-Quality-Measurements-PM-10), [sulfur dioxide (SO₂)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit003cairqualityso2), [nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit003dnrt-Air-Quality-Measurements-NO), [ozone (O₃)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit003cnrt-Air-Quality-Measurements-O), [fine particulate matter (PM2.5)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit003anrt-Air-Quality-Measurements-PM-25), and [black carbon (BC)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit003gnrt-Air-Quality-Measurements-BC_1).  
  
### Methodology  
  
The carbon monoxide station measurement dataset was produced and is continually updated by aggregating data from permanent outdoor air quality measures. Data was collected only from official sources, including government entities and international organizations. As of June 2017 OpenAQ data was available for 5,400 locations in 48 countries. For data to be included it had to meet three criteria:

  
  
1. The “raw” measurement data on physical particle concentration had to be available on the originating site.
  
  
2. The data needed to be at the “station level.” It is unacceptable if it is presented in an aggregated form for a city or region.
  
  
3. The data needed to be continuously updated at intervals between 10 minutes and 24 hours.

  
  
After the data was collected it was put into tables. Data was collected using the source organization’s Air Quality Index (AQI) classifications. The final dataset was mapped in vector format at a subnational level with each measurement station showing local particle concentration. OpenAQ continually reviews each data source website for updated values and updates the dataset every hour.

  
  
For the full documentation, please click on the “Learn more” button.
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows continually updated air quality data from OpenAQ on [inhalable particulates (PM10)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit003bnrt-Air-Quality-Measurements-PM-10), [sulfur dioxide (SO₂)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit003cairqualityso2), [nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit003dnrt-Air-Quality-Measurements-NO), [ozone (O₃)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit003cnrt-Air-Quality-Measurements-O), [fine particulate matter (PM2.5)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit003anrt-Air-Quality-Measurements-PM-25), and [black carbon (BC)](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/cit003gnrt-Air-Quality-Measurements-BC_1).
  
  

Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/nrt-scripts/tree/master/cit_003_air_quality). Coordinates provided in the source data were used to map these data for display on Resource Watch.

Air Quality: Mexico City Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Forecast
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Air Quality: Mexico City Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Forecast dataset provides weather and air quality forecasts for Mexico City. This dataset represents the forecasted density of fine particulate matter in micrograms per cubic meter (µg/m3). The forecast offers an hourly estimate on fine particulate matter density with a spatial resolution of 1 kilometer (km), encompassing Mexico CIty and its Metropolitan Area (MCMA).

  
  
PM2.5 are fine inhalable particles, with diameters that are generally 2.5 micrometers and smaller. These particles come in many sizes and shapes and can be made up of hundreds of different chemicals. Some are emitted directly from a source, such as construction sites or smokestacks, while others are created from complex reactions in the atmosphere. According to the [U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)](https://www.epa.gov/pm-pollution/particulate-matter-pm-basics) the size of these particles allows them to get deep into the lungs, and some may even go into the bloodstream. Some of the health problems related to the exposure to PM2.5 include: premature death in people with heart or lung disease, nonfatal heart attacks, irregular heartbeat, aggravated asthma, decreased lung function, and increased respiratory symptoms. People with heart or lung diseases, children, and older adults are most likely to be affected by particle pollution exposure. According to the [Mexico City Ministry of the Environment (SEDEMA)]((http://www.aire.cdmx.gob.mx/descargas/publicaciones/flippingbook/informe_anual_calidad_aire_2017/mobile/informe_anual_calidad_aire_2017v3.pdf), PM2.5 emissions in the MCMA frequently exceed the limits established byMexican regulations, as well as the standards of the World Health Organization (WHO) and the EPA. The city's suburbs tend to have the highest levels of this pollutant, which is associated with the industrial activity in the area. Showcasing the spatial distribution of PM2.5 in the MCMA will provide insight about the way a city can produce information according to its needs while complementing global air quality models. The forecast helps the Mexico CIty government to issue health warnings based on the expected air quality for a given day, like recommending citizens to avoid open-air exercise or to limit their use of fossil fuel vehicles.

  
  
The forecast was generated by the SEDEMA with help from the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC). SEDEMA provides a tool for the inhabitants of MCMA to make well-informed decisions about dangerous air pollution activity on a given day. SEDEMA works on five environmental issues: air quality and climate change, land conservation and biodiversity, sustainable urban infrastructure, water supply and quality, and environmental communication and education.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
The dataset is comprised of the following models:
  
  
Weather: Estimates the weather conditions of the MCMA using data from global systems. It harnesses the [Weather Research and Forecasting Model-Advanced Research (WRF-ARW)](https://www.mmm.ucar.edu/weather-research-and-forecasting-model), which is a mesoscale numerical weather prediction system designed for both atmospheric research and operational forecasting applications. The model generates  temperature, wind, rainfall and solar radiation, among other weather related indicators.among others.
  
  
Emissions: This model makes use of emission inventories for the MCMA to estimate PM2.5  levels on an hourly basis, as well as its geospatial distribution.
  
  
Chemical Transport: This model harnesses the outputs from the weather and emissions models as well as other chemical and physical mechanisms to simulate transformations in the atmosphere and the influence of weather dynamics in these processes. For this purpose, the [Community Multiscale Air Quality Modeling System (CMAQ)] (https://www.cmascenter.org/cmaq/) is employed to forecast the behavior of the pollutants in the MCMA.

  
  
For the full documentation, please click on the “Learn more” button.
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows forecasts for [Air Quality: Mexico City Carbon Monoxide (CO) forecast](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/e39f5910-a9b8-4ef1-b4b4-f6b141b15541), [Air Quality: Mexico City Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂) Forecast](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/918ba6bc-69ed-44fb-9b29-5fb445fdfef6),[Air Quality: Mexico City Ozone (O₃) Forecast](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/00d6bae1-e105-4165-8230-ee73a8128538) and [Air Quality: Mexico City Sulfur Dioxide (SO₂)Forecast](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/59790e64-d95d-43fa-a124-5c7eb1cb4456)

  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. The source also includes the outputs for their weather model as well as the measurements of the Mexico City Weather Monitoring System (SIMAT) using their air quality index. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.
  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/nrt-scripts/tree/master/loc_mcaqf_mexico_city_aq_forecast).

attributes.name: Crop Suitability Classes
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Global Agro-Ecological Zoning version 4 (GAEZ v4) dataset assesses current and future agricultural resources and their potential. It is a standardized framework allowing for the characterization of climate, soil, and terrain conditions that are relevant for agricultural production. Data from the Fourth theme, Suitability and Attainable Yield, is displayed here. It combines multiple inputs ranging from climatic conditions, water supply, and agricultural input levels to spatially map the suitability of 4 different crops globally. Outputs are presented at 5 arc minutes resolution, which is approximately 9 km x 9 km at the equator but [changes with distance from the equator](https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-of-latitude-and-longitude-distance-4070616).

​​Information on the current and future use of land resources are important for agricultural decision-making with implications on food security, sustainability of land and water resources, and agricultural development and policies. The GAEZ v4 dataset brings together multiple data sources to provide information on current crop suitability and assess its potential impact from climate change. Coffee, Cotton, Dryland Rice, and Wetland Rice are important commodities around the globe and the Crop Suitability Class provides important spatial information on where these commodities will thrive or face challenges in future timeframes and under different climate scenarios. Understanding what changes may occur in the future will enable different actors the ability to increase resilience, develop techniques or policies to alleviate potential challenges, and maintain food security.

The Food and Agricultural Organization of the United Nations (FAO) together with the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA) began developing the GAEZ modeling framework in the early 1980s to provide current data on the state of agricultural resources. It has since expanded to support sustainable agricultural development and provide key information on current and future risks to agricultural production, crop development, land productivity, and impacts from climate change.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
Multiple datasets were used as inputs to the GAEZ v4 modeling framework and provide data on historic and future climate attributes, soil and terrain resources, land cover, protected land, biodiversity areas, water resources, administrative units, population, and livestock. Historical climate data comes from the Climatic Research Unit TS v3.21 datasets which include monthly climate information. Future climate data is derived from multiple climate model outputs for four (2.6, 4.5, 6, 8.5) Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs) from the Fifth Assessment Report (AR5) of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change.

Data processing was broken into several steps and seven main modules summarize the necessary steps within the GAEZ v4 modeling framework. Outputs from each of the modules are categorized into six main themes: 1) Land and Water Resources, 2) Agro-climatic Resources, 3) Agro-climatic Potential Yield, 4) Suitability and Attainable Yield, 5) Actual Yields and Production, and 6) Yield and Production Gaps.
 
The Suitability Class sub-theme falls under Theme Four of the outputs and Module V of the modeling framework. Module V integrates results from the first four modules and combines agro-climatic potential yields with soil and terrain evaluation results. This Module identifies in each grid cell its respective soil types and slope classes and then assesses and assigns a suitability rating and simulated potential yield. Results are then aggregated and mapped for each historic and future 30-year period by crop, input level, and water source and have a spatial resolution of 5 arc minutes (approximately 9 km at the equator).
 
Suitability classes are calculated from the normalized Suitability Index (SI), where:
           
SI = 100 x (90 x VS + 70 x S + 50 x MS + 30 x mS + 15 x VmS + 0 x NS) / 0.9
 
SI values can range from 0 to 10,000 and the acronyms that are underlying suitability classes are defined as follows: VS = very suitable, S = suitable, MS = moderately suitable, mS = marginally suitable, VmS = very marginally suitable, and NS = not suitable. These six categories represent the shares of area extents of the different suitability classes in a grid cell. SI is calculated for each of the 53 crops by the level of input, management, and water supply system. The resultant SI in each grid cell is then grouped into eight classes depicting the aggregate crop suitability as:
- Very high: SI > 8,500
- High: 7,000 < SI ≤ 8,500
- Good: 5,550 < SI ≤ 7,000
- Medium: 4,000 < SI ≤ 5,500
- Moderate: 2,500 < SI ≤ 4,000
- Marginal: 1,000 < SI ≤ 2,500
- Very marginal: 0 < SI ≤ 1,000
- Not suitable: SI = 0
 
For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://www.fao.org/3/cb4744en/cb4744en.pdf).  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Our data catalog shows only a subset of the dataset. The Global Agro-Ecological Zoning version 4 Crop Suitability Index full dataset has data for 53 crops, additional timeframes (1961-1990, 1971-2000, and 2071-2100), RCPs (2.6 and 6.0), water supply (rainfed all phases, gravity irrigation), a low input level option, and a without CO2 fertilization option. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on WRI’s data catalog. See the documentation on how we retrieved the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/blob/master/foo_067_rw0_crop_suitability_class).  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

info.technical_title: GAEZ v4 Suitability Index in Classes; Current Cropland in Grid Cell
info.functions: Suitability for growing cotton, coffee, or rice
info.cautions:
- GAEZ v4 assessment does not encompass all activities related to agriculture. It primarily focuses on the potential for growing crops.
- Results of this dataset should be utilized at the appropriate aggregation levels, which is dependent on the underlying resolution of the input datasets. Input datasets have different spatial resolutions.
- Input datasets are known to have uneven quality and reliability.
- Newer datasets with improved resolution and accuracy were made available after GAEZ datasets were frozen, for example, land cover.
- Land degradation was minimally or not at all accounted for in GAEZ outputs.
- Global generalizations were necessary for certain variables, such as the data on environmental requirements for some crops.
- Socioeconomic data use is limited to the specifications of modes and purpose of agricultural production, the quantification of levels of inputs and management, the inclusion of agricultural prices and the consideration of population numbers and distributions.
- GAEZ utilized an exclusion layer to denote land that is marked either as protection or exclusion status from reliable datasets.

attributes.name: Clases de idoneidad de cultivos
attributes.description:
### Visión general  
  
El conjunto de datos Global Agro-Ecological Zoning versión 4 (GAEZ v4) evalúa los recursos agrícolas actuales y futuros y su potencial. Es un marco estandarizado que permite la caracterización de las condiciones climáticas, del suelo y del terreno que son relevantes para la producción agrícola. Los datos del cuarto tema, Idoneidad y rendimiento alcanzable, se muestran aquí. Combina múltiples insumos que van desde las condiciones climáticas, el suministro de agua y los niveles de insumos agrícolas para mapear espacialmente la idoneidad de 4 cultivos diferentes a nivel mundial. Las salidas se presentan a una resolución de 5 minutos de arco, que es de aproximadamente 9 km x 9 km en el ecuador, pero [cambia con la distancia desde el ecuador] (https://www.thoughtco.com/degree de latitud y longitud-distancia-4070616).

La información sobre el uso actual y futuro de los recursos de tierras es importante para la toma de decisiones agrícolas con implicaciones en la seguridad alimentaria, la sostenibilidad de los recursos de tierra y agua, y el desarrollo y las políticas agrícolas. El conjunto de datos GAEZ v4 reúne múltiples fuentes de datos para proporcionar información sobre la idoneidad actual de los cultivos y evaluar su impacto potencial del cambio climático. El café, el algodón, el arroz de las tierras secas y el arroz de humedales son productos básicos importantes en todo el mundo y la Clase de Idoneidad de Cultivos proporciona información espacial importante sobre dónde prosperarán estos productos básicos o enfrentarán desafíos en futuros marcos de tiempo y en diferentes escenarios climáticos. Comprender qué cambios pueden ocurrir en el futuro permitirá a los diferentes actores la capacidad de aumentar la resiliencia, desarrollar técnicas o políticas para aliviar los desafíos potenciales y mantener la seguridad alimentaria.

La Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Agricultura y la Alimentación (FAO) junto con el Instituto Internacional de Análisis de Sistemas Aplicados (IIASA) comenzaron a desarrollar el marco de modelado GAEZ a principios de la década de 1980 para proporcionar datos actuales sobre el estado de los recursos agrícolas. Desde entonces, se ha expandido para apoyar el desarrollo agrícola sostenible y proporcionar información clave sobre los riesgos actuales y futuros para la producción agrícola, el desarrollo de cultivos, la productividad de la tierra y los impactos del cambio climático.
  
### Metodología  
  
Se utilizaron múltiples conjuntos de datos como insumos para el marco de modelado GAEZ v4 y proporcionan datos sobre atributos climáticos históricos y futuros, recursos de suelo y terreno, cobertura terrestre, tierras protegidas, áreas de biodiversidad, recursos hídricos, unidades administrativas, población y ganado. Los datos climáticos históricos provienen de los conjuntos de datos TS v3.21 de la Unidad de Investigación Climática que incluyen información climática mensual. Los datos climáticos futuros se derivan de múltiples resultados de modelos climáticos para cuatro (2.6, 4.5, 6, 8.5) Vías de Concentración Representativas (PCR) del Quinto Informe de Evaluación (AR5) del Grupo Intergubernamental de Expertos sobre el Cambio Climático.

El procesamiento de datos se dividió en varios pasos y siete módulos principales resumen los pasos necesarios dentro del marco de modelado GAEZ v4. Los resultados de cada uno de los módulos se clasifican en seis temas principales: 1) Recursos de tierra y agua, 2) Recursos agroclimáticos, 3) Rendimiento potencial agroclimático, 4) Idoneidad y rendimiento alcanzable, 5) Rendimientos y producción reales, y 6) Brechas de rendimiento y producción.
 
El subtema de la clase de idoneidad se encuentra bajo el tema cuatro de las salidas y el módulo V del marco de modelado. El Módulo V integra los resultados de los primeros cuatro módulos y combina los rendimientos potenciales agroclimáticos con los resultados de la evaluación del suelo y el terreno. Este módulo identifica en cada celda de la cuadrícula sus respectivos tipos de suelo y clases de pendientes y luego evalúa y asigna una calificación de idoneidad y un rendimiento potencial simulado. Los resultados se agregan y mapean para cada período histórico y futuro de 30 años por cultivo, nivel de entrada y fuente de agua y tienen una resolución espacial de 5 minutos de arco (aproximadamente 9 km en el ecuador).
 
Las clases de idoneidad se calculan a partir del Índice de Idoneidad (SI) normalizado, donde:
           
SI = 100 x (90 x VS + 70 x S + 50 x MS + 30 x mS + 15 x VmS + 0 x NS) / 0,9
 
Los valores de SI pueden variar de 0 a 10.000 y los acrónimos que subyacen a las clases de idoneidad se definen de la siguiente manera: VS = muy adecuado, S = adecuado, MS = moderadamente adecuado, mS = marginalmente adecuado, VmS = muy marginalmente adecuado y NS = no adecuado. Estas seis categorías representan las partes de las extensiones de área de las diferentes clases de idoneidad en una celda de cuadrícula. El SI se calcula para cada uno de los 53 cultivos por el nivel de entrada, manejo y sistema de suministro de agua. El SI resultante en cada celda de cuadrícula se agrupa en ocho clases que representan la idoneidad agregada del cultivo como:
- Muy alto: SI > 8.500
- Alto: 7.000 < SI ≤ 8.500
- Bien: 5.550 < SI ≤ 7.000
- Medio: 4.000 < SI ≤ 5.500
- Moderado: 2.500 < SI ≤ 4.000
- Marginal: 1.000 < SI ≤ 2.500
- Muy marginal: 0 < SI ≤ 1.000
- No apto: SI = 0
 
Para obtener la documentación completa, consulte la fuente [metodología](https://www.fao.org/3/cb4744en/cb4744en.pdf).  
### Información adicional  
  
Nuestro catálogo de datos muestra solo un subconjunto del conjunto de datos. El conjunto de datos completo del Índice de Idoneidad de Cultivos de la versión 4 de la Zonificación Agroecológica Global tiene datos de 53 cultivos, marcos de tiempo adicionales (1961-1990, 1971-2000 y 2071-2100), PCR (2.6 y 6.0), suministro de agua (secano en todas las fases, riego por gravedad), una opción de bajo nivel de entrada y una opción de fertilización sin CO2. Para acceder al conjunto de datos completo e información adicional, haga clic en el botón "Más información".  
  
### Visualización de los datos  
  
Nuestro equipo reformateó este conjunto de datos antes de mostrarlo en el catálogo de datos de la IRG. Consulte la documentación sobre cómo recuperamos los datos en [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/blob/master/foo_067_rw0_crop_suitability_class).  
  
### Descargo de responsabilidad  
  
Extractos de esta página de descripción fueron tomados de los metadatos de origen.

info.cautions:
- La evaluación GAEZ v4 no abarca todas las actividades relacionadas con la agricultura. Se centra principalmente en el potencial para el crecimiento de los cultivos.
- Los resultados de este conjunto de datos deben utilizarse en los niveles de agregación apropiados, lo que depende de la resolución subyacente de los conjuntos de datos de entrada. Los datasets de entrada tienen diferentes resoluciones espaciales.
- Se sabe que los conjuntos de datos de entrada tienen una calidad y confiabilidad desiguales.
- Los conjuntos de datos más nuevos con una resolución y precisión mejoradas se pusieron a disposición después de que los conjuntos de datos GAEZ se congelaron, por ejemplo, la cubierta terrestre.
- La degradación de la tierra se tuvo en cuenta mínimamente o no se tuvo en cuenta en absoluto en los resultados de la GAEZ.
- Las generalizaciones globales fueron necesarias para ciertas variables, como los datos sobre los requisitos ambientales para algunos cultivos.
- El uso de datos socioeconómicos se limita a las especificaciones de los modos y el propósito de la producción agrícola, la cuantificación de los niveles de insumos y la gestión, la inclusión de los precios agrícolas y la consideración del número y la distribución de la población.
- GAEZ utilizó una capa de exclusión para denotar la tierra que está marcada como estado de protección o exclusión de conjuntos de datos confiables.

### கண்ணோட்டம்  
  
உலகளாவிய வேளாண் சூழலியல் மண்டல பதிப்பு 4 (GAEZ v4) தரவுத்தொகுப்பு தற்போதைய மற்றும் எதிர்கால விவசாய வளங்கள் மற்றும் அவற்றின் திறனை மதிப்பிடுகிறது. இது விவசாய உற்பத்திக்கு பொருத்தமான காலநிலை, மண் மற்றும் நிலப்பரப்பு நிலைமைகளின் சிறப்பியல்புகளை அனுமதிக்கும் ஒரு தரப்படுத்தப்பட்ட கட்டமைப்பாகும். நான்காவது கருப்பொருளான பொருத்தப்பாடு மற்றும் அடையக்கூடிய மகசூல் ஆகியவற்றிலிருந்து தரவு இங்கே காட்டப்படுகிறது. இது காலநிலை நிலைமைகள், நீர் வழங்கல் மற்றும் விவசாய உள்ளீடு மட்டங்கள் முதல் உலகளவில் 4 வெவ்வேறு பயிர்களின் பொருத்தத்தை இடஞ்சார்ந்த முறையில் வரைபடமாக்குவது வரை பல உள்ளீடுகளை ஒருங்கிணைக்கிறது. வெளியீடுகள் 5 வில் நிமிட தெளிவுத்திறனில் வழங்கப்படுகின்றன, இது பூமத்திய ரேகையில் தோராயமாக 9 கி.மீ x 9 கி.மீ ஆகும், ஆனால் [பூமத்திய ரேகையிலிருந்து தூரத்துடன் மாற்றங்கள்](https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-ன்-அட்சரேகை-மற்றும்-தீர்க்கரேகை-தூரம்-4070616).

காணி வளங்களின் தற்போதைய மற்றும் எதிர்காலப் பயன்பாடு பற்றிய தகவல்கள், உணவுப் பாதுகாப்பு, காணி மற்றும் நீர் வளங்களின் பேண்தகைமை மற்றும் விவசாய அபிவிருத்தி மற்றும் கொள்கைகள் என்பவற்றில் தாக்கங்களைக் கொண்ட விவசாய தீர்மானங்களை எடுப்பதற்கு முக்கியமானதாகும். GAEZ v4 தரவுத்தொகுப்பு தற்போதைய பயிர் பொருத்தம் பற்றிய தகவல்களை வழங்குவதற்கும் காலநிலை மாற்றத்திலிருந்து அதன் சாத்தியமான தாக்கத்தை மதிப்பிடுவதற்கும் பல தரவு ஆதாரங்களை ஒன்றிணைக்கிறது. காபி, பருத்தி, மானாவாரி நெல் மற்றும் ஈரநில நெல் ஆகியவை உலகெங்கிலும் உள்ள முக்கியமான பொருட்களாகும், மேலும் பயிர் பொருத்துத்திறன் வகுப்பு எதிர்கால கால வரையறைகள் மற்றும் வெவ்வேறு காலநிலை சூழ்நிலைகளில் இந்த பொருட்கள் எங்கு செழித்து வளரும் அல்லது சவால்களை எதிர்கொள்ளும் என்பது குறித்த முக்கியமான இடஞ்சார்ந்த தகவல்களை வழங்குகிறது. எதிர்காலத்தில் என்ன மாற்றங்கள் நிகழலாம் என்பதைப் புரிந்துகொள்வது, பல்வேறு நடிகர்களுக்கு பின்னடைவை அதிகரிக்கும் திறன், சாத்தியமான சவால்களைத் தணிப்பதற்கான நுட்பங்கள் அல்லது கொள்கைகளை உருவாக்குதல் மற்றும் உணவுப் பாதுகாப்பைப் பராமரித்தல் ஆகியவற்றை செயல்படுத்தும்.

ஐக்கிய நாடுகள் சபையின் உணவு மற்றும் விவசாய அமைப்பு (FAO) மற்றும் பிரயோக முறைமை பகுப்பாய்வுக்கான சர்வதேச நிறுவனம் (IIASA) இணைந்து விவசாய வளங்களின் நிலை பற்றிய தற்போதைய தரவுகளை வழங்குவதற்காக 1980 களின் முற்பகுதியில் GAEZ மாதிரியாக்க கட்டமைப்பை அபிவிருத்தி செய்யத் தொடங்கியது. நிலையான விவசாய அபிவிருத்திக்கு ஆதரவளிப்பதற்கும், விவசாய உற்பத்தி, பயிர் அபிவிருத்தி, நில உற்பத்தித்திறன் மற்றும் காலநிலை மாற்றத்தினால் ஏற்படும் தாக்கங்கள் தொடர்பான தற்போதைய மற்றும் எதிர்கால அபாயங்கள் பற்றிய முக்கிய தகவல்களை வழங்குவதற்கும் இது விரிவடைந்துள்ளது.
  
### முறைமை  
  
பல தரவுத்தொகுப்புகள் GAEZ V4 மாடலிங் கட்டமைப்பிற்கான உள்ளீடுகளாகப் பயன்படுத்தப்பட்டன மற்றும் வரலாற்று மற்றும் எதிர்கால காலநிலை பண்புகள், மண் மற்றும் நிலப்பரப்பு வளங்கள், நிலப்பரப்பு, பாதுகாக்கப்பட்ட நிலம், பல்லுயிர்ப் பகுதிகள், நீர் வளங்கள், நிர்வாக அலகுகள், மக்கள்தொகை மற்றும் கால்நடைகள் பற்றிய தரவுகளை வழங்குகின்றன. வரலாற்று காலநிலை தரவுகள் காலநிலை ஆராய்ச்சி அலகு TS v3.21 தரவுத் தொகுப்புகளிலிருந்து வருகின்றன, இதில் மாதாந்திர காலநிலைத் தகவல்களும் அடங்கும். எதிர்கால காலநிலை தரவு நான்கு (2.6, 4.5, 6, 8.5) பிரதிநிதித்துவ செறிவு பாதைகள் (ஆர்.சி.பி) காலநிலை மாற்றம் குறித்த அரசாங்கங்களுக்கு இடையிலான குழுவின் ஐந்தாவது மதிப்பீட்டு அறிக்கையிலிருந்து (ஏ.ஆர்.5) பல காலநிலை மாதிரி வெளியீடுகளிலிருந்து பெறப்படுகிறது.

தரவு செயலாக்கம் பல படிகளாக உடைக்கப்பட்டது மற்றும் ஏழு முக்கிய தொகுதிகள் GAEZ v4 மாடலிங் கட்டமைப்பிற்குள் தேவையான படிகளை சுருக்கமாகக் கூறுகின்றன. ஒவ்வொரு தொகுதியிலிருந்தும் வரும் வெளியீடுகள் ஆறு முக்கிய கருப்பொருள்களாக வகைப்படுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளன: 1) நிலம் மற்றும் நீர் வளங்கள், 2) விவசாய காலநிலை வளங்கள், 3) விவசாய காலநிலை சாத்தியமான மகசூல், 4) பொருத்தமான மற்றும் அடையக்கூடிய மகசூல், 5) உண்மையான மகசூல் மற்றும் உற்பத்தி மற்றும் 6) மகசூல் மற்றும் உற்பத்தி இடைவெளிகள்.
 
பொருத்தமான வகுப்பு துணை தீம் மாடலிங் கட்டமைப்பின் வெளியீடுகள் மற்றும் தொகுதி V இன் தீம் நான்கு இன் கீழ் வருகிறது. தொகுதி 5 முதல் நான்கு தொகுதிகளின் முடிவுகளை ஒருங்கிணைக்கிறது மற்றும் மண் மற்றும் நிலப்பரப்பு மதிப்பீட்டு முடிவுகளுடன் விவசாய-காலநிலை சாத்தியமான விளைச்சலை ஒருங்கிணைக்கிறது. இந்த தொகுதி ஒவ்வொரு கட்ட செல்லிலும் அதன் அந்தந்த மண் வகைகள் மற்றும் சாய்வு வகுப்புகளை அடையாளம் காண்கிறது, பின்னர் பொருத்தமான மதிப்பீடு மற்றும் உருவகப்படுத்தப்பட்ட சாத்தியமான விளைச்சலை மதிப்பீடு செய்து ஒதுக்குகிறது. முடிவுகள் பின்னர் பயிர், உள்ளீடு நிலை மற்றும் நீர் ஆதாரம் மூலம் ஒவ்வொரு வரலாற்று மற்றும் எதிர்கால 30 ஆண்டு காலத்திற்கும் தொகுக்கப்பட்டு வரைபடமாக்கப்படுகின்றன, மேலும் 5 வில் நிமிடங்கள் (பூமத்திய ரேகையில் தோராயமாக 9 கி.மீ) இடஞ்சார்ந்த தெளிவுத்திறனைக் கொண்டுள்ளன.
 
பொருத்தம் வகுப்புகள் இயல்பாக்கப்பட்ட பொருத்தப்பாடு குறியீட்டெண் (SI) இலிருந்து கணக்கிடப்படுகின்றன, அங்கு:
           
SI = 100 x (90 x VS + 70 x S + 50 x MS + 30 x mS + 15 x VmS + 0 x NS) / 0.9
 
எஸ்ஐ மதிப்புகள் 0 முதல் 10,000 வரை இருக்கலாம் மற்றும் பொருத்தமான வகுப்புகளின் அடிப்படை சுருக்கெழுத்துகள் பின்வருமாறு வரையறுக்கப்படுகின்றன: விஎஸ் = மிகவும் பொருத்தமானது, எஸ் = பொருத்தமானது, எம் எஸ் = மிதமான பொருத்தமானது, எம்.எஸ் = ஓரளவு பொருத்தமானது, வி.எம்.எஸ் = மிகவும் பொருத்தமானது, மற்றும் என்எஸ் = பொருத்தமானது அல்ல. இந்த ஆறு வகைகளும் ஒரு கட்டம் செல்லில் உள்ள வெவ்வேறு பொருத்தமான வகுப்புகளின் பரப்பளவுகளின் பங்குகளைக் குறிக்கின்றன. 53 பயிர்களில் ஒவ்வொன்றுக்கும் உள்ளீடு, மேலாண்மை மற்றும் நீர் வழங்கல் முறையின் அளவைக் கொண்டு எஸ்.ஐ கணக்கிடப்படுகிறது. ஒவ்வொரு கட்ட செல்லிலும் உள்ள விளைபயன் SI பின்னர் எட்டு வகுப்புகளாக வகைப்படுத்தப்பட்டு மொத்த பயிர் பொருத்தத்தை சித்தரிக்கிறது:
- மிக அதிகம்: எஸ்ஐ > 8,500
- உயர்: 7,000 < எஸ்ஐ ≤ 8,500
- நன்று: 5,550 < எஸ்ஐ ≤ 7,000
- நடுத்தரம்: 4,000 < எஸ்.ஐ ≤ 5,500
- மிதமானது: 2,500 < எஸ்.ஐ ≤ 4,000
- விளிம்புநிலை: 1,000 < எஸ்.ஐ ≤ 2,500
- மிகவும் விளிம்புநிலை: 0 < எஸ்ஐ ≤ 1,000
- பொருத்தமானது அல்ல: எஸ்ஐ = 0
 
முழு ஆவணப்படுத்தலுக்கு, மூலத்தைப் பார்க்கவும் [முறையியல்](https://www.fao.org/3/cb4744en/cb4744en.pdf).  
### கூடுதல் தகவல்  
  
எங்கள் தரவு அட்டவணை தரவுத்தொகுப்பின் துணைக்குழுவை மட்டுமே காட்டுகிறது. உலகளாவிய வேளாண்-சூழலியல் மண்டல பதிப்பு 4 பயிர் பொருத்தம் குறியீட்டெண் முழு தரவுத்தொகுப்பில் 53 பயிர்கள், கூடுதல் காலக்கெடு (1961-1990, 1971-2000, மற்றும் 2071-2100), ஆர்.சி.பி.க்கள் (2.6 மற்றும் 6.0), நீர் வழங்கல் (மானாவாரி அனைத்து கட்டங்களிலும், புவியீர்ப்பு நீர்ப்பாசனம்), குறைந்த உள்ளீட்டு நிலை விருப்பம் மற்றும் கார்பன் டை ஆக்ஸைடு இல்லாமல் ஒரு கருவுறுதல் விருப்பம் ஆகியவற்றுக்கான தரவுகள் உள்ளன. முழு தரவுத்தொகுப்பு மற்றும் கூடுதல் தகவலுக்கான அணுகலுக்கு, "மேலும் அறிக" பொத்தானைக் கிளிக் செய்க.  
  
### தரவை காட்சிப்படுத்தல்  
  
WRI இன் தரவு அட்டவணையில் காண்பிக்கப்படுவதற்கு முன்பு எங்கள் குழு இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பை மறுவடிவமைத்தது. [Github] இல் உள்ள தரவை நாங்கள் எவ்வாறு மீட்டெடுத்தோம் என்பதற்கான ஆவணங்களைப் பார்க்கவும் (https://github.com/resource-வாட்ச்/தரவு-முன்-செயலாக்கம்/blob/master/foo_067_rw0_crop_suitability_class).  
  
### பொறுப்புத்துறப்பு  
  
இந்த விளக்கப் பக்கத்தின் பகுதிகள் மூல மெட்டாடேட்டாவிலிருந்து எடுக்கப்பட்டன.
