attributes.description:
### கண்ணோட்டம்  
  
உலகளாவிய வேளாண் சூழலியல் மண்டல பதிப்பு 4 (GAEZ v4) தரவுத்தொகுப்பு தற்போதைய மற்றும் எதிர்கால விவசாய வளங்கள் மற்றும் அவற்றின் திறனை மதிப்பிடுகிறது. இது விவசாய உற்பத்திக்கு பொருத்தமான காலநிலை, மண் மற்றும் நிலப்பரப்பு நிலைமைகளின் சிறப்பியல்புகளை அனுமதிக்கும் ஒரு தரப்படுத்தப்பட்ட கட்டமைப்பாகும். நிலம் மற்றும் நீர் வளங்கள் என்ற முதல் கருப்பொருளின் தரவுகள் இங்கு காட்டப்பட்டு, விவசாய உற்பத்தி அமைப்புகளுக்குப் பொருத்தமான [உயிர் இயற்பியல்] (https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/biophysics) வளங்களின் சீரான வகைப்படுத்தலை அனுமதிக்கிறது. வெளியீடுகள் பூமத்திய ரேகையில் தோராயமாக 9 கி.மீ x 9 கி.மீ ஆகும், ஆனால் [தூரத்துடன் மாற்றங்கள்] (https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-ன்-அட்சரேகை-மற்றும்-தீர்க்கரேகை-தூரம்-4070616) பூமத்திய ரேகையிலிருந்து 5 வில் நிமிட தெளிவுத்திறனில் வழங்கப்படுகின்றன.

உணவு பாதுகாப்பு, நிலம் மற்றும் நீர் வளங்களின் நிலைபேறான தன்மை மற்றும் விவசாய அபிவிருத்தி மற்றும் கொள்கைகள் மீதான தாக்கங்களுடன் விவசாய தீர்மானங்களை எடுப்பதற்கு காணி வளங்களின் தற்போதைய மற்றும் எதிர்காலப் பயன்பாடு பற்றிய தகவல்கள் முக்கியமானதாகும். நிலத்தின் உயிர் இயற்பியல் வரம்புகள், தற்போதைய பயிர் பொருத்தம் மற்றும் காலநிலை மாற்றத்தால் வெவ்வேறு விவசாய வளங்கள் எவ்வாறு பாதிக்கப்படுகின்றன என்பது குறித்த தகவல்களை வழங்க பல தரவு ஆதாரங்களை ஜி.ஏ.இ.எஸ் வி 4 தரவுத்தொகுப்பு ஒன்றிணைக்கிறது. எதிர்காலத்தில் என்ன மாற்றங்கள் நிகழலாம் என்பதைப் புரிந்துகொள்வது, பல்வேறு நடிகர்களுக்கு பின்னடைவை அதிகரிக்கும் திறன், சாத்தியமான சவால்களைத் தணிப்பதற்கான நுட்பங்கள் அல்லது கொள்கைகளை உருவாக்குதல் மற்றும் உணவுப் பாதுகாப்பைப் பராமரித்தல் ஆகியவற்றை செயல்படுத்தும்.

ஐக்கிய நாடுகள் சபையின் உணவு மற்றும் விவசாய அமைப்பு (FAO) மற்றும் பிரயோக முறைமை பகுப்பாய்வுக்கான சர்வதேச நிறுவனம் (IIASA) இணைந்து விவசாய வளங்களின் நிலை பற்றிய தற்போதைய தரவுகளை வழங்குவதற்காக 1980 களின் முற்பகுதியில் GAEZ மாதிரியாக்க கட்டமைப்பை அபிவிருத்தி செய்யத் தொடங்கியது. நிலையான விவசாய அபிவிருத்திக்கு ஆதரவளிப்பதற்கும், விவசாய உற்பத்தி, பயிர் அபிவிருத்தி, நில உற்பத்தித்திறன் மற்றும் காலநிலை மாற்றத்தினால் ஏற்படும் தாக்கங்கள் தொடர்பான தற்போதைய மற்றும் எதிர்கால அபாயங்கள் பற்றிய முக்கிய தகவல்களை வழங்குவதற்கும் இது விரிவடைந்துள்ளது.
  
### முறைமை  
  
பல தரவுத்தொகுப்புகள் GAEZ V4 மாடலிங் கட்டமைப்பிற்கான உள்ளீடுகளாகப் பயன்படுத்தப்பட்டன மற்றும் வரலாற்று மற்றும் எதிர்கால காலநிலை பண்புகள், மண் மற்றும் நிலப்பரப்பு வளங்கள், நிலப்பரப்பு, பாதுகாக்கப்பட்ட நிலம், பல்லுயிர்ப் பகுதிகள், நீர் வளங்கள், நிர்வாக அலகுகள், மக்கள்தொகை மற்றும் கால்நடைகள் பற்றிய தரவுகளை வழங்குகின்றன. வரலாற்று காலநிலை தரவுகள் காலநிலை ஆராய்ச்சி அலகு TS v3.21 தரவுத் தொகுப்புகளிலிருந்து வருகின்றன, இதில் மாதாந்திர காலநிலைத் தகவல்களும் அடங்கும். காலநிலை மாற்றம் தொடர்பான அரசாங்கங்களுக்கிடையிலான குழுவின் ஐந்தாவது மதிப்பீட்டு அறிக்கையிலிருந்து (ஏ.ஆர்.5) நான்கு (2.6, 4.5, 6, 8.5) பிரதிநிதித்துவ செறிவு பாதைகள் (ஆர்.சி.பி) க்கான காலநிலை மாதிரி வெளியீடுகளிலிருந்து ஏ.இ.இசட்-க்கான எதிர்கால காலநிலை தரவு பெறப்படுகிறது.

தரவு செயலாக்கம் பல படிகளாக உடைக்கப்பட்டது மற்றும் ஏழு முக்கிய தொகுதிகள் GAEZ v4 மாடலிங் கட்டமைப்பிற்குள் தேவையான படிகளை சுருக்கமாகக் கூறுகின்றன. ஒவ்வொரு தொகுதியிலிருந்தும் வரும் வெளியீடுகள் ஆறு முக்கிய கருப்பொருள்களாக வகைப்படுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளன: 1) நிலம் மற்றும் நீர் வளங்கள், 2) விவசாய காலநிலை வளங்கள், 3) விவசாய காலநிலை சாத்தியமான மகசூல், 4) பொருத்தமான மற்றும் அடையக்கூடிய மகசூல், 5) உண்மையான மகசூல் மற்றும் உற்பத்தி மற்றும் 6) மகசூல் மற்றும் உற்பத்தி இடைவெளிகள்.
 
விவசாய சூழலியல் வலயங்கள் (AEZ) உப கருப்பொருள் வெளியீடுகள் காணி மற்றும் நீர் வளங்கள் என்ற முதலாவது கருப்பொருளின் கீழ் வருவதுடன், குறிப்பிட்ட விவசாய சூழலியல் நிலைமைகளின் கீழ் காணி உற்பத்தித்திறனை மதிப்பீடு செய்வதற்காக காணி வளங்களின் பட்டியலையும் வழங்குகின்றது. வெப்ப மற்றும் ஈரப்பத அடுக்குகள் பரந்த வகை மண் மற்றும் நிலப்பரப்பு பண்புகளுடன் இணைக்கப்படுகின்றன, இது உயிர் இயற்பியல் கட்டுப்பாடுகளுடன் நிலப் பகுதிகளை அடையாளம் காண அனுமதிக்கிறது. 

AEZ வகுப்புகள் மற்றும் வரையறைகளை ஒன்றிணைக்க ஒரு கடுமையான வழிமுறை மற்றும் வெளிப்படையான கொள்கைகளின் தொகுப்பு பின்பற்றப்படுகிறது. பின்வரும் கொள்கைகள் பின்வருவனவற்றை உறுதி செய்கின்றன: 1) வரைபட வகுப்புகள் 1981-2010 இன் அடிப்படை வரலாற்று காலத்தின் அடிப்படையில் முக்கிய காலநிலை மண்டலங்களுடன் இணைகின்றன, 2) வரைபட வகுப்புகள் வளர்ந்து வரும் கால எல்லைகளின் நீளத்தின் பரந்த வரம்புகளைப் பிரதிபலிக்கின்றன, மேலும் 3) ஏஇசட் வகுப்புகள் ஜிஏஇஎஸ் வி 4 நிலப்பரப்பு மற்றும் மண் வள இருப்புகளில் இருந்து பெறப்பட்ட நிலவும் மண் மற்றும் நிலப்பரப்பு வரம்புகள் பற்றிய பொதுவான தகவல்களைக் கொண்டுள்ளன. இறுதி AEZ அடுக்கு 57 வெவ்வேறு வகுப்புகளைக் கொண்டுள்ளது, அவை 5 வில் நிமிடங்கள் (பூமத்திய ரேகையில் தோராயமாக 9 கி.மீ) இடஞ்சார்ந்த தெளிவுத்திறனில் வரைபடமாக்கப்பட்டுள்ளன.
 
முழு ஆவணப்படுத்தலுக்கு, மூலத்தைப் பார்க்கவும் [முறையியல்](https://www.fao.org/3/cb4744en/cb4744en.pdf).
  
### கூடுதல் தகவல்  
  
எங்கள் தரவு அட்டவணை தரவுத்தொகுப்பின் துணைக்குழுவை மட்டுமே காட்டுகிறது. உலகளாவிய வேளாண் சூழலியல் மண்டல பதிப்பு 4 வேளாண் சூழலியல் மண்டலங்களின் தரவு 2071-2100 மற்றும் கூடுதல் ஆர்சிபிக்கள் (2.6 மற்றும் 6) ஆகியவற்றிற்கான கூடுதல் தரவுகளைக் கொண்டுள்ளது. முழு தரவுத்தொகுப்பு மற்றும் கூடுதல் தகவலுக்கான அணுகலுக்கு, "மேலும் அறிக" பொத்தானைக் கிளிக் செய்க.  
  
### தரவை காட்சிப்படுத்தல்  
  
WRI இன் தரவு அட்டவணையில் காண்பிக்கப்படுவதற்கு முன்பு எங்கள் குழு இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பை மறுவடிவமைத்தது. [Github] (https://github.com/resource-வாட்ச்/தரவு-முன் செயலாக்கம்/blob/master/foo_068_rw0_agro_ecological_zones/) இல் உள்ள தரவை நாங்கள் எவ்வாறு மீட்டெடுத்தோம் என்பதற்கான ஆவணப்படுத்தலைப் பார்க்கவும்.  
  
### பொறுப்புத்துறப்பு  
  
இந்த விளக்கப் பக்கத்தின் பகுதிகள் மூல மெட்டாடேட்டாவிலிருந்து எடுக்கப்பட்டன.

info.cautions:
- GAEZ V4 மதிப்பீடு விவசாயம் தொடர்பான அனைத்து நடவடிக்கைகளையும் உள்ளடக்காது. இது முதன்மையாக பயிர்களை வளர்ப்பதற்கான சாத்தியக்கூறுகளில் கவனம் செலுத்துகிறது.
- இந்த தரவுத்தொகுப்பின் முடிவுகள் பொருத்தமான திரட்டல் மட்டங்களில் பயன்படுத்தப்பட வேண்டும், அவை உள்ளீட்டு தரவுத் தொகுப்புகளின் அடிப்படைத் தீர்மானத்தைச் சார்ந்துள்ளன. உள்ளீட்டுத் தரவுத் தொகுப்புகள் வெவ்வேறு இடஞ்சார்ந்த தீர்மானங்களைக் கொண்டுள்ளன.
- உள்ளீடு தரவுத்தொகுப்புகள் சீரற்ற தரம் மற்றும் நம்பகத்தன்மையைக் கொண்டிருப்பதாக அறியப்படுகிறது.
- மேம்பட்ட தெளிவுத்திறன் மற்றும் துல்லியத்துடன் கூடிய புதிய தரவுத்தொகுப்புகள், ஜி.ஏ.இ.எஸ் தரவுத்தொகுப்புகள் உறைந்த பின்னர் கிடைக்கச் செய்யப்பட்டன, எடுத்துக்காட்டாக, நிலப் போர்வை.
- ஜி.ஏ.இ.இசட் வெளியீடுகளில் நில சீரழிவு மிகக் குறைவாகவோ அல்லது குறைவாகவோ கணக்கிடப்படவில்லை.
- சில பயிர்களுக்கான சுற்றுச்சூழல் தேவைகள் குறித்த தரவு போன்ற சில மாறிகளுக்கு உலகளாவிய பொதுமைப்படுத்தல்கள் அவசியம்.
- சமூகப் பொருளாதார தரவுப் பயன்பாடு என்பது விவசாய உற்பத்தி முறைகள் மற்றும் நோக்கங்களின் விவரக்குறிப்புகள், உள்ளீடுகள் மற்றும் மேலாண்மை அளவுகளின் அளவீடு, விவசாய விலைகளை சேர்த்தல் மற்றும் மக்கள்தொகை எண்கள் மற்றும் விநியோகங்களைக் கருத்தில் கொள்ளுதல் ஆகியவற்றுடன் மட்டுப்படுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளது.
- நம்பகமான தரவுத் தொகுப்புகளிலிருந்து பாதுகாப்பு அல்லது விலக்கு நிலை என குறிக்கப்பட்ட நிலத்தைக் குறிக்க ஜி.ஏ.இ.இ.எஸ் ஒரு விலக்கு அடுக்கைப் பயன்படுத்தியது.

attributes.name: వ్యవసాయ-పర్యావరణ మండలాలు
attributes.description:
### అవలోకనం  
  
గ్లోబల్ ఆగ్రో-ఎకలాజికల్ జోనింగ్ వెర్షన్ 4 (గెజ్ వి 4) డేటాసెట్ ప్రస్తుత మరియు భవిష్యత్తు వ్యవసాయ వనరులు మరియు వాటి సామర్థ్యాన్ని మదింపు చేస్తుంది. ఇది వ్యవసాయ ఉత్పత్తికి సంబంధించిన శీతోష్ణస్థితి, నేల మరియు భూభాగ పరిస్థితుల యొక్క లక్షణాలను అనుమతించే ఒక ప్రామాణిక ఫ్రేమ్ వర్క్. ఫస్ట్ థీమ్, ల్యాండ్ అండ్ వాటర్ రిసోర్సెస్ నుంచి డేటా ఇక్కడ డిస్ ప్లే చేయబడుతుంది మరియు వ్యవసాయ ఉత్పత్తి సిస్టమ్ లకు సంబంధించిన [బయోఫిజికల్](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/biophysics) వనరుల యొక్క ఏకరీతి వర్గీకరణకు అనుమతిస్తుంది. 5 ఆర్క్ నిమిషాల రిజల్యూషన్ వద్ద అవుట్ పుట్ లు ప్రదర్శించబడతాయి, ఇది భూమధ్యరేఖ వద్ద సుమారు 9 కి.మీ x 9 కి.మీ. అయితే [దూరంతో మారుతుంది](https://www.thoughtco.com/degree-ఆఫ్-అక్షాంశం-మరియు-రేఖాంశం-దూరం-4070616) భూమధ్యరేఖ నుండి.

ఆహార భద్రత, భూమి మరియు నీటి వనరుల సుస్థిరత, మరియు వ్యవసాయ అభివృద్ధి మరియు విధానాలపై ప్రభావంతో వ్యవసాయ నిర్ణయాలు తీసుకోవడానికి భూమి వనరుల యొక్క ప్రస్తుత మరియు భవిష్యత్తు వినియోగంపై సమాచారం చాలా ముఖ్యమైనది. భూమి యొక్క జీవభౌతిక పరిమితులు, ప్రస్తుత పంట అనుకూలత, మరియు వాతావరణ మార్పుల ద్వారా వివిధ వ్యవసాయ వనరులు ఎలా ప్రభావితమవుతాయనే దానిపై సమాచారాన్ని అందించడానికి జిఎఇజెడ్ వి4 డేటాసెట్ బహుళ డేటా వనరులను ఒకచోట చేర్చింది. భవిష్యత్తులో ఎలాంటి మార్పులు చోటు చేసుకోవచ్చో అర్థం చేసుకోవడం వల్ల విభిన్న నటులు స్థితిస్థాపకతను పెంపొందించడానికి, సంభావ్య సవాళ్లను తగ్గించడానికి మెళకువలు లేదా విధానాలను అభివృద్ధి చేయడానికి మరియు ఆహార భద్రతను నిర్వహించడానికి దోహదపడుతుంది.

ఫుడ్ అండ్ అగ్రికల్చరల్ ఆర్గనైజేషన్ ఆఫ్ ది యునైటెడ్ నేషన్స్ (ఎఫ్.ఎ.ఒ)తో కలిసి ఇంటర్నేషనల్ ఇన్స్టిట్యూట్ ఫర్ అప్లైడ్ సిస్టమ్స్ అనాలిసిస్ (ఐ.ఐ.ఎ.ఎస్.ఎ.ఎస్)తో కలిసి వ్యవసాయ వనరుల స్థితిగతులపై ప్రస్తుత డేటాను అందించడానికి 1980 ల ప్రారంభంలో GAEZ మోడలింగ్ ఫ్రేమ్వర్క్ను అభివృద్ధి చేయడం ప్రారంభించింది. అప్పటి నుండి ఇది సుస్థిర వ్యవసాయాభివృద్ధికి మద్దతు ఇవ్వడానికి మరియు వ్యవసాయ ఉత్పత్తి, పంట అభివృద్ధి, భూమి ఉత్పాదకత మరియు వాతావరణ మార్పుల నుండి ప్రభావాలకు ప్రస్తుత మరియు భవిష్యత్తు ప్రమాదాలపై కీలక సమాచారాన్ని అందించడానికి విస్తరించింది.
  
#### మెథడాలజీ  
  
బహుళ డేటాసెట్లు గెజ్ వి4 మోడలింగ్ ఫ్రేమ్ వర్క్ కు ఇన్ పుట్ లుగా ఉపయోగించబడ్డాయి మరియు చారిత్రాత్మక మరియు భవిష్యత్తు వాతావరణ లక్షణాలు, నేల మరియు భూభాగ వనరులు, భూమి కవర్, రక్షిత భూమి, జీవవైవిధ్య ప్రాంతాలు, నీటి వనరులు, పరిపాలనా యూనిట్లు, జనాభా మరియు పశువులపై డేటాను అందించాయి. చారిత్రక వాతావరణ డేటా వాతావరణ పరిశోధన యూనిట్ టిఎస్ వి 3.21 డేటాసెట్ల నుండి వస్తుంది, ఇందులో నెలవారీ వాతావరణ సమాచారం ఉంటుంది. వాతావరణ మార్పుపై ఇంటర్ గవర్నమెంటల్ ప్యానెల్ యొక్క ఐదవ అసెస్ మెంట్ రిపోర్ట్ (ఎఆర్ 5) నుండి నాలుగు (2.6, 4.5, 6, 8.5) రిప్రజెంటేటివ్ కాన్సంట్రేషన్ పాత్ వేస్ (ఆర్ సిపిలు) కొరకు వాతావరణ నమూనా అవుట్ పుట్ ల నుంచి ఎఇజెడ్ కొరకు భవిష్యత్ వాతావరణ డేటా తీసుకోబడింది.

డేటా ప్రాసెసింగ్ అనేక దశలుగా విభజించబడింది మరియు ఏడు ప్రధాన మాడ్యూల్స్ గెజ్ వి4 మోడలింగ్ ఫ్రేమ్ వర్క్ లోపల అవసరమైన దశలను సంక్షిప్తీకరించాయి. ప్రతి మాడ్యూల్ నుంచి వచ్చే అవుట్ పుట్ లు ఆరు ప్రధాన థీమ్ లుగా వర్గీకరించబడ్డాయి: 1) భూమి మరియు నీటి వనరులు, 2) వ్యవసాయ-వాతావరణ వనరులు, 3) వ్యవసాయ-వాతావరణ సంభావ్య దిగుబడి, 4) అనుకూలత మరియు సాధించదగిన దిగుబడి, 5) వాస్తవ దిగుబడి మరియు ఉత్పత్తి, మరియు 6) దిగుబడి మరియు ఉత్పత్తి అంతరాలు.
 
ఆగ్రో-ఎకలాజికల్ జోన్లు (ఎఇజెడ్) సబ్-థీమ్ అవుట్ పుట్ లు మొదటి థీమ్, ల్యాండ్ అండ్ వాటర్ రిసోర్సెస్ కిందకు వస్తాయి మరియు నిర్ధిష్ట వ్యవసాయ-పర్యావరణ పరిస్థితుల్లో భూమి ఉత్పాదకతను మదింపు చేయడం కొరకు ల్యాండ్ రిసోర్సెస్ యొక్క జాబితాను అందిస్తుంది. ఉష్ణ మరియు తేమ పొరలు నేల మరియు భూభాగ లక్షణాల యొక్క విస్తృత కేటగిరీలతో మిళితం చేయబడతాయి, ఇది బయోఫిజికల్ అడ్డంకులతో ఉన్న భూ ప్రాంతాలను గుర్తించడానికి అనుమతిస్తుంది. 

AEZ క్లాసులు మరియు నిర్వచనాలను అసెంబుల్ చేయడానికి ఒక కఠినమైన మెథడాలజీ మరియు స్పష్టమైన సూత్రాల సెట్ పాటించబడుతుంది. ఈ క్రింది సూత్రాలు ఈ క్రింది సూత్రాలను నిర్ధారిస్తాయి: 1) 1981-2010 నాటి బేస్ లైన్ చారిత్రక కాలం ఆధారంగా పటం తరగతులు ప్రధాన వాతావరణ మండలాలతో సమలేఖనం చెందుతాయి, 2) పటం తరగతులు పెరుగుతున్న కాలం సరిహద్దుల పొడవు యొక్క విస్తృత శ్రేణులను ప్రతిబింబిస్తాయి, మరియు 3) ఎఇజెడ్ తరగతులు GAEZ v4 భూభాగం మరియు మట్టి వనరుల జాబితాల నుండి గ్రహించబడిన ప్రస్తుత మట్టి మరియు భూభాగ పరిమితుల గురించి సాధారణీకరించిన సమాచారాన్ని కలిగి ఉన్నాయి. తుది AEZ పొరలో 57 విభిన్న తరగతులుంటాయి, ఇవి 5 ఆర్క్ నిమిషాల ప్రాదేశిక రిజల్యూషన్ (భూమధ్యరేఖ వద్ద సుమారు 9 కిలోమీటర్లు) వద్ద మ్యాప్ చేయబడతాయి.
 
పూర్తి డాక్యుమెంటేషన్ కొరకు, దయచేసి సోర్స్ [మెథడాలజీ](https://www.fao.org/3/cb4744en/cb4744en.pdf) చూడండి.
  
### అదనపు సమాచారం  
  
మా డేటా కేటలాగ్ డేటాసెట్ యొక్క ఉపసమితిని మాత్రమే చూపుతుంది. గ్లోబల్ ఆగ్రో-ఎకలాజికల్ జోనింగ్ వెర్షన్ 4 ఆగ్రో-ఎకలాజికల్ జోన్ల డేటా 2071-2100 మరియు అదనపు ఆర్ సిపిలు (2.6 మరియు 6) కొరకు అదనపు డేటాను కలిగి ఉంది. పూర్తి డేటాసెట్ మరియు అదనపు సమాచారాన్ని యాక్సెస్ చేసుకోవడానికి, "మరింత తెలుసుకోండి" బటన్ మీద క్లిక్ చేయండి.  
  
### డేటాను విజువలైజ్ చేయడం  
  
డబ్ల్యుఆర్ఐ యొక్క డేటా కేటలాగ్ లో ప్రదర్శించడానికి ముందు మా బృందం ఈ డేటాసెట్ ను పునర్నిర్మించింది. [Github](https://github.com/resource-వాచ్/డేటా-ప్రీ-ప్రాసెసింగ్/బ్లాబ్/మాస్టర్/foo_068_rw0_agro_ecological_zones/)పై డేటాను మేం ఏవిధంగా తిరిగి పొందాం అనే దానిపై డాక్యుమెంటేషన్ ని చూడండి.  
  
### డిస్ క్లెయిమర్  
  
ఈ వివరణ పేజీ యొక్క సారాంశాలు మూల మెటాడేటా నుండి తీసుకోబడ్డాయి.

attributes.name: Migrant Deaths
attributes.description:
The Missing Migrants Project by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) counts migrants who have died or gone missing at the external borders of states, or in the process of migration toward an international destination. The IOM defines a migrant as any person who is moving or has moved across an international border or within a state away from his or her habitual place of residence. Data are obtained from local authorities (coast guards, sheriff’s offices, medical examiners), interviews with survivors provided by IOM field offices, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) and media reports. The count excludes deaths that occur in immigration detention facilities, during deportation, or after forced return to a migrant’s homeland, as well as deaths more loosely connected with migrants’ irregular status, such as those resulting from labor exploitation. Migrants who die or go missing after they are established in a new home are also not included in the data, so deaths in refugee camps or housing are excluded. This approach is chosen because deaths that occur at physical borders and while en route represent a more clearly definable category and inform which migration routes are most dangerous. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, see the Learn More link.  
  
### Additional Information

info.name: Migrant Deaths
info.technical_title: Missing Migrants - Tracking Deaths Along Migratory Routes
info.functions: Deaths along migratory routes worldwide from 2014 to the present
info.cautions: Data on fatalities during the migration process are challenging to collect for a number of reasons, most stemming from the irregular nature of migratory journeys on which deaths tend to occur. For one, deaths often occur in remote areas on routes chosen with the explicit aim of evading detection. Countless bodies are never found, and rarely do these deaths come to the attention of authorities or the media. Furthermore, when deaths occur at sea, frequently not all bodies are recovered—sometimes with hundreds missing from one shipwreck—and the precise number of missing is often unknown. In 2015, over 50% of deaths recorded by the Missing Migrants Project refer to migrants who are presumed dead and whose bodies have not been found, mainly at sea. Data are also challenging to collect as reporting on deaths is poor, and the data that do exist are highly scattered. Few official sources are collecting data systematically. Many counts of death rely on the media as a source. Coverage can be spotty and incomplete. In addition, the involvement of criminal actors in incidents means there may be fear among survivors of reporting deaths, and some deaths may be actively covered up. The irregular immigration status of many migrants, and at times their families as well, also impedes reporting of missing persons or deaths. The varying quality and comprehensiveness of data by region in attempting to estimate deaths globally may exaggerate the share of deaths that occur in some regions, while underrepresenting the share occurring in others. However, it is important to note that because of the challenges in data collection for the missing and dead, basic demographic information on the deceased is rarely known. Often migrants in mixed migration flows do not carry appropriate identification. When bodies are found, it may not be possible to identify them or to determine basic demographic information. In the data compiled by the Missing Migrants Project, the sex of the deceased is unknown in over 80% of cases. Region of origin has been determined for the majority of the deceased. Even this information is at times extrapolated based on available information—for instance, if all survivors of a shipwreck are of one origin it was assumed those missing also came from the same region. The Missing Migrants Project data set includes coordinates for where incidents of death took place, which indicates where the risks to migrants may be highest. However, it should be noted that all coordinates are estimates.
info.citation: International Organization for Migration. 2017. "Missing Migrants." Accessed through Resource Watch, (date). [www.resourcewatch.org](https://www.resourcewatch.org).

attributes.name: Climate Hazard Indicators (Extreme rainy days) Historical and SSP scenarios - Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
attributes.description:
### Overview
 
 
The dataset includes five major climatic indicators viz. annual values for minimum temperature (℃), maximum temperature (℃), mean temperature (℃), total precipitation (mm/year), and the number of rainy days (represented as integers) for two Indian states, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. It features decadal averages from 2020-2100 for Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs), including SSP5-8.5, which reflects a high emissions scenario, and SSP2-4.5, representing moderate challenges to both mitigation and adaptation. Additionally, the dataset provides historical data for all the five indicators averaged over the period from 2005 to 2014.
 
 
### Methodology
 
 
**Pre-Processing**: The decadal time periods were labeled as follows: 2020-2029 as 2020, 2030-2039 as 2030, 2040-2049 as 2040, 2050-2059 as 2050, 2060-2069 as 2060, 2070-2079 as 2070, 2080-2089 as 2080, and 2090-2099 as 2090.
 
 
**Layers of interest**: Annual averages of minimum temperature (℃), maximum temperature (℃), mean temperature (℃), Annual total precipitation (mm/year), and the annual total number of rainy days (represented as integers).
 
 
**Data**: The ERA5 reanalysis dataset (ECMWF 2022), a satellite data product of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts with a spatial resolution of 31 kilometers (km), is used as a reference dataset. The ensemble of downscaled daily time series outputs from global climate models (GCMs). These time series include the historical years covered by the observation time series as well as the specified future years of interest. We have used the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 product, which includes outputs from 34 Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) models at approximately 25 km spatial resolution.
 
 
### Estimation Methods
 
 
Out of the 35 models, we select the top 3 climate models that perform best for a specific weather variable in a particular geographic region, and present the ensemble mean of these models. The ERA5 dataset is used as a reference, and the comparison is made for the historical period between 1980 and 2014. After selecting the models, we apply a calibration/bias correction procedure to the future time series of the models. This involves aligning the model's frequency distribution with the historical data by shifting the percentiles of the model's distribution. For instance, if the 20th percentile of the model data corresponds to the 30th percentile of the observations, then the 30th percentile of the calibrated model data will match the 20th percentile of the uncalibrated model data.
 
 
For the full documentation, please see the source methodology at Wong, T., and P Switzer. 2023. 'Estimating future local climate hazard probabilities.' Technical Note. Washington, DC: World Resources Institute. Available online at: doi.org/10.46830/writn.22.00074.v2.
 
 
### Description of the Layers
 
 
**Annual Maximum Temperature (℃)**: The daily maximum temperature data for each year is extracted and averaged to calculate the yearly average maximum temperature. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
**Annual Minimum Temperature (℃)**: The daily minimum temperature data for each year is extracted and averaged to calculate the yearly average minimum temperature. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
**Annual Mean Temperature (℃)**: The daily mean temperature is calculated by averaging the daily minimum and maximum temperatures. The annual mean temperature is obtained by averaging the daily mean temperatures over the course of a year. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
**Annual Total Precipitation (mm/year)**: The daily precipitation values are summed over the entire year to calculate the annual total precipitation. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
**Annual Rainy Days (represented as integers)**: A rainy day is defined as a day with precipitation exceeding 2.5 mm (as per the India Meteorological Department). The total number of rainy days in a year is calculated by summing the rainy days throughout the year. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
### Visualizing the Data
 
 
The data is provided at a 25-km resolution and is presented as a raster with a time slider with a separate layer for each variable. The values are visualized using a gradient based on the selected year in the slider, ranging from lighter shade (indicating low values) to darker shade (representing higher values).
 
 
### Disclaimer

attributes.name: Biodiversity Hotspots
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
Biodiversity hotspots, a classification system created by the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF), include some of our planet’s most biologically diverse yet threatened terrestrial areas. An area is qualified as a hotspot if it contains at least 1,500 species of vascular plants found nowhere else on Earth (known as “endemic” species) and it has lost at least 70 percent of its primary native vegetation. Between 1988 and 2016, 36 biodiversity hotspots have been identified globally.   
  
### Methodology  
  
Hotspots were defined by Norman Myers in 1988 when he published a seminal paper identifying 10 tropical forest “hotspots.” These regions were characterized both by exceptional levels of plant endemism, meaning plants found nowhere else on Earth, and serious levels of habitat loss. Conservation International (CI) adopted Myers’s hotspots as its institutional blueprint in 1989. In 1999, CI undertook a global review, which introduced quantitative thresholds for the designation of biodiversity hotspots and resulted in the identification of 25. 

  
  
In 2005, an additional analysis brought the total number of biodiversity hotspots to 34, based on the work of nearly 400 specialists. In 2011, the Forests of East Australia were identified as the 35th hotspot by a team of researchers from the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organization working with CI. In February 2016, the North American Coastal Plain was recognized as meeting the criteria and became the world’s 36th hotspot. For the full documentation, please click on the “Learn more” button.
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. Additional data on the offshore extents of biodiversity hotspots is available from the data provider. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.

These time series include the historical years covered by the observation time series as well as the specified future years of interest. We have used the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 product, which includes outputs from 34 Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) models at approximately 25 km spatial resolution.
 
 
### Estimation Methods
 
 
Out of the 35 models, we select the top 3 climate models that perform best for a specific weather variable in a particular geographic region, and present the ensemble mean of these models. The ERA5 dataset is used as a reference, and the comparison is made for the historical period between 1980 and 2014. After selecting the models, we apply a calibration/bias correction procedure to the future time series of the models. This involves aligning the model's frequency distribution with the historical data by shifting the percentiles of the model's distribution. For instance, if the 20th percentile of the model data corresponds to the 30th percentile of the observations, then the 30th percentile of the calibrated model data will match the 20th percentile of the uncalibrated model data.
 
 
For the full documentation, please see the source methodology at Wong, T., and P Switzer. 2023. 'Estimating future local climate hazard probabilities.' Technical Note. Washington, DC: World Resources Institute. Available online at: doi.org/10.46830/writn.22.00074.v2.
 
 
### Description of the Layers
 
 
**Annual Maximum Temperature (℃)**: The daily maximum temperature data for each year is extracted and averaged to calculate the yearly average maximum temperature. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
**Annual Minimum Temperature (℃)**: The daily minimum temperature data for each year is extracted and averaged to calculate the yearly average minimum temperature. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
**Annual Mean Temperature (℃)**: The daily mean temperature is calculated by averaging the daily minimum and maximum temperatures. The annual mean temperature is obtained by averaging the daily mean temperatures over the course of a year. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
**Annual Total Precipitation (mm/year)**: The daily precipitation values are summed over the entire year to calculate the annual total precipitation. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
**Annual Rainy Days (represented as integers)**: A rainy day is defined as a day with precipitation exceeding 2.5 mm (as per the India Meteorological Department). The total number of rainy days in a year is calculated by summing the rainy days throughout the year. The decadal average is the average of the annual values across 10 years.
 
 
### Visualizing the Data
 
 
The data is provided at a 25-km resolution and is presented as a raster with a time slider with a separate layer for each variable. The values are visualized using a gradient based on the selected year in the slider, ranging from lighter shade (indicating low values) to darker shade (representing higher values).

attributes.name: Gender Development Index
attributes.description:
The Gender Development Index (GDI), published by the UN Development Programme (UNDP), measures gender gaps in human development achievements by accounting for disparities between women and men in 3 basic dimensions of human development using the same component indicators as in the Human Development Index (HDI). The HDI is a summary measure of average achievement in key dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, being knowledgeable, and a decent standard of living. The HDI is the geometric mean of normalized indices for each of the 3 dimensions. The health dimension is assessed by life expectancy at birth; the education dimension is measured by mean of years of schooling for adults aged 25 years and more and expected years of schooling for children of school-entering age. The standard-of-living dimension is measured by gross national income per capita. The HDI uses the logarithm of income to reflect the diminishing importance of income with increasing gross national income (GNI). The scores for the 3 HDI dimension indices are then aggregated into a composite index using geometric mean. The GDI is the ratio of the HDIs calculated separately for females and males using the same methodology as in the HDI. It is a direct measure of gender gap, showing the female HDI as a percentage of the male HDI. The GDI is calculated for 161 countries in 2015 and shows how much women are lagging behind their male counterparts in each dimension of human development. It facilitates understanding of the real gender gap in human development achievements and is useful in designing policy tools to close the gap. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Learn More link.

attributes.name: bio.007 World Database on Protected Areas_replacement
World Database on Protected Areas
attributes.description:
The World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA) is the most comprehensive global spatial data set on marine and terrestrial protected areas available. Protected area data are provided via Protected Planet, the online interface for the WDPA. The WDPA is a joint initiative of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and the UN Environment Programme's World Conservation Monitoring Centre (UNEP-WCMC) to compile spatially referenced information about protected areas. The data are provided as shapefiles and updated monthly.   
  
Not all protected areas receive the same degree of protection. While some have strict guidelines designed to preserve intact ecosystems, others allow for sustainable land use, often including limited resource extraction. In addition, not all countries use the same terminology when designating a protected area. Universal management categories are designated by the IUCN that stipulate the level of protection for most protected areas. These categories are defined as follows:   
  
(Ia) Strict Nature Reserves: protected areas designed to preserve biodiversity and all geological features. Limited human use (e.g., scientific study, education) is allowed and carefully monitored. Strict nature reserves are often used to understand the impact of indirect human disturbance (e.g., burning fossil fuels) because of the area’s high level of preservation.   
  
(Ib) Wilderness Areas: protected areas managed to preserve ecosystem processes with limited human use. Wilderness areas cannot contain modern infrastructure (e.g., a visitor’s center), but they allow for local indigenous groups to maintain subsistence lifestyles. These areas are often established to restore disturbed environments.   
  
(II) National Parks: protected areas designed to preserve large-scale ecosystems and support human visitation. With conservation as a priority, these areas allow infrastructure and contribute to the local economy by providing opportunities for environmental educational and recreation.   
  
(III) National Monuments or Features: areas established to protect a specific natural feature (e.g., cave, grove) or human-made monument with significant historical, spiritual, or environmental importance and the immediate surroundings. Accordingly, natural monuments or features are typically smaller in area and have high human impact resulting from visitor traffic.   
  
(IV) Habitat and Species Management Areas: areas designed to conserve specific wildlife populations and/or habitats. Habitat and species management areas often exist within a larger ecosystem or protected area and are carefully managed (e.g., through hunting abatement or habitat restoration) to conserve a target species or habitat.   
  
(V) Protected Landscapes and Seascapes: protected areas with ecological, biological, or cultural importance that have been shaped by human use of the landscape. Protected landscapes and seascapes typically cover entire bodies of land or ocean and allow for a number of for-profit activities (e.g., ecotourism) in accordance with the region’s management plan.   
  
(VI) Protected Areas with Sustainable Use of Natural Resources: areas designed to manage natural resources and uphold the livelihoods of surrounding communities. These regions have a low level of human occupation, small-scale developments (i.e., not industrial), and part of the landscape in its natural condition.

attributes.name: Aqueduct Seasonal Variability
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
Seasonal variability measures the average within-year variability of available water supply, including both renewable surface and groundwater supplies. Higher values indicate wider variations of available supply within a year. These values were then converted into risk scores based on the thresholds defined in the methodology. These risk scores range from low variability (coefficient of variation <0.33) to extremely high variability (coefficient of variation >1.33). Seasonal variability values are available per sub-basin (HydroBASIN level 6).  
  
### Methodology  
  
Aqueduct used the global hydrological model, PCRaster Global Water Balance (PCR-GLOBWB
2), to calculate five indicators. Seasonal variability is one of those indicators and was calculated using the available water supply time series from the default PCR-GLOBWB 2. 

  
  
Seasonal or within-year variability is defined as the coefficient of variation (CV) of available water between months in a year for each sub-basin. The CV was calculated by dividing the standard deviation (SD) of the available water supply within a year by the year’s mean available water supply.

  
  
Finally, raw baseline seasonal variability were converted to risk scores between 0 and 5, based on quantiles. These scores were placed into categories indicating how high the risk for this indicator is. The thresholds for raw seasonal variability values and the corresponding risk scores that were used in each category are defined below as Risk Category (Risk Scores): Raw Value Thresholds.

- Low (0-1): < 0.33
- Low to medium (1-2): 0.33 - 0.66
- Medium to high (2-3): 0.66 - 1.0
- High (3-4): 1.0 - 1.33
- Extremely high (4-5): > 1.33

  
  
For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://www.wri.org/publication/aqueduct-30).  
  
### Additional Information

info.name: Aqueduct Seasonal Variability
info.technical_title: Seasonal Variability, Aqueduct 4.0
info.functions: Measures the average within-year variability of available water supply, including both renewable surface and groundwater supplies
info.cautions:
Although the underlying models have been validated, the results were not. Seasonal variability remains subjective and cannot be measured directly. The lack of direct validation makes it impossible to assess some of the parameters in our calculation such as the length of the input time series, regression method and optimal moving window size.

  
  
In addition, the full timeseries of PCR-GLOBWB 2 (1979 to 2019) was analyzed.Seasonal variability using different ranges was not analyzed. The human and climatic influence and on available water is likely to be more profound in recent years.

  
  
Coastal and island sub-basins were often grouped to make the area of the sub-basins more homogeneous. The assumption of shared water resources might not hold in aggregated coastal sub-basins.
 
  
  
Water resources in PCR-GLOBWB 2 were pooled in abstraction zones. This assumption differs from the sub-basin approach in Aqueduct. This was one of the prime reasons for further processing of the PCR-GLOBWB 2 data.
 
  
  
Results were tailored towards large scale comparison of water related risks. The indicators have limited added value on a local scale.

attributes.name: Variabilidad estacional del acueducto
attributes.description:
### Visión general  
  
La variabilidad estacional mide la variabilidad promedio dentro del año del suministro de agua disponible, incluidos los suministros renovables de aguas superficiales y subterráneas. Los valores más altos indican variaciones más amplias de la oferta disponible dentro de un año. Estos valores se convirtieron en puntuaciones de riesgo basadas en los umbrales definidos en la metodología. Estas puntuaciones de riesgo van desde una baja variabilidad (coeficiente de variación <0,33) hasta una variabilidad extremadamente alta (coeficiente de variación >1,33). Los valores de variabilidad estacional están disponibles por subcuenca (nivel 6 de HydroBASIN).  
  
### Metodología  
  
Acueducto utilizó el modelo hidrológico global, PCRaster Global Water Balance (PCR-GLOBWB
2), para calcular cinco indicadores. La variabilidad estacional es uno de esos indicadores y se calculó utilizando la serie temporal de suministro de agua disponible a partir de la PCR-GLOBWB 2 predeterminada. 

La variabilidad estacional o dentro del año se define como el coeficiente de variación (CV) del agua disponible entre meses en un año para cada subcuenca. El CV se calculó dividiendo la desviación estándar (DE) del suministro de agua disponible dentro de un año por el suministro medio de agua disponible del año.

Finalmente, la variabilidad estacional basal bruta se convirtió en puntuaciones de riesgo entre 0 y 5, basadas en cuantiles. Estos puntajes se colocaron en categorías que indican qué tan alto es el riesgo para este indicador. Los umbrales para los valores brutos de variabilidad estacional y las puntuaciones de riesgo correspondientes que se utilizaron en cada categoría se definen a continuación como Categoría de riesgo (Puntuaciones de riesgo): Umbrales de valor bruto.

- Baja (0-1): < 0,33 - Baja a media (1-2): 0,33 - 0,66 - Media a alta (2-3): 0,66 - 1,0 - Alta (3-4): 1,0 - 1,33 - Extremadamente alta (4-5): > 1,33

Para obtener la documentación completa, consulte la fuente [metodología](https://www.wri.org/publication/aqueduct-30).  
  
### Información adicional  
  
Resource Watch muestra solo un subconjunto del conjunto de datos. Para acceder al conjunto de datos completo e información adicional, haga clic en el botón "Más información".  
  
### Descargo de responsabilidad  
  
Extractos de esta página de descripción fueron tomados de los metadatos de origen.

info.name: Variabilidad estacional del acueducto
info.technical_title: Variabilidad estacional, Acueducto 3.0
info.functions: Mide la variabilidad media dentro de un año del suministro de agua disponible, incluidos los suministros renovables de aguas superficiales y subterráneas
info.cautions:
Aunque los modelos subyacentes han sido validados, los resultados no lo fueron. La variabilidad estacional sigue siendo subjetiva y no se puede medir directamente. La falta de validación directa hace que sea imposible evaluar algunos de los parámetros en nuestro cálculo, como la longitud de la serie de tiempo de entrada, el método de regresión y el tamaño óptimo de la ventana móvil.

Además, se analizaron las series completas de PCR-GLOBWB 2 (1960 a 2014). No se analizó la variabilidad estacional utilizando diferentes rangos. Es probable que la influencia humana y climática y sobre el agua disponible sea más profunda en los últimos años.

Las subcuencas costeras e insulares a menudo se agrupaban para hacer que el área de las subcuencas fuera más homogénea. La suposición de recursos hídricos compartidos podría no mantenerse en las subcuencas costeras agregadas.
 
Los recursos hídricos en PCR-GLOBWB 2 se agruparon en zonas de extracción. Este supuesto difiere del enfoque de subcuenca en Acueducto. Esta fue una de las principales razones para el procesamiento posterior de los datos de PCR-GLOBWB 2.
 
Los resultados se adaptaron a la comparación a gran escala de los riesgos relacionados con el agua. Los indicadores tienen un valor añadido limitado a escala local.

attributes.name: நீர்க்குழாய் பருவகால மாறுபாடு
attributes.description:
### கண்ணோட்டம்  
  
பருவகால மாறுபாடுகள் புதுப்பிக்கத்தக்க மேற்பரப்பு மற்றும் நிலத்தடி நீர் வழங்கல்கள் உட்பட, கிடைக்கக்கூடிய நீர் வழங்கலின் சராசரி மாறுபாட்டை ஆண்டுக்குள் அளவிடுகிறது. உயர்ந்த மதிப்புகள் ஒரு வருடத்திற்குள் கிடைக்கக்கூடிய வழங்கலின் பரந்த வேறுபாடுகளைக் குறிக்கின்றன. இந்த மதிப்புகள் பின்னர் வழிமுறையில் வரையறுக்கப்பட்ட வரம்புகளின் அடிப்படையில் ஆபத்து மதிப்பெண்களாக மாற்றப்பட்டன. இந்த ஆபத்து மதிப்பெண்கள் குறைந்த மாறுபாடு (மாறுபாட்டின் குணகம் <0.33) முதல் மிக உயர்ந்த மாறுபாடு (மாறுபாட்டின் குணகம் >1.33) வரை இருக்கும். பருவகால மாறுபாடு மதிப்புகள் ஒரு துணை வடிநிலத்திற்கு கிடைக்கின்றன (ஹைட்ரோபேசின் நிலை 6).  
  
### முறைமை  
  
Aqueduct உலகளாவிய நீரியல் மாதிரி, PCRaster Global Water Balance (PCR-GLOBWB) ஐப் பயன்படுத்தியது
2) ஐந்து குறிகாட்டிகள் கணக்கிட. பருவகால மாறுபாடு என்பது அந்த குறிகாட்டிகளில் ஒன்றாகும், மேலும் இயல்புநிலை பி.சி.ஆர்-குளோப்டபிள்யுபி 2 இலிருந்து கிடைக்கக்கூடிய நீர் வழங்கல் நேரத் தொடரைப் பயன்படுத்தி கணக்கிடப்பட்டது. 

பருவகால அல்லது வருடத்திற்குள் ஏற்படும் மாறுபாடு என்பது ஒவ்வொரு உப வடிநிலத்திற்கும் ஒரு வருடத்தில் மாதங்களுக்கிடையிலான கிடைக்கக்கூடிய நீரின் மாறுபாட்டின் குணகம் (சி.வி) என வரையறுக்கப்படுகிறது. கிடைக்கக்கூடிய நீர் வழங்கலின் நிலையான விலகலை (எஸ்டி) ஒரு வருடத்திற்குள் ஆண்டின் சராசரி கிடைக்கக்கூடிய நீர் வழங்கலால் வகுத்து சி.வி கணக்கிடப்பட்டது.

இறுதியாக, மூல அடிப்படை பருவகால மாறுபாடுகள் குவான்டைல்களின் அடிப்படையில் 0 முதல் 5 வரையிலான ஆபத்து மதிப்பெண்களாக மாற்றப்பட்டன. இந்த குறிகாட்டிக்கான ஆபத்து எவ்வளவு அதிகமாக உள்ளது என்பதைக் குறிக்கும் வகைகளாக இந்த மதிப்பெண்கள் வைக்கப்பட்டன. மூல பருவகால மாறுபாடு மதிப்புகளுக்கான நுழைவாயில்கள் மற்றும் ஒவ்வொரு பிரிவிலும் பயன்படுத்தப்படும் தொடர்புடைய ஆபத்து மதிப்பெண்கள் கீழே இடர் வகை (இடர் மதிப்பெண்கள்) என வரையறுக்கப்படுகின்றன: மூல மதிப்பு வரம்புகள்.

- லோ (0-1): < 0.33 - குறைந்த நடுத்தரம் (1-2): 0.33 - 0.66 - நடுத்தரத்திலிருந்து உயர் (2-3): 0.66 - 1.0 - உயர் (3-4): 1.0 - 1.33 - மிக அதிக (4-5): > 1.33

முழு ஆவணப்படுத்தலுக்கு, மூலத்தைப் பார்க்கவும் [முறையியல்](https://www.wri.org/publication/aqueduct-30).  
  
### கூடுதல் தகவல்  
  
Resource Watch தரவுத்தொகுப்பின் ஒரு துணைக்குழுவை மட்டுமே காட்டுகிறது. முழு தரவுத்தொகுப்பு மற்றும் கூடுதல் தகவலுக்கான அணுகலுக்கு, "மேலும் அறிக" பொத்தானைக் கிளிக் செய்க.  
  
### பொறுப்புத்துறப்பு  
  
இந்த விளக்கப் பக்கத்தின் பகுதிகள் மூல மெட்டாடேட்டாவிலிருந்து எடுக்கப்பட்டன.

info.name: நீர்க்குழாய் பருவகால மாறுபாடு
info.technical_title: பருவகால மாறுபாடு, நீர்க்குழாய் 3.0
info.functions: புதுப்பிக்கத்தக்க மேற்பரப்பு மற்றும் நிலத்தடி நீர் வழங்கல்கள் உட்பட கிடைக்கக்கூடிய நீர் வழங்கலின் சராசரி மாறுபாட்டை அளவிடுகிறது
info.cautions:
அடிப்படை மாதிரிகள் சரிபார்க்கப்பட்டிருந்தாலும், முடிவுகள் இல்லை. பருவகால மாறுபாடு அகநிலையாக உள்ளது மற்றும் நேரடியாக அளவிட முடியாது. நேரடி சரிபார்ப்பு இல்லாததால், உள்ளீட்டு நேரத் தொடரின் நீளம், பின்னடைவு முறை மற்றும் உகந்த நகரும் சாளர அளவு போன்ற எங்கள் கணக்கீட்டில் உள்ள சில அளவுருக்களை மதிப்பிடுவது சாத்தியமற்றது.

கூடுதலாக, பி.சி.ஆர்-குளோப்டபிள்யூபி 2 (1960 முதல் 2014 வரை) இன் முழு நேரங்களும் பகுப்பாய்வு செய்யப்பட்டன. வெவ்வேறு வரம்புகளைப் பயன்படுத்தி பருவகால மாறுபாடு பகுப்பாய்வு செய்யப்படவில்லை. மனித மற்றும் தட்பவெப்பநிலை தாக்கம் மற்றும் கிடைக்கக்கூடிய நீரின் மீதான தாக்கம் சமீபத்திய ஆண்டுகளில் மிகவும் ஆழமாக இருக்க வாய்ப்புள்ளது.

கரையோர மற்றும் தீவு உப வடிநிலங்கள் பெரும்பாலும் துணை-படுகைகளின் பரப்பளவை மேலும் ஒரே மாதிரியானதாக மாற்றுவதற்காக வகைப்படுத்தப்பட்டன. பகிரப்பட்ட நீர் வளங்களின் அனுமானம் ஒருங்கிணைக்கப்பட்ட கரையோர உப வடிநிலங்களில் நீடிக்காமல் போகலாம்.
 
பி.சி.ஆர்-குளோப்டபிள்யுபி 2 இல் உள்ள நீர் வளங்கள் அருவமான மண்டலங்களில் தொகுக்கப்பட்டன. இந்த அனுமானம் அக்யூடக்டில் உள்ள துணை-பேசின் அணுகுமுறையிலிருந்து வேறுபடுகிறது. இது பி.சி.ஆர்-குளோப்டபிள்யுபி 2 தரவுகளின் மேலும் செயலாக்கத்திற்கான முக்கிய காரணங்களில் ஒன்றாகும்.
 
முடிவுகள் நீர் தொடர்பான அபாயங்களின் பெரிய அளவிலான ஒப்பீட்டை நோக்கி வடிவமைக்கப்பட்டன. குறிகாட்டிகள் உள்ளூர் அளவில் மட்டுப்படுத்தப்பட்ட கூடுதல் மதிப்பைக் கொண்டுள்ளன.
info.citation: ஹோஃப்ஸ்டே, ஆர்., எஸ்.குஸ்மா, எஸ்.வாக்கர், ஈ.எச்.சுடனுட்ஜாஜா, மற்றும் பலர். அல். 2019. "நீர்க்குழாய் 3.0: புதுப்பிக்கப்பட்ட முடிவு-தொடர்புடைய உலகளாவிய நீர் ஆபத்து குறிகாட்டிகள்." தொழில்நுட்ப குறிப்பு. வாஷிங்டன், டி.சி: வேர்ல்ட் ரிசோர்சஸ் இன்ஸ்டிடியூட். ஆன்லைனில் கிடைக்கும் முகவரி: https://www.wri.org/publication/aqueduct-30. Resource Watch, (date) மூலம் அணுகப்பட்டது. [www.resourcewatch.org] (https://www.resourcewatch.org)

attributes.name: ఆక్విడక్ట్ సీజనల్ వేరియబిలిటీ
attributes.description:
### అవలోకనం  
  
సీజనల్ వేరియబిలిటీ పునరుత్పాదక ఉపరితలం మరియు భూగర్భ జలాల సరఫరా రెండింటితో సహా, లభ్యం అవుతున్న నీటి సరఫరా యొక్క ఏడాదిలోపు సగటు వైవిధ్యాన్ని కొలుస్తుంది. అధిక విలువలు ఒక సంవత్సరంలోపు లభ్యం అవుతున్న సప్లై యొక్క విస్తృత వైవిధ్యాలను సూచిస్తాయి. ఈ విలువలు తరువాత మెథడాలజీలో నిర్వచించబడ్డ త్రెష్ హోల్డ్ ల ఆధారంగా రిస్క్ స్కోర్ లుగా మార్చబడ్డాయి. ఈ రిస్క్ స్కోర్ లు తక్కువ వేరియబిలిటీ (వైవిధ్యం యొక్క గుణకం <0.33) నుంచి అత్యంత అధిక వేరియబిలిటీ (వైవిధ్యం యొక్క గుణకం >1.33) వరకు ఉంటాయి. సీజనల్ వేరియబిలిటీ విలువలు ప్రతి సబ్ బేసిన్ కు లభ్యం అవుతాయి (హైడ్రోబాసిన్ లెవల్ 6).  
  
#### మెథడాలజీ  
  
అక్విడక్ట్ గ్లోబల్ హైడ్రోలాజికల్ మోడల్, PCRAster గ్లోబల్ వాటర్ బ్యాలెన్స్ (PCR-GLOBWB) ను ఉపయోగించింది.
2), ఐదు ఇండికేటర్లను లెక్కించడానికి. సీజనల్ వేరియబిలిటీ అనేది ఆ సూచికల్లో ఒకటి మరియు డిఫాల్ట్ పిసిఆర్-గ్లోబ్ డబ్ల్యుబి 2 నుండి లభ్యం అవుతున్న నీటి సరఫరా సమయ శ్రేణిని ఉపయోగించి లెక్కించబడింది. 

సీజనల్ లేదా ఇన్-ఇయర్ వేరియబిలిటీ అనేది ప్రతి సబ్ బేసిన్ కొరకు ఒక సంవత్సరంలో నెలల మధ్య లభ్యం అవుతున్న నీటి యొక్క వైవిధ్యం యొక్క గుణకం (సివి)గా నిర్వచించబడుతుంది. ఒక సంవత్సరంలోపు లభ్యమయ్యే నీటి సరఫరా యొక్క స్టాండర్డ్ డీవియేషన్ (ఎస్ డి)ని సంవత్సరం యొక్క సగటు నీటి సరఫరా ద్వారా భాగించడం ద్వారా సివిని లెక్కించారు.

చివరగా, ముడి బేస్ లైన్ సీజనల్ వేరియబిలిటీని క్వాంటిల్స్ ఆధారంగా 0 మరియు 5 మధ్య రిస్క్ స్కోర్ లుగా మార్చారు. ఈ స్కోర్లు ఈ ఇండికేటర్ కు రిస్క్ ఎంత ఎక్కువగా ఉందో సూచించే కేటగిరీల్లో ఉంచబడ్డాయి. ముడి సీజనల్ వేరియబిలిటీ విలువల కొరకు త్రెష్ హోల్డ్ లు మరియు ప్రతి కేటగిరీలో ఉపయోగించే సంబంధిత రిస్క్ స్కోర్ లు రిస్క్ కేటగిరీ (రిస్క్ స్కోర్ లు): రా వాల్యూ త్రెష్ హోల్డ్స్ గా దిగువన నిర్వచించబడ్డాయి.

- తక్కువ (0-1): < 0.33 - తక్కువ నుండి మధ్యస్థం (1-2): 0.33 - 0.66 - మధ్యస్థం నుండి ఎక్కువ (2-3): 0.66 - 1.0 - అధిక (3-4): 1.0 - 1.33 - చాలా ఎక్కువ (4-5): > 1.33

పూర్తి డాక్యుమెంటేషన్ కొరకు, దయచేసి సోర్స్ [మెథడాలజీ](https://www.wri.org/publication/aqueduct-30) చూడండి.  
  
### అదనపు సమాచారం  
  
రిసోర్స్ వాచ్ డేటాసెట్ యొక్క ఉపసమితిని మాత్రమే చూపుతుంది. పూర్తి డేటాసెట్ మరియు అదనపు సమాచారాన్ని యాక్సెస్ చేసుకోవడానికి, "మరింత తెలుసుకోండి" బటన్ మీద క్లిక్ చేయండి.  
  
### డిస్ క్లెయిమర్  
  
ఈ వివరణ పేజీ యొక్క సారాంశాలు మూల మెటాడేటా నుండి తీసుకోబడ్డాయి.

info.technical_title: సీజనల్ వేరియబిలిటీ, అక్విడక్ట్ 3.0
info.functions: పునరుత్పాదక ఉపరితలం మరియు భూగర్భ జలాల సరఫరా రెండింటితో సహా లభ్యం అవుతున్న నీటి సరఫరా యొక్క సగటును ఏడాదిలోపు వ్యత్యాసాన్ని లెక్కిస్తుంది.
info.cautions:
అంతర్లీన నమూనాలు ధృవీకరించబడినప్పటికీ, ఫలితాలు లేవు. సీజనల్ వేరియబిలిటీ సబ్జెక్టివ్ గా ఉంటుంది మరియు నేరుగా కొలవలేం. ప్రత్యక్ష ధ్రువీకరణ లేకపోవడం వల్ల, ఇన్ పుట్ టైమ్ సిరీస్ యొక్క పొడవు, రిగ్రెషన్ విధానం మరియు ఆప్టిమల్ మూవింగ్ విండో సైజు వంటి మా లెక్కింపులోని కొన్ని పరామీటర్లను మదింపు చేయడం అసాధ్యం చేస్తుంది.

దీనికి అదనంగా, పిసిఆర్-గ్లోబ్ డబ్ల్యుబి 2 (1960 నుండి 2014 వరకు) యొక్క పూర్తి కాలవ్యవధులను విశ్లేషించారు. వివిధ శ్రేణులను ఉపయోగించి కాలానుగుణ వైవిధ్యతను విశ్లేషించలేదు. మానవ మరియు వాతావరణ ప్రభావం మరియు అందుబాటులో ఉన్న నీటిపై ఇటీవలి సంవత్సరాల్లో మరింత లోతుగా ఉండే అవకాశం ఉంది.

తీరప్రాంత మరియు ద్వీప ఉప-బేసిన్లు తరచుగా ఉప-బేసిన్ల యొక్క వైశాల్యాన్ని మరింత సజాతీయంగా చేయడానికి సమూహం చేయబడ్డాయి. ఉమ్మడి నీటి వనరుల ఊహ మొత్తం తీర ఉప-బేసిన్లలో ఉండకపోవచ్చు.
 
పిసిఆర్-గ్లోబ్ డబ్ల్యుబి ౨ లోని నీటి వనరులు అబ్ స్ట్రాక్షన్ జోన్లలో పూల్ చేయబడ్డాయి. ఈ ఊహ ఆక్విడక్ట్ లోని సబ్ బేసిన్ అప్రోచ్ కు భిన్నంగా ఉంటుంది. పిసిఆర్-గ్లోబ్యుబి 2 డేటాను తదుపరి ప్రాసెసింగ్ చేయడానికి ఇది ప్రధాన కారణాలలో ఒకటి.
 
నీటి సంబంధిత ప్రమాదాలను పెద్ద ఎత్తున పోల్చడానికి ఫలితాలు రూపొందించబడ్డాయి. ఇండికేటర్లు స్థానిక స్థాయిలో పరిమిత అదనపు విలువను కలిగి ఉంటాయి.

attributes.name: ocn.018 Fully and Highly Protected Marine Areas
Fully and Highly Protected Marine Areas
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Fully and Highly Protected Marine Areas dataset as shown on Resource Watch presents marine protected areas (MPAs) that are fully or highly protected. The [Marine Protection Atlas (MPAtlas)](https://mpatlas.org/) uses the [World Database on Protected Areas](https://www.protectedplanet.net/en/thematic-areas/marine-protected-areas) as a starting point, then assesses the current protection status of listed MPAs based on additional sources and research. This global dataset was first created in 2020 and in the future will be regularly updated, as new MPAs are created, protections change, and currently designated areas are implemented.

  
  
MPAs are essential for safeguarding biodiversity and the health of marine ecosystems. They provide sanctuary for species to mature and reproduce, and they help restore healthy populations within and beyond their borders. MPAs also build resilience against threats such as climate change and pollution by maintaining vital natural processes, storing carbon, buffering coastlines, and ensuring sustainable food supplies for coastal communities. However, different MPAs may offer different levels of protection, from minor restrictions to the full exclusion of most commercial activity. Robust scientific evidence indicates that no-take zones (where no extractive activities are allowed) and highly protected areas yield the greatest conservation benefits.

  
  
The MPAtlas brings together the best available information on marine protection around the world, so that the marine conservation community can work together to protect at least [30% of the world's oceans by 2030](https://www.campaignfornature.org/science-page). This more detailed approach to MPA data provides a more nuanced look at progress toward conservation goals and the outcomes that can be expected from existing protections.
  
  
### Methodology  
  
MPAtlas takes the WDPA as its starting point and examines the listed MPAs in depth, adding to or replacing WDPA records with information from original research using more detailed or up-to-date sources, such as national or regional databases, official documentation, or management plans. These additions can include more accurate spatial data, such as the addition of boundaries for individual zones within an MPA. It can also include more detailed information about site regulations and management, both of which are directly related to conservation outcomes.

  
  
MPAtlas coverage numbers differ from those of other sources for two primary reasons:
1. MPAtlas attempts to identify and distinguish protected areas that are legally designated but are still awaiting implementation from those that are fully in effect on the water. The project also identifies committed or proposed protected areas that have not yet achieved legal or authoritative recognition.
2. MPA coverage data is reported by protection level, as no-take and fully and highly protected areas are those which afford the greatest conservation benefits. The project accomplishes this by conducting detailed assessments using widely-accepted, scientifically-based criteria for measuring an MPA’s protection level and associated conservation outcomes. Detailed information about the assessment process [can be found here](https://marine-conservation.org/mpatlas-assessments/).

  
  
For the full documentation, please see the source [methodology](https://mpatlas.org/methods).
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows [the full WDPA](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/bio007-World-Database-on-Protected-Areas_replacement) and [the MPA subset](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/bio007b-Marine-Protected-Areas), on which the MPAtlas is based.

  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the Marine Protected Atlas. The MPAtlas includes all MPAs in the WDPA, but because these are already mapped elsewhere, Resource Watch displays only those MPAtlas entries with confirmed partial or complete protections from fishing and extractive commercial activity.

  
  
For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.
  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [GitHub](https://github.com/resource-watch/nrt-scripts/tree/master/ocn_018_fully_highly_protected_marine_areas).
  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

attributes.name: cli.059.rw1 Projected Change in Extreme Precipitation Days
Projected Change in Extreme Precipitation Days
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Projected Change in Extreme Precipitation Days dataset shows the change in annual average days of extreme precipitation at ten year intervals between 2000 and 2080, compared to a baseline time period of 1960-1990. An extreme precipitation day is defined as a day where precipitation is greater than the 99th percentile precipitation compared to the baseline period. The data shown at each ten year interval represents a 31-year average, centered around the indicated year. For example, the number of extreme precipitation days in 2000 is actually an average of the annual number of extreme precipitation days between the years 1985 and 2015. Precipitation projections are based on the future greenhouse gas emission rates determined by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change’s (IPCC’s) Representative Concentration Pathways (RCP) 8.5. RCP 8.5 is a hypothetical scenario where there is no decrease in greenhouse gas emission rates within the 21st century. The change in extreme precipitation is shown as the multiplicative difference between annual average days of extreme precipitation during the projected decade and the baseline time period. Values greater than 1 indicate that extreme precipitation is increasing, while values less than one indicate that the number is decreasing. Data is presented at a spatial resolution of 0.25°.
  
  
The increase in global greenhouse gas concentrations, and the resulting change in climate, is set to fundamentally alter our relationship with the planet, impacting agriculture, infrastructure, disaster management, and human conflict. In order to anticipate and adapt to these changes, the Projected Change in Extreme Precipitation Days dataset provides projections on how extreme precipitation patterns are likely to change in the coming decades. Generally, extreme precipitation events are expected to become more frequent worldwide. 
  
  
This dataset has been processed by Vizzuality and the World Resources Institute using the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Earth Exchange Global Daily Downscaled Projections (NEX-GDDP). The NEX-GDDP dataset is intended to assist the scientific community in conducting studies of climate change impacts at local to regional scales, and to enhance public understanding of possible future global climate patterns at the spatial scale of individual towns, cities, and watersheds. A previous version of this dataset was processed and produced by the [Partnership for Resilience and Preparedness (PREP)](https://prepdata.org/), aiding in PREP’s mission to build resilience to climate change by improving access to climate data.  
  
### Methodology  
  
The Projected Change in Extreme Precipitation Days dataset was created with precipitation data from NEX-GDDP. The NEX-GDDP datasets were derived from Global Circulation Model (GCM) experiments that were produced for the [Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fifth Assessment Report (AR5)](https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/05/SYR_AR5_FINAL_full_wcover.pdf). These experiments, known as the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project phase 5 (CMIP5) included results from climate models designed to simulate climate under different levels of greenhouse gas concentrations.  

  
  
CMIP5 data include a large number of models (45), climate scenarios (4), years (150+), and variables (20-40). Even at its coarse resolution (1-4°) this results in billions of layers. By downscaling, NEX-GDDP extracts only the data they require and reduces the overall size of the data, using the [Sheffield et al. (2006)](https://journals.ametsoc.org/jcli/article/19/13/3088/30860/Development-of-a-50-Year-High-Resolution-Global) dataset as historical reference.  

  
  
The annual average extreme precipitation days for each year, climate model, and scenario were calculated using NEX-GDDP data on a per-pixel basis. This was done by extracting the daily precipitation values for a given year and summing the number of days where precipitation was greater than the 99th percentile precipitation during the baseline period. The annual average extreme precipitation days were combined into 31-year averages for the baseline time period of 1960-1990 and nine periods centered on the start of each decade from 2000 to 2080. Then each of the nine projected decades were divided by the baseline average to calculate the projected change in extreme precipitation. Values greater than 1 indicate that extreme precipitation is increasing, while values less than one indicate that the number is decreasing.

  
  
The data shown at each ten year interval represents a 31-year average, centered around the indicated year. For example, the extreme precipitation days in 2000 is actually an average of the annual extreme precipitation days between the years 1985 and 2015. 31-year averages were chosen because they minimize the effects of annual and decadal variation and highlight the long-term climate signal. The baseline period was selected to align with longstanding guidance from the World Meteorological Association.
  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch also shows projected change NEX-GDDP RCP 8.5 data for [Projected Change in Annual Average Temperature](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/4ca6826c-718d-457d-b4e2-e9277d7ed62c), [Projected Change in Annual Average Minimum Temperature](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/3d8e2e82-b33a-4898-90e5-6e4a1d007b82), [Projected Change in Annual Average Maximum Temperature](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/c4b12251-2d61-458f-a2c0-096c37901ade), [Projected Change in Heating Degree Days](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/1d2f4eae-10e1-4ea6-980c-501b34106de2), [Projected Change in Cooling Degree Days](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/6fa000b5-8d91-46c8-8502-07427bc5eafc), [Projected Change in Frost Free Season](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/d3f512c0-fbb0-47d5-9ac9-a452574c8e58), [Projected Change in Extreme Heat Days](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/3941bbba-181b-434a-84c3-fcdfa5234735), [Projected Change in Cumulative Precipitation](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/faf79d2c-5e54-4591-9d70-4bd1029c18e6), and [Projected Change in Dry Spells](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/d0f46576-411d-48aa-8df8-d89a3792cdce).

  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the data. Additional data is available for emissions scenario RCP 4.5. For access to the original NEX-GDDP dataset and additional information, see the Learn More link.
  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/tree/master/cli_050-059_066-075_nexgddp_and_loca).  
  
### Disclaimer

info.name: Projected Change in Extreme Precipitation Days
info.technical_title: Extreme Precipitation Days, derived from NASA Earth Exchange Global Daily Downscaled Projections (NEX-GDDP)
info.functions: Projected change in annual average days of extreme precipitation
info.cautions:
- Some GCM perform better than others in recreating regional climate patterns, such as monsoons, in hindcasts. For specific applications, it may be appropriate to select individual models based on regional performance.
- The downscaling approaches used to produce these indicators inherently assume that the relative spatial patterns in temperature and precipitation will remain constant under future climate change. Dramatic shifts in global weather patterns, such as the slowing or reversal of major air and ocean currents are possible, but will not be captured in these indicators.
- The historical data used for downscaling varies in quality across the world. In particular, areas that have short records or sparse coverage of in situ weather observations may have reduced accuracy.
- Because GCM are developed by independent research teams and incorporate different assumptions and mechanisms, it is likely that they cover a substantial range of probable futures. We provide both low and high estimates so that users can see and evaluate this likely range of outcomes.
info.citation:
Gassert, F., E. Cornejo, and E. Nilson. 2021. “Making Climate Data Accessible: Methods for Producing NEX-GDDP and LOCA Downscaled Climate Indicators” Technical Note. Washington, DC: World Resources Institute. Available online at https://www.wri.org/research/making-climate-data-accessible. [www.resourcewatch.org](https://www.resourcewatch.org/).

  
  
We acknowledge the World Climate Research Programme's Working Group on Coupled Modelling, which is responsible for CMIP, and we thank the climate modeling groups for producing and making available their model output. The U.S. Department of Energy's Program for Climate Model Diagnosis and Intercomparison provides coordinating support and development of software infrastructure in partnership with the Global Organization for Earth System Science Portals for CMIP.

  
  
Climate scenarios used were from the NEX-GDDP dataset, prepared by the Climate Analytics Group and NASA Ames Research Center using the NASA Earth Exchange, and distributed by the NASA Center for Climate Simulation (NCCS).

Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/tree/master/cli_050-059_066-075_nexgddp_and_loca).  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.

info.name: Projected Change in Extreme Precipitation Days
info.technical_title: Extreme Precipitation Days, derived from NASA Earth Exchange Global Daily Downscaled Projections (NEX-GDDP)
info.functions: Projected change in annual average days of extreme precipitation
info.cautions:
- Some GCM perform better than others in recreating regional climate patterns, such as monsoons, in hindcasts. For specific applications, it may be appropriate to select individual models based on regional performance.
- The downscaling approaches used to produce these indicators inherently assume that the relative spatial patterns in temperature and precipitation will remain constant under future climate change. Dramatic shifts in global weather patterns, such as the slowing or reversal of major air and ocean currents are possible, but will not be captured in these indicators.
- The historical data used for downscaling varies in quality across the world. In particular, areas that have short records or sparse coverage of in situ weather observations may have reduced accuracy.
- Because GCM are developed by independent research teams and incorporate different assumptions and mechanisms, it is likely that they cover a substantial range of probable futures. We provide both low and high estimates so that users can see and evaluate this likely range of outcomes.

attributes.name: Cambio proyectado en días de precipitación extrema
attributes.description:
### Visión general  
  
El conjunto de datos de cambio proyectado en días de precipitación extrema muestra el cambio en los días promedio anuales de precipitación extrema a intervalos de diez años entre 2000 y 2080, en comparación con un período de referencia de 1960-1990. Un día de precipitación extrema se define como un día en el que la precipitación es mayor que la precipitación del percentil 99 en comparación con el período de referencia. Los datos mostrados en cada intervalo de diez años representan un promedio de 31 años, centrado en torno al año indicado. Por ejemplo, el número de días de precipitación extrema en 2000 es en realidad un promedio del número anual de días de precipitación extrema entre los años 1985 y 2015. Las proyecciones de precipitación se basan en las futuras tasas de emisión de gases de efecto invernadero determinadas por las Vías de Concentración Representativa (RCP) 8.5 del Grupo Intergubernamental de Expertos sobre el Cambio Climático (IPCC). RCP 8.5 es un escenario hipotético en el que no hay disminución en las tasas de emisión de gases de efecto invernadero dentro del siglo XXI. El cambio en la precipitación extrema se muestra como la diferencia multiplicativa entre los días promedio anuales de precipitación extrema durante la década proyectada y el período de referencia. Los valores mayores que 1 indican que la precipitación extrema está aumentando, mientras que los valores menores de uno indican que el número está disminuyendo. Los datos se presentan a una resolución espacial de 0,25°.
  
El aumento en las concentraciones globales de gases de efecto invernadero, y el cambio resultante en el clima, alterará fundamentalmente nuestra relación con el planeta, impactando la agricultura, la infraestructura, la gestión de desastres y los conflictos humanos. Con el fin de anticipar y adaptarse a estos cambios, el conjunto de datos de Cambio proyectado en días de precipitación extrema proporciona proyecciones sobre cómo es probable que cambien los patrones de precipitación extrema en las próximas décadas. En general, se espera que los eventos de precipitación extrema sean más frecuentes en todo el mundo. 
  
Este conjunto de datos ha sido procesado por Vizzuality y el Instituto de Recursos Mundiales utilizando el National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Earth Exchange Global Daily Downscaled Projections (NEX-GDDP). El conjunto de datos NEX-GDDP está destinado a ayudar a la comunidad científica a realizar estudios de los impactos del cambio climático a escala local a regional, y mejorar la comprensión pública de los posibles patrones climáticos globales futuros a escala espacial de pueblos, ciudades y cuencas hidrográficas individuales. Una versión anterior de este conjunto de datos fue procesada y producida por la [Asociación para la Resiliencia y la Preparación (PREP)](https://prepdata.org/), ayudando en la misión de PREP de construir resiliencia al cambio climático mejorando el acceso a los datos climáticos.  
  
### Metodología  
  
El conjunto de datos De Cambio Proyectado en Días de Precipitación Extrema se creó con datos de precipitación de NEX-GDDP. Los conjuntos de datos NEX-GDDP se derivaron de los experimentos del Modelo de Circulación Global (GCM) que se produjeron para el [Quinto Informe de Evaluación (AR5) del Grupo Intergubernamental de Expertos sobre el Cambio Climático (IPCC)](https://www.ipcc.ch/site/assets/uploads/2018/05/SYR_AR5_FINAL_full_wcover.pdf). Estos experimentos, conocidos como el Proyecto de Intercomparación de Modelos Acoplados fase 5 (CMIP5) incluyeron resultados de modelos climáticos diseñados para simular el clima bajo diferentes niveles de concentraciones de gases de efecto invernadero.  

Los datos de CMIP5 incluyen un gran número de modelos (45), escenarios climáticos (4), años (más de 150) y variables (20-40). Incluso a su resolución gruesa (1-4 °) esto resulta en miles de millones de capas. Al reducir la escala, NEX-GDDP extrae solo los datos que requieren y reduce el tamaño general de los datos, utilizando el conjunto de datos [Sheffield et al. (2006)](https://journals.ametsoc.org/jcli/article/19/13/3088/30860/Development-of-a-50-Year-High-Resolution-Global) como referencia histórica.  

El promedio anual de días de precipitación extrema para cada año, modelo climático y escenario se calculó utilizando datos de NEX-GDDP por píxel. Esto se hizo extrayendo los valores diarios de precipitación para un año determinado y sumando el número de días en que la precipitación fue mayor que la precipitación del percentil 99 durante el período de referencia. El promedio anual de días de precipitación extrema se combinó en promedios de 31 años para el período de referencia de 1960-1990 y nueve períodos centrados en el comienzo de cada década de 2000 a 2080. Luego, cada una de las nueve décadas proyectadas se dividió por el promedio de referencia para calcular el cambio proyectado en la precipitación extrema. Los valores mayores que 1 indican que la precipitación extrema está aumentando, mientras que los valores menores de uno indican que el número está disminuyendo.

Los datos mostrados en cada intervalo de diez años representan un promedio de 31 años, centrado en torno al año indicado. Por ejemplo, los días de precipitación extrema en 2000 son en realidad un promedio de los días anuales de precipitación extrema entre los años 1985 y 2015. Se eligieron promedios de 31 años porque minimizan los efectos de la variación anual y decenal y resaltan la señal climática a largo plazo. El período de referencia se seleccionó para alinearse con la orientación de larga data de la Asociación Meteorológica Mundial.
  
### Información adicional  
  
Resource Watch también muestra el cambio proyectado NEX-GDDP RCP 8.5 datos para [Cambio proyectado en la temperatura media anual](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/4ca6826c-718d-457d-b4e2-e9277d7ed62c), [Cambio proyectado en la temperatura mínima promedio anual](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/3d8e2e82-b33a-4898-90e5-6e4a1d007b82), [Cambio proyectado en la temperatura máxima promedio anual](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/c4b12251-2d61-458f-a2c0-096c37901ade), [Proyectado Cambio en los días de grado de calefacción](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/1d2f4eae-10e1-4ea6-980c-501b34106de2), [Cambio proyectado en los días de grado de enfriamiento](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/6fa000b5-8d91-46c8-8502-07427bc5eafc), [Cambio proyectado en la temporada libre de heladas](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/d3f512c0-fbb0-47d5-9ac9-a452574c8e58), [Cambio proyectado en días de calor extremo](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/3941bbba-181b-434a-84c3-fcdfa5234735), [ Cambio proyectado en la precipitación acumulada](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/faf79d2c-5e54-4591-9d70-4bd1029c18e6), y [Cambio proyectado en períodos secos](https://resourcewatch.org/data/explore/d0f46576-411d-48aa-8df8-d89a3792cdce).

Resource Watch muestra solo un subconjunto de los datos. Se dispone de datos adicionales para el escenario de emisiones RCP 4.5. Para obtener acceso al conjunto de datos original de NEX-GDDP e información adicional, consulte el vínculo Más información.
  
### Visualización de los datos  
  
Nuestro equipo reformateó este conjunto de datos antes de mostrarlo en Resource Watch. Consulte la documentación sobre cómo Resource Watch procesó los datos en [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/data-pre-processing/tree/master/cli_050-059_066-075_nexgddp_and_loca).  
  
### Descargo de responsabilidad

info.technical_title: Días de precipitación extrema, derivados de nasa Earth Exchange Global Daily Downscale Projections (NEX-GDDP)
info.functions: Cambio proyectado en el promedio anual de días de precipitación extrema
info.cautions:
- Algunos GCM se desempeñan mejor que otros en la recreación de patrones climáticos regionales, como los monzones, en hindcasts. Para aplicaciones específicas, puede ser apropiado seleccionar modelos individuales basados en el rendimiento regional.
Los enfoques de reducción de escala utilizados para producir estos indicadores asumen inherentemente que los patrones espaciales relativos en temperatura y precipitación se mantendrán constantes bajo el cambio climático futuro. Los cambios dramáticos en los patrones climáticos globales, como la desaceleración o reversión de las principales corrientes aéreas y oceánicas son posibles, pero no se capturarán en estos indicadores.
- Los datos históricos utilizados para la reducción de escala varían en calidad en todo el mundo. En particular, las áreas que tienen registros cortos o una cobertura escasa de observaciones meteorológicas in situ pueden tener una precisión reducida.
Debido a que los GCM son desarrollados por equipos de investigación independientes e incorporan diferentes supuestos y mecanismos, es probable que cubran un rango sustancial de futuros probables. Proporcionamos estimaciones bajas y altas para que los usuarios puedan ver y evaluar este rango probable de resultados.

Gassert, F., E. Cornejo y E. Nilson. 2021. Nota técnica "Making Climate Data Accessible: Methods for Producing NEX-GDDP and LOCA Downscaled Climate Indicators". Washington, DC: Instituto de Recursos Mundiales. Disponible en línea en https://www.wri.org/research/making-climate-data-accessible. [www.resourcewatch.org] (https://www.resourcewatch.org/).

Reconocemos al Grupo de Trabajo sobre Modelización Acoplada del Programa Mundial de Investigación Climática, que es responsable de CMIP, y agradecemos a los grupos de modelado climático por producir y poner a disposición sus resultados de modelos. El Programa de Diagnóstico e Intercomparación de Modelos Climáticos del Departamento de Energía de los Estados Unidos proporciona apoyo coordinado y desarrollo de infraestructura de software en asociación con la Organización Global de Portales de Ciencias del Sistema Terrestre para CMIP.

Los escenarios climáticos utilizados fueron del conjunto de datos NEX-GDDP, preparado por el Climate Analytics Group y el Centro de Investigación Ames de la NASA utilizando el NASA Earth Exchange, y distribuido por el Centro de Simulación Climática de la NASA (NCCS).
