attributes.name: Precipitation (5-Day)
attributes.description:
CHIRPS data, production led by the Climate Hazards Group at University of California, Santa Barbara (CHG UCSB), is a 30+ year quasi-global rainfall dataset. This data set spans 50°S-50°N (and all longitudes), starting in 1981 and spanning to near-present. As of February 12, 2015, version 2.0 of CHIRPS is complete and available to the public. CHIRPS incorporates 0.05°-resolution satellite imagery with on-the-ground precipitation station data to create gridded rainfall time series. Satellite data are derived from both microwave and infrared sensors. On-the-ground precipitation station data come from the Agromet Group of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the Global Historical Climate Network (GHCN). Two CHIRPS products are produced operationally: a rapid preliminary version and a later final version. The preliminary CHIRPS product is available, for the entire domain, 2 days after the end of a pentad (2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd, and 27th). The preliminary CHIRPS uses two station sources: GTS and Mexico. The final CHIRPS product takes advantage of several other station sources and is complete sometime in the 3rd week of the following month. Final products for all times/domains/formats are calculated at that time. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, see the Learn More link.  
  
### Additional Information

attributes.name: Conflict and Protest Events
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
The Conflict and Protest Events dataset displays the dates, actors, types of violence, locations, and fatalities of all reported political violence and protest events across Africa, South and Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Europe. Political violence and protest includes events that occur in the context of civil wars and periods of instability, public protest, and regime breakdown. This data can be used for immediate and long-term analysis and mapping of political violence and protest across developing countries through the use of historical data, as well as to inform humanitarian and development work in crisis- and conflict-affected contexts through real-time data updates and reports. 
 
This data is produced by the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED). The project covers all African countries from 1997 to the present, and select countries in the Middle East, Asia, and Europe from 2010 or 2018.   
  
### Methodology  
  
ACLED data was coded by a range of experienced researchers, who collected information primarily from secondary source information and applied the guidelines outlined in the codebook to extract information from news reports. ACLED data was collected each week after individual researchers had scrutinized the information from reports; it was then aggregated and revised by the first coding reviewer and investigated and cross-checked by the second reviewer. The third and final reviewer inspected event notes and details. For full documentation, please read the source [methodology](https://www.acleddata.com/resources/general-guides/).   
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/nrt-scripts/tree/master/soc_016_conflict_protest_events). Coordinates provided in the source data were used to map this data for display on Resource Watch.

info.cautions: ACLED data remains subject to some limitations, and this is particularly true of fatality data. While the "hard facts" of data, such as the date, location, and actors, have been shown to be largely consistent with those of private, closed security sources, fatality data is particularly vulnerable to bias and inaccurate reporting. If there are conflicting reports of the number of fatalities, ACLED researchers will note the varying reported figures in the Notes column and use the figure cited by the most authoritative source. In the absence of a definitive authoritative source, ACLED will assign the most conservative estimate cited to the Fatalities column. Users are urged to remember that fatality figures reflect reported levels of deaths and have not been independently verified by team researchers.

attributes.name: Elevation
attributes.description:
The Elevation data set is produced by the Earth Observation Research Center (EORC) at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). These data represent a global digital surface model (DSM) with 30 m resolution. This data set was created using observations acquired by the PRISM panchromatic stereo mapping sensor on the Advanced Land Observing Satellite “DIACHI” (ALOS). This satellite collected data from 2006-2011. These observations were initially used to create a 5 m resolution DSM with 5 m height accuracy (standard deviation). The 5 m resolution data were upscaled to produce the 30 m resolution, freely-available data set that is displayed here. The value in each 30 m grid cell is calculated by taking the median value of the 5 m grid cells within that area. Resource Watch shows only a subset of the data set. For access to the full data set and additional information, see the Learn More link.  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.

sources.source-description: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency Earth Observation Research Center (JAXA EORC)

info.technical_title: Advanced Land Observing Satellite (ALOS) Global Digital Surface Model (DSM) 30 m, Version 3.2
info.functions: Global elevation, representing a location's height above sea level
info.cautions: - Some pixels were missing data due to cloud or snow cover. The missing data between 60 degrees North and 60 degrees South were filled using the Delta Surface Fill (DSF) method. DSF fills missing values by taking an average of the surrounding cell values from an existing reference digital elevation model (DEM). This average value is adjusted to account for the difference in elevation values between the surrounding cells in the reference DEM and those in the new DEM to ensure a smooth, continuous surface model.

attributes.name: Elevación
attributes.description:
El conjunto de datos de elevación es producido por el Centro de Investigación de Observación de la Tierra (EORC) de la Agencia de Exploración Aeroespacial de Japón (JAXA). Estos datos representan un modelo de superficie digital global (DSM) con una resolución de 30 m. Este conjunto de datos se creó utilizando observaciones adquiridas por el sensor de mapeo estéreo pancromático PRISM en el Satélite Avanzado de Observación de la Tierra "DIACHI" (ALOS). Este satélite recopiló datos de 2006-2011. Estas observaciones se utilizaron inicialmente para crear un DSM de 5 m de resolución con una precisión de altura de 5 m (desviación estándar). Los datos de resolución de 5 m se ampliaron para producir la resolución de 30 m, un conjunto de datos disponible gratuitamente que se muestra aquí. El valor en cada celda de cuadrícula de 30 m se calcula tomando el valor medio de las celdas de cuadrícula de 5 m dentro de esa área. Resource Watch muestra solo un subconjunto del conjunto de datos. Para acceder al conjunto de datos completo e información adicional, consulte el vínculo Más información.  
  
### Información adicional  
  
Resource Watch muestra solo un subconjunto del conjunto de datos. Para acceder al conjunto de datos completo e información adicional, haga clic en el botón "Más información".

Los datos faltantes entre 60 grados Norte y 60 grados Sur se llenaron utilizando el método Delta Surface Fill (DSF). DSF rellena los valores que faltan tomando un promedio de los valores de celda circundantes de un modelo de elevación digital de referencia (DEM) existente. Este valor medio se ajusta para tener en cuenta la diferencia en los valores de elevación entre las celdas circundantes en el DEM de referencia y las del nuevo DEM para garantizar un modelo de superficie suave y continuo.

attributes.name: எழுச்சி
attributes.description:
ஜப்பான் வான்வெளி ஆய்வு முகமையில் (ஜாக்ஸா) புவி அவதானிப்பு ஆராய்ச்சி மையம் (ஈ.ஓ.ஆர்.சி) உயர தரவுத் தொகுப்பு தயாரிக்கிறது. இந்த தரவு 30 மீ தெளிவுத்திறன் கொண்ட உலகளாவிய டிஜிட்டல் மேற்பரப்பு மாதிரியை (டி.எஸ்.எம்) பிரதிபலிக்கிறது. மேம்பட்ட நில அவதானிப்பு செயற்கைக்கோள் "டியாச்சி" (ஏ.எல்.ஓ.எஸ்) இல் பிரிஸ்ம் பஞ்ச்ரோமாடிக் ஸ்டீரியோ மேப்பிங் சென்சார் வாங்கிய அவதானிப்புகளைப் பயன்படுத்தி இந்த தரவுத் தொகுப்பு உருவாக்கப்பட்டது. இந்த செயற்கைக்கோள் 2006-2011 வரையிலான தரவுகளை சேகரித்தது. இந்த அவதானிப்புகள் ஆரம்பத்தில் 5 மீ உயர துல்லியத்துடன் (நியமவிலகல்) 5 மீ தெளிவுத்திறன் கொண்ட டிஎஸ்எம் ஐ உருவாக்க பயன்படுத்தப்பட்டன. 5 மீ தெளிவுத்திறன் தரவு 30 மீ தெளிவுத்திறன், இங்கே காட்டப்படும் சுதந்திரமாக கிடைக்கக்கூடிய தரவுத் தொகுப்பை உருவாக்க மேல்தட்டுப்படுத்தப்பட்டது. ஒவ்வொரு 30 மீ கட்ட கலத்திலும் உள்ள மதிப்பு, அந்தப் பகுதிக்குள் உள்ள 5 மீ கட்டச் செல்களின் சராசரி மதிப்பை எடுத்துக்கொள்வதன் மூலம் கணக்கிடப்படுகிறது. Resource Watch தரவுத் தொகுப்பின் ஒரு துணைக்குழுவை மட்டுமே காட்டுகிறது. முழு தரவுத் தொகுப்பு மற்றும் கூடுதல் தகவலுக்கான அணுகலுக்கு, மேலும் அறிக இணைப்பைப் பார்க்கவும்.  
  
### கூடுதல் தகவல்  
  
Resource Watch தரவுத்தொகுப்பின் ஒரு துணைக்குழுவை மட்டுமே காட்டுகிறது. முழு தரவுத்தொகுப்பு மற்றும் கூடுதல் தகவலுக்கான அணுகலுக்கு, "மேலும் அறிக" பொத்தானைக் கிளிக் செய்க.  
  
### பொறுப்புத்துறப்பு  
  
இந்த விளக்கப் பக்கத்தின் பகுதிகள் மூல மெட்டாடேட்டாவிலிருந்து எடுக்கப்பட்டன.

info.functions: உலகளாவிய உயரம், கடல் மட்டத்திற்கு மேலே ஒரு இடத்தின் உயரத்தைக் குறிக்கிறது
info.cautions: - மேகம் அல்லது பனி மூடி காரணமாக சில பிக்சல்கள் தரவைக் காணவில்லை. 60 டிகிரி வடக்கு மற்றும் 60 டிகிரி தெற்கிற்கு இடையில் காணாமல் போன தரவு டெல்டா மேற்பரப்பு நிரப்பு (டி.எஸ்.எஃப்) முறையைப் பயன்படுத்தி நிரப்பப்பட்டது. DSF தற்போதுள்ள குறிப்பு டிஜிட்டல் உயர்வு மாதிரி (DEM) இலிருந்து சுற்றியுள்ள செல் மதிப்புகளின் சராசரியை எடுத்துக்கொள்வதன் மூலம் காணாமல் போன மதிப்புகளை நிரப்புகிறது. இந்த சராசரி மதிப்பு ஒரு மென்மையான, தொடர்ச்சியான மேற்பரப்பு மாதிரியை உறுதி செய்வதற்காக குறிப்பு DEM இல் உள்ள சுற்றியுள்ள செல்களுக்கும் புதிய DEM இல் உள்ள செல்களுக்கும் இடையிலான உயர மதிப்புகளில் உள்ள வேறுபாட்டைக் கணக்கிடுவதற்காக சரிசெய்யப்படுகிறது.

attributes.name: ఉన్నతి
attributes.description:
జపాన్ ఏరోస్పేస్ ఎక్స్ప్లోరేషన్ ఏజెన్సీ (జేఏఎక్స్ఏ)లోని ఎర్త్ అబ్జర్వేషన్ రీసెర్చ్ సెంటర్ (ఈవోఆర్సీ) ద్వారా ఎలివేషన్ డేటా సెట్ తయారు చేయబడింది. ఈ డేటా 30 మీటర్ల రిజల్యూషన్ తో గ్లోబల్ డిజిటల్ సర్ఫేస్ మోడల్ (DSM)కు ప్రాతినిధ్యం వహిస్తుంది. అడ్వాన్స్ డ్ ల్యాండ్ అబ్జర్వేషన్ శాటిలైట్ "DIACHI" (ALOS)పై ప్రిజం పాంక్రోమాటిక్ స్టీరియో మ్యాపింగ్ సెన్సార్ ద్వారా పొందిన పరిశీలనలను ఉపయోగించి ఈ డేటా సెట్ రూపొందించబడింది. ఈ ఉపగ్రహం 2006-2011 నుండి డేటాను సేకరించింది. ఈ పరిశీలనలు ప్రాథమికంగా 5 మీటర్ల ఎత్తు కచ్చితత్త్వం (స్టాండర్డ్ డీవియేషన్) తో 5 మీటర్ల రిజల్యూషన్ కలిగిన డిఎస్ఎమ్ ను సృష్టించడానికి ఉపయోగించబడ్డాయి. ఇక్కడ ప్రదర్శించబడే 30 మీటర్ల రిజల్యూషన్, స్వేచ్ఛగా లభ్యం అయ్యే డేటా సెట్ ను ఉత్పత్తి చేయడానికి 5 మీటర్ల రిజల్యూషన్ డేటా అప్ స్కేల్ చేయబడింది. ప్రతి 30 m గ్రిడ్ సెల్ లోని విలువ, ఆ ప్రాంతంలోని 5 m గ్రిడ్ సెల్స్ యొక్క మధ్యగత విలువను తీసుకోవడం ద్వారా లెక్కించబడుతుంది. రిసోర్స్ వాచ్ డేటా సెట్ యొక్క ఉపసమితిని మాత్రమే చూపుతుంది. పూర్తి డేటా సెట్ మరియు అదనపు సమాచారానికి ప్రాప్యత కోసం, మరింత తెలుసుకోండి లింక్ చూడండి.  
  
### అదనపు సమాచారం  
  
రిసోర్స్ వాచ్ డేటాసెట్ యొక్క ఉపసమితిని మాత్రమే చూపుతుంది. పూర్తి డేటాసెట్ మరియు అదనపు సమాచారాన్ని యాక్సెస్ చేసుకోవడానికి, "మరింత తెలుసుకోండి" బటన్ మీద క్లిక్ చేయండి.  
  
### డిస్ క్లెయిమర్  
  
ఈ వివరణ పేజీ యొక్క సారాంశాలు మూల మెటాడేటా నుండి తీసుకోబడ్డాయి.

info.functions: గ్లోబల్ ఎలివేషన్, సముద్ర మట్టానికి ఎగువన ఒక ప్రదేశం యొక్క ఎత్తుకు ప్రాతినిధ్యం వహిస్తుంది
info.cautions: - మేఘం లేదా మంచు కవర్ కారణంగా కొన్ని పిక్సెల్స్ డేటాను కోల్పోయాయి. డెల్టా సర్ఫేస్ ఫిల్ (డిఎస్ఎఫ్) పద్ధతిని ఉపయోగించి 60 డిగ్రీల ఉత్తరం మరియు 60 డిగ్రీల దక్షిణం మధ్య తప్పిపోయిన డేటాను నింపారు. ఇప్పటికే ఉన్న రిఫరెన్స్ డిజిటల్ ఎలివేషన్ మోడల్ (DEM) నుంచి చుట్టుపక్కల సెల్ విలువల యొక్క సగటును తీసుకోవడం ద్వారా DSF మిస్ అయిన విలువలను నింపుతుంది. మృదువైన, నిరంతర ఉపరితల నమూనాను ధృవీకరించడం కొరకు రిఫరెన్స్ డిఈఎమ్ లోని చుట్టుపక్కల ఉండే సెల్స్ మరియు కొత్త డిఈఎమ్ లోని సెల్స్ మధ్య ఎలివేషన్ విలువల్లో ఉండే వ్యత్యాసాన్ని లెక్కించడానికి ఈ సగటు విలువ సర్దుబాటు చేయబడుతుంది.
info.citation: జాక్సా ఈవోఆర్ సి. 2021. ఎఎల్ఓఎస్ గ్లోబల్ డిజిటల్ సర్ఫేస్ మోడల్ "ఎఎల్ఓఎస్ వరల్డ్ 3డి - 30 మీ (ఎడబ్ల్యు3డి30)". [http://www.eorc.jaxa.jp/ALOS/en/aw3d30/] (http://www.eorc.jaxa.jp/ALOS/en/aw3d30/). రిసోర్స్ వాచ్, (తేదీ) ద్వారా యాక్సెస్ చేసుకోబడింది. [www.resourcewatch.org] (https://www.resourcewatch.org).

attributes.name: Certified Forest
attributes.description:
The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations includes global country-level statistics for areas of forest under forest certification by the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) and the Programme for the
Endorsement of Forest Certification (PEFC) from 2000 to 2019 . The latter includes
several national/regional certification schemes that have been endorsed according to the PEFC standards.
Data on forest certification are submitted annually to FAO by the head offices of the respective forest
certification scheme. Data include the area certified by each scheme, as well as areas that are double certified by the two schemes. Certification programs such as the FSC and PEFC developed in the late 1990s as voluntary tools to promote sustainable forest management and include criteria for best practices to achieve sustainable forest management from environmental, social, and economic perspectives  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.

attributes.name: Cities with Transit Feed Data
attributes.description:
### Overview  
  
This dataset from MobilityData shows cities where transportation providers publish General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) information.  
  
GTFS feeds are produced by the transit operators themselves and contain information about the operator’s stops, routes, trips, and other scheduling data. The feed covers various different modes of transportation: tram, streetcar, light rail, subway, metro, rail, bus, ferry, cable car, gondola, suspended cable car, and funiculars.This dataset highlights cities where transportation data is publicly available in a common, accessible format for general intracity accessibility and planning usages.  
  
This dataset is compiled from MobilityData’s archive of GTFS feeds from transportation operators. Individual transit feeds are published by the transit operators themselves thereafter and aggregated by MobilityData. The data has global coverage and is expanding as transit operators increasingly publish GTFS feeds. The individual feeds are updated irregularly and depend entirely on the transit operators.  
  
### Methodology  
  
MobilityData creates the GTFS dataset by both seeking out new GTFS feeds and being notified by individual transit operators when they publish a GTFS feed. Mobility data aggregates these feeds into their Application Programing Interface (API) for public use.  
  
The transit operators who are producing and consuming the data drive the additions of specification features. Therefore, MobilityData does not curate data specifications but rather aggregates all the feeds into one dataset.  
  
For the full documentation, please click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Additional Information  
  
Resource Watch shows only a subset of the dataset. Data on GTFS feeds is available on MobilityData’s API as provided by the transportation operator. For access to the full dataset and additional information, click on the “Learn more” button.  
  
### Visualizing the Data  
  
Our team reformatted this dataset before displaying it on Resource Watch. See the documentation on how Resource Watch processed the data on [Github](https://github.com/resource-watch/nrt-scripts/tree/master/cit_041a_gtfs_point_locations). Coordinates provided in the source data were used to map this data for display on Resource Watch.  
  
### Disclaimer  
  
Excerpts of this description page were taken from the source metadata.
